# Emetos: Specification

Emetos is a code editor in the spirit of Visual Studio Code, written in Go on the [Glutter](https://github.com/rm4n0s/glutter) GUI toolkit, for the Linux desktop. This file is the source of truth: when the code and this file disagree, one of them is wrong, and the user decides which.

The work is split into the eleven areas of VS Code listed in §3. **This version of the spec covers areas 1 (the editor) and 2 (the workbench).** The other areas are listed so that the architecture leaves room for them, and get their own sections when they are planned.

"VS Code" below means VS Code 1.143.0, the version pinned in `scripts/reference-versions.txt` (§17). Where this spec says "as VS Code", VS Code's source at that version is the definition, and this spec's description is a summary.

---

## 1. Goals

| # | Goal |
|---|---|
| G1 | **What VS Code has.** Areas 1 and 2 (§3) match VS Code's behavior, defaults, command ids and Linux keyboard shortcuts closely enough that a VS Code user feels at home. When in doubt, do what VS Code does |
| G2 | **Private.** No telemetry, no crash reporting, no update checks (§12) |
| G3 | **Native and light.** One Go binary, no Electron, no Node.js, no cgo. Starts fast, stays responsive on large files, uses no CPU when idle (§14) |
| G4 | **Compatible file formats.** VS Code's color themes, file icon themes, TextMate grammars, language configurations, snippet files, `settings.json` and `keybindings.json` formats work, so existing material can be reused |
| G5 | **Core and UI apart.** The editor core never imports Glutter. It is tested without a display, and the UI only shows and edits its state (§5) |
| G6 | **Testable.** Every feature has tests; UI features have widget tests and golden images that run without a display (§15) |

## 2. Non-goals

- Running VS Code extensions or a Node.js extension host.
- Windows, macOS, the web. Linux desktop only (Wayland and X11 through Glutter).
- Areas 3–11 of §3, until they are planned. Their hooks are listed where they matter (for example, the Problems panel exists but has no producers until area 3).
- Microsoft's proprietary features: Marketplace, Settings Sync with a Microsoft/GitHub account, Live Share, Copilot.
- Workspace trust (it guards extensions and tasks, which don't exist yet).
- Multi-root workspaces (`.code-workspace` with several folders). One window opens one folder or loose files.
- Vim/Emacs emulation (in VS Code they are extensions).
- Moved-code detection in the diff editor, and the accessible diff viewer.

| # | Area | Status |

| 1 | **The editor**: editing, multi-cursor, find/replace, highlighting, brackets, folding, minimap, sticky scroll, breadcrumbs, undo, auto-save, hot exit, snippets, Emmet, diff and merge editors, encodings, line endings, large files | **this spec** |
| 2 | **The workbench**: layout, editor groups and tabs, explorer, command palette, quick open, status bar, notifications, Output and Problems panels, zen mode, windows, themes, keybindings, settings and their UIs, profiles | **this spec** |
| 3 | Language intelligence through LSP | **this spec**: §9.12, D20, milestone M12 (steps 12.2–12.9) |
| 4 | Project-wide search and replace | later |
| 5 | Source control (git) | later |
| 6 | Run and debug through DAP | later |
| 7 | Integrated terminal | **this spec**: an extension (§10.25, D27), milestone M17d |
| 8 | Tasks | later |
| 9 | Remote development | later |
| 10 | Notebooks, testing UI, multi-root workspaces, settings sync | later |
| 11 | Extensions | **this spec**: compiled-in extensions (D18, §10.15), milestone M11; Go (§10.17, M14) and Remote Work (§10.18, D19, M15) and Relay (§10.19, D21, M16) extensions |

### 3.1 Area 1 in detail

| Feature | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Editing | Typing, overtype mode (Insert key, `OVR` in the status bar, `editor.overtypeCursorStyle`, `editor.overtypeOnPaste`; step 10.2), delete/backspace by character and word (and word part), new line with auto-indent, indent/outdent, tab size and spaces/tabs per file, detect indentation from content |
| Line commands | Move line up/down, copy line up/down, delete line, insert line above/below, join lines, transpose, sort lines ascending/descending, trim trailing whitespace, change case (upper, lower, title), toggle line comment, toggle block comment |
| Cursors and selections | Multiple cursors (Alt+Click, Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down... as VS Code's Linux keymap), add next occurrence (Ctrl+D), select all occurrences (Ctrl+Shift+L), column selection (Shift+Alt+drag and keyboard), expand/shrink selection (by word, string, brackets, line), cursor undo (Ctrl+U), primary selection on X11 and Wayland |
| Find and replace | Find widget with regex, match case, whole word, find in selection, preserve case, replace one/all, match count, highlight all matches, seed the search from the selection |
| Highlighting | TextMate grammars (§8.3), VS Code color themes (§8.4), current line highlight, selection and word highlights |
| Brackets | Matching bracket highlight, jump to bracket, bracket pair colorization, bracket pair guides, auto-closing and auto-surrounding pairs, auto-closing quotes, over-typing an auto-inserted closing character |
| Indentation | Indent guides (active guide highlighted), indentation rules and on-enter rules from language configurations, convert/reindent commands |
| Folding | Fold by indentation and by `#region` markers (§8.7); fold/unfold one, recursively, all, by level; folding gutter controls |
| Display | Line numbers (absolute, relative, off), rulers, word wrap (off, on, at column, bounded), render whitespace (none, boundary, selection, trailing, all), render control characters, cursor styles and blinking modes, smooth scrolling, font size and zoom, font ligatures on/off, letter spacing, line height |
| Minimap | Rendered blocks of the text with token colors, viewport slider, click and drag to scroll, show on the right or left, scale 1–3, hide setting (§9.5) |
| Sticky scroll | The headers of the folding ranges that contain the top line stay at the top of the editor (up to 5 lines); click jumps to the header |
| Breadcrumbs | The file path above the editor, each segment a picker of its siblings. Symbols come with area 3 |
| Undo/redo | Per document, grouped as VS Code groups edits, with cursor state restored. Survives save, not restart |
| Saving | Save, Save As, Save All, Revert, Save without Formatting (no save participants), Save with Encoding; untitled files (Ctrl+N); auto save by `files.autoSave`: `off`, `afterDelay` (after `files.autoSaveDelay` without edits), `onFocusChange` (the editor loses the focus, another editor becomes active, or the window loses the focus), `onWindowChange` (the window loses the focus), with `files.autoSaveWorkspaceFilesOnly` and `files.autoSaveWhenNoErrors`, and File > Auto Save (as built in §6.3); trim trailing whitespace, insert final newline and trim final newlines on save (as built in §6.3); closing an editor, a group, a folder or the window with unsaved changes asks Save / Don't Save / Cancel in one dialog (step 7.2, §10.3, §10.10) |
| Hot exit | Unsaved changes of every editor, including untitled ones, are backed up a second after the last change and when the window closes, and come back dirty on the next start, also after a crash; `files.hotExit` (`off`, `onExit`, `onExitAndWindowClose`) decides whether closing asks about them. A file that changed or was deleted since its backup opens with a notice (step 7.6, §10.10) |
| Snippets | VS Code snippet syntax (tab stops, placeholders, choices, variables, transforms, nested); user snippet files (global and per language); insert snippet command; tab-completion of snippet prefixes (`editor.tabCompletion`) |
| Emmet | HTML and CSS abbreviation expansion with the "Emmet: Expand Abbreviation" command, and with Tab when `emmet.triggerExpansionOnTab` is on |
| Diff editor | Side-by-side and inline views, character-level changes, ignore trim whitespace, next/previous change (Alt+F5, Shift+Alt+F5), compare two files, compare with saved, read-only original (§9.11; side-by-side built in step 9.5, inline and the compare commands in 9.6) |
| Merge editor | Three-way merge (incoming, current, result panes) of a file with conflict markers or of `--merge` inputs, conflicts outlined and navigable, accept incoming/current/both per conflict and for all, reset, edit the result, complete merge with `--wait` exit codes (§9.11; layout, checkboxes and navigation built in step 9.7, the actions and Complete Merge in 9.8) |
| Files | Encodings (§6.3), line endings LF and CRLF (detect, convert), BOM, read-only files, files changed on disk (a clean editor reloads, a dirty one asks: Compare, Overwrite and Revert; a deleted file stays open, struck through; as built in §6.3 "External changes"), large files (§6.4), binary files (refused with a notice) |

### 3.2 Area 2 in detail

| Feature | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Layout | Menu bar, activity bar, primary side bar, editor area, panel (bottom, or left/right), status bar; each part can be hidden, and sizes are remembered (§10.1) |
| Editor groups | Split editors right/down/left/up, any number of groups in a grid, move/copy editors between groups, focus groups by number or direction, close, maximize a group, join groups, move groups, editor layouts (§10.3) |
| Tabs | Preview editors (italic, replaced by the next preview), pinned tabs, dirty indicator, close button, close others/to the right/saved/all, reorder and move by drag, scroll when they overflow, reveal in explorer, copy path |
| Navigation | Back/forward history across editors (Ctrl+Alt+- / Ctrl+Shift+-, VS Code's Linux keys), last edit location (Ctrl+K Ctrl+Q), reopen closed editor (Ctrl+Shift+T), go to line (Ctrl+G), switch editors (Ctrl+Tab, a picker that chooses when Ctrl is released; Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown), quick open (Ctrl+P) with recent files and fuzzy file search, command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) |
| Explorer | Folder tree with file watching, `files.exclude`, new file/folder, rename (F2), delete to trash, cut/copy/paste, drag to move, drop files from the file manager, compact folders, reveal active file, Open Editors section, collapse all |
| Status bar | Line/column and selection count, indentation, encoding, line endings, language mode (each one opens its picker), notifications bell, problem counts, the message of a pending chord (§10.1 "Status bar as built") |
| Notifications | Info, warning and error toasts with actions, notification center, do-not-disturb |
| Panels | Output (channels: the Emetos log, and more later), Problems (the model and the view exist; nothing reports markers until area 3) (§10.13) |
| Zen mode and full screen | Zen mode hides everything but the editor; full screen; centered layout |
| Workspace tabs and tray | One window (D17): every folder is a workspace tab in a strip at the very top (folder name with a workspace icon, unsaved-changes dot, close button); `emetos <path>` reaches the running instance and opens or focuses a tab; new, close, switch (Ctrl+Alt+PageUp/PageDown, Ctrl+Alt+1–9, a picker) and reorder tabs; a system tray icon whose menu lists the tabs; the window's close button hides the window to the tray (`window.closeToTray`); tabs, their editors and the window come back on restart (§10.14). Built as several windows by step 7.8, turned into tabs by milestone M9b |
| Restore and recent lists | The window comes back as it was: layout, groups with their editors (pinned, preview, sticky, the active ones) and each editor's cursors, scroll position and folds, the Explorer's expanded folders, the size and the maximized or full-screen state (`window.restoreWindows`, `window.restoreFullscreen`); editors whose files are gone are dropped with a notification. File > Open Recent and Ctrl+R list the recently opened folders and files, "Clear Recently Opened..." clears them (step 7.5, §10.10) |
| Themes | Color theme picker (Ctrl+K Ctrl+T) that previews the active theme in every window of the same profile, writes `workbench.colorTheme` on Enter and goes back on Escape; file icon theme picker (Seti, None); follow the system's dark/light mode; user themes folder (§8.4, §10.8) |
| Settings | Default/user/workspace/language-specific layers; `settings.json` (JSON with comments); settings UI (Ctrl+,) with User and Workspace tabs, a tree of VS Code's categories, a row for each setting by type (check box, number and text boxes, list of values, link to the JSON for the rest), modified marks, Reset Setting and search; it edits the JSON and keeps comments, and edits the open `settings.json` editor instead of the file while there is one (§11.1) |
| Keybindings | VS Code's Linux keymap (§11.3); `keybindings.json`; keybindings editor ("Keyboard Shortcuts", §11.3) with search by name, key, source or command id, record a key, add/change/remove/reset, conflicts, and the when-clause |
| Profiles | Named sets of settings, keybindings, snippets and UI state; create, rename, switch, delete, export/import as a file (§10.12), from the Profiles submenu of the Manage menu and the palette, with the name in the status bar when it is not the default |

## 4. Decisions log

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Go, Glutter, Linux desktop only | The user's choice; Glutter is the user's toolkit |
| D2 | No cgo, ever | Glutter is cgo-free; `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build` keeps the build to Go alone |
| D3 | The core (`internal/core/...`) never imports Glutter; the UI (`internal/gui/...`) imports the core (§5.2) | Testable core, a UI that can change |
| D4 | No telemetry, crash reports or update checks (§12). Features and extensions may use the network for what the user asks of them (the user's choice, 2026-10-25: the earlier rule of no network access at all is gone) | G2 |
| D5 | Language intelligence comes only from LSP and debugging only from DAP (areas 3 and 6) | One mechanism for every language |
| D6 | Text is UTF-8 in memory; positions are zero-based lines and byte columns; visual columns are computed for display (§6.2) | Matches Glutter's text API; LSP 3.17 can negotiate UTF-8 positions, and UTF-16 is converted when a server can't |
| D7 | VS Code's file formats for themes, icon themes, grammars, language configurations, snippets, settings and keybindings (G4) | Reuse of existing material |
| D8 | When Glutter lacks something, Emetos works around it, marks the code with `// Glutter:`, and lists it in `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md` (which exists only while there are open issues) | The user's rule (CLAUDE.md) |
| D9 | Every workbench widget, including the menu bar and menus, is Emetos's own (`gui/kit`) on Glutter's `widgets` layer, themed by VS Code workbench colors. No Material widgets | A dense IDE look, one look for every menu |
| D10 | Glutter v1.4.0 or newer: fonts loaded at run time (`RunAppOpts.Fonts`, `PlatformDispatcher.LoadFontFromList`), fonts in `gluttertest` (`Opts.Fonts`), family fallback in order, font queries and the desktop's font settings, `TreeSliver`, tab stops (`ParagraphStyleOpts.TabSize`), the cache of shaped runs | What the editor needs |
| D11 | Regular expressions with `github.com/dlclark/regexp2` (§8.2) | TextMate grammars need lookbehind and backreferences |
| D12 | Workspace settings only in `<folder>/.emetos/settings.json`; `.vscode/` is not read | The user's choice |
| D13 | Bundled languages: the list in §8.1. Go, Markdown, JSON, YAML, Python, JavaScript and TypeScript come first and get the deepest tests. Each is a **language pack**, an extension under `extensions/` (step 11.4, §10.15); the list of the bundled languages is the list of the packs in `extensions/all.go` | The user's priorities |
| D14 | Fonts: the editor uses the desktop's monospace font (`MonospaceFont()`), then `monospace`; the workbench uses the desktop's UI font (`UIFont()`), then `sans-serif`. Codicons and the Seti icon font are bundled and loaded through `RunAppOpts.Fonts`. Tests use Go Mono (from `golang.org/x/image/font/gofont`) through `gluttertest.Opts.Fonts` | Looks like the desktop; deterministic tests with no extra dependency |
| D15 | Debug-only **dev commands** (`EMETOS_DEV_COMMANDS`, §15.2) run commands after the first frame, to reach states for proof screenshots and performance runs. They exist in debug builds and in builds with the `emetos_dev` tag, never in release builds | Proofs and measurements without a mouse |
| D16 | Users install release builds: `go install -tags glutter_release github.com/rm4n0s/emetos/cmd/emetos@latest` | Glutter's debug builds are 8–10 times slower in the framework |
| D17 | One window: every folder is a workspace tab in a strip at the top of Emetos's own title bar, with a system tray icon; the window's close button hides the window to the tray (§10.14). It replaces the several windows of step 7.8 | The user's choice; one place for every project, the editor stays running |
| D18 | Extensions are Go packages compiled into Emetos: one folder per extension under `extensions/`, their constructors listed in `extensions/all.go`; one extension contributes to many places (window tabs, file views, side bar views, commands, settings, languages, language servers...); extensions talk to each other only through events, scoped to a window tab, and across window tabs only along links the user allowed, in their direction, kept in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/event-sharing.json` (§10.15). The bundled languages are extensions too | The user's choice: no plugin loading and no extension processes; the editor stays one Go program |
| D19 | Remote Work, the remote control of a workspace (§10.18): an Emetos lets listed SSH keys use one workspace from another Emetos, in a view of its own; login over SSH (key only, the host key pinned), then QUIC over UDP with a session token and a pinned certificate, falling back to SSH over TCP | The user's choice: no passwords, UDP for a fluid picture, the security of SSH keys |
| D20 | Language features have one client (`core/lsp`) and one UI; servers and Go providers are contributions of extensions, started per workspace tab | One mechanism for every language (D5), language packs stay extensions (D18) |
| D21 | Relay (§10.19): a user controls a shared workspace of another Emetos through its events and commands over SSH (TCP), watch-only or watch and send per key and workspace; only `emetos.relay` gets the privileges to publish any topic and execute any command, and only in the workspace it was given | The user's design for research and experiment; the privileges stay out of every other extension |
| D22 | Containers (§10.20): two extensions, Docker (`emetos.containers`, in the spirit of VS Code's Container Tools, MIT, ported where it helps) and Podman (`emetos.podman`), sharing one engine client over the engines' HTTP APIs on a Unix socket (no Docker SDK, no new module) and one set of views; the CLI is used only for build, push, Compose and Kube, where the user's credential helpers and plugins matter | The user's request of 2026-10-27; the APIs are stable and documented, and the CLI keeps the user's own setup |
| D23 | Databases (§10.21–§10.23): SQL (PostgreSQL with pgx, MySQL and MariaDB, SQLite with the pure-Go modernc driver, SQL Server), MongoDB with its official driver, Redis with go-redis; all pure Go, so Emetos stays cgo-free | The user's choices of 2026-10-27 |
| D24 | Database passwords are never written to an Emetos file: the desktop keyring (Secret Service over D-Bus) when the user asks to save one, otherwise asked and kept in memory | A state file is not a safe place for a password; every Linux desktop has a keyring |
| D25 | The commands of the container and database extensions are refused to Relay clients (`command.ClientRefusal` class `outside`): they reach beyond the workspace, and the Docker socket is power over the computer | Relay's confinement (D21) stays true |
| D26 | **No Claude Code in Emetos.** The Agents extension (§10.16, M13) was removed by step 17c.1 at the user's request of 2026-10-27 ("Remove claude code extension. I don't want to read any conditions or accept any terms"); Emetos neither runs nor downloads the Claude Code program. Its pseudo-terminal code moved to `extensions/internal/pty` for the terminal (§10.25) | no third-party terms to accept to publish Emetos |
| D27 | **The terminal is an extension** (`emetos.terminal`, §10.25): VS Code's integrated terminal with an emulator ported from xterm.js (MIT), whose terminals are events and requests, so Relay (§10.19) shows them to clients and lets a client type only where the host checked **Allow terminals** (off by default) | the user's request of 2026-10-27; a terminal is the most powerful thing a client can reach, so it has its own permission |

## 5. Architecture

### 5.1 Processes, windows and threads

Emetos is one process with one or more windows. Glutter's UI goroutine owns every widget and render object.

**Per process**: settings registry and default/user layers, command registry, default keymap, theme service, language and grammar registries, the notification and log sinks, `core/ipc`, the profile in use by default.

**Per window** (a `Window` value created by `gui/app` for each Glutter window): the folder (workspace) or none, the workspace settings layer, the root context key scope, the documents (the same file open in two windows is two documents, as in VS Code's separate windows), editor groups, the file watcher, UI state, backups, the profile in use by that window.

Threads:
- **Documents** are changed only on the UI goroutine. Every change produces a new immutable **snapshot** of the buffer (§6.1) that background goroutines read freely.
- **Background work** (tokenizing, folding ranges, wrapping, file watching, fuzzy file search, diffing, backups) runs on goroutines with a `ctx`, reads snapshots, and posts results to the UI goroutine through `WidgetsBinding.Post` or `State.SetState`. A result for an older document version is dropped.
- **Child processes** (language servers, debug adapters, terminals) come with later areas and follow the same rule.

**Several windows as built (step 7.8), and as tabs since step 9b.1 (`gui/app/workspaces.go`).** Step 7.8 built one Glutter window per folder; step 9b.1 (D17, §10.14) turned them into **workspace tabs of one window**: `Process.Workspaces` (`*Workspaces`) is the manager of the window tabs (the list in the order of the strip, which one is active, what opens, activates, moves, replaces and closes a tab; all on the UI goroutine, the list has a mutex because a change of the settings of one workspace reaches the others from the goroutine that made it), `app.Workspace` (was `Window`) is what a tab holds, and the one Glutter window is the implicit window of `RunApp`, showing the active tab through `tabsHost` (an `IndexedStack`; §10.14 "As built"). The rest of this paragraph is the design of step 7.8 and still holds with "window" read as "workspace tab" (it also names `Windows`, `windowHost` and `WindowManager`, which are gone). *Shared by the tabs of the process:* the registries of settings, commands (the definitions), menus, views and default keys, the language and grammar registries, the user's color themes (read once; each workspace's theme service gets them), the logs, the profiles (`Process.Profiles`), the state store of the default profile (`state.json`, shared by all the profiles: its recently opened lists, the open tabs and the profile of each folder are written once, whichever tab changes them; the stores of the other profiles hold the state files of their workspaces, `Process.StateFor`) and the launcher of the socket. *Per workspace:* the theme service (`Workspace.Themes`: the color theme comes from the settings of the workspace, which follow its profile, §10.12) and the snippet service (`Workspace.Snippets`), a fork of the command registry (`Workspace.Commands`: the commands are the process's, the handlers the shell sets are the workspace's, so a key pressed in one tab never runs another's handler; handlers set on the process registry before a workspace is made, such as the dev commands, are copied), the notification service and its presenter (`Workspace.Notify`: what a workspace reports is shown in that tab), the settings store with the layer of its folder (a change of the user's `settings.json` in one store is read again at once by the stores of the workspaces that use the same profile, whose `settings.json` it is), the documents, the editor groups, the layout, the quick input, the watcher, the file index, the backups and the UI state. Workspace-bound work (a notification, a command) goes through the `Workspace`, never through the process. Widgets find their workspace with `WorkspaceOf`/`PeekWorkspace`; no Glutter type is in the core.

### 5.2 Package layout

```
cmd/emetos/                    main: command line, single instance, app start; the only place that lists the extensions (§10.15)
extension/                     the public contract of the extensions: Factory, Extension, Manifest, API and the interfaces it returns (§10.15, D18); imports nothing of Emetos
extension/ui/                  the widgets of the editor an extension builds its views with: the theme, the Codicons, the kit's lists, trees, buttons and inputs; the one place of the contract that imports internal/gui/kit (§10.15)
extension/ui/uitest/           the test harness of the widgets of an extension (the theme in dark and light, the test fonts, goldens)
extensions/                    the extensions compiled into Emetos, one folder each, and all.go with the list; imports only extension/ (§10.15, D18)
extensions/internal/testext/   the extension that tests the contract; never in the list
extensions/internal/fakeapi/   an extension.API in memory for the tests of the extensions (views, Output channels, markers, commands, settings, events)
extensions/todo/, tasks/       the TODOs view of the side bar and the Tasks tab of the panel (§10.15)
extensions/internal/langpack/  what the language packs share: an extension whose only contribution is languages (§8.1, §10.15)
extensions/<pack>/             the 22 language packs (golang, json, yaml, markdown, python, javascript, typescript, html, css, scss, less, xml, sql, shellscript, makefile, docker, ini, cpp, rust, diff, git, gomod), each with its grammars and language configurations in assets/ (§8.1)
internal/core/                 no Glutter import anywhere below (checked by internal/archtest)
  buffer/                      positions, piece tree, snapshots, line index (§6.1, §6.2)
  fileio/                      read/write, encodings, line endings, atomic save, trash (§6.3)
  document/                    document = buffer + metadata + undo + decorations (§7.1)
  edit/                        columns, boundaries, selections, cursor movement, editing commands (§6.2, §7.2)
  vstest/                      test helpers: VS Code positions (1-based, UTF-16) to Emetos positions (§15.1)
  glob/                        VS Code glob patterns, and .gitignore matching (§10.5, §10.6)
  language/                    language registry (plain text only of its own), language configurations; packfs and languagetest give the tests the files of the language packs (§8.1, §10.15)
  regex/                       Oniguruma-style regular expressions for grammars, ECMAScript mode for find (§8.2)
  textmate/                    grammar loading and line tokenizer (§8.3)
  tokens/                      per-document tokenization state, background tokenizer (§8.3)
  theme/                       color themes, token colors, workbench color registry (§8.4), file icon themes (§10.8)
  brackets/                    bracket pairs, matching, colorization (§8.5)
  indent/                      indentation rules, detection, on-enter rules, guides (§8.6)
  autoclose/                   auto-closing and surrounding pairs of the languages (§8.6.4)
  comment/                     comment tokens of the languages (§8.6.5)
  folding/                     folding range providers and model (§8.7)
  find/                        find/replace model (§9.8)
  snippet/                     snippet parser, variables and session (§9.9)
  emmet/                       Emmet abbreviations (§9.10)
  diff/                        line and character diff, three-way merge model (§9.11)
  jsonc/                       JSON with comments: parse, and edit keeping comments (§11.1)
  plist/                       XML property lists, the format of TextMate themes and of one grammar (§8.1, §8.4)
  settings/                    settings registry, layers, change events (§11.1)
  contextkey/                  context keys and when-clause expressions (§11.2)
  command/                     command registry, menu registry, view registry (§11.2, §10.1, §10.4)
  keybinding/                  keys, keymap, chords, resolver, default Linux keymap (§11.3)
  editorgroup/                 editor inputs, editor groups and their grid, as data (§10.3)
  workspace/                   folder, file tree model, watcher, file operations, file list and search of the quick open (§10.5, §10.6)
  fuzzy/                       fuzzy matching and scoring (§10.6)
  storage/                     paths, UI state, backups (hot exit), profiles (§10.10, §10.12)
  ipc/                         single instance over a Unix socket (§10.11)
  logs/                        log channels shown in the Output panel (§13)
  notify/                      notification model (§10.7)
  lsp/                         the LSP client: framing, JSON-RPC, the handshake, positions in the negotiated encoding, document sync, the wire types of area 3, the server process (§9.12)
  lsp/lsptest/                 the fake language server, as a program (fakeserver/) and in process, its JSON script, and the harness that connects a client to it (§9.12)
  langfeatures/                language feature types, the provider registry (servers and Go providers alike), merging, LSP to Emetos conversions, the server provider, `WorkspaceEdit` application (§9.12)
internal/gui/                  imports Glutter and the core
  app/                         app start, windows, wiring of the services, dev commands (§5.1, §15.2)
  kit/                         the IDE widget kit: theme, icons, split view, tree, list, tabs, inputs, buttons, menus, hovers, dialogs (§10.2)
  kit/fonts/                   bundled icon fonts and their family names
  editor/                      the editor widget (§9)
  diffeditor/, mergeeditor/    §9.11
  workbench/                   layout parts, editor group views, title/menu bar, activity bar, status bar (§10)
  quickinput/                  command palette, quick open, pickers (§10.6)
  exthost/                     the extension host: activation per window tab, contained failures, the API bound to a tab (§10.15)
  extensionsui/                the page "Extensions" (§10.15)
  views/explorer/, views/outline/, views/output/, views/problems/   (problems also holds the markers model, which has no Glutter import: §10.13)
  settingsui/, keybindingsui/  §11
  testutil/                    widget-test helpers: fonts, isolated paths, proof images (§15)
internal/archtest/             tests of package boundaries, forbidden imports and where errors are built (§5.3, §12, §13); cmd/errortags lists the error Tags (scripts/error-tags.sh)
third_party/                   licenses of bundled assets (§17)
assets/                        dev.emetos.Emetos.desktop, the desktop entry that scripts/install-desktop.sh installs (§10.14, §16)
assets/icons/                  the application icon as PNG files (emetos-16.png ... emetos-512.png) and the package that embeds them (§10.14, §17); the tests of the desktop entry and of scripts/install-desktop.sh
scripts/                       fetching references, copying assets, proofs, headless runs, performance, installing the desktop entry and the icons, the screenshots of the README (`scripts/screenshots.sh`, from `testdata/screenshots/` into `docs/screenshots/`)
```

Directories hold a `doc.go` only when they hold Go code.

### 5.3 Boundary rules (checked by `internal/archtest`)

- No package under `internal/core/` imports `github.com/rm4n0s/glutter/...` or `internal/gui/...`.
- No `import "C"`.
- `github.com/dlclark/regexp2` only in `internal/core/regex`.
- No import of the standard library `errors`, and no call of `fmt.Errorf` (CLAUDE.md "Error handling").
- Errors are built where the failure is found (§13). `Check` fails on: a package-level `errors.New`, `errors.NewErr` or `errors.NewErrf` (`PackageLevelError`, in code and in tests; a sentinel is `&errors.Error{Tag: ...}`); a function in non-test code that only builds an error (`ErrorHelper`: it returns `error` or `*errors.Error`, its body is assignments and declarations followed by one `return` with a constructor, with its `SetMetadata` chain, among the results, and another function of the package returns a call of it or panics with one; a function that tests something first, and a stub that always fails and is not returned from, are not matched); a constructor in non-test code whose tag is not a string literal (`NonLiteralTag`); and `errors.NewErr` or `errors.NewErrf` (with `%w`) that wraps a variable whose nearest definition in scope is a call of a function of another package of Emetos, found by the import path of the selector (`ProjectErrorRewrapped`: such an error already has its Tag and route and is returned as it is; an `if` whose init or condition calls `FromError` is the guard that keeps tagged errors and is not reported; calls of methods and of functions of the same package are not seen by this check and are left to review).
- Extensions (§10.15): a package under `extensions/` imports only `extension/`, the standard library, its own subpackages, `extensions/internal/...` and the dependencies CLAUDE.md allows (`ExtensionImportsInternal` for `internal/...` or `cmd/...`, `ExtensionImportsExtension` for another extension, `ExtensionImportsForbidden` for any other module or a package in Glutter's `internal` folders; `extensions/all.go` may import every extension); and a package under `internal/` never imports `extensions/...` (`ExtensionsImportedByInternal`: only `cmd/emetos` lists the extensions, so the editor has no special case for a bundled one; a `_test.go` file under `internal/gui/` is the one exception, for the end-to-end tests of two instances, step 15.4).
- The public contract (§10.15): a package under `extension/` imports no other package of Emetos than those of `extension/` (`ExtensionContractImportsEmetos`), except `extension/ui`, which may import `internal/gui/kit` and `internal/gui/kit/fonts` and nothing else of the editor, and its test harness `extension/ui/uitest`, which may also import `internal/gui/testutil` (`ExtensionUIImportsInternal`). So the contract stays free of the editor, and the one bridge to its widgets is a list that review can read.
- Every error Tag has a test (§13): `TestEveryErrorTagHasARouteTest` fails for a Tag that no test asserts, unless `docs/ERROR-TAGS-UNTESTED.md` lists it; `scripts/error-tags.sh` prints the Tags and, with `--untested`, those without a test.

### 5.4 Key handling

One **key dispatcher** per window, a `Focus` node at the root of the window's widget tree, resolves every key event through `core/keybinding` against the context key scope of the focused widget (§11.2), so a shortcut works wherever focus is (editor, explorer, quick input). Widgets below it handle a key themselves only for text entry. A key with no binding is left unhandled, and Glutter types its character into the focused text input client. Modifier-only key events never cancel a pending chord.

**Implementation (step 3.5).** `app.KeyDispatcher` sits above the app in the window's tree: it registers an early key handler of the focus manager, so a bound key is used before focus traversal and before the focused widget; `ChordOf` turns a key event into a chord (`KeyOf`: a Latin letter or digit comes from the logical key, any other key, and a letter on a layout without Latin letters, from the name of the physical key on a US keyboard); `Window.DispatchKey` resolves it with the window's `Dispatcher` in the context key scope of the focus node (`kit.FocusScopes` maps nodes to scopes; the nearest ancestor with a scope counts, the window's root scope otherwise), runs the command and reports whether the key was used. Key ups dispatch nothing; a press of a modifier alone keeps a pending chord; a chord's status is passed to `Window.OnChordStatus` (logged until the status bar shows it). A command that fails is logged; the key counts as used. The editor (`editor.EditorOpts`) makes its own scope under the window's with `editorTextFocus`, `editorFocus`, `textInputFocus`, `editorHasSelection` (any selection with text), `editorHasMultipleSelections`, `editorColumnSelection`, `editorReadonly`, `editorTabMovesFocus` (false) and `editorLangId`, and binds the handlers of its commands (`editor.BindCommands`, which uses the registry's handler stack) while it has the focus and unbinds them when it loses it.

**Text input (step 3.6).** The editor connects to the platform's text input (`services.TextInputConnection`) when its focus node gets the focus and closes it when it loses it. `editor/input.go`: the client speaks the delta model and gives the input method the current line of the primary cursor (a selection over several lines is a caret at its active end; the value is given again whenever the line, its text or the selection differs, which moves the input method's window with the cursor). A change of the input method is the difference between the line it was given and the text it holds apart from the composing range, found as one replaced stretch aligned to characters; it is typed at every cursor (`Commands.Type` for a stretch that is the selection, `CompositionType` with the characters before and after the cursor for a replacement around it). The composing range is the view model's `Preedit`: drawn above the text at the primary cursor, on the editor's color, with a line below it and a thicker one below the part the method highlights, with the cursor inside it; it is never in the document or the undo history, and it ends when the editor loses the focus. After each frame in which the editor moved, scrolled or changed, `SetEditableSizeAndTransform` and `SetCaretRect` tell the method where the editor and its caret are (the caret rect is the cursor, or the method's cursor inside the preedit): Glutter's `SetComposingRect` does not reach the platform. Characters of keys that no binding takes reach the editor through Glutter's `HandleUnhandledKey` (a key with a character commits it; Enter commits "\n", typed as a new line with the indentation of the line; keys with Control, Alt or Meta type nothing).

## 6. Text core

### 6.1 Buffer (`core/buffer`)

- A **piece tree**: a balanced tree of pieces pointing into read-only original chunks and an append-only add buffer, using VS Code's `PieceTreeTextBuffer` algorithms. Each node keeps the byte length and the number of line feeds of its subtree.
- **Persistent**: nodes are never changed after they are shared; an edit copies the path from the root to the changed nodes (no parent pointers). `Snapshot()` returns an immutable view in O(1), safe to read from any goroutine.
- Operations: insert, delete, replace at byte offsets; `LineCount`, `LineContent(n)`, `LineLength(n)`, `OffsetAt(Position)`, `PositionAt(offset)`, `Text(Range)`, iteration over chunks and lines. All are O(log n) in the number of pieces plus the size of the result.
- The buffer holds only `\n` line endings: `fileio` converts `\r\n` and lone `\r` when it reads (§6.3), and the document remembers the file's line ending for saving.

### 6.2 Positions and columns

- `Position{Line, Col int}`: zero-based line and **byte** column. `Range{Start, End Position}`. `Selection{Anchor, Active Position}`.
- **Visual columns** (column selection, rulers, `editor.tabSize`, vertical cursor movement, the status bar's "Col") follow VS Code's `CursorColumns`: walk the grapheme clusters of the line; for each cluster, take its first code point: a tab advances to the next tab stop, a full-width character or an emoji counts 2, anything else 1. The status bar's "Col" is not the visual column: as VS Code's `toStatusbarColumn`, it counts every code point as 1 (a tab goes to the next tab stop) and adds one, so a wide character or an emoji counts 1 there.
- Grapheme clusters (go-text's segmenter, through Glutter's dependencies) bound cursor movement and deletion.

### 6.3 Files (`core/fileio`)

- Reading returns the text (line endings converted to `\n`), the encoding, the BOM flag, the line ending (`\n` or `\r\n`; mixed endings become the most common one and are reported), and a `FileStat` (modification time, size, mode). Writing returns the new `FileStat`, so the watcher can ignore Emetos's own writes (§10.5).
- Encodings: UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE (BOM), and the encodings of VS Code's `files.encoding` list that `golang.org/x/text/encoding` has; the others are left out of the list. `files.autoGuessEncoding` (off by default, as in VS Code) tries, in order, a BOM, valid UTF-8, then `files.encoding`; VS Code's statistical guessing (jschardet) is not done.
- Saving is atomic: write to a temporary file in the same folder, `fsync`, rename over the original, keep the original mode. When the folder isn't writable, write in place. A read-only file fails with a tagged error; "Overwrite" adds the owner's write permission (`chmod u+w`) and saves, as VS Code does.
- Binary detection, as VS Code's `detectEncodingFromBuffer`: a byte order mark decides the encoding; without one, the first 512 bytes are looked at: if every other byte is a NUL the file is UTF-16 (little or big endian), which is true of Latin-1 text and not of other scripts (those open with "Reopen with Encoding"); any other NUL byte means binary. Binary files open as a notice with "Open anyway".
- "Reopen with Encoding" (the status bar, §10.1) reads the file again with `ForceEncoding` and `Document.Reload` replaces the text and the properties of the document; the picker's guess is the encoding `AutoGuess` finds in at most the first MiB of the file.
- Delete moves to the freedesktop.org home trash (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/Trash`, with `.trashinfo` files); a file on another filesystem than the home trash can't be trashed, and the caller asks to delete permanently. A trashed item can be restored (used by undo in the explorer).

**Saving as built (step 7.1; `core/fileio`, `core/document`, `core/edit`, `gui/app/save.go`).**
- **Pipeline.** A save is three steps so that the disk never blocks the UI thread: `Document.BeginSave(opts)` (UI thread: runs the save participants, takes the text, encoding, byte order mark and line ending, and the alternative version id), `SaveJob.Write(ctx)` (a goroutine: `fileio.Write`, which checks the file against the stat the document last saw and replaces it atomically), and `Document.FinishSave(job, stat)` (UI thread). `Save` and `SaveAs` run the three in a row for callers with no goroutine. The window runs `Write` with `s.Go` and calls `Watcher.Suppress(path, stat)` on that goroutine right after the write, before it hands the result over (§10.5).
- **The race rule.** `FinishSave` makes the version that was *written* the saved version (`savedVersion = job's alternative version id`), and always records the stat of the write. A document that was edited while the write went on therefore stays dirty, and the next save is not a conflict with its own write; an edit that was undone during the write leaves it clean again. A save that comes while one runs waits and runs again when the first ends.
- **Conflicts.** `fileio.WriteOptions.IfUnchanged` is the `FileStat` the document read or wrote last: a file that exists with another size or modification time fails with `FileModifiedSince` (a deleted file is written again, as §7.4 says). `SaveOptions.IgnoreConflict` skips the check (the Overwrite button; or always with `files.saveConflictResolution` = `overwriteFileOnDisk`, whose default is `askUser`). The buttons of the notification are Compare (step 9.6, the diff of the file on disk and the document, §9.11), Overwrite, Revert and Save As.
- **Files.** `fileio.Write` also gives the new file the owner and group of the original when the process may (best effort), keeps the mode, follows a link and writes its target, and fails with `FileNotFound` when the folder is missing, `FileReadOnly` (Overwrite adds `u+w`), `FileIsDirectory`, `FilePermissionDenied`, `FileWriteFailed`, `EncodingCannotRepresent`, `FileExists` (`FailIfExists`, used by Save As) and `WriteCancelled`. Core tags added: `SaveReadOnlyDocument`, `SaveNoFile` (untitled or virtual: needs Save As), `SavePathInvalid`, `SaveParticipantFailed`, `SaveEncodingUnknown`, `RevertNoFile`; app tags: `SaveDialogFailed`, `SaveAsTargetOpen`.
- **Save As.** `BeginSaveAs(path)` writes a new file (`FileExists` unless `Overwrite`), then `FinishSave` gives the document the URI of the file (`SetURI`: `Documents` re-keys it, the watch of a file outside the folder follows, the tab and input follow), looks for the language of the new name (a name no language claims keeps the language: VS Code re-detects only when the new name has a language), and keeps the undo history. The old file is left as it was. A path that is the document's own saves in place. The window refuses a path that another document has open (`SaveAsTargetOpen`; VS Code merges the two editors, Emetos asks to close one first). The recent files and the history follow (an untitled URI in the history goes to the new file URI).
- **The dialog.** The portal (`desktop.SaveFile`) on a goroutine with `Post` back; the name is the file's, or `Untitled-n` plus the first extension of the language, in the file's folder, the window's folder or the home folder. When it fails with `FileChooserUnavailable`, the quick input asks for the path (§10.6) with the suggestion in full to edit: an empty path, a relative path, a folder, or a path whose folder does not exist shows the message under the input and is not accepted; Escape cancels. A target that exists asks "'x' already exists. Do you want to replace it?" (button Replace, as VS Code's `confirmOverwrite`). Cancelling anywhere changes nothing. `Window.SaveDialog` replaces the dialog in tests.
- **Save All** saves the dirty documents of the groups in the order of the tabs, one after the other; an untitled one asks for its file, and cancelling (or a failure of it) stops the rest; a file that fails is reported and the others go on.
- **Revert** (`BeginRevert`/`RevertJob.Read`/`FinishRevert`) reads the file again in the encoding the document has now (so a "Reopen with Encoding" choice is kept) with `Document.Reload`, which drops the undo history (VS Code keeps the history through a revert); an untitled document becomes empty.
- **Participants** (`edit.Commands.SaveParticipants`, `ViewModel.ApplySaveParticipants`, the settings of the language of the document): `files.trimTrailingWhitespace`, `files.insertFinalNewline` and `files.trimFinalNewlines` are applied in that order as one batch, one step of the undo history of their own, with the cursors of the editor kept in the text that is left. A save for `SaveAuto` (auto save after a delay, §6.3 "Auto save") keeps the white space in front of a cursor and the lines up to the lowest cursor; the saves of `onFocusChange` and `onWindowChange` (`SaveFocusChange`, `SaveWindowChange`) trim like an explicit save, as VS Code's `TrimWhitespaceParticipant` only looks at `SaveReason.AUTO`. `files.trimTrailingWhitespaceInRegexAndStrings` is not registered (always on); the lines of a snippet session and `files.trimTrailingWhitespaceInChangedLines` are not built.
- **Auto save** (step 7.3; `document.AutoSave` in `core/document/autosave.go`, `gui/app/autosave.go`). Pure Go: a controller over an injectable clock (`AutoSaveClock.AfterFunc`) and a host (`AutoSaveHost`: the settings of the document, whether it is inside the folder, whether the markers have an error for it, and `Save(doc, reason)`); it does no I/O and starts no goroutine, everything runs on the UI thread. `SaveReason` has `SaveExplicit`, `SaveAuto`, `SaveFocusChange` and `SaveWindowChange`, as VS Code's.
  - *Settings* (registered, scope language-overridable, VS Code's defaults and descriptions): `files.autoSave` (`off` default, `afterDelay`, `onFocusChange`, `onWindowChange`; VS Code's default is `afterDelay` on the web only), `files.autoSaveDelay` (1000 ms, minimum 0; a value that is not a number of 0 or more means 1000, as VS Code's `computeAutoSaveConfiguration`), `files.autoSaveWorkspaceFilesOnly` and `files.autoSaveWhenNoErrors` (false). An unknown mode (the registry already turns it into the default) is logged and means off.
  - *Events.* `afterDelay`: the timer of a dirty document starts at its first edit and starts again with every edit, so it saves `delay` after the last edit; a save, an undo back to the saved text or a revert cancels it; the reason is `SaveAuto`. `onFocusChange`: the editor widget of the document loses the keyboard focus (to another editor, the Explorer, the quick input, anything; an editor that goes away because its tab closed or the window closes does not count, since the decision waits for the next frame), or another editor becomes active in a group or another group becomes active (`onDidActiveEditorChange`: the previous editor "lost the focus"; editors that are being closed do not) saves that document with `SaveFocusChange`; the window losing the keyboard focus (`WidgetsBindingObserver.DidChangeViewFocus`) saves every dirty document with `SaveWindowChange`. `onWindowChange`: only the window losing the focus, with `SaveWindowChange`. Time alone saves nothing in the two focus modes, and focus changes save nothing with `afterDelay`. `AppLifecycleState` is not used.
  - *Eligibility* (`AutoSave.Check`, VS Code's `getAutoSaveMode`): a document that has no file (untitled, virtual) is never auto saved; a read-only one neither; `files.autoSaveWorkspaceFilesOnly` leaves out files outside the folder of the window (none is inside when no folder is open); with `files.autoSaveWhenNoErrors` a document with an error marker (`problems.Service`, severity error) is not saved and waits: when the markers change and it has no error any more, it is saved with the reason it was held back for (VS Code's `waitingOnConditionAutoSave`); a new edit forgets the wait. A document with a Save As dialog or prompt open is left alone, and tried again if that ends without a save.
  - *Failure and pause.* Any failed save of a document (an auto save or not) calls `AutoSave.SaveFailed`: the failure is the one sticky notification of the document that §6.3 "Failures" describes, and the document is **paused**, as VS Code's text file model ignores the auto saves of a model in conflict or error state: no timer, no focus or window save, no save before a close, until a save succeeds, or the document is read again (revert, reload: `CauseSetText`). Editing, dismissing the notification or changing a setting does not resume it. So an unwritable file is tried once, not on every key. The buttons of the notification save with the explicit reason.
  - *Changing the settings* while the window runs: a document whose configuration changed loses its timer and, when auto save is on for it, is saved at once with the reason of its mode (VS Code saves all the dirty documents when the configuration of auto save changes, so switching auto save on with unsaved changes saves them); switching off cancels what is pending; a new delay is used from the next edit.
  - *Closing.* An editor that closes with unsaved changes is saved instead of asked about when `files.autoSave` is `onFocusChange` or `onWindowChange` (VS Code: "a dialog would take the focus"), for documents that may be auto saved (`AutoSave.OnClose`), with the reasons `SaveFocusChange` and `SaveWindowChange` and the save participants; `afterDelay` and `off` ask (VS Code does not save on an editor close with `afterDelay`). The saves are awaited one after the other before the question; a document that fails (its notification shows) or cannot be auto saved (an untitled one, a read-only one, one outside the folder, one with errors, a paused one) stays in the dialog, and Cancel keeps what was saved saved. When the window closes (`Window.RequestClose`), every dirty document that may be auto saved in any mode but `off` (`AutoSave.OnShutdown`) is saved first with `SaveAuto` and without the save participants (VS Code's backup tracker `onBeforeShutdownWithModified`), before the dialog (or the backups of step 7.6) takes the rest. While these saves go on `closeState.busy` is set.
  - *Toggle Auto Save* (`workbench.action.toggleAutoSave`, category File, no key): any mode but `off` becomes `off`, and `off` becomes `afterDelay`; written to the user's settings, or to the workspace's when it sets `files.autoSave`. File menu row "A&&uto Save" (group `5_autosave`, order 1) is checked while `config.files.autoSave != 'off'`.
  - *Not built:* VS Code's `AFTER_SHORT_DELAY` and `AFTER_LONG_DELAY` modes and the context key `autoSaveAfterShortDelay` (they serve backups and the settings editor), the per-resource overrides `enableAutoSaveAfterShortDelay` and `disableAutoSave`, the delay of an auto save after an undo or redo that keeps the participants from undoing the user's undo (`UNDO_REDO_SAVE_PARTICIPANTS_AUTO_SAVE_THROTTLE_THRESHOLD`), the wait for a window of another application (several windows: step 7.8), and a status bar item.
- **Failures** are one sticky notification for the document (a new one replaces the old; a successful save or a revert dismisses it): "Failed to save 'x': ..." with Retry; Overwrite (and Revert) for a conflict; Overwrite for a read-only file; Save with Encoding... for a character the encoding lacks; and always Save As.... A read-only document (`ReadOnly`) is not saved: a quiet (silent) notification says so.
- **External changes** (step 7.4; `core/document/external.go`, `gui/app/external.go`). What the watcher says about the file of an open document is only a hint to look at the file: the window stats it and decides from what it finds, so a batch of events is idempotent and a late or repeated event does nothing. Like a save, a look is three steps so the disk never blocks the UI thread: `Document.BeginExternal` (UI thread: the stat the document has, and whether it has unsaved changes), `ExternalJob.Probe(ctx, Disk)` (a goroutine: the stat, and, when the file differs and the document is clean, the read, with the stat taken again after it) and `Document.ApplyExternal` (UI thread). `Disk` (`Stat`, `Read`; `OSDisk` by default) is the seam tests use to make a read fail or a file change between two steps. "Differs" is `SameStat`: another size or modification time (the mode is not compared), as for the editor's own writes (§10.5).
  - *The file is gone* (stat says so, also when a folder above it is gone, or a folder or a file stands in the place): the document is **orphaned** (`Orphaned()`, VS Code's `TextFileEditorModelState.ORPHAN`; the state is the result of looking, never of the event alone, as VS Code's check that the file is really gone). It keeps its text, its undo history and its dirty state (a clean one stays clean, a dirty one stays dirty); `OnExternalStateChange` tells the listeners. The tab and the row of Open Editors are drawn struck through in `list.errorForeground` (VS Code's file decoration of a deleted model: strikethrough, the color when `workbench.editor.decorations.colors` is on, the tooltip "path • Deleted"); the name is not changed. With `workbench.editor.closeOnFileDelete` on, the clean editors of the file close when the document becomes orphaned (an editor with unsaved changes never closes). A **save** makes the file again (§7.1's write of a deleted file) and clears the state; a file that comes back (an event for its path, or a folder above it, and a look) is read again when the document is clean (a different stat), left alone when the stat is the document's own (git restoring the same file), and a **conflict** when the document is dirty and the stat differs.
  - *The file changed* and the document is clean: it is read again in the encoding the document has (VS Code resolves a model again with the encoding it has; a byte order mark that the file has now still wins, and no guessing replaces the choice of "Reopen with Encoding") and `Document.Reload` replaces the text and the properties (undo history dropped, as for a revert; large-file mode kept). A file whose content is the same (only its time changed) updates the stat and keeps the history. The editors that show the document keep their view state: `ViewModel.ViewState` is taken before and `RestoreView` after (cursors moved into the new text, the scroll position, the folds whose lines still exist), and the keyboard focus is not taken. No notification. A read that fails (permission, a file that became binary or too large) is logged and the document is left as it is: it is looked at again after 300 ms and 2 s and at the next event; a file that changes between the stat before and after the read, or while it is read (a program is still writing it), is left for the next event or those retries. A save of the document that would be racing the look is safe: a save in flight defers the look until it ends (`Document.SaveInFlight`; the editor's own write is also filtered by `Suppress`), and a look that began before a save, a reload, a rename or an edit that matters is thrown away and made again (at most 3 times in a row).
  - *The file changed* and the document has unsaved changes: the text is never touched. The document is marked **conflicted** (`Conflicted()`; `DiskStat()` is the stat on disk) and the window shows ONE sticky notification for it (the slot of the failed-save notification, so a later failed save replaces it with its own, which has the same choices, §6.3 "Failures"): "The file 'x' has changed on disk and you have unsaved changes." with the buttons **Compare** (the diff of the file on disk and the document, step 9.6, §9.11), **Overwrite** (save with `IgnoreConflict`) and **Revert** (§6.3 "Revert": the text of the file, the unsaved changes dropped). More changes of the file do not make more notifications. The notification goes away when the document is saved, reverted or read again, when the file returns to the document's own stat, when the document is closed, and when the changes are undone (a document that is clean again takes the file: it reloads). A plain save of a conflicted document fails as §6.3 "Conflicts" says. A conflicted or orphaned document is **not auto saved** (`AutoSaveBlockedExternal`: no timer, no focus or window save, no save on shutdown; it is asked about when closed like any dirty document, §10.3); VS Code does not do this for an orphaned model, Emetos does so that a deleted file is not made again by itself. Auto save starts again when the state is mended.
  - *Renames.* A rename that the watcher pairs (`Renamed` with `OldPath`, both inside the watched folders) re-points the document with `Document.SetURI` through the code of the Explorer's operations (`followPaths`: the tab, the title, the language by the new extension, the recent files and the history follow; the text, the undo history and the unsaved changes stay), for a file and for every open file below a renamed folder; several renames in one batch are applied in order. The echo of a rename the Explorer made itself finds the document at its new path and changes nothing. A move to a place the watcher does not watch is a deletion (the document is orphaned), and so is a rename the polling fallback cannot pair (§10.5; the new name is not followed). A rename onto a path that another document has open leaves the document at the old path, which is gone (orphaned).
  - *Deleted and renamed folders, rescans.* A `Deleted` or `Renamed` event of a folder and a `Rescan` (the queue of inotify overflowed) touch every open file below the path: each is looked at. Untitled and virtual documents are never looked at.
  - *Deviations from VS Code.* VS Code shows no notification for a dirty model whose file changed (it reports the conflict when the user saves); Emetos asks when it hears of the change, as the step says. A reload drops the undo history (VS Code keeps the model's history through a reload of a clean file). Deleted editors are not given a "(deleted)" in the name (VS Code uses the decoration).
- **Not built:** saving as administrator, `workbench.action.files.saveFiles` and `workbench.files.action.saveAllInGroup`, the Save row of the Open Editors context menu, the Save All button of the Open Editors header, and the "New Text File" rows of the menu of empty editor groups and of the tab strip.

### 6.4 Large files and long lines

| File size | Behavior |
|---|---|
| < 20 MB and < 300,000 li
- **Save participants of the language features** (step 12.8, §9.12): after the trim of trailing white space, `editor.codeActionsOnSave` and then `editor.formatOnSave` run, each bounded by its timeout, before the final-newline participants and the write; a timeout or a failure never stops the save.nes | Everything on |
| 20 MB – 256 MB, or ≥ 300,000 lines | "Large file mode" (`editor.largeFileOptimizations`): no tokenization (plain text), no bracket colorization, no folding, no minimap, no word wrap, and a notice saying so. The decision is made when the document opens and stored on the document; every feature checks it |
| > 256 MB | Refused with an error notice (VS Code's default limit) |

Long lines, as VS Code: a line is drawn up to `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter` (10,000 characters) and the rest is not drawn (cursor positions beyond it are computed with the monospace advance); tokenization of a line stops after `editor.maxTokenizationLineLength` (20,000 bytes). Word wrap does not wrap a line longer than `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter`.

As built (step 5.12): `editor.largeFileOptimizations` (default true; window scope) turns large file mode off when false. In large file mode the tokenizer, the bracket pairs, the folding regions, the minimap, word wrap, sticky scroll and the occurrence and selection highlights are off, and the window shows one notification (`LargeFileNotice`, a warning, once for each document) that says which. Sizes are checked when the file is read (`fileio.Read`: 20 MB or 300,000 lines for large file mode, 256 MB for `FileTooLarge`, which the window shows as "Cannot open <path>: ..."). A file that looks binary fails with `FileBinary`; the window then shows a notice in place of the editor (`editor.Notice`: "The file is not displayed in the editor because it is either binary or uses an unsupported text encoding." and a button "Open Anyway", also reached with Enter or Space) and "Open Anyway" reads it again with `AllowBinary`. Long lines: a row is laid out and drawn up to `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter` bytes (cut at the start of a character; zero or less means no limit); the x of a column past that is the width of the drawn part plus one character width for each byte, the point of a click there is the nearest such column, a selection reaches to the end of the line, and the horizontal scroll extent counts the whole line. `editor.maxTokenizationLineLength` is passed to the grammar of every document (`tokens`). The benchmark of a 200 MB file is `BenchmarkOpen200MB` (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md`).

## 7. Documents and editing

### 7.1 Document (`core/document`)

- A document has: a URI, the buffer, a version id (incremented by every change), an **alternative version id** (as VS Code's: incremented by a change, and restored by undo/redo to the value it had at that point), the saved alternative version id, language id, encoding, line ending, BOM flag, indentation options (`tabSize`, `insertSpaces`, detected or from settings), large-file flag, read-only flag, and the `FileStat` of the last read or write.
- **Dirty** means the alternative version id differs from the saved one, so undoing back to the saved state clears it.
- URI schemes: `file:` (a path), `untitled:<n>` (the lowest free number among the open documents, so a number is used again after its document closes; title "Untitled-n"; made by `Documents.NewUntitled`, in the language of `files.defaultLanguage` (`${activeEditorLanguage}` is the active editor's), with the encoding of `files.encoding` and the line ending of `files.eol`; it is dirty while it has any text, as VS Code's, and a Save As turns it into a `file:` document), and `emetos-virtual:` (read-only generated content, such as the default settings JSON or the saved version of a file for "Compare with Saved"). **`emetos-virtual:` as built (step 8.2; `core/document/virtual.go`, `gui/app/window.go`, `gui/app/virtualdocs.go`).** The URI is `emetos-virtual:<path>` (`emetos-virtual:/defaultSettings.json`). The process owns a `document.VirtualRegistry` (`Process.Virtual`, no global): `Register(path, VirtualProvider{Label, Language, Text(ctx)})` fails with the tags `VirtualProviderInvalid` and `VirtualProviderDuplicate`, `Generate(ctx, uri)` with `VirtualURIUnknown` (no provider has the path, or the URI is not virtual) and `VirtualGenerateFailed` (the provider failed). `Documents.OpenVirtual(ctx, uri)` / `AcquireVirtual` make the document each time they are called: new, with the content and the language the provider says, `ReadOnly` and with the provider's label as its name (`Document.Label()`, which `TextInput.Name` shows: the tab of `emetos-virtual:/defaultSettings.json` is "Default Settings", language `jsonc`); a document that is open already is given the new content (`SetText`) and shown again, never a second one, so it reflects the registry as it is now. A virtual document is never dirty, is not backed up (the tracker takes only files and untitled documents), cannot be edited (typing, pasting and deleting do nothing, the editor shows its read-only state as for a read-only file) and cannot be saved (`workbench.action.files.save` and `saveAs` show the quiet message "Cannot save '…': it is read-only." and write nothing); closing its tab asks nothing and closes the document. `TextInput.Serialize` gives its URI (§10.3, §10.10): the window restores it by asking the provider again, and an editor whose provider is gone is dropped without a word. Providers of Emetos: `/defaultSettings.json` (§11.1). The comparisons add their own (step 9.6, §9.11 "Inline view and compare commands as built"): `/saved/<path of a file>` (the file as it is on disk, tab name `<file> (in file)`, language by the file name) and `/clipboard/<n>/<file name>` (the text the clipboard had, tab name `Clipboard ↔ <file name>`), made by `VirtualRegistry.RegisterPrefix`: a provider for every path that starts with a prefix, given the rest of the path (`VirtualPrefixInvalid` and `VirtualPrefixDuplicate` fail the registration; a path with a provider of its own wins over a prefix, and of two prefixes the longer wins).
- **Edits** are applied as a batch of non-overlapping replacements; the document returns the inverse batch.
- **Undo/redo** stack of edit groups, as VS Code's `EditStack`: a group stores the edits, their inverses, and the selections before and after; consecutive edits of the same kind (typing, deleting left, deleting right, other) from the same cursors merge into one group, and a cursor move by other means, a different kind, or an explicit `PushStackElement` closes the group. Typing also follows VS Code's rule for spaces: a space typed after other characters starts a new group, spaces typed one after the other stay together, and the characters typed after a single space join it. Undo and redo restore the selections.
- **Decorations**: ranges that move with edits, with VS Code's four stickiness modes, kept in an interval tree; used for find matches, bracket highlights, snippet tab stops, auto-closed characters, diff changes, folded regions and, later, diagnostics. Every decoration has an **owner** (a number of 1 or more) that the feature that made it passes in; two editors that show one document (two editor groups, §10.3) must not share owners, so each takes a block of them from `Document.AllocOwners(n)` (the first reservation of a document starts at 1).
- Change events carry the version, the edits and the new snapshot.

### 7.2 Editing commands (`core/edit`)

Pure functions from (snapshot, cursors, options) to (edit batch, new cursors, edit kind), so they are tested without a document or a UI. A cursor whose edits overlap the edits of an earlier cursor is dropped from the result, as in VS Code. They cover every row of §3.1 under "Editing", "Line commands" and "Cursors and selections". One options struct carries everything they read (tab size, insert spaces, word separators, auto-closing, indentation rules...), so later features add fields, not parameters. Word boundaries follow `editor.wordSeparators` (VS Code's default) and word parts split camelCase and snake_case.

Cursor movement keeps a **desired visual column** for vertical moves. Movements that depend on the view (page up/down, vertical moves over wrapped or folded lines, Home/End on a wrapped line) ask a `LineLayout` interface, which the editor's view model implements; its default implementation treats every model line as one row.

## 8. Language support without a language server

### 8.1 Languages (`core/language`)

- A **registry** of languages: id, aliases, file extensions, file names, file name globs, first-line regex, MIME types, configuration, grammar, embedded languages and token types. Language of a file, as VS Code's `languagesAssociations.ts`: the user's `files.associations` first (globs, on the whole path when they have a slash and on the file name otherwise; the longest glob wins), then the languages' own: an exact file name, then the longest glob (`filenamePatterns`), then the longest extension; among equals the one registered last wins; the first line is looked at only when nothing else claims the file; otherwise `plaintext`. Paths and extensions are matched without regard to case. A `firstLine` that matches the empty text is left out.
- The registry (`language.Registry`) is filled by `AddExtension(fs.FS)` from the `package.json` of a VS Code extension at the root of the file system: `contributes.languages` (merged when several extensions contribute to one id, as `languagesRegistry.ts` does) and `contributes.grammars` (`language`, `scopeName`, `path`, `embeddedLanguages`, `tokenTypes`, `injectTo`). Entries that are not valid are left out and listed in `Problems`. Languages have a number (0 none, 1 plain text, then in order of registration), which the tokens of the grammars carry as their language. `Registry` is the `textmate.Registry` of the grammars (a grammar file is read when first asked for; `Injections` of a scope include those of the scopes that start it, as `TMGrammarFactory` does) and `NewGrammar(language)` makes the tokenizer of a language with its embedded languages (those of the injected grammars too) and token types. Grammars must be JSON; the one grammar of the reference extensions in the plist format (`source.js.regexp`) is converted to JSON by `scripts/update-assets.sh` (with `internal/core/language/internal/plist2json`, which also changes the path in the copied `package.json`) when JavaScript is bundled (step 4.6b). Since step 11.4 the registry has **plain text and nothing else of its own**: the languages come from the language packs (below, §10.15), which the extension host adds with `AddNamedExtension(key, fs.FS)` and takes away with `RemoveExtension(key)` (the registry is made again from the extensions that remain; the numbers of the languages stay reserved, so tokens and grammars that carry a number stay valid and a pack that comes back gets its number back; `Version()` counts the changes). `AddExtension` adds an extension for good (the tests and `ProcessOptions.Languages`). `language.Bundled()` is gone: the tests of the packages under `internal/` read the very same files from the source tree, in the order of `extensions.All`, through `internal/core/language/packfs` (the folders of the packs) and `internal/core/language/languagetest.Bundled()` (the registry), because `internal/` never imports `extensions/`; `cmd/emetos/languagepacks_test.go` keeps that order the same as `extensions.All` and checks that the registry the host makes equals the one the tests make. The oracle test (`oracle_test.go`) tokenizes the colorize fixtures of the bundled languages as the Snapper of VS Code does and compares each line with `colorize-results`; the lines where Emetos differs are listed in `testdata/expected-differences.txt` (`<fixture> <lines> <reason>`), and an entry whose lines no longer differ fails the test. A rule whose included grammar is not bundled is left out, as vscode-textmate does, so a fenced block of such a language is not highlighted.
- **Language configuration** in VS Code's `language-configuration.json` format: comments, brackets, colorized bracket pairs, auto-closing pairs (with `notIn`), auto-close-before characters, surrounding pairs, folding markers and `offSide`, word pattern, indentation rules, on-enter rules. Its regular expressions are JavaScript syntax (as a string or `{pattern, flags}`) and compile with `core/regex`'s ECMAScript mode (the `u` flag turns on `\p{..}` property escapes, which `core/regex` translates). A field of the wrong type, or a regular expression that does not compile, is left out and listed as a problem; the other fields are kept (`ParseConfiguration`).
- **Bundled languages** (the language packs `extensions/<pack>/`, assets embedded with `embed` from `extensions/<pack>/assets/`, copied from the pinned references by `scripts/update-assets.sh`, with their licenses in `third_party/` and `NOTICE`; the pack ids are `emetos.<pack>`; a pack groups the languages of one VS Code extension folder, as VS Code does):
  - First (D13): Go (`golang`), Markdown (`markdown`, with embedded code blocks for the bundled languages), JSON, JSON with Comments, JSON Lines and Code Snippets (`json`), YAML and Compose (`yaml`), Python (`python`), JavaScript and JavaScript React (`javascript`), TypeScript and TypeScript React (`typescript`; it also gives `tsconfig.json` and friends to JSON with Comments).
  - Added by step 4.10: HTML (`html`; it embeds CSS and JavaScript), CSS (`css`), SCSS (`scss`), Less (`less`), XML and XSL (`xml`), SQL (`sql`), Shell Script (`shellscript`), Makefile (`makefile`), Dockerfile (`docker`), INI and Properties (`ini`).
  - Added by step 4.11: C, C++ and CUDA C++ (`cpp`), Rust (`rust`), Diff (`diff`), Git commit, Git rebase and Ignore files (`.gitignore` and others; `git`) and the Go module files (`go.mod`, `go.sum`; `go.work` uses the `go.mod` grammar; from `golang/vscode-go`, as the pack `gomod` whose package.json `scripts/update-assets.sh` writes). `.h` is C++ as in VS Code. Plain text needs no grammar and is the core's own.
  - VS Code's snippets of these languages (`contributes.snippets`) are not bundled: nothing in Emetos reads a language's snippets from an extension yet (the snippet service reads the user's files), and Emmet stays in `core/emmet`. When a step adds snippet contributions, the packs' snippets go into their `assets/`.
  - VS Code has no TOML grammar of its own; TOML is left for later.

### 8.2 Regular expressions (`core/regex`)

TextMate grammars use Oniguruma regular expressions; Go's `regexp` (RE2) lacks lookbehind and backreferences. `core/regex` wraps `github.com/dlclark/regexp2` (D11):

- Translation of Oniguruma-only syntax to regexp2: `\h`, `\H`, `\A`, `\z`, `\Z`, `\G` (an anchor position given by the tokenizer), `\K`, possessive quantifiers (as atomic groups), POSIX bracket classes, `\p{Alpha}`-style property names, class intersection `&&`, `(?x)` comments, and `(?m)` (Oniguruma's dot-matches-newline). A pattern that can't be translated is reported with a tag, and the rule using it never matches.
  - The pattern is parsed into a tree and written out again (`regex.Compile`), as vscode-oniguruma compiles it (`ONIG_OPTION_CAPTURE_GROUP`): every group captures and the groups are numbered by their opening parentheses, named ones included (regexp2 numbers named groups after the others, so names become numbers: `\k<name>` is `\k<n>`). `^` and `$` are lines anchors (`^` does not match after a final line break); `(?m)` is dot-all; `(?i)` and `(?x)` last to the end of the group, alternatives that follow included (`a(?i)b|c` is `a(?i:b|c)`); `(?x)` whitespace and comments are removed by the translator.
  - Repetition: `a*+` as an atomic group; `{n,m}+` repeats the interval (the Ruby syntax); `{n}?` is optional; `{,m}` is `{0,m}`; `{n,m}` with `n > m` is `{m,n}` that does not give back.
  - Classes: nested classes, `&&`, POSIX brackets (`[:alpha:]`, `[:^alpha:]`) and `\p{..}` (POSIX names, general categories long and short, Go's script tables) for Unicode text; `\x{85 2028}` (several code points) and `\x{...}`, `\h`, `\H`, `\R`, `\X`, `\N`, `\O`.
  - Calls of groups (`\g<name>`, `\g<1>`, `\g<-1>`, `\g<0>`) are replaced by a copy of the group that does not capture, with the ignore-case flag of the group; a group may be called inside itself 6 times, and the copy at the limit never matches, so recursive patterns (balanced parentheses) match up to that depth. When the pattern gets longer than 256 KB plus twice its source, the depth is lowered until it fits (`RegexTooLarge` when depth 1 does not).
  - `\K` is an empty group that marks the start of the match; the absence operator `(?~x)` is `(?:(?!x)[\s\S])*`; conditionals `(?(1)a|b)` and `(?(<name>)a|b)`.
  - Alternatives that match without consuming text and without capturing (`(?<=\W)|(?=\W)|^`), when they are next to each other in an alternation, are written as one atomic group: after one of them has matched, the others lead to the same state, and regexp2, unlike Oniguruma 6.9.9+, does not remember failed searches, so a loop around them (the whitespace of the C++ grammar) would take time exponential in the text it runs over.
  - Not supported, with a tag: options `W D S P y`, `\C-x`, `\M-x`, `\y`, `\Y`, levels in references (`\k<name+1>`).
  - `regex.Compile(pattern, Options)` takes the syntax, ignore case, the timeout, and `DisableA`/`DisableG` (the scanner asks for `\A` and `\G` that never match when the position is not the start of the text or the anchor). `regex.Cache` compiles a pattern once, failures included.
  A pattern that can't be translated is reported with a tag, and the rule using it never matches. All 5,900 patterns of the grammars under `reference/` compile (the corpus test of step 4.1).
- A **scanner** over several patterns, as vscode-textmate's `OnigScanner`: `Find(line, pos, anchorPos, isFirstLine)` returns the earliest match, ties broken by the lowest pattern index, with captures as byte offsets. A line is converted to runes once (`regex.NewLine`, which the tokenizer makes once per line and uses for every search of it); invalid UTF-8 bytes are treated as U+FFFD, one rune per byte, with the byte mapping kept. `\G` is allowed when `pos == anchorPos` and `\A` on the first line, as vscode-textmate's `compileAG` resolves them: the scanner compiles a variant of a pattern with the anchor that never matches the first time a line needs it. A pattern that does not compile never matches (`Scanner.Err` gives the reason).
- Every match runs with a time limit (100 ms, tag `RegexTimeout`); a line whose tokenization times out is plain text from that point.
- An **ECMAScript mode** (`regexp2.ECMAScript`) for find (§9.8) and for language configurations (§8.1).

### 8.3 Tokenization (`core/textmate`, `core/tokens`)
