Name `"<original> ↔ <modified>"` (names as `TextInput` gives them, so a virtual document shows its label), title with both paths, `Resource()` is not set (it is no file: the recent-files list, Reveal and the like skip it), `Dirty()` is the modified document's, capabilities are `CapCanSplit` (it can be split) plus Readonly and Untitled when the modified document is. Two inputs with the same pair are the same tab (`Matches`), and a diff of the same pair opened again activates the tab. Save, Save All, auto save and external-change handling act on the modified document (`editorgroup.EditedDocument`, the interface `DocumentEditor`); a close asks about the modified document, naming it ("Do you want to save the changes you made to new.go?"), and the dirty original is never saved or asked about (a document that a diff shows read-only can still be changed by another editor). `PlanClose` treats inputs that edit the same document as showing the same thing: closing a diff while a text editor of the modified document remains in another group asks nothing. The pane counts one use of each document while it lives and releases them when it closes.
  - *Restore.* The input serializes as `{"original": <uri>, "modified": <uri>}`; the documents are opened by `PrepareRestore` with those of the text editors (hot-exit backups of the modified side come back as for any document). A diff whose file is gone is dropped with the same notice as a text editor ("1 editor could not be restored ..." counts one editor even if both sides are gone); a virtual original whose provider no longer exists is dropped silently (as a virtual text editor is); a saved value that cannot be parsed (`DiffInputInvalid`) is logged and dropped.
  - *`dev.openDiff {"original", "modified"}`* (§15.2) opens a comparison in the active group as a kept tab.
  - *Editor extensions* (`gui/editor`, used by the diff editor): `Options.ReadOnly` (the view model refuses every edit with the error tag `EditorReadOnly` -- typing, undo/redo, clipboard cut/paste, snippets and replace -- while movement, selection and copy work; the `editorReadonly` key follows `ViewModel.ReadOnly()`, which is `Options.ReadOnly || document.ReadOnly()`; this option did not exist before step 9.5); background marks (`SetBackgroundMarks([]BackgroundMark)`: a range, whole-line or not, a fill, an optional border and an optional gutter fill; they are decorations in the view model's owner slot 7, so they follow edits, and are painted under everything else, zone rows skipped); scroll listeners (`AddScrollListener` / `RemoveScrollListener`, `ScrollTo`; `SetScrollTop` notifies only when the value changes).
  - *Not built:* collapsing unchanged regions, moved-code detection and its arrows, the sash, the accessible diff viewer (F7), the revert arrows and "Revert Block" / "Stage" actions, `diffEditor.originalEditable`, `openSide` and swap-sides actions, `diffEditor.renderIndicators`, `diffEditor.wordWrap` (the editors use `editor.wordWrap`), editor title buttons, and the status bar items of the compared editors (the sub-editors are not in the group's editor map: no status bar for the cursor, no language-follow, no context menu of their own).

- **Inline view and compare commands as built (step 9.6; `gui/diffeditor/inline.go`, `gui/editor/linesview.go`, `gui/app/compare.go`, `gui/app/launch.go`).**
  - *The choice of the view.* `diffeditor.Mode` is `SideBySide` or `Inline`. The settings (language overridable, in the "Diff Editor" group, read live; VS Code's keys, defaults and descriptions): `diffEditor.renderSideBySide` (boolean, true: "Controls whether the diff editor shows the diff side by side or inline."), `diffEditor.renderSideBySideInlineBreakpoint` (number, 900: "If the diff editor width is smaller than this value, the inline view is used.") and `diffEditor.useInlineViewWhenSpaceIsLimited` (boolean, true: "If enabled and the editor width is too small, the inline view is used."). The view is inline when `renderSideBySide` is off, or when `useInlineViewWhenSpaceIsLimited` is on and the width of the diff editor (the whole widget, the ruler included) is **no more than** the breakpoint (VS Code's `<=`: 900 px is inline). The widget tells the model its width while it is built (`Model.SetWidth`); the model changes its mode on the UI thread a frame later (`SetMode`, never during a build), so a resize across the breakpoint shows the old view for one frame. The context keys of the scope of the diff editor are `diffEditorInlineMode` and `diffEditorRenderSideBySideInlineBreakpointReached` (VS Code's `couldShowInlineViewBecauseOfSize`: `renderSideBySide` on and the width at or under the breakpoint, whatever the other setting says). Not built: VS Code's "smooth resize" (staying inline while a drag ends past the breakpoint), compact mode and its smart choice, the screen reader rule, `diffEditor.experimental.useTrueInlineView`, the keys `diffEditorTemporaryInlineMode` and `diffEditorAutomaticRenderSideBySide`, the "Diff View" submenu and "Inline View" button of the editor title (there is no editor title toolbar yet).
  - *Switching.* The row of the widget has keyed children (`original`, `divider`, `modified`, `ruler`), so the modified editor is the same element in both views: its view model, cursors, selections, scroll position, find state and keyboard focus stay; coming back to side by side scrolls the original editor to where the modified one is. The view model of the modified side is never replaced. Switching takes the zones and marks of the other view off (the filler of the side by side view, the zones of the deleted lines, the marks of the original editor) and puts the ones of the new view on; a diff computed in one view is shown in the other without being computed again.
  - *Inline layout* (`Model.setInlineZones`, VS Code's inline branch of `diffEditorViewZones.ts`). One editor shows the modified document, editable as in the side by side view, with the inserted lines and characters marked as there (`insertedLineBackground`, `insertedTextBackground`, the gutter strips). For each change that has original lines there is one view zone in the modified editor, **above the line that took their place**: `AfterLine` is the change's first modified line minus 1 (0 above the first line; the number of lines for a change at the end), and it has as many rows as the change has original lines (a pure insertion has no zone; a pure deletion has a zone and no marked lines; a replacement has both). Zones follow the edits of the modified document as every zone does (§9.1) until the next diff replaces them; a diff whose changes and colors are those of the zones in place leaves the zones alone (so a recompute after an edit that is no change, such as trailing white space, makes no new widgets). No filler zones are used: the original editor's zones, scroll sync and marks are off while inline, and the original view model only supplies the text, the tokens and the brackets of the deleted lines. A diff that is a little behind the text names lines that are gone: the zone is put after the last line instead.
  - *The deleted lines* (`editor.NewLinesView`, `RenderLinesView`). The widget of a zone draws the lines of the original document, one row each, in the font, the size, the tab size, the syntax colors and the bracket colors of the original editor's view model (so the colors of the original text, tokenized as far as the budget allows, as a text layer does), with the whole-line fill `diffEditor.removedLineBackground` and the removed characters in `diffEditor.removedTextBackground` (and `removedTextBorder`), from the character changes of the diff. The text follows the horizontal scroll of the modified editor. Its margin is the gutter strip of the zone (`ZoneSpec.Gutter`: `diffEditorGutter.removedLineBackground`) with a minus sign (`ZoneSpec.GutterGlyph`: the Codicon `remove`, 11 px, 70% opacity, at the right of the line decorations column on every row: VS Code's `delete-sign`). The zone takes no pointer events. Not built: selecting or copying the deleted text ("Copy deleted lines" and "Revert this change" of its margin menu), the plus sign of the inserted lines (VS Code's `renderIndicators`; the side by side view has no indicators either), wrapping of the deleted lines (with word wrap on, a deleted line stays one row, as long as it is, and scrolls with the editor; the rows of the zone are the number of deleted lines; the horizontal scroll range is the modified editor's, so a deleted line wider than every modified line cannot be scrolled to its end), the rows of the original line numbers (`diffEditor.hideOriginalLineNumbers`).
  - *Ruler and navigation.* The overview ruler measures the one editor: its left half marks the zone of the deleted lines of each change (`diffEditorOverview.removedForeground`), its right half the modified lines (`insertedForeground`). Alt+F5 and Shift+Alt+F5 go to the first line of the modified range of the next or previous change as in the side by side view (`ChangeToGo`); for a pure deletion that is the line after the zone, the zone being above the cursor. `focusSecondarySide` and `focusOtherSide` focus the one editor; `diffEditor.switchSide` does nothing while inline.
  - *Commands.* `toggle.diff.renderSideBySide` ("Toggle Inline View", category "Compare", in the palette while `textCompareEditorActive`; no key) writes `!diffEditor.renderSideBySide`; `diffEditor.toggleUseInlineViewWhenSpaceIsLimited` ("Toggle Use Inline View When Space Is Limited", precondition `isInDiffEditor`, not in the palette, as in VS Code) writes `!diffEditor.useInlineViewWhenSpaceIsLimited`; `diffEditor.setViewMode.inline` (`renderSideBySide` false), `.sideBySide` (`renderSideBySide` true and `useInlineViewWhenSpaceIsLimited` false) and `.automatic` (both true) have no title and no key (VS Code gives them titles in the "Diff View" submenu only). The settings are written where the user has them: the workspace settings when the workspace sets the key, else the user's.
  - *Compare with Saved* (`workbench.files.action.compareWithSaved`, palette "Compare Active File with Saved" in "File", **Ctrl+K D**, no `when`). The left side is the file as it is on disk, the right side the live document, opened as a kept tab named `<file> (in file) ↔ <file>` (VS Code's `{0} (in file) ↔ {1}`). The file is the argument (a path or a `file://` URI of a file that an editor has open; anything else that is not nothing fails with `CompareResourceInvalid`), else the file of the active editor, which for a diff editor is its modified side. A document that is not a file (untitled, virtual) or no editor: nothing happens. The left side is the read-only virtual document `emetos-virtual:/saved/<path>` (§7.1), whose provider reads the file with `fileio.Read` (the encoding detection and the line endings of a file read) each time it is opened, with the language of the file's name; it is read on the UI thread when the diff opens (as an opened file is) and **again, in the background, when the file changes**: when the modified document is saved (`Document.OnSaved`, followed by the pane of the diff) and when the watcher reports a change of the file (`externalEvents`), the document gets the new text (`SetText`) when it differs and the diff is computed again. A file that cannot be read again (deleted) leaves the text as it was. The same comparison again activates the tab.
  - *Compare Active File with Clipboard* (`workbench.files.action.compareWithClipboard`, **Ctrl+K C**, "File"). The left side is a read-only virtual document `emetos-virtual:/clipboard/<n>/<file name>` (a new number for each run: the clipboard may have changed, so each is a tab of its own) with the text the clipboard had when the command ran, tab name `Clipboard ↔ <file name>` (VS Code's label `Clipboard ↔ {0}`: the left side's name is "Clipboard"), the right side is the active file's document (not for virtual documents). The texts are kept in the process while it runs (`Process.clipboard`); after a restart a restored comparison finds its text gone (`CompareClipboardGone`) and is dropped silently like a virtual document whose provider is gone. `CompareClipboardNumberInvalid` is a path that has no number.
  - *Compare Active File With...* (`workbench.files.action.compareFileWith`, "File", precondition `activeEditor`). The quick open of files is shown with the second item active (`ItemSecond`: the first is the file that is open); the file that is chosen is not opened: the diff of the active editor's document (left) and that file (right) opens instead (`quickinput.ShowOptions.OnFile`, which gives the chosen `FileOpen` to the function of the session; Escape ends the pick and the next quick open opens files as usual). The file is read in the background; one that cannot be opened is a notification. Without an editor the command does nothing.
  - *The Explorer's comparisons.* `selectForCompare` ("Select for Compare", group `3_compare`, order 30), `compareFiles` ("Compare with Selected", order 20) and `compareSelected` ("Compare Selected", order 30) are rows of the Explorer's context menu (VS Code's `when` clauses: the pressed row is not a folder and has a resource; Compare with Selected also needs the context key `resourceSelectedForCompare` and not two selected rows; Select for Compare not two selected rows; Compare Selected two selected rows, the key `listDoubleSelection`, which the menu context of the Explorer sets from the selection). They have no title as commands, no key, and are not in the palette. `selectForCompare` remembers the file of the focused row (or the argument's, or the active editor's) and sets the window's key `resourceSelectedForCompare` (cleared when the shell goes away); a folder is not selected. `compareFiles` opens the remembered file (left) and the file it is run on (right); `compareSelected` the two selected files, in the order of the selection (the tree's order), left first; with a folder among them, or with nothing remembered, nothing happens. Files are read in the background. Not built: the same rows in the Open Editors view and in the tab menu (`OpenEditorsContext`, `TwoEditorsSelectedInGroup`: Emetos has no Open Editors context menu, and tabs have no multi-selection), "Compare New Untitled Text Files" (the original side of Emetos's diff editor is read-only).
  - *`emetos --diff a b`* (§10.11). The two files are read in the background and compared in the active group of the window the launch opens in: the first on the left, kept tab `a ↔ b`; relative paths were made absolute against the working directory of the launch by the parser. The first instance does the same on top of its restored editors. With `--wait` the client waits until the **diff editor's tab is closed** (not until the files are closed: another editor may still show a file; closing the window ends the wait too); the exit code is 0, or 1 when a file cannot be opened (a notification names it; also when a different number of files than two arrives, which the parser does not allow). `--merge` still gets its notice (step 9.7).
  - *The notice of a conflict* (§6.3 "External changes"). The notification about a dirty document whose file changed on disk, and the one of a save that finds the file newer (`FileModifiedSince`), have a first button **Compare** (VS Code's "Compare", `workbench.files.action.resolveConflict`): the same diff as Compare with Saved, with the file on disk (`<file> (in file)`, read-only) on the left and the document with its unsaved changes on the right. The notification stays: **Overwrite** and **Revert** resolve it as before, and the left side then shows what was written. VS Code's title of this diff, `{0} (in file) ↔ {1} (in Emetos) - Resolve save conflict`, and the "Learn More" help are not built.
  - *Registered by this step.* Commands: `toggle.diff.renderSideBySide`, `diffEditor.toggleUseInlineViewWhenSpaceIsLimited`, `diffEditor.setViewMode.inline|sideBySide|automatic`, `workbench.files.action.compareWithSaved`, `compareFileWith`, `compareWithClipboard`, `selectForCompare`, `compareFiles`, `compareSelected`. Keys: Ctrl+K D and Ctrl+K C. Menu rows: the three of the Explorer's context menu, and the palette rules for Toggle Inline View and the toggle of the limited space. Settings: the three above. Context keys: `diffEditorInlineMode`, `diffEditorRenderSideBySideInlineBreakpointReached` (the scope of the diff editor), `resourceSelectedForCompare` (the window), `listDoubleSelection` (the menu context of the Explorer). Errors: `VirtualPrefixInvalid`, `VirtualPrefixDuplicate`, `CompareResourceInvalid`, `CompareClipboardNumberInvalid`, `CompareClipboardGone`. Editor extensions (`gui/editor`): `ZoneSpec.Gutter` and `ZoneSpec.GutterGlyph` (the margin of a zone), `NewLinesView`.
- **Proposed changes (step 13.3; `gui/app/exproposed.go`, `core/editorgroup.DiffProposal`).** The diff editor also shows a change that an extension proposes to a file (§10.16 "As built (step 13.3)"): a `DiffInput` with a `DiffProposal` whose right side is an editable document of its own and whose tab strip has Accept and Reject; it is never dirty, is not saved or restored and cannot be split. The settings of the diff editor (inline view below 900 px, ignore trim whitespace) apply as for any diff.
- `gui/mergeeditor`: incoming (left) and current (right) on top, the result below, with accept incoming/current/both (current then incoming) per conflict and for all, and "Complete Merge": for a marker file it saves the file; for `--merge` it writes the `result` path and exits 0 when `--wait` is on (1 if the window closes without completing).

- **Merge editor layout as built (step 9.7; `gui/mergeeditor`, the pane in `gui/app/mergepane.go`).** This step shows the merge, outlines and navigates its conflicts, and has the checkboxes; the actions, "Complete Merge" and the exit code of `--wait` are step 9.8 ("Merge editor actions as built", below). Ported from `mergeEditor.ts`, `viewModel.ts`, `scrollSynchronizer.ts`, `lineAlignment.ts`, `viewZones.ts`, `colors.ts`, `inputCodeEditorView.ts`, `resultCodeEditorView.ts` and `commands.ts` of VS Code's merge editor.
  - *Layout.* A column: a row with the incoming editor (input 1, left) and the current editor (input 2, right) of the same width with a 1 px divider (`editorGroup.border`), a 1 px line, and the result editor below, the two halves of the same height (no sashes, no layout toggles: VS Code's "mixed" layout without the base). Over each editor a 30 px header with its title (`Incoming`, `Current`, `Result`) and, in `descriptionForeground` at 12 px, its label: the branch of the marker (`feature` of `>>>>>>> feature`, `HEAD` of `<<<<<<< HEAD`; the first label of the file), the file name of the `--merge` path (or the `description` that `_open.mergeEditor` gives), and for the result the base name of its file (never a path, as VS Code labels a file; the tooltip of the tab has the whole path). At the right of the result header, `N Conflicts Remaining` (`1 Conflict Remaining`; the pinned VS Code has no text for zero, so it says `0 Conflicts Remaining`, dimmed): pressing it goes to the next unhandled conflict. The inputs have a 24 px gutter at the left with the checkboxes. Each editor is an ordinary `editor.Editor` over its own view model; `AdjustOptions` turns the minimap, the glyph margin, folding and sticky scroll off, sets `lineNumbersMinChars` to 2 and makes the inputs read-only. The two inputs are in-memory read-only documents (`emetos-virtual:/merge/<n>/incoming` and `/current`) that are not in the window's set of documents: they are never saved, backed up or restored (the merge is made again from the files). The base view of VS Code (`baseCodeEditorView`), the column layout, `merge.toggleLayout`-style commands, "Open File", the telemetry and the accessibility help are not built.
  - *The session* (`mergeeditor.Session`, no Glutter): the `MergeModel` of §9.11 and the result document, kept the same. A change event of the document, whoever makes it (typing, undo, redo, a reload), is turned by `LineEdits` into replacements of whole lines for `ApplyResultEdit` (changes that share a line are one edit; a change that starts and ends at line starts on both sides replaces only whole lines, so deleting `x\n` does not touch the line after it) and the regions follow it; when that fails, or the document was replaced (`SetText`), `resync` diffs the model's result against the text and applies the hunks, so the regions that were not touched keep their states. An edit of the session itself (the toggle of a checkbox) is made to the model first and applied to the document as one undoable edit (`documentEdit`, which knows that the last line has no line break); the undo of that edit changes the region's state to the one its lines equal (`StateBase`, an input, both), and since step 9.8 also gives the conflict the handled flag it had at that version of the document ("Merge editor actions as built", below). The model's line break is always `\n`: the document keeps the line ending of its file. Manual edits of the result do not change the handled flag of a conflict, as in VS Code (the 9.7 text said VS Code marks them handled; its `mergeEditorModel.ts` recomputes the handled flags from the states only once, when the model starts, and `setState` is the only thing that sets them afterwards).
  - *Alignment.* The inputs are lined up with spacer zones (`InputSpacers`, the filler of the diff editor, `diffEditor.diagonalFill`): `Alignments` is a port of `getAlignments` (the equal character ranges of both inputs against the base, cut where the inputs have text in common, with the half and full syncs of VS Code) and the spacer rows are computed as `computeViewZones` does with the result and the base not aligned; the first and the last alignment of a range are always kept, so the line after every range is on the same row in both inputs. The zones are made once (the inputs are never edited). A wrapped line counts as one row (VS Code does not re-fit either).
  - *Scroll sync* (`LineMap`, `ScrollFor`, `Model.follow`): every editor has the horizontal scroll of the one that moved; the inputs have the same vertical scroll (the zones line them up); the result is scrolled to the place that corresponds to the top of an input, and an input to the place that corresponds to the top of the result: the top line is looked up in the map of the regions (each region pairs the range it has in the input with the range it has in the result now; the lines between regions are one to one) and the scroll position is the same fraction of the range's height in pixels (`_synchronizeScrolling`; it uses the line at the top, where VS Code uses the line above it). VS Code diffs the result against the base to make that map; here the regions that follow the edits make it, so an edit of the result outside the regions does not move the map. A guard stops the echo, the editor that scrolled last keeps the lead when the sizes change, and a change of the regions scrolls the others again.
  - *Decorations.* In each input every conflict region has a border around its range (`mergeEditor.conflict.unhandledUnfocused.border` 1 px, `unhandledFocused.border` 2 px, `handledUnfocused.border` and `handledFocused.border` 1 px; a range with no line is a line between two lines) and its changed lines are `mergeEditor.change.background` with the characters of its inner changes in `mergeEditor.change.word.background`; the changes that do not conflict are in the result already and are not marked (VS Code's `showNonConflictingChanges` is off). In the result every conflict has the same borders (an unhandled conflict whose base is empty is the line between two lines) and, when its lines are not the base's, they are `mergeEditor.change.background` (VS Code colors the diffs of the result against the base; its word marks are not built). Borders are a new editor extension, `editor.LineBlock` / `SetLineBlocks` (line numbers, not decorations of the document: the model moves them as it changes). The active region (the one the cursor of the editor that was used last is in: `ActiveConflict`) has the focused border. Not built: the deletion markers (`mergeEditor.showDeletionMarkers`, the bar of an empty word change), `mergeEditor.useSimplifiedDecorations` (and the `mergeEditor.conflict.input1/2.background` colors it would use are registered only), the ruler and minimap marks, the "Conflicting Lines" zone over markers.
  - *Checkboxes.* One per conflict that an input changed, drawn in the gutter of that input and kept in view while a tall conflict scrolls (`CheckboxTop`, VS Code's layout of an item): an 18 px box with the border of the conflict's state (`mergeEditor.conflict.*.border` while it is unhandled, `checkbox.border` once handled), a bracket along the lines of a conflict taller than 30 px, and a check mark when the result has the input's lines, two marks when it has them after the other input's (`StateBoth`: the input that was in the result first comes first, so the second one clicked shows two marks), a dot when the result of the conflict was edited by hand (`StateUnrecognized`). A press toggles the input (`Session.Toggle`: `MergeModel.Toggle`, which includes or excludes the input and marks the conflict handled, applied as one undoable edit) and makes the conflict the active one. VS Code hides them by default (`mergeEditor.showCheckboxes`, not a registered setting) behind the code lenses ("Accept Incoming | Accept Combination | Ignore") that step 9.8 builds; Emetos shows both. Not built: VS Code's context menu of a checkbox (Accept, Accept Both, Swap, Mark as Handled) and its middle click.
  - *Navigation.* `merge.goToNextUnhandledConflict` and `merge.goToPreviousUnhandledConflict` ("Go to Next Unhandled Conflict" / "Go to Previous Unhandled Conflict", category "Merge Editor", precondition `isMergeEditor`; VS Code binds no keys to them and neither does Emetos) go from the cursor of the editor that was used last (the result at first) to the first conflict that starts after its line (the last that ends before it), wrapping around (`ConflictToGo`): the cursors of the three editors go to the start of that conflict (the first non-blank of its first line; an empty range at the end of the text or past it shows the last line, `RevealLines`), the editor that was used shows it in the middle and takes the focus, the others follow the scroll, and the conflict is the active one. With no unhandled conflict they do nothing. Pressing "N Conflicts Remaining" is the next command.
  - *Context keys.* `isMergeEditor` (the active editor of the window is a merge editor), `mergeEditorResultUri` (its result) and `mergeEditorLayout` (`mixed`) are set in the window's keys while a merge editor is the active editor and reset otherwise; in the scopes of the widget `isMergeEditor` is set for the three editors and `isMergeResultEditor` for the result. `activeEditor` is `emetos.merge`. VS Code's `mergeEditorBaseUri`, `mergeEditorShowBase`, `mergeEditorShowBaseAtTop` and `mergeEditorShowNonConflictingChanges` are not set.
  - *The input* (`core/editorgroup.MergeInput`, type `emetos.merge`; VS Code's is `mergeEditor.Input`). It holds the result document and a `MergeSource` (`Kind` `markers` or `files`, the paths of `--merge`, the result path). Name `Merging: <result name>` (VS Code's), title `Merging: <path>`, description the folder of the result; `Resource()` is not set (it is no file: the recent files, Reveal and the history of locations skip it), `Dirty()` is the result document's, no capabilities (it is shown in one group: a split or a copy leaves it out); two merges of the same result are one tab. Save, Save All, auto save and the external-change handling act on the result document (`EditedDocument`); closing asks about the result ("Do you want to save the changes you made to c.go?") unless another editor shows the same document. *Opening* replaces the result: for a marker file the inputs and the base come from the markers (`MergeInputsFromMarkerText`) and the result document is the file's own document, whose text becomes the model's result (the text outside the conflicts, and each conflict with the base lines, which is nothing without a `|||||||` section; the changes that did not conflict applied) as **one undoable edit that leaves the document dirty** (Undo brings the markers back; Complete Merge of step 9.8 saves it; a text editor of the same file in the group shows the same document and so shows the change); for `--merge` the result document is the file of the fourth path, or a new empty document with that path when it does not exist (it is created when it is saved), and its text is replaced the same way even when the file has content (VS Code starts from the computed result too). *Restore*: `Serialize` gives `{"kind", "input1", "input2", "base", "result"}` (a marker file only `kind` and `result`); the result document is opened like the documents of text editors (a hot exit backup comes back), the merge is made again from the files (the markers are read from the **disk**, since the document may hold the merged text) and the result keeps its text: the model follows it (`InitialSync`, with the conflicts whose lines are not the base's taken as handled). A merge that cannot be made again (a file of `--merge` is gone, or the marker file lost its markers) is dropped with a log entry, and its result document opens as a text editor when it has unsaved changes. A value that cannot be parsed is `MergeInputInvalid`, `MergeInputIncomplete`, `MergeInputFilesIncomplete` or `MergeInputResultNotFile` and is dropped. A merge that cannot be shown leaves a pane that says why.
  - *Opening.* (1) **The notification**: when a text editor of a file opens (a command, the Explorer, quick open, the command line: not a restored editor, nor one that comes back from the closed ones, nor a file the window had open already) and the text has a complete conflict (a text up to 2 MiB; `ContainsConflictMarkers` first, then the parser), an information notification "This file has merge conflicts. (c.go)" with the button **Resolve in Merge Editor** (VS Code's title of `git.openMergeEditor`) opens the merge editor in the active group; the file is looked at when it opens, not when an external change brings the markers. (2) **`git.openMergeEditor`** ("Resolve in Merge Editor", category "Git", as in VS Code's Git extension): the same for the file of the active text editor (or of the tab the command names); it says "This file has no merge conflicts." for a file without markers or without an editor, and refuses a file that cannot be edited; when the merge editor of the file is open it is activated. (3) **`_open.mergeEditor {"input1", "input2", "base", "output"}`** (VS Code's internal command, no title): absolute paths or `file://` URIs, the inputs also `{"uri", "description"}`; wrong arguments are `MergeOpenInvalid` and `MergeOpenSideInvalid`. (4) **`emetos --merge path1 path2 base result`** (§10.11), for the first instance and over the socket: the files are read and the merge computed in the background (`MergeResultUnreadable` for a result that cannot be looked at); a file that cannot be read is reported and nothing opens. With `--wait` the launch ends when the merge editor's tab is closed: with **exit code 0** when Complete Merge closed it and with **exit code 1** and the message "The merge was not completed." when it was closed any other way, or the window was (step 9.8, below). The diffs of a merge run with a limit of 5 s, after which the ranges are coarse.
  - *Registered by this step.* Commands: `merge.goToNextUnhandledConflict`, `merge.goToPreviousUnhandledConflict`, `git.openMergeEditor`, `_open.mergeEditor` (no keybindings, no menu entries). Colors (all of VS Code's merge colors, with its Dark Modern, Light Modern and high contrast defaults): `merge.currentHeaderBackground`, `merge.currentContentBackground`, `merge.incomingHeaderBackground`, `merge.incomingContentBackground`, `merge.commonHeaderBackground`, `merge.commonContentBackground`, `merge.border`, `mergeEditor.change.background`, `mergeEditor.change.word.background`, `mergeEditor.changeBase.background`, `mergeEditor.changeBase.word.background` (the two for the base view, which is not built), `mergeEditor.conflict.unhandledUnfocused.border`, `unhandledFocused.border`, `handledUnfocused.border`, `handledFocused.border`, `mergeEditor.conflict.handled.minimapOverViewRuler`, `unhandled.minimapOverViewRuler`, `mergeEditor.conflictingLines.background`, `mergeEditor.conflict.input1.background`, `input2.background`. Settings: none (VS Code's `mergeEditor.diffAlgorithm` and `showDeletionMarkers` are not built). Context keys: see above. Error tags: `MergeInputInvalid`, `MergeInputIncomplete`, `MergeInputFilesIncomplete`, `MergeInputResultNotFile`, `MergeOpenInvalid`, `MergeOpenSideInvalid`, `MergeResultUnreadable`.

- **Merge editor actions as built (step 9.8; `gui/mergeeditor` `actions.go`, `actionrow.go`, `session.go`, `widget.go`, the flows in `gui/app/mergepane.go`, `launch.go` and `devmerge.go`).** Ported from `conflictActions.ts`, `viewZones.ts`, `viewModel.ts` (`acceptAll`, `toggleActiveConflict`) and `commands.ts` (`AcceptMerge` and the accept commands) of VS Code's merge editor, and from `mergeEditorModel.ts` (`setState`, the handled flags).
  - *The rows of actions* (VS Code's code lenses). Above every conflict, in each of the three editors, a view zone of one row (the zones of §9.1, `ZoneSpec.Ordinal` -1 so that they come before the alignment fillers of the inputs) holds a row of links in `editorCodeLens.foreground` (new color, VS Code's `#999999` dark, `#919191` light, `#292929` high contrast light), 90 % of the font size of the editor (whole pixels, at least 5), separated by `\u00a0|\u00a0`, underlined while the pointer is over a link, each with a hover (VS Code's `title`). The zones are at the same place of both inputs (one for every conflict, empty when the input has no action, so the inputs stay lined up with the fillers of step 9.7 and the 9.7 scroll map still holds: the rows are in all three editors); the zone of the result follows the regions (it moves with the edits of the document and is put right by the model afterwards). `Model.Actions(side, conflict)` gives the items (`ActionItem{Text, Tooltip, Run}`, `Run` nil for a text): **in an input** (VS Code's `itemsInput1/2`, titled with the side's title): nothing when the result of the conflict has the input's lines or was edited by hand; else "Accept Incoming" / "Accept Current" (the input's lines; when the other input is in the result already they come after its lines: `RangeState.WithInputValue`, VS Code's `state.withInputValue(n, true)`) and, for a conflict both inputs changed, "Accept Combination (Incoming First)" / "Accept Combination (Current First)" (both inputs, this one first, `StateBoth`); **in the result** (`resultItems`): what the result has as a text ("No Changes Accepted", "Incoming", "Current", "Incoming + Current", "Current + Incoming" when the current input is first, "Manual Resolution"), then "Remove Incoming" / "Remove Current" for each input it has (in the order they are in the result) and, for a result edited by hand, "Reset to base" (a state of base, handled). The tooltips are VS Code's. Every action is one undoable edit of the result made through the `Session`, makes the conflict the active one (the focused border) and updates the states, the borders, the colors, the checkboxes, the rows and the count. The checkboxes of 9.7 stay (VS Code hides them by default behind these rows; Emetos shows both). After an action the cursor does not move to the next conflict (VS Code does not either; `merge.goToNextUnhandledConflict` does that). Not built: "Ignore" (VS Code's per-input handled flags: the model has one flag per conflict), "Append" (`mergeEditor.shouldUseAppendInsteadOfAccept` is not a setting), the smart combination (so "Accept Combination" is the plain one of both inputs, whose order always matters, and the label always has "First"), the context menu of a checkbox and of the conflict.
  - *The header buttons.* The header of each input has an icon button "Accept All Incoming Changes from Left" / "Accept All Current Changes from Right" (check-all, disabled when no conflict is unhandled: VS Code's `MergeInput1Toolbar` and `MergeInput2Toolbar`); the header of the result has "Reset Result" (discard) next to the count and the primary button **Complete Merge**, always enabled (`WidgetOpts.OnCompleteMerge`; the button is left out when it is not given).
  - *The session* (`Session.Accept`, `SetState`, `AcceptAll`, `AcceptAllCombination`, `ResetResult`, `Toggle`): each asks the model for its edits and applies them to the document as ONE undoable edit (`applyEdits`: a batch against the text before, from the last edit to the first; a stack element is closed before and after, so typing does not join it; an edit that puts the lines that are there changes nothing and an action that changes no text makes no undo step). **Accept All** (`merge.acceptAllInput1`, `merge.acceptAllInput2`) resolves the conflicts that are not handled with the input (`MergeModel.AcceptAll`; VS Code puts the input into every range, including the handled ones, which can make "both" of a conflict that took the other input; Emetos leaves the handled ones). **Accept All Combination** (`mergeEditor.acceptAllCombination`) gives both inputs, the incoming first, to every conflict whose result has not the incoming lines and was not edited by hand. **Reset Result** (`mergeEditor.resetResultToBaseAndAutoMerge`) puts the lines of the base back in every conflict that is resolved and marks it unhandled, as one edit; VS Code rewrites the whole result with the auto-merged text, which also drops the edits made outside the conflicts and to the changes that did not conflict: Emetos keeps those (the regions stay one to one with the text, so an undo is exact). `merge.toggleActiveConflictInput1/2` toggle the input in the active conflict (the one the cursor of the editor used last is in, or the last made active); with no active conflict they say "There is currently no conflict focused that can be toggled." in an error notification.
  - *Undo, redo and manual edits.* An undo or a redo of the document is followed by the model as before (the regions take the lines they have, the states are the ones those lines equal) and now also gives the handled flags back: the session remembers, for the alternative versions of the document that an action left and reached, the flags of every conflict (VS Code's `MarkAsHandledUndoRedoElement`; the version ids come back after an undo, so the flags of that version do). So the undo of an accept makes the conflict unhandled and the redo handled again, and "N Conflicts Remaining" follows. A **manual edit** of the result changes the state of a conflict it touches (`StateUnrecognized`, or the state its lines equal) and never its handled flag, as in VS Code (the 9.7 text claimed the contrary): a conflict resolved by hand stays unhandled until an action (for instance "Reset to base", or Accept All) handles it; typing outside the conflicts only moves the regions. Typing is not grouped with an action in the undo stack.
  - *Complete Merge* (`mergeEditor.acceptMerge`, "Complete Merge", category "Merge Editor", Ctrl+Enter while `isMergeEditor`, weight of the editor contributions and registered after the line commands so it wins over Insert Line Below in the result; the palette entry, the key and the button run the same code). When conflicts are not handled a modal question asks first (VS Code's words): "Do you want to complete the merge of <file name>?", detail "The file contains unhandled conflicts.", buttons **Complete with Conflicts** and Cancel (the 9.8 brief had "still contains <n> unhandled conflicts"; VS Code's text was kept); Cancel and Escape change nothing; a second press while it asks does nothing. Then the result document is saved like any save (`workbench.action.files.save`: save participants, a conflict with the file on disk, a failure notification with its buttons; the result of `--merge` that does not exist is created; a save that fails or is cancelled leaves the merge editor open and the merge not completed) and the merge editor closes. For a **marker file** the result document is the file's own document: after the save the file shows again in a text editor in the same group (kept, active, no "This file has merge conflicts" notice) and the merge tab closes (VS Code closes the merge editor and leaves what was open before it; Emetos shows the file, since the merge editor replaced the text of an editor the user had). For `--merge` the `result` path is written and the merge tab closes, and no text editor opens (the files of `--merge` are not part of the project). The merge counts as **completed** (`mergeState.completed`) from the save to the close of its tab.
  - *Exit codes of `emetos --merge … --wait`* (§10.11). The launch ends when the merge tab is closed: **0** when Complete Merge closed it (with the conflicts handled or not, as the question allowed), **1** with the message "The merge was not completed." when it was closed any other way (the close button or `workbench.action.closeActiveEditor`, with Save or Don't Save: saving the result is not completing the merge) or when the window closes first. A launch that opened a diff and a merge, or several merges, ends with 1 when any of its merges was given up. Without `--wait` the client is told at once, as before.
  - *Dev commands* (debug and `emetos_dev` builds, §15.2): `dev.openMergeEditor` and `dev.acceptMerge`.
  - *Registered by this step.* Commands (category "Merge Editor", precondition `isMergeEditor`, VS Code's ids and titles): `merge.acceptAllInput1` ("Accept All Incoming Changes from Left"), `merge.acceptAllInput2` ("Accept All Current Changes from Right"), `mergeEditor.resetResultToBaseAndAutoMerge` ("Reset Result"), `mergeEditor.acceptAllCombination` ("Accept All Combination"; VS Code has no precondition for it, but it only acts in a merge editor), `merge.toggleActiveConflictInput1` ("Toggle Current Conflict from Left"), `merge.toggleActiveConflictInput2` ("Toggle Current Conflict from Right"), `mergeEditor.acceptMerge` ("Complete Merge"). Keys: `ctrl+enter` for `mergeEditor.acceptMerge` when `isMergeEditor`. Color: `editorCodeLens.foreground`. Settings, context keys and menu entries: none new (the accept-all and reset commands are in the palette and in the headers, not in the editor context menu). Not built: `mergeEditor.resetCloseWithConflictsChoice` (VS Code's "Close with Conflicts" choice is a different dialog that Emetos does not have), `mergeEditor.toggleBetweenInputs`, the layout commands. Error tags: `DevOpenMergeInvalid`, `DevOpenMergePathFailed`, `DevAcceptMergeInvalid`, `DevAcceptMergeConflictInvalid`, `DevAcceptMergeSideInvalid`, `DevAcceptMergeNoEditor`.

### 9.12 Language intelligence (area 3: `core/lsp`, `core/langfeatures`, `gui/editor`, `gui/views/...`, `extension/`)

Language features come from **language servers** (LSP 3.17) and, for a language without a server, from **providers written in Go** by an extension (D5, D20). Everything below follows VS Code's behavior, commands, keys and settings; the UI is drawn by Emetos.

**The client (`core/lsp`).** JSON-RPC 2.0 over the server's stdin/stdout with `Content-Length` framing (stdio only; no TCP or pipes): requests with ids and cancellation (`$/cancelRequest` when the `ctx` of a request ends), notifications, server-to-client requests (`workspace/configuration`, `workspace/applyEdit`, `window/showMessageRequest`, `window/workDoneProgress/create`, `client/registerCapability` and `unregisterCapability`), `$/progress`, `window/logMessage` and `window/showMessage`, `initialize` with Emetos's client capabilities and the server's capabilities kept, `initialized`, `shutdown`/`exit`. Positions are converted between Emetos's byte columns (D6) and the negotiated position encoding (`utf-8` when the server offers it, else UTF-16). Document sync: `didOpen`, `didChange` (incremental when the server supports it, else full), `willSave`, `didSave`, `didClose`, for the documents of the server's languages inside the workspace folder (and open untitled ones, `untitled:` URIs). Every request runs off the UI thread with a `ctx`; results come back through the binding's `Post`; a result for a document version that changed meanwhile is dropped (VS Code's rule for completion, hover and the rest: the newest request wins).

**Features model (`core/langfeatures`).** The registry of providers per feature and language selector (servers and Go providers alike), the merging of their results, the conversion of LSP results to Emetos's types, and the application of a `WorkspaceEdit` (text edits per document with one undo step each, file operations); no UI and no Glutter, so it is tested without a UI.

**Servers and their lifetime.** An extension declares a language server in its manifest (`Contributes.LanguageServers`: an id, the language ids it serves, the program and arguments with the setting that overrides the path, `initializationOptions` and the settings section it reads through `workspace/configuration`, and file watch globs). The host starts one server per workspace tab and server id when the first document of its languages opens there (or at activation), in the folder, in its own process group, with the environment of Emetos; it restarts a crashed server up to 5 times in 3 minutes, then shows a notification with Restart and Show Output; it stops it on `shutdown`/`exit` with a 3 s grace when the tab closes or the extension is disabled. Each server has an Output channel "<Server name>" (its `window/logMessage`, stderr, and with `<id>.trace.server` `messages`/`verbose` the traffic) and a status bar item while it starts or works (`$/progress`). `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` is sent from the file watcher for the server's globs. `<extension id>.restartServer` restarts it.

**Providers in Go (`extension/`).** `api.Languages().Register<Feature>Provider(selector, provider)` for completion, hover, signature help, definition, references, document symbols, code actions, formatting, rename, document highlights, diagnostics (a push API: `api.Problems()` per document with ranges); they run on goroutines with a `ctx`, are guarded like every call into an extension, and are merged with the server's results the way VS Code merges several providers (completion lists concatenated and sorted, hovers stacked, definitions joined).

**Features (what the user sees).**
- *Diagnostics*: `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` (and pull diagnostics when the server prefers them) become Problems markers owned by the server and squiggles in the editor (error, warning, info, hint as VS Code draws them: wavy underline, hint as three dots, `unnecessary` faded, `deprecated` struck through); hovering a squiggle shows the message with its source and code (a link when it has one) and the quick fixes; `editor.action.marker.next`/`prev` (F8, Shift+F8) and the Problems panel's navigation work as before; the overview ruler and minimap show them.
- *Completion* (the suggest widget): triggered by typing (`editor.quickSuggestions`, `editor.suggestOnTriggerCharacters` with the server's trigger characters), Ctrl+Space, and re-filtered as the user types (VS Code's fuzzy score and sort: `sortText`, `filterText`, `preselect`, `editor.suggestSelection`); rows with the kind icon, the label, `labelDetails` and `detail`; the details pane (Ctrl+Space again, the documentation as Markdown with `extension/ui/markdown`); accept with Enter or Tab (`editor.acceptSuggestionOnEnter`), Escape closes; inserting a snippet (`insertTextFormat` 2, through `core/snippet`), `textEdit` with insert/replace ranges (`editor.suggest.insertMode`), `additionalTextEdits` (imports), `command`, `completionItem/resolve` for the focused row, commit characters; word-based suggestions from the open documents when no provider answers (`editor.wordBasedSuggestions`). Snippets of the user's snippet files are rows too (`editor.snippetSuggestions`).
- *Hover*: after `editor.hover.delay` (300 ms) over a word, or Ctrl+K Ctrl+I (pressed again it gives the keys to the box); Markdown content with code blocks colored by the language's grammar and the theme; it stays while the pointer moves into it (`editor.hover.sticky`); several providers stack, with the diagnostics of the position in the same box (step 12.4).
- *Signature help* (the parameter hints): on the server's trigger characters (`editor.parameterHints.enabled`) and Ctrl+Shift+Space; the active signature and parameter highlighted, with the documentation of the parameter and of the signature; it asks again while it shows (the retrigger characters, typing, moving the cursor) and closes as VS Code's does; Up/Down (and the arrows of the widget, with the counter "1/3") between overloads (`editor.parameterHints.cycle`).
- *Navigation*: Go to Definition (F12, Ctrl+click with the link underline on Ctrl+hover), Go to Declaration, Type Definition, Implementations (Ctrl+F12), References (Shift+F12); one result jumps, several open the **peek view** (an inline zone under the line with the list of locations grouped by file on the right and a read-only-looking editor of the selected location on the left, Escape closes, Enter or double-click opens) as VS Code's `editor.gotoLocation.multiple: peek`; Peek Definition (Alt+F12); the navigation history (Alt+Left/Right, §10.9) records each jump. Document highlights (the other occurrences of the symbol under the cursor, read and write kinds) replace the word-based occurrence highlight when a provider answers.
- *Symbols*: document symbols feed the Outline view (in the Explorer, a tree with the symbol kind icons, following the cursor, `outline.*` settings), the breadcrumbs (§9.7: the symbol path after the file, with the symbol picker), sticky scroll (§9.6: the outline model replaces the indentation candidates when available) and Go to Symbol in Editor (Ctrl+Shift+O, `@` in quick open, `@:` grouped by kind); workspace symbols feed Go to Symbol in Workspace (Ctrl+T, `#` in quick open).
- *Code actions*: the light bulb at the start of the line when actions exist for the cursor or a diagnostic (`editor.lightbulb.enabled`), Ctrl+. and the context menu's Quick Fix... and Refactor... and Source Action... open the action list (preferred first, kinds grouped, disabled ones with their reason); applying an action applies its `WorkspaceEdit` (text edits in open or closed files with one undo per document, file create/rename/delete with the explorer's rules) and runs its command (`workspace/executeCommand`); `editor.codeActionsOnSave` (`source.organizeImports`, `source.fixAll`; `explicit`, `always`, `never`, and the older `true`/`false` and array forms) runs before formatting on save.
- *Formatting*: Format Document (Ctrl+Shift+I on Linux, as VS Code's), Format Selection (Ctrl+K Ctrl+F), `editor.formatOnSave` (with `editor.formatOnSaveMode`: `file`, `modifications`, `modificationsIfAvailable`; the lines that differ from the file on disk, which needs a formatter that formats ranges), `editor.formatOnType` (the server's trigger characters), `editor.formatOnPaste`; one undo step each; `editor.defaultFormatter` per language when several formatters exist; a participant of a save that takes longer than its timeout (`editor.formatOnSaveTimeout` and `editor.codeActionsOnSaveTimeout`, 750 ms each) is given up with a silent notification and the save goes on.
- *Rename*: F2 opens the rename input box on the symbol (with `prepareRename` deciding the range and refusing with its message), Enter applies the `WorkspaceEdit` across files, Ctrl+Enter (VS Code's key, `editor.rename.enablePreview`) previews it in a list with a check box per file and per change (Apply or Discard); one undo per document.
- *Code lens*: lenses above lines (`editor.codeLens`), resolved when they come into view, clicking runs the command (step 14.3 uses them for Go tests).
- *Inlay hints*: `editor.inlayHints.enabled` (`on`, `off`, `onUnlessPressed`, `offUnlessPressed` with Ctrl+Alt), drawn as faded labels between characters that do not change the text; hover and click as the server says.
- *Semantic tokens*: full and delta requests for the visible documents, mapped to the theme's semantic token colors (`semanticHighlighting.enabled` per theme, `editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations`), drawn over the TextMate colors.
- *Folding and selection ranges*: `textDocument/foldingRange` replaces the indentation provider when a server answers (§8.6's commands unchanged); Expand/Shrink Selection (Shift+Alt+Right/Left) use `textDocument/selectionRange`, else the word/bracket rules.

**As built (step 12.2, `core/lsp` and `core/lsp/lsptest`).** Files of `core/lsp`: `frame.go` (`ReadFrame`, `WriteFrame`), `conn.go` and `queue.go` (the JSON-RPC connection), `client.go` (the handshake, the handlers, `Request`, shutdown), `sync.go` (document sync), `position.go` and `uri.go`, `capabilities.go` (client and server capabilities), `types.go` and `types_features.go` (the wire types), `methods.go` (method names and enum values). `core/langfeatures` is step 12.3's.
- *API.* `NewClient(ctx, rwc, ClientOptions)` starts a `Conn` over any `io.ReadWriteCloser` (a server process is `lsp.StartProcess`, step 12.3's), sends `initialize` and `initialized`, and returns an initialized `*Client` (or closes `rwc` and fails). `Client.Call`/`Notify` and the generic `Request[R](ctx, c, method, params)` run any method; `Capabilities()`, `ServerInfo()`, `Encoding()`, `Registrations()`/`Registered(method)`, `Done()`, `Err()`, `Wait()`; `Shutdown(ctx)` (the `shutdown` request, `exit`, then close; the connection is closed in every case) and `Close()` (no handshake, for a dead server); `ErrorCode(err)` reads the code of a `ServerError`. `OpenDocument(*document.Document)` returns a `*SyncedDocument` with `Close`, `WillSave(reason)` and `WillSaveWaitUntil(ctx, reason)`. Server requests and notifications go to the optional members of `Handlers` (`Configuration`, `ApplyEdit`, `ShowMessageRequest`, `ShowMessage`, `LogMessage`, `CreateProgress`, `Progress`, `PublishDiagnostics`, `Refresh`, `RegistrationsChanged`, `Notification` for the rest); without a handler `workspace/configuration` answers null per item, `workspace/applyEdit` answers `applied: false`, `window/showMessageRequest` null, progress creation and the refresh requests are accepted, `workspace/workspaceFolders` gives the folder, `window/showDocument` `success: false`, and an unknown request `MethodNotFound` (-32601). A handler's error becomes the response error: the tags `MethodNotFound` and `InvalidParams` give -32601 and -32602, an `int` `"code"` in the error's metadata gives that code, anything else -32603.
- *Concurrency.* One goroutine reads; one writes an **unbounded queue** of outgoing messages in the order they were queued (so a `didChange` queued before a request is written before it, and `Notify` never blocks the UI thread; a server that stops reading makes the queue grow with the edits made); one delivers the server's notifications **one at a time in arrival order** (a slow handler cannot stop the reader, and may wait for a response); each server request is answered on its own goroutine with a context that ends when the server sends `$/cancelRequest` for it or the connection ends. Nothing in `core/lsp` touches a widget; handlers hand their work to the UI thread (`SetState`/`Post`, §5.1).
- *Cancellation, timeouts, errors.* A request has **no timeout** of its own (the protocol has none, nor has VS Code): the `ctx` of the caller is the limit. When it ends, `$/cancelRequest` is queued, the call returns at once with `RequestCancelled` (the error wraps the context's error, so `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` works) and a late response is dropped; a context that was already done sends nothing. An error response is `ServerError` (metadata `code`, `method`, `data`), a connection that ended is `ServerClosed` (metadata `cause`), a result that does not fit its type is `ResultInvalid`, or the tag of the type that could not read it (`HoverInvalid`, ...). `-32801 ContentModified` and `-32802 ServerCancelled` are the server's way to say "ask again" and are left to the caller (`ErrorCode`).
- *Framing and limits.* `Content-Length` is required, `Content-Type` is accepted when it names `utf-8` or `utf8`, header names are case-insensitive, lines end in CRLF, at most 32 header lines, a header line at most the reader's buffer (64 KiB in a `Conn`). **A message body over 64 MiB** (`DefaultMaxMessageSize`, `ClientOptions.MaxMessageSize`) **and every framing error are fatal**: the stream cannot be resynchronized, so the connection ends and the pending calls fail with `ServerClosed` carrying the cause (`Client.Err()` is the framing error itself; at the end of the server's output it is `io.EOF`). A message that is not JSON-RPC (bad JSON, neither method nor id, a response nobody waits for) is logged and skipped. Notifications that arrived before the end are still delivered, so a crashing server's last `logMessage` is not lost.
- *Trace.* `ClientOptions.Trace` (`ConnOptions.Trace`) is called for every message, with direction, kind, method, id, the whole JSON body, the time and, for a response, the time since its request; outgoing messages just before they are written, so the order is the wire's. Step 12.3 formats it by `<id>.trace.server`: `messages` shows direction, method and id, `verbose` adds the body. The callback must not block.
- *Client capabilities* (`DefaultClientCapabilities`, only what area 3 builds). `general`: `positionEncodings` `["utf-8", "utf-16"]`, `staleRequestSupport` (cancel, and `retryOnContentModified` for the requests that are asked again). `window`: `workDoneProgress`, `showMessage`. `workspace`: `applyEdit`; `workspaceEdit` with `documentChanges`, the resource operations create, rename and delete, `failureHandling` `textOnlyTransactional`; `didChangeConfiguration` (static), `didChangeWatchedFiles` (dynamic, relative patterns), `symbol`, `executeCommand`, `configuration`, `workspaceFolders`, and `refreshSupport` of semantic tokens, code lenses, inlay hints and diagnostics. `textDocument`: synchronization with `willSave`, `willSaveWaitUntil` and `didSave`; completion (snippets, commit characters, markdown documentation, deprecated and tags, preselect, insert/replace, resolve of `documentation`, `detail` and `additionalTextEdits`, label details, `itemDefaults`, context); hover (markdown, plain text); signature help (offset labels, active parameter, context); declaration, definition, type definition and implementation with `linkSupport`; references; document highlight; document symbol (hierarchical, tags, label); code action (literals with the kinds `quickfix`, `refactor*`, `source`, `source.organizeImports`, `source.fixAll`; preferred, disabled, data, resolve of `edit`); code lens; formatting, range formatting, on-type formatting; rename with `prepareSupport`; `publishDiagnostics` (related information, tags, version, code description, data); pull `diagnostic`; folding range (line folding only, kinds, collapsed text); selection range; semantic tokens (range, full and delta, the standard legend, `serverCancelSupport`, `augmentsSyntaxTokens`); inlay hints with `resolveSupport`. **Not advertised**: linked editing, document colors, document links, call and type hierarchies, inline values, monikers, notebooks, file operations, `window/showDocument`, and the 3.18 additions. A request for a feature the server did not declare is the caller's to refuse (`ServerCapabilities` and `Registered`).
- *Position conversion.* `Encoding.Column`/`ByteColumn` convert one line; `PositionToLSP`/`PositionFromLSP`/`RangeToLSP`/`RangeFromLSP` convert in a `buffer.Snapshot` (or anything with `LineCount` and `LineContent`). The encoding is the server's `capabilities.positionEncoding` (absent: UTF-16); `utf-32`, which the client does not offer, is understood if a server picks it, any other value fails `NewClient` with `PositionEncodingUnsupported`. A byte column inside a character counts as its start; a character offset inside a surrogate pair rounds back to the start of the character; a character past the end of its line is the end of the line and a line past the end is the end of the text (the protocol's rules for a server's positions). A byte that is not UTF-8 is, for the server, the character U+FFFD that JSON carries (3 bytes in UTF-8, 1 unit otherwise), and counts as that. The offsets in the parameter labels of signature help are UTF-16 offsets in the label whatever the encoding (the protocol says so) and are not converted.
- *Document sync.* The server's copy is the document's text **with the document's line ending** (the buffer has `\n` only; a CRLF document is sent with `\r\n`, in `didOpen`, in the inserted text of changes and in `didSave` text). The `version` is `Document.Version()`, which goes up with every change, undo and redo. Every `ChangeEvent` becomes one `didChange`; an undo of several steps sends one per step, each with its own `Before` snapshot. For an incremental server the edits of a batch are sent **last position first**: a batch's ranges are in the text before it, and an edit at a later position does not move an earlier one, so the server applying them in order gets every range right; ranges are converted with the line texts of the text before the batch (the column of a position only depends on the characters in front of it, which the edits behind it do not change). A full-sync server, a `SetText` (reload, `Reopen with Encoding`) and a change of the line ending (every line end changes) send the whole text. `OpenDocument` sends `didOpen` only when the server wants open/close notifications (`textDocumentSync` as a number is `openClose: true`); the sync kind is the static one raised by a dynamic registration of `textDocument/didChange` (its `syncKind`); `didSave` text is sent when `includeText` is set and is the document's text now, not the saved text (the server already has every later change); `willSave` and `willSaveWaitUntil` are sent only when offered. The selectors of dynamic registrations are not looked at: the host decides which documents are opened. A registration that arrives after a document was opened does not open it retroactively. A renamed or saved-as document (`SetURI`) is closed under its old URI and opened under the new one. `SyncedDocument` methods, like the document's, belong to the goroutine that owns the document; after the connection has ended they do nothing but log at debug level (the host learns of the end from `Done` and opens its documents on the new client). The save pipeline calling `WillSave`/`WillSaveWaitUntil` before the text is taken is step 12.8's.
- *URIs.* `DocumentURI` gives `file:///path` with the path percent-encoded, `untitled:Untitled-N` and `emetos-virtual:/path`; `ParseDocumentURI` reads them back and refuses other schemes (`DocumentURIUnsupported`) and malformed ones (`DocumentURIInvalid`).
- *Wire types.* A subset written by hand, no generator. Members the protocol gives several shapes get one: `Hover.Contents` is always a list of `MarkupContent`; `MarkupContent` reads a plain string as plain text; `LocationLinks` reads a `Location`, `Location[]` or `LocationLink[]`; `CompletionList` reads an item array; `DocumentSymbols` reads `DocumentSymbol[]` or flat `SymbolInformation[]` (as symbols without children, `ContainerName` filled); `CodeActions` reads bare `Command`s as actions; `DocumentChange` covers text document edits and the three file operations; `PrepareRenameResult`, `InlayHintLabel`, `ParameterLabel`, `SemanticTokensDeltaResult` and `Provider` (a boolean or an options object, with `Bool` and `Strings` readers) do the same. A value the server expects back unchanged (`data`) is kept as raw JSON, and the types that are sent back (completion items, code actions, inlay hints) write the shape they read.
- *The fake server.* `lsptest.Server` answers from a JSON `Script`: `capabilities` (which decide the sync kind and the encoding), `serverInfo`, `responses` by method (a result, an error, a delay, or a `sequence` indexed by the number of the request), `send` (notifications or requests it sends after receiving a given method), `crashOn` and `stallOn` (a method). A response with `insideParens` (step 17b.3) answers null unless the position of the request is inside a `(` of the server's copy of the document that is not closed yet, as a server's signature help is none outside the arguments of a call. It records all traffic, keeps its own copy of every document by applying `didOpen`/`didChange`/`didClose` with code of its own that counts characters as a server of the encoding does (a position that is outside the text, in the middle of a character or past the end of its line, and a version that does not go up, are listed by `Violations`), and answers `$/lsptest/document`, `$/lsptest/traffic` and `$/lsptest/violations`; `$/lsptest/crash` and `$/lsptest/stall` make it die or stop answering on command. Most tests run it **in process over `io.Pipe`** (`lsptest.Start`: fast, deterministic, and the race detector sees both sides); a few run **the real program** (`lsptest/fakeserver`, built with `go build` into the test's folder at every `StartProcess`, quick through Go's build cache, started in its own process group with its output on an `os.Pipe` so that the last answer is never lost, and killed with the whole group when the test ends) to cover real pipes, a process that exits, and a crash with an exit status. The tests of `core/lsp` include a seeded random test (`TestRandomEditsKeepTheServerInSync`: 6 seeds for each of 5 server kinds, incremental UTF-16, UTF-8 and UTF-32 and full UTF-16 and UTF-8, each for LF and CRLF documents, 150 operations a run, texts up to about 1.5 KB made of 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-byte characters, tabs and line breaks; batches of one to three edits, undo, redo, `SetText` and changes of the line ending) that compares the server's copy with the document, with `Violations` empty.

**As built (step 12.3, `extension/`, `core/lsp/process.go`, `core/langfeatures`, `gui/exthost/{servers,providers}.go`, `gui/app/lsphost.go`).** Where the text above leaves room:
- *The manifest.* `Contributes.LanguageServers []LanguageServerSpec{ID, Name, Languages, Program, Args, Env, PathSetting, InitializationOptions, ConfigurationSection, WatchedFiles, OnActivation}` (`extension/languageservers.go`; `extension.CheckManifest` refuses an id that is not lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, a missing name, languages or program, and two servers with one id: `ExtensionServerInvalid`, `ExtensionServerDuplicate`). The server `ID` is local to the extension; its qualified id is `<extension id>.<ID>` (`extension.QualifiedServerID`). The langpack `Spec` has `LanguageServers`, which the pack puts in its manifest.
- *Who runs it.* A server belongs to the **activation** of its extension in a tab: the host makes it (`Scope.startServers`) right after `Activate` returned, so the end of the activation (the tab closes, the extension is turned off or fails, Emetos quits) stops it, and the extension's own `Activate` does not start it. It starts when the first document of its languages is open in the tab (the documents open at that time count), or at once with `OnActivation`. The documents it follows are those of its languages that are untitled or files below the folder of the tab (a tab with no folder serves untitled documents only and starts the program in Emetos's folder); a document whose language changes later keeps the server it had. Documents opened before the server is ready are opened on it when it is; a closed document is closed on it; a renamed one follows (`SyncedDocument`).
- *The process* (`lsp.StartProcess`, `lsp.FindProgram`). `Program` is looked up in `PATH` (a name with a slash is a path), unless the setting named by `PathSetting` is not empty. It runs in the folder, with the environment of Emetos plus `Env`, in a process group of its own (`Setpgid`); its standard output is the stream of the `Client`, its standard error is read line by line (a line over 64 KiB is cut) into the Output channel, and whatever it left in the group is killed when it ends. `Process.Stop(grace)` closes its input and waits `grace`, then sends SIGTERM to the group and, 2 s later, SIGKILL. The tags are `ProgramNotFound` and `ProcessStartFailed`.
- *Start, crash, restart, stop.* The handshake runs off the UI thread (60 s limit); a server of an older generation (stopped or restarted meanwhile) is shut down when its start ends. A server whose connection ends without our asking, or whose start fails, **crashed**; the policy is that of VS Code's default error handler: it is started again at once unless it is the fifth crash within 3 minutes (the clock of the scope), which leaves it `ServerFailed` and shows an error notification "The <Name> server crashed 5 times in the last 3 minutes. The server will not be restarted." with **Restart** (forgets the crashes and starts it) and **Show Output**. A program that is not found (`ServerMissing`) is told once, as an error notification "<Program> was not found. Install it, or set the path in the settings." with **Open Settings** (the command `workbench.action.openSettings` with the key of `PathSetting`) and is not started again until that setting changes (then it starts at once) or the server is restarted. Stopping (the tab closes, the extension goes) does `shutdown`/`exit` within the grace period (`HostOptions.ServerGrace`, 3 s by default) and then stops the program as above; it happens in the background and `Scope.Close` does not wait, but `Host.Shutdown` and `Host.WaitServers` do, so no program outlives Emetos. `<extension id>.restartServer` ("Restart Language Server", category the name of the extension; registered with the other declarations, so it is in the palette before the extension runs) restarts every server of the extension in the tab and starts an idle one. `Scope.ServerStatus(extension, server)` gives the state (`ServerIdle`, `Starting`, `Running`, `Failed`, `Missing`, `Stopped`), the number of starts and crashes and the PID, for the tests and the pages that show it; the extension reads it with `api.LanguageServers()` (step 14.1, §10.17 "As built (step 14.1)").
- *Settings the host registers* (while the extension is enabled in a tab, held by count like the settings of 11.1): `<extension id>.<ID>.trace.server` (`off`, `messages`, `verbose`; default `off`) and the `PathSetting` key (string, empty). Neither follows the "key starts with the id of the extension" rule of `Settings().Register`, which is for the extension's own registrations; the host registers `PathSetting` as the spec gives it (`go.goplsPath`).
- *Output channel, trace, status.* The channel is named `Name`. Lines have the form of VS Code's language clients, `[Level - 15:04:05] text`, with the levels `Info`, `Warn`, `Error`, `Log` (from `window/logMessage`, `window/showMessage` and the host's own lines such as "Starting ..." and "Restarting ...") and `Stderr`. With the trace on, each message is `[Trace - time] Sending request 'method - (id)'.`, `Received response 'method - (id)' in 12ms.`, `Sending notification 'm'.`, `Received notification 'm'.`, `Received request 'm - (id)'.` or `Sending response 'm - (id)'.`; `verbose` adds the whole JSON message as the next line. The level is read on the UI thread when the setting changes. The status bar item (`extension.<extension id>.server.<ID>`, left; a server declared with `OwnUI` has none, §10.17) is visible while the server starts ("$(sync) <Name>: starting") and while a `$/progress` work done progress runs ("$(sync) <Name>: <title> <message> <n>%", the last one that began); a click shows the channel.
- *Messages.* `window/showMessage` is a notification (error, warning or info; a log message goes to the Output channel only) with the name of the extension as its source. `window/showMessageRequest` is a sticky notification whose buttons are the actions; the answer is the button pressed, or null when the notification is dismissed or the request ends first (the notification is then dismissed too).
- *Configuration.* `workspace/configuration` is answered per item: no section or the server's `ID` is the settings at `ConfigurationSection`; `<ID>.rest` is `ConfigurationSection.rest`; any other section is the settings of that name (`editor.tabSize` is 4 by default); a section with no value is null. The values come from `settings.Store.Section`, which reads the consolidated settings whether or not a setting is registered. A change of the settings that changes the section is sent as `workspace/didChangeConfiguration` with the section as `settings`.
- *Watched files.* The batches of the window's file watcher become `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` for the files below the folder that match the `WatchedFiles` globs (relative to the folder) or a watcher the server registered (`client/registerCapability`: a glob string, or a relative pattern with a base URI; the `kind` mask is honored). A rename is a delete of the old path and a create of the new; a rescan is not sent.
- *`workspace/applyEdit`* is applied on the UI thread with `langfeatures.Apply` and answered with `applied` (and `failureReason`, `failedChange`); the refusal is written to the Output channel.
- *Features model* (`core/langfeatures`, no UI, no Glutter). Types: `Document` (an immutable snapshot of one version, safe for goroutines), `Position`/`Range` (Emetos's byte columns), `CompletionItem`/`CompletionList`, `Hover`, `SignatureHelp`, `LocationLink`, `DocumentSymbol`, `DocumentHighlight`, `Diagnostic`, `CodeAction`, `TextEdit`, `PrepareRename`, `WorkspaceEdit`. The `Registry` has a list of providers per feature; a provider is registered by an owner (the id of the extension, which is also what `editor.defaultFormatter` names) with a `Selector{Languages, Pattern, Schemes, Folder}` whose score is VS Code's (10 for a language or a pattern, 5 for every document, 0 for none) and is asked in the order higher score first, the newer registration first among equals. *Merging*: **completion** asks the best group (equal scores) together and goes to the next group only when it had no items and no incomplete list, joining the items in provider order with the owner on each; **hover** stacks every provider's non-empty hover; **definition, declaration, type definition and implementation** (`NavigationProvider` with a kind) and **references** join every answer without the same place twice; **signature help, document symbols and document highlights** take the first non-empty answer; **code actions** are joined; **formatting** is one formatter (`PickFormatter`: the owner named by `editor.defaultFormatter`, else the first in order; it says how many others there are; `FormatRange` only asks those that implement `RangeFormattingProvider`); **rename** asks the providers in order and the first that answers wins (`PrepareRename` returns nil for "use the word"; an error is a refusal). Providers are asked on goroutines of their own with the request's `ctx`; a provider that fails does not hide the others (`[]ProviderError`). Trigger characters are those registered with the provider or, for a server, those it declared.
- *The server as a provider* (`ServerProvider`, `langfeatures.Server` is what `*lsp.Client` offers): one value implements every provider interface; it asks `Client()` for the current client at each request, so a restarted server keeps its registration, and answers nothing without a client or for a feature the server does not offer (capability on, or the method registered dynamically). Conversions (`HoverFromLSP`, `CompletionFromLSP` with the list's `itemDefaults`, `SignatureHelpFromLSP` with the parameter offsets counted in UTF-16, `LocationsFromLSP`, `ReferencesFromLSP`, `SymbolsFromLSP`, `HighlightsFromLSP`, `DiagnosticsFromLSP` for step 12.4, `TextEditsFromLSP`, `CodeActionsFromLSP`) convert positions with the text of the document they are in: the document of the request, or, for a location in another file, the `TextSource` (the snapshot of the open document taken on the UI thread, else the file read from disk; without a text the columns are taken as byte columns). Not built here: completion resolve and `workspace/executeCommand` (built in step 12.5 for completion, §9.12 "As built (step 12.5)"; the code actions' use of the command is 12.8), `publishDiagnostics` and pull diagnostics (12.4), workspace symbols (12.7), code lens, inlay hints, semantic tokens, folding and selection ranges (12.9), `willSave` before the text is taken (12.8).
- *Providers in Go* (`extension/providers.go`; `api.Languages().Register{Completion,Hover,SignatureHelp,Definition,Reference,DocumentSymbol,DocumentHighlight,CodeAction,Formatting,Rename,CodeLens}Provider(selector, provider)` (the code lens provider is step 14.3's: §10.17 "As built (step 14.3)") returning the function that takes it away, also taken with the activation). The types mirror the shapes the features need and import nothing of Emetos: positions are the core events' (`Position{Line, Col}`, zero-based, bytes), a provider gets a `TextDocument{URI, LanguageID, Version, Text}` copy of the document, kinds are the LSP's numbers, `WorkspaceEdit` has `ResourceChange`s of kind `edit`, `create`, `rename` and `delete`. Diagnostics stay `api.Problems()`. A provider's call is made by `Scope.guardProvider`: a panic gives `ExtensionProviderPanicked` to the caller (its answer is dropped), fails the extension in that tab on the UI thread's next turn (the contributions of the extension, its providers and its servers go, one notification, the log has the route) and touches no other tab or extension; an error of the provider is `ExtensionProviderFailed`, reported with the others and not a failure; `ExtensionProviderInvalid` is a nil provider and `ExtensionEditInvalid` a change of an unknown kind. `Scope.Features()` is the registry of the tab; the UI of 12.4–12.9 calls it.
- *Applying a `WorkspaceEdit`* (`langfeatures.Apply(ctx, EditHost, *WorkspaceEdit)`, on the goroutine that owns the documents, the UI thread). The changes are made in order; the text changes between two file operations form a run, and the edits of one document in a run are one batch, so **one undo step per document**. An edit that has only text changes is **all or nothing**: every document is found (a closed file is opened by the host), its version checked (a change that names a version the document no longer has fails with `WorkspaceEditStale`), it is not read-only (`WorkspaceEditReadOnly`) and its edits do not overlap (`WorkspaceEditOverlap`) before the first is changed. With file operations the first failure stops the rest, after the earlier changes were made (the protocol's "abort"; `ApplyResult.FailedChange` is the index). Edits from a server are converted when applied, with the text of each document as it is then. **Closed files follow VS Code**: they are opened as documents of the window and **left open and unsaved**; in the window (`workspaceEdits.OpenForEdit`) they get an editor in the active group that is not the active editor and does not take the focus (`openOptions.Inactive`), so the changes are visible, in the close question and in the hot exit; the file on disk is written when the user saves.
