File operations go through the window's `FileOps` (so they are in its undo history and follow the explorer's rules): a create makes the folders above it and is refused over a file unless `ignoreIfExists` (left alone) or `overwrite` (the old file goes to the trash); a rename in one folder is the explorer's rename, to another folder it is a move after making the folder (and a rename if the name changes), refused over a file unless `ignoreIfExists` or `overwrite` (trash); a delete goes to the trash, `ignoreIfNotExists` forgives a missing path. The open documents under a renamed path follow, as after an explorer operation. These operations and the read of a closed file run on the UI thread (a refactoring is a few small files).
- *Tags* (each has a route test): `ExtensionServerInvalid`, `ExtensionServerDuplicate`, `ExtensionProviderInvalid`, `ExtensionProviderPanicked`, `ExtensionProviderFailed`, `ExtensionEditInvalid`, `ProgramNotFound`, `ProcessStartFailed`, `NoFormatter`, `NotRenameable`, `WorkspaceEditInvalid`, `WorkspaceEditDocumentUnavailable`, `WorkspaceEditStale`, `WorkspaceEditReadOnly`, `WorkspaceEditOverlap`, `WorkspaceEditFileFailed`, `LanguageTextUnavailable`, `LanguageEditFileExists` and `FakeProviderInvalid` (`extensions/internal/fakeapi`).
- *Tests.* `core/lsp/process_test.go` (the process, its group, stderr), `core/langfeatures` (registry order and groups, every merge rule, conversions with non-ASCII positions, the server provider on the fake server, `Apply` with open and closed documents, versions, overlaps, file operations and server edits), `gui/exthost/servers_test.go` and `providers_test.go` (the lifetime, one server per tab, documents, settings, crashes with the fake clock, a missing program, trace levels, Output, progress, messages, watched files, the restart command, `workspace/applyEdit`, a Go provider and a server merged, a panic contained to one extension in one tab, every feature of the Go API), `gui/app/lsphost_test.go` (edits and file operations through the window), `extensions/golang` (the declaration of `gopls`) and, with the build tag `emetos_gopls`, `gui/exthost/gopls_test.go` (the real `gopls`: it starts, hovers and lists symbols for a Go file, and stops without leaving a process).

**As built (step 12.4, `gui/exthost/diagnostics.go`, `gui/editor/{diagnostics,diagnostics_paint,hover,hover_widget}.go`, `gui/views/problems/navigation.go`, `gui/app/diagnostics.go`).** Where the text above leaves room:
- *Push.* `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` is handled on the goroutine of the connection (`Handlers.PublishDiagnostics`), which only queues it: a publication of a URI that waits is replaced by the newer one, and one worker converts and sets the publications one after the other, so those of a file stay in order. The worker asks the UI thread for the open document with the URI (its version and a snapshot of its text, the same function that reads the version) and, for a file that is not open, reads it from disk; positions in the server's encoding become Problems columns (**UTF-16 units counted from 1**, VS Code's) with that text (UTF-16 servers need none; a file that cannot be read keeps the columns as they came). The markers are set with `Service.Set(owner, path, markers)` where the **owner is the qualified id of the server** (`<extension id>.<server id>`, so `Markers.Remove(owner)` takes them all away). A marker carries the severity (none is an error), code (a number is its text), `codeDescription.href` (`Marker.CodeHref`), source, message, the tags (`Marker.Unnecessary`, `Marker.Deprecated`) and the related information (positions taken as UTF-16 whatever the encoding: the text of the other file is not at hand). Only `file:` URIs are kept.
- *Versions.* A publication that carries a `version` older than the version of the open document is **dropped** (its positions are not those of the text, and the server republishes for the newer one); a publication for the version of the text, one without a version, and one for a file that is not open are applied. The squiggles do not wait for the next publication to be in the right place: they move with the edits (below).
- *Pull* (`diagnosticProvider` in the capabilities, or `textDocument/diagnostic` registered dynamically). The document is pulled when it opens on the server and 250 ms after its last change (`pullDelay`, restarted by each change), and every open document is pulled again on `workspace/diagnostic/refresh` and when the registration changes. The request is made off the UI thread with the identifier of the server and `previousResultId` of the last full report of the document; a `full` report sets the markers and keeps its `resultId`, an `unchanged` one leaves them, and `relatedDocuments` of full reports set the markers of those files too (from the open document or the file). A report for an older version than the one open when it comes is dropped and the document is pulled again after the quiet time; `ServerCancelled` and `ContentModified` answers are not an error. Workspace diagnostics (`workspace/diagnostic`) are not asked for.
- *Closing and stopping* (VS Code's rule). The markers that were **pushed** for a file stay when its document closes (the server decides when to send an empty list; gopls reports the files of its packages); those that came from a **pull** go with the document (nothing republishes for a closed document), and the result id is forgotten. **Every marker of the server goes** when the connection ends (a crash, a restart, Restart Language Server, the end of the activation, the tab closing), as `vscode-languageclient` clears its diagnostic collection; a publication that was queued for the old connection is dropped (it carries the generation of the client it came from).
- *Squiggles.* The window gives every text editor the markers of its file (`gui/app/diagnostics.go`: it follows the marker service, posts one update per burst of changes to the UI thread and converts the columns to bytes with the text of the document); the editor holds them as **decorations of the document** of its own owner slot (`diagnosticsOwner`, slot 8; a view model now reserves **9** owners), `NeverGrowsWhenTypingAtEdges`, so they follow every edit until the producer sets its markers again. The ranges are made as VS Code's `_createDecorationRange`: a hint without a tag covers two characters on its line, an empty range covers the word it is in unless it is at the end of the text of the line (then one character wide), and a marker whose range is the whole line to `MaxInt` starts at its first non-blank. A read-only editor shows none (`editor.renderValidationDecorations` is `editable`, VS Code's default, which has no setting). Painting looks up only the decorations of the rows in view (`DecorationsIn` of those lines), so a file with thousands of problems costs a frame what a few do; the view model has `SetDiagnostics`, `Diagnostics`, `DiagnosticsAt`, `DisposeDiagnostics`.
- *Drawing* (the pattern of VS Code's `getSquigglySVGData`: a zigzag 6 pixels wide and 3 high, its low point 1.8 pixels from the left of the range and its high point 4.8, drawn in a 3 pixel strip at the bottom of the row and clipped to the range, over several rows when the range has them). Error, warning and info are squiggles in `editorError.foreground`, `editorWarning.foreground`, `editorInfo.foreground`; a theme can add the double underline of `editorError.border`, `editorWarning.border`, `editorInfo.border`, `editorHint.border`. A hint is three dots (`editorHint.foreground`) at the start of its range; a hint with the tag `unnecessary` has none and, with `editor.showUnused`, a dashed line when `editorUnnecessaryCode.border` is set. The tag **unnecessary** with `editor.showUnused` (true) fades the text of the range: the layer above the text draws the color of the editor over it with `1 - alpha(editorUnnecessaryCode.opacity)` (VS Code sets the opacity of the text; the difference is that a selection under the text is faded too). The tag **deprecated** with `editor.showDeprecated` (true) strikes the text through, at 54% of the row, in the foreground color (a marker with both tags is only struck, as in VS Code). The most serious squiggle is drawn last.
- *Overview ruler and minimap.* The right lane of the ruler (the right third) has a mark for each stretch of the ruler (a pixel at least 2 high) where the most serious diagnostic is the same, in `editorOverviewRuler.errorForeground`, `.warningForeground`, `.infoForeground`; hints have none. The marks are worked out when the diagnostics, the height of the ruler, the height of the text or its number of lines change, not when a line is typed in (`rulerCache`), so six thousand diagnostics cost one pass per set and per change of the line count. The minimap marks the characters of the range of an error, warning or info in `minimap.errorHighlight`, `minimap.warningHighlight`, `minimap.infoHighlight`.
- *The hover* (`hover.go`, `hover_widget.go`, the part 12.6 stacks the providers of §9.12 "Hover" into). `ViewModel.Hover()` is the `Hover{Range, Parts, Pinned}` that shows; `HoverPart{Kind, Diagnostic, Actions}` is one part of its box (`HoverPartDiagnostic`; step 12.6 added `HoverPartMarkdown`, the content of the providers, see "As built (step 12.6)": the participants are `diagnosticHover` and the providers). The pointer rests on a squiggle (`HoverPointerMoved`, from the `OnHover` of the text region) and after `editor.hover.delay` (300; `editor.hover.enabled` `off` shows none, `onKeyboardModifier` is registered and acts as `on`) the hover shows; moving inside its range keeps it, a place with nothing starts `editor.hover.hidingDelay` (300) and hides it, `editor.hover.sticky` (true) lets the pointer go into the box (`HoverBoxEntered`) and keeps it there, and without stickiness it hides at once. It also hides when the text changes, when the selections change, on a press in the editor and when the editor scrolls (not a pinned one). The box is placed over the start of the range, above it when `editor.hover.above` (true) and there is room (it is estimated from the text before it is laid out), else below, kept inside the editor; 500 pixels wide at most, in `editorHoverWidget.background`, `.foreground`, `.border` with the action row in `editorHoverWidget.statusBarBackground`. A diagnostic part has the message, then `source(code)` dimmed (the code is a link in `textLink.foreground` when the diagnostic has a `codeDescription`, opened through the OpenURI portal), a row for each related place (`file.go(line, column): message`, a link that opens the file there) and the row of actions: **View Problem** (it puts the cursor at the start of the problem and shows its hover again, pinned; `SetViewProblem`). The **quick fixes** (step 12.8) come as more `HoverAction`s of the part (the seam is `HoverPart.Actions`), and "Quick Fix..." with them. `editor.hover.*` are in `Options.Hover`; `SetOpeners(openURI, openAt)` gives the links their openers (the window's). Step 12.6 built the Markdown part, Ctrl+K Ctrl+I and the focus and scroll of the box (below); not built: the verbosity commands.
- *Go to Next Problem* (`gui/views/problems/navigation.go` `MarkerList`, `gui/app/diagnostics.go`). `editor.action.marker.nextInFiles` (F8), `.prevInFiles` (Shift+F8), `.next` (Alt+F8) and `.prev` (Shift+Alt+F8) go through the errors, warnings and infos (no hints) of every file, or of the file of the editor for the last two, in VS Code's order (`problems.sortOrder` `severity`, its default): by file path, then errors before warnings before infos, then by position. The first move starts from the cursor: the first marker of its file that holds the cursor or comes after it (going back, the one before), the first marker of the file that follows by path when its file has none, the first (last) marker of all when the cursor is after the last (a deviation: VS Code also compares the cursor with the first marker of the next file there); the next moves go on from the one shown, wrapping at the ends, until the cursor leaves it or the markers change. A marker of another file opens that file (as a kept editor, `openMarker`) and goes there. **The marker navigation widget (the inline zone) is not built**: the cursor goes to the start of the marker, it is brought into view, and its hover opens and stays (pinned) until the cursor moves, the text changes or Escape (`closeMarkersNavigation`, context key `markersNavigationVisible`). The commands are in the Go menu (Next Problem, Previous Problem) in the group `6_problem_nav`.
- *Registered* (rule 7). Settings: `editor.showUnused`, `editor.showDeprecated`, `editor.hover.enabled` (`on`, `off`, `onKeyboardModifier`), `.delay`, `.sticky`, `.hidingDelay`, `.above`. Colors: `editorError.border`, `editorWarning.border`, `editorInfo.border`, `editorHint.foreground`, `editorHint.border`, `editorUnnecessaryCode.border`, `editorUnnecessaryCode.opacity`, `editorOverviewRuler.errorForeground`, `.warningForeground`, `.infoForeground`, `minimap.errorHighlight`, `.warningHighlight`, `.infoHighlight`, `editorHoverWidget.statusBarBackground` (`editorError.foreground`, `editorWarning.foreground` and `editorInfo.foreground` came with step 6.5). Commands and keys: the four `editor.action.marker.*` and `closeMarkersNavigation` (Escape while `markersNavigationVisible`), with VS Code's keys; the dev command `dev.showHover` (§15.2).
- *Not built.* Diagnostics for `untitled:` documents (the marker service is keyed by path), the `Marker` tags and `CodeHref` in the extension contract of `api.Problems()` (an extension's markers have neither; the server's do), `editor.hover.enabled: onKeyboardModifier`'s modifier, the Problems panel rows' related information and its "View Problem" menu, `problems.decorations.enabled` and `problems.visibility` (they hide the squiggles in VS Code: nothing here reads them yet), workspace diagnostics (pull), and the markers of closed files that a push server keeps are not removed when its documents close.
- *Tests.* `gui/exthost/diagnostics_test.go` (push into markers with every field, the latest of a burst, versions, encodings, a closed file from disk, the closed-file rule for push and pull, restart, crash, a late publication, pull on open and on change with result ids, an older report, refresh, related documents) and, with `emetos_gopls`, `TestGoplsPublishesDiagnosticsForAGoFile`; `gui/editor/diagnostics_test.go` (squiggle goldens of every severity and tag in Dark and Light Modern, the ranges, moving with edits, the right lane marks, six thousand diagnostics with typing and benchmarks), `hover_test.go` (the delays, stickiness, options, stacking, what hides it, the links, placement, goldens), `gui/views/problems/navigation_test.go` (the order and the start of `MarkerList`) and `gui/app/diagnostics_test.go` (squiggles from markers with non-ASCII text, F8 across files, Escape). No new error tag: a failure to read a file or a request is logged.

**As built (step 12.5, `core/fuzzy/completion.go`, `core/langfeatures/{suggest,suggestmemory,resolve,snippetitems,words}.go`, `gui/editor/suggest*.go`, `gui/app/suggest.go`).** Where the text above leaves room:
- *Filtering and sorting (ported).* `core/fuzzy`: `AnyScore`, `FuzzyScoreGraceful`, `FuzzyScoreGracefulAggressive`, `IsPatternInWord` (VS Code's `filters.ts`, with its test cases). `langfeatures.SuggestModel` is `completionModel.ts`: `NewSuggestItems` builds the rows of the answers of the providers (the word before the cursor, the `filterText` or the label, the insert and replace ranges as byte columns of the request line, the kind filter and `editor.suggest.showDeprecated`), `SuggestModel.SetLineContext` filters them again for the text typed since (an incremental refilter with the `delta` of the characters typed, `FilterGraceful` and `MatchOnWordStartOnly`), and `SortSuggestItems`/`CompareSuggestItems` are `suggest.ts`'s comparators: score, then the `sortText`, then the label, then VS Code's order of the kinds; `editor.snippetSuggestions` puts the snippet rows on top, at the bottom or in line. Positions of the score are rune offsets of the label (the widget draws them in bold). The test table is the cases of `completionModel.test.ts`.
- *Selection memory* (`SuggestMemory`, `suggestMemory.ts`): `editor.suggestSelection` `first`, `recentlyUsed` and `recentlyUsedByPrefix` (the LRU of 300 entries that shrinks to two thirds when full). A preselected item wins among the best scored. The memory is per window tab and lives for the session; VS Code stores it in the workspace state (not built).
- *Triggers* (`gui/editor/suggest.go`, VS Code's `suggestModel.ts`). **Quick suggestions** after `editor.quickSuggestionsDelay` (10 ms) for text typed on a word (not in the middle of a word, not a number) by the kind of text under the cursor (`other`, `comments`, `strings` from the token type before the cursor); `inline` and `off` give no widget, `on` and `offWhenInlineCompletions` do (there are no inline completions yet, so the second acts as `on`); `editor.suggest.snippetsPreventQuickSuggestions` holds them back inside a snippet. **Trigger characters** (`editor.suggestOnTriggerCharacters`) of the providers: the request asks only the providers that have the character. **Ctrl+Space** (`editor.action.triggerSuggest`) asks at the cursor (the widget says "Loading..." after 50 ms, 250 ms for a request made on the quiet; "No suggestions." when nothing comes). **While typing** the text is filtered again without a request; a character that no item matches closes the widget (kept frozen for a request the user made, until they leave the word); a list that was `isIncomplete` is asked again from its providers only (`CompletionQuery.Owners`, `TriggerIncomplete`) and the items of the others are kept; a new word, or the cursor moved to the left of the request, asks again. The cursor moved by a key inside the word filters again; any other command, a change of line, of the indentation before the word, or a lost focus ends the run. **Every request runs off the UI thread** with a `ctx` that the next request or the end of the run cancels; the answer is posted back and dropped when its generation is not the current one or the text before the place of the request changed. Typing never waits for a server. `editor.suggest.selectionMode` (`always`, `never`, `whenTriggerCharacter`, `whenQuickSuggestion`) decides whether a row is focused for a widget that was not asked for by the user.
- *The widget* (`suggest_widget.go`, `suggest_commands.go`): 430 pixels wide, at most 12 rows, a row as high as `editor.suggestLineHeight` (the editor's line height when 0) in `editor.suggestFontSize`; it stands under the line, or over it when there is more room above, at the start of the word being completed (stable while the user types), kept inside the editor. A row has the kind icon (the codicon of VS Code's `completionKindToCodicon`, in `symbolIcon.<kind>Foreground`), the label with the matched characters in bold in `editorSuggestWidget.highlightForeground`, the `labelDetails` after it and the description at the right (the `detail` of the focused row while the details pane is closed, with the read-more icon); a deprecated item is struck through; a scroll bar when more than 12. The **details pane** (330 pixels, 220 at least; at the right of the list, at the left when there is no room) has the detail in a code font and the documentation: Markdown through `extension/ui/markdown` with the new `Options.Compact` (13 px, small margins, the suggest widget's colors), plain text otherwise; "Loading..." while the item is resolved. Mouse: a click accepts the row, the wheel scrolls, the read-more icon toggles the pane. Keys (weight `EditorContrib+90`): Ctrl+Space and Ctrl+I trigger the widget, focus the first row when none is focused, and toggle the details pane when one is; Tab and Enter accept (Enter when `acceptSuggestionOnEnter` allows: `on`, or `smart` when the text changes), Shift+Enter and Shift+Tab the alternative insert mode, Escape closes, Up/Down/PageUp/PageDown and Ctrl+Up/Down move the focus (wrapping round; VS Code's Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown are shadowed by the workbench's editor switching, so they are not bound), Ctrl+Alt+Space toggles the pane too. Context keys: `suggestWidgetVisible`, `suggestWidgetHasFocusedSuggestion`, `suggestWidgetMultipleSuggestions`, `suggestWidgetDetailsVisible`, `suggestWidgetDetailsFocused` (never true), `suggestionMakesTextEdit`, `acceptSuggestionOnEnter`, `suggestionHasInsertAndReplaceRange`, `suggestionInsertMode`, `suggestionCanResolve`, `editorHasCompletionItemProvider`. Whether the details show is shared by the editors of a window tab and not saved.
- *Accepting* (`suggest_accept.go`, `suggestController.ts`'s `_insertSuggestion`). One undo stop before and one after: the additional edits, the text and the cursor move are **one undo step** (`document.EditOptions.Join` joins an edit to the open group, `snippet.InsertOptions.JoinUndo`). The text is the `textEdit` or the `insertText` or the label, inserted through `core/snippet` (a plain text is escaped, so `$` stays; `insertTextFormat` 2 starts a session with its tab stops; `insertTextMode` `asIs` keeps the white space, else it is adjusted to the line). The range is the insert range, or the replace range with `editor.suggest.insertMode` `replace` (the alternative commands swap them); an item with one range only uses it; without ranges the word before the cursor is replaced and, in `replace` mode, the rest of the word too. The text right of the cursor is followed through the edit with a decoration (`lineSuffix`). `additionalTextEdits` are made first (the cursors follow the text; an edit after the place of the request on its line moves with what was typed since, as in VS Code); an item that was not resolved yet is inserted at once and asked for its additional edits, which are made when they come as one more step of the same undo group, and not at all when the text changed before them since (it would be the wrong place). The **command** of the item runs after the insert: `editor.action.triggerSuggest` asks again; a command of a language server goes to it with `workspace/executeCommand` (the item's `Command.Owner` is the server, `Scope.ExecuteServerCommand`) off the UI thread; any other is a command of the window, run with the first of its arguments. **Commit characters** of the focused item accept it before the character is typed (`editor.acceptSuggestionOnCommitCharacter`). A read-only editor reports the refusal and changes nothing.
- *Resolve* (`resolve.go`, `startResolve`): `completionItem/resolve` is asked for the **focused row only**, when the provider says it can (`CompletionResolver`; the server advertises `resolveProvider`; the `data` of a list's `itemDefaults` is sent), the earlier request is cancelled when the focus moves, a resolved row is not asked again, and the answer fills the documentation, the detail, the additional edits and the command only (`MergeResolvedCompletion`: the label, the text and the ranges stay those of the list, which the sort and the insert were made from). gopls does not resolve (it sends the documentation in the list).
- *Words and snippets.* `WordProvider` is a provider with the score of every document (5, empty selector), so it is asked only when no provider of the language answered (VS Code's fallback group): `editor.wordBasedSuggestions` `off`, `currentDocument`, `matchingDocuments` (same language; `offWithInlineSuggestions`, the VS Code default, acts as `matchingDocuments`) and `allDocuments`; documents over 5 MiB give no words, the word at the cursor is not a suggestion, a number is not a word. `gui/app/suggest.go` registers it for the tab and takes the snapshots of the open documents on the UI thread. The snippets of the snippet service are rows of the editor itself (kind snippet, `SnippetItems`, VS Code's `snippetCompletionProvider`: the prefix matched anywhere in the word, `isPatternInWord`, the replace range covers the prefix typed), computed synchronously at each request and merged with the answers; the auto-closing-pair "eat" step and VS Code's label disambiguation of equal prefixes are not ported.
- *Registered* (rule 7). Settings: `editor.quickSuggestions` (object, boolean or string), `editor.quickSuggestionsDelay`, `editor.suggestOnTriggerCharacters`, `editor.acceptSuggestionOnEnter`, `editor.acceptSuggestionOnCommitCharacter`, `editor.suggestSelection`, `editor.snippetSuggestions`, `editor.wordBasedSuggestions`, `editor.suggestFontSize`, `editor.suggestLineHeight`, `editor.suggest.{insertMode, filterGraceful, localityBonus, shareSuggestSelections, selectionMode, snippetsPreventQuickSuggestions, showIcons, showStatusBar, preview, showInlineDetails, showDeprecated, matchOnWordStartOnly}` and the 25 `editor.suggest.show<Kind>` (`settings.SuggestKinds`). Colors: `editorSuggestWidget.{background, border, foreground, selectedForeground, selectedIconForeground, selectedBackground, focusHighlightForeground, highlightForeground}`, `.focusOutline`, `editorSuggestWidgetStatus.foreground` and the 33 `symbolIcon.<name>Foreground` (`kit.Colors.SymbolIcons`, `SymbolIconColor`). Commands: `editor.action.triggerSuggest`, `acceptSelectedSuggestion`, `acceptAlternativeSelectedSuggestion`, `hideSuggestWidget`, `selectNextSuggestion`, `selectPrevSuggestion`, `selectNextPageSuggestion`, `selectPrevPageSuggestion`, `selectFirstSuggestion`, `selectLastSuggestion`, `focusSuggestion`, `focusAndAcceptSuggestion`, `toggleSuggestionDetails`, `toggleSuggestionFocus`; dev commands `dev.triggerSuggest` and `dev.toggleSuggestDetails` (§15.2).
- *Not built.* `editor.suggest.localityBonus`, `shareSuggestSelections` and `preview` (read, no effect); `showStatusBar` (read, there is no status bar); `editor.tabCompletion`; Toggle Explain Mode; focusing the details pane (`toggleSuggestionFocus` toggles it); `fitWidthToDetails` and the resizable widget with its saved size; the hover style of a row under the pointer; the kinds `Customcolor`, `User` and `Issue`; persisting the selection memory and the details state; the wait of `offWhenInlineCompletions` for inline completions.
- *Tests.* `core/fuzzy/completion_test.go` (the cases of `filters.test.ts`), `core/langfeatures/{suggest,completion}_test.go` (the cases of `completionModel.test.ts`, the sort, the memory modes and their eviction, trigger-character and owner filtering, incomplete marks, resolve on the fake server with `itemDefaults.data`, `executeCommand`, the merge of a resolved item, the word provider modes and its fallback, snippet rows), `core/document` and `core/snippet` (the joined undo group), `gui/editor/suggest_test.go` (every trigger, quick-suggestion settings, delay, "Loading..." and "No suggestions.", stale answers, incomplete re-request, refilter, navigation and scrolling, selection modes, each edit kind, a snippet item, white space, additional edits in one undo step, async edits and their drop, resolve of the focused row only and its cancellation, commit characters, the item command, the details pane, words, snippet rows in the four orders, kind filters), `gui/editor/suggest_widget_test.go` (goldens `suggest_list_{dark,light}`, `suggest_details_{dark,light}`, `suggest_loading`, `suggest_empty`), `gui/exthost/completion_test.go` (the fake server: list, resolve, command), `gui/app/suggest_test.go`, `gui/kit` and `core/settings` tests for the colors and settings, and with `-tags emetos_gopls` `TestGoplsCompletesAMemberOfAPackage`.

**As built (step 12.6, `core/langfeatures/{types,registry,merge,server,convert}.go`, `gui/editor/{hover,hover_widget,signature,signature_widget}.go`, `extension/ui/markdown/view.go`, `gui/app/suggest.go`).** Where the text above leaves room:
- *What the hover is about.* The pointer rests on a **word** (editor.wordSeparators), the range of the first **diagnostic** there, or the single character when it is not in a word; there is no hover, and no request, over white space, an empty line or past the end of a line (VS Code asks the providers at every position of the text; a decision: the answer would be empty). The providers are asked at the position of the pointer. One computation (`hoverOp`) stands for the whole word: moving the pointer inside it neither restarts the wait nor asks again (VS Code makes a new anchor for each character). Ctrl+K Ctrl+I (`editor.action.showHover`) is about the cursor: the word it is in or at the end of, else an empty range at the cursor.
- *Timing* (VS Code's `HoverOperation`, with `editor.hover.delay` = H): at H/2 the hover providers are asked (the answers are kept and not shown), at H the diagnostics are computed and what there is shows, each answer that comes after is added to the box, and at 3H, while a provider has not answered, a part "Loading..." is added (the command starts at once: no wait and no "Loading..."). A box that shows with the complete answer is not replaced by a partial one of the next computation. The providers run off the UI thread with a `ctx` (`Registry.HoverEach` hands each answer over as it resolves, with the place of the provider in the order of the providers); an answer is **dropped** when the computation was replaced or cancelled (the pointer went to another word, the box hid) or the document changed, and the requests of such a computation are cancelled (`$/cancelRequest` for a server). A provider that fails is logged (`SuggestHost.Log`), not shown.
- *Stacking.* The parts are sorted as VS Code's participants: the diagnostics first (most serious first), then the providers in the order of the providers (the one that registered last first, §9.12 "Providers"), each as one part with its contents one under the other, the "Loading..." part last; a separator line (1 pixel, `editorHoverWidget.border`) between parts. The range of the box is the union of the ranges of the parts (the range of a provider's answer, else the word); the box is placed over its start as in 12.4, above the line when `editor.hover.above` and the estimated height fits, else below, and its height is limited by the room on that side.
- *Staying and hiding.* As 12.4's, with VS Code's grace period: while a sticky hover shows and the pointer goes to a place outside its range, the hover waits `editor.hover.hidingDelay` before it reacts (so the pointer can get into the box); then it hides and the new place starts its own wait. A pointer in the box keeps it (the box is a scrolled area with an overlay scrollbar, 500 pixels wide at most and as high as a quarter of the editor, 250 at least, then it scrolls with the wheel). The hover hides when the text or the selections change, on a press, when the editor scrolls (not a pinned one) and with Escape (`editor.action.hideHover`, weight +40, while `editorHoverVisible`; a pinned hover has `closeMarkersNavigation`, as before). **Deviation:** VS Code hides it on any key; here only the keys that change the text or the cursor do, and Escape. The hover of a command that has nothing to show (the providers answered nothing, no diagnostic) does not stay, so it does not hold the pointer back.
- *Focus.* Ctrl+K Ctrl+I while a hover shows gives its keys to the box (`ViewModel.FocusHover`, the keys `editorHoverFocused`, `editorHoverVisible`): the editor keeps the keyboard, the box gets the `focusBorder` and Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home and End scroll it (`editor.action.scrollUpHover`, `scrollDownHover`, `pageUpHover`, `pageDownHover`, `goToTopHover`, `goToBottomHover`; `scrollLeftHover` and `scrollRightHover` exist and do nothing, the box wraps its text). A focused hover does not hide with the pointer; a change of text or cursor hides it.
- *Markdown.* `extension/ui/markdown` has `Options.Hover`: the blocks one under the other at their natural height (no scroll, no page background), 13 pixel text on a 19 pixel line in `editorHoverWidget.foreground`, 8 pixels between blocks, a rule of 1 pixel, code blocks with no background of their own; the code is in the monospace font of the platform at 13 pixels (VS Code uses the editor's font and size) and **colored** with the grammar of the language the fence names (`SuggestHost.Tokenize`, the window's `extLanguages`: the same grammars and theme as the editor) and with the token colors of the theme. A plain-text content is drawn as text in the UI font. A link opens through the OpenURI portal (`SetOpeners`); the `command:` links of VS Code are not supported (no trusted Markdown).
- *Signature help: the model* (`signature.go`, VS Code's `ParameterHintsModel`). The trigger characters come from the providers (`Registry.SignatureCharacters`: a server's `triggerCharacters` and `retriggerCharacters`; a trigger character is a retrigger character too). A trigger waits 120 ms (a new trigger restarts the wait, and the triggers that waited are one request: the last typed character, an invoke wins over everything before it, a content change does not) and Ctrl+Shift+Space (`editor.action.triggerParameterHints`) asks at once. **Typing** a trigger character asks (`editor.parameterHints.enabled`; the command works with it off), a retrigger character asks only while the hints show, are being asked for, or a trigger waits. **While the hints are on** any change of the text or of the cursor made by a command or typing asks again (kind content change), and the request carries `isRetrigger` and the hints that showed (`SignatureContext.Active`; for a server `activeSignatureHelp` is its own answer with the signature the user moved to as the active one; hints of another provider are not sent to it). A request that is pending when the next is made is cancelled, its answer is dropped, and an answer for a document that changed with no trigger after the change (nothing asks again) closes the hints and ends the wait (before, the model stayed waiting and the hints stayed as they were; step 17b.3). The hints **close** with Escape (`closeParameterHints`), when the editor loses the focus, on a press with the mouse, when the setting is turned off, and when a request has no signature. The providers are asked together and the first of them, in the order of the providers, that has signatures answers (VS Code asks one after the other). The active signature outside the signatures is the first; the active parameter is the signature's own, else the help's. Up and Down (and Alt+Up and Alt+Down) go through the signatures while there are several (`showPrevParameterHint`, `showNextParameterHint`, keys `parameterHintsVisible` and `parameterHintsMultipleSignatures`); on the last (first) signature they go to the first (last) with `editor.parameterHints.cycle` (true), else the hints close. The key `editorHasSignatureHelpProvider` is the precondition of the command.
- *Signature help: the widget* (`signature_widget.go`). It stands above the cursor, below it when the estimated height does not fit above, at most 440 pixels wide, at most a quarter of the editor high (250 pixels at least) and then scrolls. The label of the signature is in the editor's font and size, with the active parameter bold in `editorHoverWidget.highlightForeground` (VS Code's color, a new color of Emetos's registry: `list.highlightForeground`); a parameter is found by the offsets the provider gave (counted in UTF-16 units by the protocol, kept as bytes: `Parameter.Offsets`), else by the first place its text stands as a word of its own (`Signature.LabelRange`, VS Code's regular expression). Under it, after a line, the documentation of the active parameter and of the signature (Markdown as the hover's, in the UI font; VS Code uses the editor's font size). With several signatures a column at the left has the two arrows (they are clickable) and the counter, zero-padded to the width of the count ("1/3", "02/12"), at the bottom, and a line (half seen) separates it from the body, which is 3.3 lines high at least. The widget is under the suggest widget and the hover in the stack, and works with them as in VS Code: both can show; Escape closes the suggest widget first (weight +90 against +75) and Up and Down move in the suggest list while it has several rows.
- *Registered* (rule 7). Settings: `editor.parameterHints.enabled` (true), `editor.parameterHints.cycle` (true; the VS Code defaults). Color: `editorHoverWidget.highlightForeground`. Commands and keys: `editor.action.showHover` (Ctrl+K Ctrl+I), `editor.action.hideHover` (Escape), the eight scroll commands (the arrows, the page keys, Home and End while `editorHoverFocused`), `editor.action.triggerParameterHints` (Ctrl+Shift+Space), `closeParameterHints` (Escape, Shift+Escape), `showPrevParameterHint` (Up, Alt+Up), `showNextParameterHint` (Down, Alt+Down); context keys `editorHoverVisible`, `editorHoverFocused`, `parameterHintsVisible`, `parameterHintsMultipleSignatures`, `editorHasSignatureHelpProvider`; the dev command `dev.triggerParameterHints` (`dev.showHover` asks the providers now, so it shows when they answer, §15.2).
- *Not built.* The verbosity commands (`increaseHoverVerbosityLevel`, `decreaseHoverVerbosityLevel`), Show Definition Preview Hover, the hover in the glyph margin, the copy button, `editor.hover.showLongLineWarning`, the resize of the box and of the parameter hints, `command:` links, the colors and the inline code actions of the hover (12.8), the 100 ms fade-in of the parameter hints, `editor.hover.enabled: onKeyboardModifier`'s modifier (it acts as `on`), hiding the hover on any key, focusing the parameter hints, and `isValid` of VS Code's `getHover.ts` (it drops an answer with no range; here the word is the range).
- *Tests.* `core/langfeatures` (`HoverEach` order, ordinals and cancel, `HasHover`, `SignatureCharacters`, `Signature.LabelRange` with offsets, text, word boundaries and non-ASCII, the offsets in bytes, and, on the fake server, the context of a signature help request with the trigger kind, `isRetrigger` and the `activeSignatureHelp` with the signature the user moved to and the offsets sent back as they came), `gui/editor/hover_providers_test.go` (the timing at H/2, H and 3H on the fake clock, "Loading...", stacking order with diagnostics and a late provider, the range of the provider, stale answers (a pointer that moved, a document that changed), cancel when the box hides, a failing provider, no request over white space, Show Hover, its focus, the scroll commands and Hide Hover, a hover with nothing to show, stickiness, the setting off, the pointer leaving early), `signature_test.go` (a port of the cases of `parameterHintsModel.test.ts`: the trigger character with its context and delay, several triggers one request, retrigger while active with the active help, retrigger characters only while on, content-change retriggers, close on an empty answer, on Escape, on blur and with the setting off, not retriggered after it closed, the command with the setting off, an outdated request cancelled and its answer dropped, a document that changed, the previous active help kept while pending, the first provider with signatures, overloads with and without cycle, the keys, the counter), `hover_markdown_widget_test.go` (goldens `hover_markdown_{dark,light}`, `parameter_hints_{dark,light}`, `parameter_hints_overloads_{dark,light}`, the focused box scrolling, a link, the arrows and the counter, the placement above or below), `gui/app/keys_hover_test.go` (the states that the default-keybindings test needs for the new keys) and, with `-tags emetos_gopls`, `TestGoplsAnswersHoverAndSignatureHelp`. No new error tag.

**As built (step 12.7, `core/langfeatures/{symbols,workspacesymbols}.go`, `core/settings/navigation.go`, `core/command/navigation.go`, `core/keybinding/navigation.go`, `gui/editor/{navigation,peek,peek_widget,link,symbols,symbolicons}.go`, `gui/views/outline`, `gui/app/{navhost,outline,symbolpick}.go`).** Where the text above leaves room:
- *Requests.* Every request goes through the editor (`ViewModel.GoTo(kind, GoConfig)`, `LinkPointerMoved`, the highlights and the symbols), runs on a goroutine with a context that ends with the window tab, and hands its answer back through the poster. A new request cancels the one in flight; an answer is dropped when the request was replaced or cancelled, when the document has another version than the request had, or (go to, highlights) when the cursor moved. The kinds are `GoDefinition`, `GoDeclaration`, `GoTypeDefinition`, `GoImplementation` and `GoReferences`; a provider offers a kind when `Registry.Has(doc, feature)` (a `ServerProvider` offers what the server's capabilities say; the `Features().OnChange` of the registry, fired when a server starts, crashes or stops, makes every editor ask for its symbols and highlights again and set its `editorHas*Provider` keys). One result is a jump; several open the peek view (`editor.gotoLocation.multiple*`: `peek`, also when empty, `gotoAndPeek` goes to the first and opens the peek view in the editor that shows it, `goto` goes to the first); the Peek commands always open the peek view; when the cursor is on the only result the alternative command runs (`editor.gotoLocation.alternative*Command`; a command that is not there does nothing, and one command never runs itself as its own alternative); no result shows the message "No definition found for 'word'" as a pinned hover. The locations are sorted by file then position (VS Code's `ReferencesModel`); the first result of the providers is the one a jump goes to. An editor of a peek view never opens another peek view (its navigations go to the editor of the window).
- *Jumps and history.* A location in the active file is a jump of the history (`ReasonJump`: the place left and the place reached are both entries, SPEC §10.3) and scrolls to the middle of the editor only when it is out of view; a location in another file opens it as a preview editor (`workbench.editor.enablePreview`) at the start of the range, in the group beside the active one for `revealDefinitionAside`, Ctrl+Alt+click on a link and the peek view's Ctrl+Enter. Opening a location from the peek view keeps the editor (not a preview). A location of a file that cannot be read is a warning notification. Choosing a symbol in the Outline, the breadcrumbs or the picker is a jump of the history too (`SuggestHost.JumpTo`).
- *Commands and keys.* `editor.action.{revealDefinition (F12), revealDefinitionAside (Ctrl+K F12), peekDefinition (Alt+F12, Ctrl+Shift+F10), revealDeclaration, peekDeclaration, goToTypeDefinition, peekTypeDefinition, goToImplementation (Ctrl+F12), peekImplementation (Ctrl+Shift+F12), goToReferences (Shift+F12), referenceSearch.trigger (Shift+Alt+F12)}` with `editorTextFocus && editorHas<Kind>Provider`; the peek view's `closeReferenceSearch` (Escape, Shift+Escape), `goToNextReference`/`goToPreviousReference` (F4, Shift+F4), `selectNextReference`/`selectPreviousReference` (Down, Up unless the suggest widget shows), `openReference` (Enter), `openReferenceToSide` (Ctrl+Enter) with `editorTextFocus && referenceSearchVisible` at a weight above the editor's own keys; `workbench.action.gotoSymbol` (Ctrl+Shift+O), `workbench.action.showAllSymbols` (Ctrl+T), `outline.focus`, `outline.collapse`, `outline.followCursor`. The Go menu has Go to Symbol in Workspace, Go to Symbol in Editor, Go to Definition, Declaration, Type Definition, Implementations and References (groups `3_global_nav`, `4_symbol_nav`); the context menu of the editor has the Go to rows (shown while the language has the provider) and a **Peek** submenu. The context keys of the editor: `referenceSearchVisible`, `editorHasDefinitionProvider`, `editorHasDeclarationProvider`, `editorHasTypeDefinitionProvider`, `editorHasImplementationProvider`, `editorHasReferenceProvider`, `isInEmbeddedEditor`; of the window: `outlineFocus`.
- *Link.* With Ctrl held (Alt with `editor.multiCursorModifier` `ctrlCmd`) over a word that has a definition the word is underlined in `editorLink.activeForeground` and the pointer is a hand; the request starts when the pointer rests on a word, is cancelled when it moves to another, and goes when the key is let go. Ctrl+click puts the cursor on the word and goes to the definition (the peek view with `editor.definitionLinkOpensInPeek`; beside with Ctrl+Alt+click). A press that is not on a word with a definition is an ordinary press.
- *The peek view.* An inline zone (§9.7 zones) under the line of the cursor, 18 rows high (fewer in a small editor), with a 2 pixel border in `peekView.border`, a title bar (the file name, its folder dimmed, "N references" or "1 reference", a close button), and below it, left to right, an embedded editor of the selected location (seven parts) and, when there are several locations, the list (three parts): a row per file (icon, name, count; the title bar and the rows write the folder relative to the folder of the window, with the home folder as `~`: `SuggestHost.DirLabel`) with the lines of its references under it (the text before, cut to its last 14 characters after an ellipsis so that the match stays on the row (a deviation: VS Code lets the row's ellipsis cut the end), the match in `peekViewResult.matchHighlightBackground`, the text after; read from the open document or from the file off the UI thread). The zone stops 14 pixels (the scrollbar) short of the right edge of the text area, as the zones of VS Code are as wide as the content; the other zones (§9.1) keep the whole width. The selected row is the reference nearest to the cursor (the file that shares the longest path prefix with the editor's, then the closest line and column). The embedded editor is a view model over the document of the location (the open document, shared, or the file read for it and let go of when the peek view moves on or closes; no tab, no history entries), with the language, tokens and token theme of any editor (the zone's theme keeps the window's token theme), with no minimap, folding controls or sticky scroll, editable, with its references marked in `peekViewEditor.matchHighlightBackground` and the cursor at the selected one, which is scrolled to the middle once the editor is laid out. Click a row to select it; double click, or Enter, opens it as a kept editor (the peek view closes); Ctrl+Enter beside. A press in the editor outside the zone closes the peek view; the embedded editor never takes the keyboard from the editor of the zone (its keys are the peek commands). Colors: `peekView.border`, `peekViewEditor.background`, `peekViewEditorGutter.background`, `peekViewResult.background`, `.selectionBackground`, `.selectionForeground`, `.lineForeground`, `.fileForeground`, `.matchHighlightBackground`, `peekViewTitle.background`, `peekViewTitleLabel.foreground`, `peekViewTitleDescription.foreground`, `peekViewEditor.matchHighlightBackground`.
- *Document highlights.* The word under the cursor is highlighted by the providers when one offers highlights (`FeatureDocumentHighlights`): read in `editor.wordHighlightBackground`, write in `editor.wordHighlightStrongBackground`, text in `editor.wordHighlightTextBackground` (and their borders), after `editor.occurrencesHighlightDelay`; with no provider, or when the providers answer nothing, the textual occurrences of the word are marked as before (§9.6). `editor.occurrencesHighlight` (`off`, `singleFile`, `multiFile`: multi-file acts as single file) decides. Stale answers are dropped.
- *Symbols.* `Registry.DocumentSymbols` is cached per URI and version by `langfeatures.SymbolCache` (one per window tab, memoized with the registry): requests for one version are single flight, a request for a newer version cancels the older (its callers get `context.Canceled`), an answer in which no provider had symbols and one failed is not kept, and at most 64 documents are kept. An editor asks 300 ms after the last change (and at once when it gets its host or a server starts), so typing never waits; `ViewModel.Symbols()` gives the last answer (for `SymbolsVersion()`, possibly older than the text) and whether a provider answered at all. The Outline, the breadcrumbs, sticky scroll and the `@` picker all read it. `SymbolIcon(kind)` gives the Codicon and `symbolIcon.*Foreground` color of a kind.
- *Outline* (`gui/views/outline`; the Outline view of the Explorer, collapsed, below the folder). A `kit.Tree` of the symbols of the active text editor keyed by the path of names and kinds (a repeated name has a count), each row with the icon of its kind, the name, the detail dimmed, and struck through when deprecated; it follows the cursor (the symbol that holds it, innermost first, its folders opened and the row scrolled into view; `outline.followCursor` toggles) and a click or Enter goes to the name of the symbol. `outline.showXxx` (26 settings, one for each kind) hide a kind and promote its children, `outline.icons`, `outline.collapseItems` (`alwaysExpand` default, `alwaysCollapse`), and `outline.focus`/`outline.collapse`. An editor with no provider (or a tab that is not a text editor) shows "The active editor cannot provide outline information." Not built: `outline.problems.*`, the filter box, the sort and the group-by buttons of the view.
- *Breadcrumbs and sticky scroll from symbols.* The breadcrumbs (§9.7) show the symbols that hold the cursor after the file (`breadcrumbs.symbolPath`: `on`, `last`, `off`; `breadcrumbs.showXxx`), each with its icon; clicking one opens a picker of the symbols of its level (`breadcrumbs.symbolSortOrder`: `position`, `name`, `type`) and choosing one goes to it. Sticky scroll (§9.6) takes its scopes from the symbols (a symbol sticks from the line of its name to the end of its range) when `editor.stickyScroll.defaultModel` is `outlineModel` (the default) and a provider answered symbols; with `foldingProviderModel`, `indentationModel`, or no symbols it uses the folding regions as before (the indentation model is the folding regions here).
- *The pickers.* `@` (Ctrl+Shift+O) lists the symbols of the active editor with their icons in document order (`Description` is the container, "Outer.inner"), filtered by `MatchesFuzzy` on the name and ordered by score once there is a filter; a filter that starts with `:` (`@:`) groups them by kind under headings "functions (2)"; the list is made again when the symbols arrive after it opened. Enter goes to the name of the symbol as a jump. Without a provider the list says "The active text editor does not provide symbol information." `#` (Ctrl+T) asks `workspace/symbol` (all servers, merged) 200 ms after the last key, cancelling the earlier request, and lists the symbols with the container, the path relative to the folder, ordered by fuzzy score of the name; Enter opens the location (a symbol the server left unresolved is resolved first with `workspaceSymbol/resolve`, off the UI thread), Ctrl+Enter beside.
- *Settings* (rule 7). **As built (step 12.8, `core/langfeatures/{codeaction,format,edit,merge,registry,server,types,convert,workspacesymbols}.go`, `core/settings/codeactions.go`, `core/command/codeactions.go`, `core/keybinding/codeactions.go`, `core/theme/colors_builtin.go`, `gui/editor/{codeaction,codeaction_widget,format,rename,rename_widget,refactor_preview,saveparticipants}.go`, `gui/app/{saveformat,suggest,lsphost,save}.go`).**
- *Code actions (the model).* `Registry.GetCodeActions(ctx, doc, req, trigger)` is VS Code's `getCodeActions`: the trigger has a type (invoked or automatic), a source (the light bulb, Quick Fix, Refactor, Source Action, on save, ...), a filter (`Include` kind, `Excludes`, `IncludeSourceActions`, `OnlyPreferred`) and an auto-apply mode (`never`, `ifSingle`, `first`). Kinds are `HierarchicalKind`s (`Contains`, `Intersects`); a provider that declares its kinds (`CodeActionKinds`) is not asked for a request none of them can match, and the request carries the filter's kind as `only`. `NewCodeActionSet` sorts as `ManagedCodeActionSet` does (the actions that fix a diagnostic first, preferred first, and the disabled ones apart). The server's action keeps the action as the server sent it, so that `codeAction/resolve` sends it back whole and only the `edit` is taken from the answer (`CodeActionResolver`).
- *Code actions (the editor).* The light bulb asks 250 ms after the cursor rests or the diagnostics change (VS Code's `CodeActionOracle` delay), for the line of the cursor with the diagnostics that touch it (the marker's `Data` is the server's diagnostic as JSON, sent back with the range refreshed), and shows only when the editor has the focus and `editor.lightbulb.enabled` says so (`onCode`: the cursor is not in white space of an empty line or the margin of a line; `on`; `off`). It is the light bulb icon (`editorLightBulb.foreground`) or the auto-fix one (`editorLightBulbAutoFix.foreground`, when a preferred quick fix exists); it sits in the glyph margin, or in front of the text when the line's indentation is wider than the icon, and clicking it opens the list. The list (Ctrl+. is Quick Fix; Ctrl+Shift+R Refactor; Shift+Alt+O Organize Imports; Shift+Alt+. Auto Fix; `editor.action.codeAction` and `editor.action.sourceAction` take the arguments of VS Code) is a popup under the line (above when there is no room) with the headers of the groups (`editor.codeActionWidget.showHeaders`), the preferred action first, a disabled action greyed with its reason (a link "Show Disabled" for Refactor and Source Action), the keys of Organize Imports and Fix All, and a bar. Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown move over the enabled rows, Enter and Ctrl+. apply, Ctrl+Enter previews the edit, Escape closes. Quick Fix with no fix at the cursor asks again at the end of the nearest diagnostic of the line (`editor.codeActionWidget.includeNearbyQuickFixes`). Applying an action resolves it when it has no edit, applies the edit (through the window, below), then runs the command. A request whose answer arrives after the cursor moved to another line or the text changed is dropped, and a newer request replaces an older one. The hover of a diagnostic has "Quick Fix..." (status "Checking for quick fixes..." after 200 ms, "No quick fixes available").
- *Workspace edits.* The window applies an edit with `langfeatures.Apply` (12.3), through `workspaceEdits`, whose `BeginEdit` (`EditTracker`) makes every editor keep its cursors in the text while documents change. `ApplyOptions{JoinUndo}` makes the edits join the undo group that is open instead of closing their own. A closed file is opened as an unsaved document, the text edits of a document are all or nothing, and `workspace/applyEdit` of a server answers `ApplyWorkspaceEditResult` with the failure reason and the index of the failed change. `ExpandEdit` turns an edit as the server sent it into the window's own form, with the text of each document, for the preview.
- *Formatting.* `FormatDocument` and `FormatSelection` (an empty selection formats its line; several selections are merged and formatted together) ask the formatter that `PickFormatter` chooses: `editor.defaultFormatter` when it is the owner of one, else the first (VS Code asks; Emetos has no picker yet). A formatter that only formats ranges serves Format Document with the range of the whole text. The edits are reduced by `MinimalEdits` (VS Code's `computeMoreMinimalEdits`: the common prefix and suffix, and a replacement of lines by lines by the line diff) so that the cursors, the folding and the undo stack are disturbed no more than the change needs, and are made as one undo step with the cursors following. On type (`editor.formatOnType`) asks `textDocument/onTypeFormatting` for the server's trigger characters and is cancelled when a change ends on a line at or above the cursor's; on paste (`editor.formatOnPaste`) formats the pasted range. An answer for a text that changed is dropped. The commands are `editor.action.formatDocument`, `formatSelection` and `format` (the keys of VS Code: Ctrl+Shift+I, Ctrl+K Ctrl+F).
- *Save participants.* Before `document.BeginSave` (whose participants are synchronous), the window runs those that need a server: first the trim of trailing white space, then each kind of `editor.codeActionsOnSave` (one request per kind, with the text the one before left; `source.fixAll` first, a kind that another contains left out, the `never` kinds as excludes; the first valid action of a kind is resolved and applied, edit then command), then `editor.formatOnSave`, then the final-newline settings. Every edit joins one undo step, so one Ctrl+Z undoes the whole save's changes. Each of the two language participants has its own timeout (`editor.codeActionsOnSaveTimeout`, `editor.formatOnSaveTimeout`, 750 ms; the code actions share one deadline); on a timeout the request is cancelled, a silent notification says "Aborted format on save after 750ms" and the save goes on; a failure is logged and the save goes on; a document that changed while a server worked drops that answer and the steps after it. An auto save (`files.autoSave: afterDelay`) skips both; a save for a change of focus or window runs the actions marked `always` and the formatter; the older array form of `codeActionsOnSave` runs on explicit saves only. Save without Formatting skips all of it. A save with neither participant does no extra work and takes no extra turn of the UI thread.
- *Format on save mode.* `file` formats the whole document. `modifications` formats the lines that differ from the file on disk (Emetos has no source control: the file is the baseline, read off the UI thread and compared by the line diff of `core/diff`), one range request per changed block, the edits merged without overlaps; with no file on disk or no formatter that formats ranges it formats nothing. `modificationsIfAvailable` does the same and formats the whole file when there is nothing to compare with.
- *Rename.* F2 asks `prepareRename` off the UI thread; a refusal is shown as a message at the cursor ("The element can't be renamed." for the tag `NotRenameable`, else the provider's reason); with no answer the word at the cursor is used ("No result." with no word). The input box is over the symbol, with the name selected and the line "Enter to Rename, Ctrl+Enter to Preview" under it (the preview is offered when `editor.rename.enablePreview` is on); it closes when the cursor moves or the text changes. Enter (`acceptRenameInput`) asks `textDocument/rename` and applies the edit, an empty or unchanged name asks nothing; Ctrl+Enter (`acceptRenameInputWithPreview`) shows the preview first. The answer is dropped when the text changed meanwhile.
- *The refactor preview.* A panel over the lower part of the editor (VS Code's bottom-panel view is not built) with the title ("Renaming 'a' to 'b'"), Apply and Discard, and a list of the files and, under each, the changes with the line, the text around, the old text struck through and the new one in bold; a check box per file and per change (a file whose changes are partly checked says "partly"); Space or Enter toggles the focused row, Up and Down move, Ctrl+Enter applies the checked changes (all or nothing per document), Escape discards. File operations (create, rename, delete) are rows with their own check boxes. Code actions with Ctrl+Enter use the same panel.
- *Commands and keys* (VS Code's ids and Linux keys): `editor.action.quickFix` (Ctrl+.), `editor.action.codeAction`, `editor.action.refactor` (Ctrl+Shift+R), `editor.action.sourceAction`, `editor.action.organizeImports` (Shift+Alt+O), `editor.action.fixAll`, `editor.action.autoFix` (Shift+Alt+.), the widget's `hideCodeActionWidget`, `selectPrevCodeAction`, `selectNextCodeAction`, `acceptSelectedCodeAction`, `previewSelectedCodeAction`, `editor.action.formatDocument` (Ctrl+Shift+I), `editor.action.formatSelection` (Ctrl+K Ctrl+F), `editor.action.format`, `editor.action.rename` (F2), `acceptRenameInput`, `acceptRenameInputWithPreview`, `cancelRenameInput`, and `refactorPreview.apply`, `discard`, `toggleCheckedState`, `focusNext`, `focusPrevious` (the last two are Emetos's own). The editor context menu has Rename Symbol, Format Document, Format Selection (with a selection), Refactor... and Source Action... (when a provider offers the kind), each shown only when its provider exists. The keys of the widgets are context keys of the editor: `codeActionMenuVisible`, `renameInputVisible`, `refactorPreview.visible`, `editorHasCodeActionsProvider`, `supportedCodeAction` (the kinds, matched by a regular expression), `editorHasDocumentFormattingProvider`, `editorHasDocumentSelectionFormattingProvider`, `editorHasRenameProvider`.
- *Settings* (rule 7). Registered: `editor.lightbulb.enabled`, `editor.codeActionWidget.showHeaders`, `editor.codeActionWidget.includeNearbyQuickFixes`, `editor.codeActions.triggerOnFocusChange` (read, no effect), `editor.codeActionsOnSave`, `editor.codeActionsOnSaveTimeout`, `editor.formatOnSave`, `editor.formatOnSaveMode`, `editor.formatOnSaveTimeout`, `editor.formatOnType`, `editor.formatOnPaste`, `editor.defaultFormatter`, `editor.rename.enablePreview`. Colors: `editorLightBulb.foreground`, `editorLightBulbAutoFix.foreground`, `editorLightBulbAi.foreground`. No new error tags: `ExpandEdit` fails with `WorkspaceEditDocumentUnavailable` (12.3) when the text of a document the preview needs cannot be read.
- *Decisions.* (1) The key of the preview is Ctrl+Enter, as VS Code's, not Shift+Enter. (2) The formatter chosen with no `editor.defaultFormatter` is the first, without asking. (3) "Modifications" compare with the file on disk, not source control. (4) The two save timeouts are VS Code's per-participant settings, not the newer single one. (5) The trim of trailing white space goes first, and the final-newline settings after the formatter, as VS Code orders them; with a language participant on, all of them join one undo step. (6) The first valid action of each kind of `codeActionsOnSave` is applied, not all. (7) The preview is an overlay panel, and a partly checked file shows no indeterminate box (the text says "partly"). (8) The diagnostics sent with a request are those that touch the range; `codeActionsOnSave` sends none. (9) The light bulb is in the glyph margin or in front of the text; VS Code's placing on the line above or below is not ported. (10) The row of the list that is focused does not highlight the range of its diagnostic.
- *Not built.* Format Document With... and the formatter picker, "Configure Default Formatter", rename suggestions (`provideNewSymbolNames`) and the rename box's candidate list, the diff view in the preview and its grouping by category, `editor.codeActions.triggerOnFocusChange`, the registration at run time of the trigger characters of on-type formatting, code actions on a selection with several cursors, the AI light bulb, "Change All Occurrences" (linked editing is step 12.9's), notebook code actions on save.
- *Tests.* `core/langfeatures/codeaction_test.go` (kinds, the filter, the order of the set, the filtering and failure of providers, resolve, `MinimalEdits`, `ModifiedRanges`, on-type formatting through the server, a range formatter standing in for a document formatter, `ExpandEdit` and `FilterEdit`), `gui/editor/codeaction_test.go` (the light bulb for a diagnostic and the list, applying with a multi-file edit and a command, resolve, no actions, stale and superseded answers, the light bulb settings, each formatting mode as one undo step, format on type and its cancel rule, rename refused by `prepareRename`, applied across files, previewed and partly accepted, discarded), `gui/editor/codeaction_widget_test.go` (goldens `code_actions_{dark,light}`, `light_bulb_dark`, `rename_box_{dark,light}`, `refactor_preview_{dark,light}`), `gui/app/saveformat_test.go` (organize imports before formatting as one undo step, both timeouts, auto save, the forms of the setting, Save without Formatting, no server asked without participants, an answer for changed text dropped, the modifications mode, and the window applying an edit to open and closed files with the cursor following), and `gui/exthost/gopls_test.go` (`emetos_gopls`: a quick fix resolved and applied, organize imports, formatting and a rename across three files with the real `gopls`).

**As built (step 12.9, `core/langfeatures/{lens,ranges,semantic}.go`, `core/folding/{syntax,provider,regions}.go`, `core/theme/semantic.go`, `core/settings/lens.go`, `core/theme/colors_builtin.go`, `gui/editor/{codelens,inlay,inlay_interact,semantic,selectionranges,lensoptions,geometry,folding,render,highlight,hover,pointer}.go`, `gui/app/{navhost,editors,suggest}.go`, `gui/exthost/servers.go`).**
- *Providers.* The registry has a list for each of `CodeLensProvider` (+ `CodeLensResolver`), `InlayHintProvider` (+ `InlayHintResolver`), `SemanticTokensProvider` (+ `SemanticRangeProvider`), `FoldingRangeProvider` and `SelectionRangeProvider`; `ServerProvider` implements them for a language server (`Offers` and `Registry.Has` know the features `FeatureCodeLens`, `FeatureInlayHints`, `FeatureSemanticTokens`, `FeatureFoldingRanges`, `FeatureSelectionRanges`; the semantic tokens are offered by the capability or by dynamic registration). `workspace/{semanticTokens,codeLens,inlayHint}/refresh` become `Registry.Refreshed(feature)`; the editors ask again at once (and the semantic cache forgets its freshness, keeping the data for the next delta).
- *Code lenses.* The editor asks `textDocument/codeLens` after `editor.codeLens` is on and the document is open or changed (a debounce of 250 ms to 2.5 s, the average of the last answers' times as VS Code's `FeatureDebounce`; stale answers, by generation and document version, are dropped). A lens is a row of its own above its line (a view zone of one line; the zones follow the edits), indented as the line, in the font of `editor.codeLensFontFamily` at `editor.codeLensFontSize` (0: 90% of the editor's), the titles of the lenses of the line joined with ` | ` in `editorCodeLens.foreground`. A lens without a command is resolved (`codeLens/resolve`) when its row is in the viewport, at most once. A click on a title runs its command (`SuggestHost.Execute`; a failure is logged and shown). Lenses whose range starts on the same line share the row; none in an embedded editor or in a document in large file mode.
- *Inlay hints.* Asked for the viewport and 30 lines around it after `editor.inlayHints.enabled` is not `off` (debounce 25 ms to 2.5 s; the hints of the lines that did not change are kept, the others replaced, a stale answer dropped). A hint is a decoration (owner slot 12) that follows the edits, and it is injected into the text of its row when the row is laid out: the document, the cursors, the clipboard, the search and the undo never see it. `geometry` maps between the columns of the document and the offsets of the laid-out row (`injectedRow.viewOffset`/`modelOffset`), so that `x`, `positionAt`, the selection rectangles and the cursor are correct with hints, and an arrow key moves over the characters of the document (a cursor never rests inside a hint; a click on a hint puts the cursor at the place the hint is before, `injectedRow.modelOffset`). Layout as VS Code's: the label in `editor.inlayHints.fontSize` (0 or outside 5..editor size: 90% of the editor's) and `fontFamily`, margins of 4 px (a rounded background in `editorInlayHint.background`, the kind's `typeBackground`/`parameterBackground`), `editor.inlayHints.padding` adds a space on each side, a label longer than `editor.inlayHints.maximumLength` (43; 0 for no limit) is cut with an ellipsis, a hint asks for padding with `paddingLeft`/`paddingRight`. Hover on a hint shows its tooltip and the places/commands of its label parts (hover model, the part under the pointer; `inlayHint/resolve` when the hint can be resolved); The link modifier (Ctrl) held on a click on a part with a location opens it (`OpenLocation` with the side of the modifiers), and on a part with a command runs it; the hint is resolved first when it can be and has neither. Modes: `on`, `off`, `onUnlessPressed` (hidden while Ctrl+Alt is down) and `offUnlessPressed` (shown while Ctrl+Alt is down), by the modifier keys of the editor (`InlayModifiersChanged`).
- *Semantic tokens.* `SemanticTokensCache` (one per window, `gui/app/navhost.go`) holds per document the last result and its `resultId`: `Get` asks `textDocument/semanticTokens/full/delta` with the previous id when the server has deltas (the edits are applied to the previous data by `ApplySemanticEdits`, which validates them: tag `SemanticTokensEditInvalid`; a delta answer to a request that was not a delta is the tag `SemanticTokensDeltaUnexpected`), else `full`; a request waits for the one before it. `DecodeSemanticTokens` turns the relative 5-number data into `SemanticToken{Line, Col, Len, Type, Modifiers}` with the columns in UTF-16 units of the document (a server that negotiated UTF-8 or UTF-32 is converted), dropping tokens that are outside the text. The editor asks 300 ms (up to 2 s, the average) after a change, and the first time for a document the range request (`textDocument/semanticTokens/range`, the viewport) goes out beside the full one when the server has it, so the first paint does not wait for the whole document; the full answer replaces it. Until the next answer the tokens follow the edits (`moveTokens`: a change inside a token drops it, one before it moves it, a line break moves the rest of the lines); the cost of a key is a pass over the token slice, measured in `BenchmarkSemanticTokensEditCost` with 100,000 tokens on 20,000 lines at about 0.26 ms for a letter and 0.6 ms for a line break near the top (`go test ./internal/gui/editor -run X -bench SemanticTokensEditCost`; the test `TestTheCostOfAKeyIsBounded` fails over 8 ms). Styling is VS Code's: `theme.SemanticTheme` selects the rule of a token from `semanticTokenColors` of the theme (selectors `type`, `type.modifier`, `*.modifier`, `type:language`; the best score wins, `parseTokenSelector` ported), the rules of `editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations` (`rules`, which win) and, when the theme has no rule, the default rules that map the token types onto TextMate scopes (`namespace` is `entity.name.namespace`, `function` `entity.name.function`, `variable` `variable.other.readwrite`, `parameter` `variable.parameter`, ...: the color is what the theme's TextMate rules give those scopes, as VS Code's `semanticTokenStyling` fallback to `tokenColors`). A style sets a foreground and any of bold, italic, underline and strikethrough (the flags merge: a rule that sets one leaves the others); the result is drawn over the TextMate spans of the row (`mergeSemantic`: the foreground replaces, the font style adds, text no grammar span covers takes the editor's color). `editor.semanticHighlighting.enabled` `true` or `false` decides for every theme, `configuredByTheme` (the default) uses the theme's `semanticHighlighting` (on in Dark Modern and Light Modern); the "enabled" of `semanticTokenColorCustomizations` is used between them.
- *Folding ranges.* `FoldingProvider` (the `folding.Provider` of a document of the window, `gui/app/editors.go`) asks `textDocument/foldingRange` of the providers through the updater's `Tag`: the `langfeatures.Document` of the text being computed. When a provider answered with a list (even an empty one), `folding.Sanitize` (a port of `sanitizeRanges`) makes the regions: sorted by start, a range that starts on the line a previous one starts or ends on is dropped, a range that crosses another is dropped, at most `editor.foldingMaximumRegions` (the outermost levels are kept); the `kind`s (`comment`, `imports`, `region`) are kept; a `collapsedText` of a range is shown after the first line of the folded region in place of the ellipsis. When no provider answered, or `editor.foldingStrategy` is `indentation`, or the document is not in a language with a server, the indentation provider (4.20) is the fallback, so a server that stops leaves the editor folding by indentation. `editor.foldingImportsByDefault` folds the `imports` regions the first time a provider gives some (not again once the user unfolded them). The updater is asked again at once when the servers change (`RefreshFolding`).
- *Selection ranges.* Expand Selection (Shift+Alt+Right) first asks `textDocument/selectionRange` for the positions of all the cursors (2 s at most), then starts the expansion with the ranges of the server together with the editor's (word, brackets, strings, lines); the command returns at once, and the answer is dropped when the document changed or the cursors moved meanwhile. Shrink goes back through the steps. Without a provider, or when it fails or times out, the expansion is the editor's own, as before.
- *Gopls.* gopls gives semantic tokens and inlay hints only when told to, as the section `go.gopls` of the settings (§9.12 "The first server"): `"go.gopls": {"semanticTokens": true, "hints": {"parameterNames": true, "assignVariableTypes": true, "compositeLiteralFields": true, "constantValues": true, "rangeVariableTypes": true}}`. The code lenses `generate`, `tidy` and `upgrade_dependency` are on by default (the lens of a `//go:generate` line: "run go generate | run go generate ./..."). The fixture of the proof and the test with the real gopls (`-tags emetos_gopls`) use these settings.
- *Settings* (rule 7). Registered: `editor.codeLens`, `editor.codeLensFontFamily`, `editor.codeLensFontSize`, `editor.inlayHints.enabled`, `editor.inlayHints.fontSize`, `editor.inlayHints.fontFamily`, `editor.inlayHints.padding`, `editor.inlayHints.maximumLength`, `editor.semanticHighlighting.enabled`, `editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations` (the `rules` and `enabled` keys, with the per-theme blocks left out); `editor.foldingStrategy`, `editor.foldingImportsByDefault` and `editor.foldingMaximumRegions` (4.20) now also drive the server's ranges. Colors: `editorInlayHint.foreground`, `.background`, `.typeForeground`, `.typeBackground`, `.parameterForeground`, `.parameterBackground`; `editorCodeLens.foreground` (registered before). New error tags: `SemanticTokensEditInvalid`, `SemanticTokensDeltaUnexpected` (route tests in `core/langfeatures`).
- *Decisions.* (1) A code lens is a view zone row, not a decoration, so the line numbers skip it and the text below moves down, as in VS Code. (2) The hints are injected into the paragraph of the row, and the geometry of the row (x, hit testing, cursors, selections) goes through one map, so that the cost of a hint is in one place. (3) A cursor never rests inside a hint: arrow keys move over the characters of the document, and a click inside a hint goes to the place it is before. (4) The tokens move with the edits (not dropped) until the next answer, to keep the colors from flickering while typing, at the price of one pass over the tokens per edit (measured above). (5) The semantic cache is per window, not per editor, so two editors of one document share the request and the delta base. (6) The range request is made only while the editor holds no full answer. (7) A semantic style merges with the TextMate one flag by flag (VS Code's `TokenStyle` merge), so `fontStyle: italic` of a rule does not remove bold from the grammar. (8) Selection ranges are asked once when an expansion starts; Shrink does not ask again. (9) Folding ranges that cross or share a start line are dropped as VS Code does, even when the server sent them. (10) The fallback of the semantic types is the table of VS Code's `tokenClassificationRegistry` (type and modifier selectors, each with the TextMate scopes to probe in the theme), ported into `core/theme/semantic.go`.
- *Not built.* Semantic tokens for a theme-specific block of `editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations` (`"[Theme]": {...}`); the `semanticTokenScopes` mapping of extensions (the table is fixed); the double click on an inlay hint that applies its `textEdits`; inlay hints in the minimap; the registration of code lens, hint, semantic and folding providers by extensions written in Go (the extension API, not part of this step); `editor.linkedEditing` (not part of this step).
- *Tests.* `core/langfeatures/{lens,semantic}_test.go` (lens and hint conversion and resolve, ordering and failing providers, folding ranges of several providers and the null answer, selection range sets driving the expansion, decoding of the data in UTF-16, UTF-8 and with astral characters, the edits of a delta and the two tags with their routes, the cache for the same version, a refresh, a failed delta), `core/folding/syntax_test.go` (the sanitizing table: sorting, crossing, nesting, the limit, kinds, same-start ranges), `core/theme/semantic_test.go` (selector parsing, scoring, the default rules, the fallback to TextMate scopes, the flag merge), `core/settings/lens_test.go`, `gui/editor/{codelens,inlay,semantic,ranges129}_test.go` (the lens rows and their click, the re-ask after an edit, `editor.codeLens` off, hints that do not change the text, the cursor over them, the four modes with Ctrl+Alt, truncation and padding, hover and click on a hint, the follow of the tokens through a table of edits, the merge table, the request flow with stale answers dropped, the range request before the full one, the refresh, golden images of the semantic colors in Dark Modern and Light Modern, the server's folding regions and the fallback, the collapsed text, imports folded once, the refresh of folding, the expansion with the server's ranges, a failing server and a late answer for moved cursors); with the real gopls (`go test -tags emetos_gopls -run Gopls ./internal/gui/exthost/`): hints (`p:`, `factor:`, `label:`, `X:`, `Y:`, types), semantic tokens (`scale` is a function, `Point` a type, `fmt` a namespace, `limit` a variable), folding ranges, selection ranges and the lens of `//go:generate`. Existing tests changed: the settings search goldens `settings_font_dark.png` and `settings_font_light.png` of `gui/settingsui` (a search for "font" now finds the four new settings of the code lens and the inlay hints: 11 instead of 7), `TestOptionsFromSettingsDefaults` (the new options), and the span literals of `brackets_test.go`, `highlight_test.go` and `hittest_test.go` (spans have a size, a family and a line height for the hints). The semantic theme is set while the widgets are built, so the listeners of the view model hear of it after the frame (the framework refuses a `SetState` during a build). Proof: `docs/implemented-proof-images/12.9-hints-tokens-lens.png`.

**The first server.** `extensions/golang` declares `gopls` (`go.goplsPath` else `PATH`; the `gopls` settings under `go.gopls`) so that the steps of this area are proved on Go; the rest of the Go extension is §10.17 (M14). As built (step 12.3): the declaration is `LanguageServerSpec{ID: "gopls", Languages: go, go.mod, go.work, Program: "gopls", PathSetting: "go.goplsPath", ConfigurationSection: "go.gopls"}`, and `go.goplsPath` is registered by the host from the spec (a string setting, empty by default). `go.gopls` is served from the settings whether or not a setting is registered under it; step 14.1 registers the `gopls` settings under it.

**Tests.** A fake language server (`internal/core/lsp/lsptest`: a Go program built by the tests that answers from scripted JSON, records the traffic and can crash or stall on command) drives every feature's tests; tests against the real `gopls` carry the build tag `emetos_gopls` and are skipped when it is not installed. Every server-to-client request and every error path has a route test.

**Not built in area 3:** TCP/socket transports, notebooks' LSP, `textDocument/linkedEditingRange`, `textDocument/documentColor` (color decorators), `textDocument/documentLink` beyond plain URLs, call and type hierarchy views, the inline completions API (ghost text), multi-root workspaces' `workspaceFolders` beyond the one folder.

## 10. The workbench (`gui/workbench` and others)

### 10.1 Layout
