**As built (step 11.7: window tabs of extensions; `gui/app/exttab.go`, `gui/workbench/titlebar.go`, §10.15 "As built (step 11.7)").** The strip holds the tab of an extension (`TabExtension`; `WindowTab.KindID` is the id of its kind) beside the workspaces. `WindowTab.Workspace()` is never nil for it: the `Workspace` of the tab is the host of its services, with no folder and no documents, and `Workspace.ext` marks it. What each part of this section does with it: the **strip** shows its title and the icon of its kind, no dirty dot; the **`+` menu** is Workspace... and then an entry for each kind of window tab of the extensions that are turned on; the **tray** lists it by its title (the tooltip counts workspaces only); the **picker** (Switch Workspace Tab...) lists it with its icon and the name of its extension; the **keys** of 9b.5 and the context keys work from it; **close** asks nothing, and when it is the last tab a No Folder tab replaces it; **quit** asks nothing of it; a **launch** goes to the workspace tab used last (`Workspaces.launchTarget`), or to a new No Folder tab when only tabs of extensions are open; **`workspaceTabs`** has an entry `{id, kind, title, state}` for it (§10.15), written with the other tabs and restored in the same place (`window.restoreWindows` as for workspaces: `folders` leaves it out); the saved **window geometry** is written by the workspace tabs, so resizing while a tab of an extension is active is saved the next time a workspace tab is on screen.

**Not built:** several windows (D17); dragging a tab out into a window of its own; a tab for a multi-root workspace (Emetos has one folder per tab); pinning workspace tabs; colors of their own for workspace tabs (they reuse the editor tab and title bar colors); a folder's own icon on its tab; starting with the desktop session (autostart) and starting hidden.

### 10.15 Extensions (`extension/`, `extensions/`)

Emetos's extensions are **Go packages compiled into Emetos** (D18): one folder per extension under `extensions/`, and one list of their constructors in `extensions/all.go`. There are no plugins loaded at run time, no extension processes and no extension marketplace; adding an extension is adding its folder and a line to the list, and building Emetos again. VS Code extensions and a Node.js host stay a non-goal (§2).

**The contract** (package `extension/`, public, the only Emetos package an extension may import, §5.3):
- `type Factory func() Extension`; `extensions.All() []extension.Factory` (a function in `extensions/all.go` that returns a new slice of the constructors, in activation order; no `init()` registration, no global mutable state, so nobody can change the list).
- `type Extension interface { Manifest() Manifest; Activate(ctx context.Context, api API) error }`. `ctx` is cancelled when the extension is deactivated (its window tab closes, it is disabled, Emetos quits); everything the extension started must end with it.
- `Manifest`: `ID` (lowercase, dotted, unique: `emetos.markdown`, `sqltools`), `Name`, `Version`, `Description`, `ActivationEvents` (`onStartup`; `onLanguage:<id>`; `onFile:<glob>` for a file in the folder such as `go.mod`; `onCommand:<id>`; `onView:<id>`; `onWindowTab:<kind>`), the contributions it declares (below, so they show before activation: menu items, commands in the palette, the `+` menu entries, micro-tab icons, activity bar icons), the event topics it publishes and subscribes to, and the cross-tab topics it may ask for (§ "Event sharing").
- **One extension, many contribution points.** Through `API` an extension contributes any mix of:
  - *UI, always contained in the box the workbench gives it* (the widget gets that box's constraints and cannot paint outside it; it uses the `kit` widgets and the theme colors; focus and keys stay in the box while it has the focus; Escape and the global keys still work). The contributions, by what they belong to:

    | Contribution | Belongs to | Where |
    |---|---|---|
    | **Window tab** | the window | a tab kind in the window's tab strip beside the workspaces (§10.14): an office suite, a scratchpad |
    | **Side bar view** | a workspace | an activity bar icon with a view container and its views, with title actions (Docker containers, SQL tables, an agent's sessions) |
    | **Panel view** | a workspace | a tab of the bottom panel beside Problems and Output (a terminal, a task runner, a log stream), with title actions and a badge; it moves and maximizes with the panel |
    | **Editor tab** | a workspace | a tab kind in the editor area beside the file tabs, with no file: several can be open (an agent's sessions, a query console); it splits, moves between groups, pins, closes, and is restored when the extension saves its state as data; it may show a dirty or busy mark |
    | **Editor title action** | a workspace | a micro icon at the right end of every editor group's tab strip (an icon, a tooltip, a command, an optional `when` condition): agents' "New Session" icons always shown, "Open Preview to the Side" only for Markdown; icons that do not fit go into a `...` menu |
    | **File view** | a file | micro-tabs inside a file's editor tab, for the files the extension declares: Text always first, then the extension's views (a Markdown preview, a CSV grid) |
    | **Contributions to the built-in parts** | a workspace | Output channels (`api.Output().Channel(name)`), Problems markers (`api.Problems().Set(owner, uri, markers)`), status bar items, notifications |

    One extension may contribute any number of each (the Go pack writes its log to an Output channel and its diagnostics to Problems; an agent extension adds a side bar view of sessions, an editor tab kind for a session and an editor title action that opens a new session).
  - *Workbench*: commands (in the palette, menus and keys; extensions never call each other's commands), keybindings with `when` clauses on the extension's own context keys, menu items, settings (registered under the extension's ID prefix, or declared in `Manifest.Contributes.Settings` with a key of their own such as `go.gopls`, read per workspace like every setting), a list to choose from (`api.QuickPick().Show`, the quick input of the window; step 14.1) a line of text (`api.InputBox().Show`, the input box of the quick input; step 14.2), banners across the top of the window tab (`api.Banners().Show`, step 15.2) and a file from the file dialog of the desktop (`api.FileChooser().Open`, step 15.2; §10.18 "As built (step 15.2)").
  - *Language*: languages, grammars, language configurations, snippets, color themes and file icon themes, as VS Code `package.json` contributions in an `embed.FS` (`Manifest.Contributes.Languages`, which the host gives to `language.Registry.AddNamedExtension`, §8.1; snippets and themes are not read from extensions yet); language servers (`Manifest.Contributes.LanguageServers`, run by the host as part of the activation, §9.12 "As built (step 12.3)"; the extension follows and restarts them with `api.LanguageServers()`, step 14.1, and asks them for their commands and code actions, step 14.2; it edits documents with `api.Documents().Apply`, step 14.2); providers written in Go (`api.Languages().Register...Provider`: completion, hover, signature help, definition, references, symbols, highlights, code actions, formatting, rename; diagnostics through `api.Problems()`) for languages without a server, or to add to one (area 3).
  - *Tools* (later areas): tasks, formatters run as processes, debug adapters.
- **Language packs are extensions**: every bundled language of §8.1 is an extension under `extensions/` (`extensions/golang`: the grammar, the language configuration, and from area 3 `gopls`, the Go commands and tasks; `extensions/markdown`: the grammar and the preview file view; and so on). They are compiled in, so a new install has all of them; D13's list of bundled languages is the list of language packs in `extensions/all.go`. The core keeps the machinery (the TextMate engine, the language registry, the theme service, from area 3 the LSP client and the completion, hover and diagnostics UI) and no language of its own except plain text.

**Lifetime.** Every window tab (a workspace, or an extension tab, §10.14) is its own **scope**: an extension is activated once per scope that needs it (by its activation events) with an `API` bound to that scope, and deactivated when the scope closes. An extension's error from `Activate`, or a panic in any call into it (activation, a widget build, an event handler, a provider), is caught at the boundary: the extension is deactivated in that scope for the rest of the session, its boxes show "<Name> failed" with a Show Log action, a notification says so once, and the log gets the error with its route. A file view that fails falls back to the Text view; a window tab of a failed extension shows the failure in the tab. `extensions.disabled` (application scope, a list of extension IDs) turns extensions off; the page "Extensions" (command `workbench.extensions.action.showInstalledExtensions`; the activity bar entry comes with the side bar views of step 11.5) lists the compiled-in extensions with their manifests, their state (active in which tabs, disabled, failed) and Enable/Disable.

**Events: the only way extensions talk to each other.** `api.Events()`:
- `Publish(topic, value)`; `Subscribe(topic pattern, func(Event)) (cancel func())` with `*` patterns (`emetos.document.*`); `Request(ctx, topic, value, reply)` (step 11.2: it never blocks, the reply comes to a function) and `Handle(topic, func(ctx, Event) (any, error))` for actions of another extension (request and reply; `EventNoHandler` when nobody handles the topic, `EventTimeout` after the `ctx` deadline, default 10 s). Topics are dotted and owned: an extension publishes and handles only topics under its own ID (`markdown.preview.open`) and the topics it declared; Emetos owns `emetos.*`.
- An `Event` carries the topic, the publishing extension's ID, the source scope (the window tab: its kind, folder or extension), a monotonic sequence number and the value. Values are copied (they must be JSON-encodable: the bus encodes and decodes them), so no live object crosses: a document can only be edited through the API of its own scope.
- Delivery is asynchronous on the UI thread, in order per publisher and topic; fast streams (typing) are delivered once per frame with every change of that frame. A handler that takes longer than 50 ms is logged; long work goes to a goroutine with the `ctx` of the scope.
- **Emetos publishes core events** in every workspace scope: `emetos.document.opened`, `.changed` (the document, its version and the changes: ranges and text), `.saved`, `.closed`; `emetos.editor.activeChanged`, `emetos.editor.selectionChanged`; `emetos.workspace.opened`, `.closed`; `emetos.windowTab.activated`. An extension reads a document's full text with `api.Documents().Read(uri)`, which follows the same scope and sharing rules as the events of that document.

**Event sharing between window tabs.** Inside one scope every event reaches every subscriber, with no question. Across scopes an event goes **only along a link that the user allowed, in that direction**: a link `notes → office` (optionally limited to some topics, such as `emetos.document.*`) lets events published in the workspace `notes` reach the extensions of the tab `office`; nothing goes from `office` to `notes` unless the link `office → notes` exists too. A request crosses the same links, in the direction of the data: a request made in `office` for a handler in `notes` needs the link `notes → office` (the answer is `notes`' data reaching `office`), and the reply comes back along that link and no other (see "As built (step 11.3)").
- **Where the links are kept**: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/event-sharing.json` (`storage.Paths`, §10.10; the same for every profile): `{"version": 1, "links": [{"from": <scope>, "to": <scope>, "events": [patterns]}], "private": [<scope>]}`, where a scope is a workspace by its folder (absolute, cleaned) or an extension tab by `<extension id>:<tab id>`. It is written atomically with mode 0600 and only by Emetos's own permission UI; **no settings file can create or change a link** (settings files configure only the workspace they belong to, §11.1), and no extension can write it.
- **Asking**: when an extension subscribes to, or requests, a topic from another scope (`Subscribe(topic, extension.FromScopes(...))` or from all scopes), and the topic is among the cross-tab topics of its manifest, and no link covers it, Emetos asks once in the receiving tab: "Let events from **notes** reach **office**?" with the topics, and the buttons **Allow** (adds the link and writes the file), **This Session Only** (a link kept in memory and never written) and **Deny** (nothing is stored; the extension can ask again on its next activation). A topic outside the manifest's cross-tab topics is never asked about and never crosses.
- **The page "Extensions › Event Sharing"** (command `emetos.extensions.manageEventSharing`; a page of its own, not part of the settings editor) lists the links as `from → to` with their topics and a Remove button, the session links, and the private workspaces with a switch "Private: never send events to other tabs". Removing a link stops delivery at once (the check is at delivery) and tells the receiving extension with `emetos.sharing.revoked`.
- A **private** workspace sends no event and allows no `Read` to other scopes, whatever the links say.

**Rules kept by tests** (`internal/archtest`, §5.3): a package under `extensions/` imports only `extension/`, the standard library, its own subpackages and the allowed dependencies (CLAUDE.md); never `internal/...`, Glutter's internals or another extension. `extension/` is the only bridge: it holds the contract (a widget type for the UI contributions is Glutter's `widgets.Widget`; the theme and kit helpers come through `extension/ui`, which may import the editor's kit and nothing else, §5.3), and the editor implements it in `internal/gui/exthost` (the package that imports `extension/`; the editor never imports `extensions/`, only `cmd/emetos` lists them).

**As built (step 11.1).** What the first step of M11 decided where the text above leaves room:
- **Packages.** `extension/` is the contract alone (types and interfaces, `CheckManifest`, `SettingValue`; it imports nothing of Emetos). The host is `internal/gui/exthost`: `Host` (the manifests of the process, the scopes, the settings the extensions registered) and `Scope` (the extension host of one window tab). `internal/gui/extensionsui` is the page. `internal/gui/app` binds a scope to its workspace (`extensions.go`). `extensions.All()` is a function; it is empty and `extensions/internal/testext` is the extension that tests the contract and is never listed. `cmd/emetos` passes the list to `app.ProcessOptions.Extensions`.
- **The contract.** `Manifest{ID, Name, Version, Description, ActivationEvents, Contributes}`; `Contributes{Commands, Menus, Keybindings}` are the declared contributions: they are installed in a scope when the extension is enabled there, before it is activated (a command is in the palette, a menu item and a key are there), and a declared command is an `onCommand` event of its own. `API` has `Scope()` (kind, tab name, folder), `Log()`, `Post(fn)` (a goroutine hands work to the UI thread), `Commands()` (`Handle` the handler of a declared command, `Register` a command the manifest did not declare), `Keybindings().Add`, `Menus().Add` (the menu ids are the `extension.Menu...` constants), `Settings()` (`Register` under the extension's id and a dot, `Get`, `OnChange`; `extension.SettingValue[T]` converts), `Notifications()` (`Info`, `Warn`, `Error` with the name of the extension as source and buttons), `StatusBar().Add` (an item with a `Command` or an `OnClick` callback and a handle to `Update`, `SetVisible`, `Dispose`) and `Documents()` (`Read(ctx, uri)` of an open document, with its unsaved changes, or of a file of the folder; `Open()`). The API is for any goroutine except `Documents().Read`.
- **Activation events.** `onStartup`, `onLanguage:<id>` (a document of the language opens in the tab; the documents of the command line count), `onFile:<glob>` (a file of the folder matches the glob, written relative to the folder as the file index lists it, `go.mod` for the root and `**/go.mod` anywhere; checked at the start and whenever the file index changes), `onCommand:<id>`, `onView:<id>` and `onWindowTab:<kind>` (accepted and fired through `Scope.Fire`; the views of step 11.5 and the window tabs of step 11.7 fire theirs). An extension with no event is never activated by itself. An event that happened is remembered, so an extension that the user turns on later is activated for it.
- **One activation per scope.** The factory is called once to read the manifest and again for each activation, so two tabs never share an instance. The `ctx` of Activate is cancelled when the tab closes (`Workspace.release`), the extension is turned off or fails, or Emetos quits; then everything tracked in the activation (commands, keys, menu items, status items, settings, listeners) is removed, last first, and a call of the API that changes something fails with `ExtensionDeactivated`. The commands and the menus of a tab are its own forks (`Workspace.Commands`, `Workspace.Menus`), the keys of the extensions are a layer over the default keymap of the tab (they win over the built-in keys, and the user's `keybindings.json` over both), and the settings are registered once in the registry of the process (counted: the last scope that holds one removes it) with `ScopeWindow`.
- **Containment.** Every call into an extension is made by a function of `Scope` that catches the panic and the error: `ExtensionFactoryPanicked`/`ExtensionFactoryNil` (the factory), `ExtensionActivatePanicked`/`ExtensionActivateFailed`, `ExtensionCommandPanicked`, `ExtensionStatusCallbackPanicked`, `ExtensionNotificationActionPanicked`, `ExtensionSettingsCallbackPanicked`, `ExtensionPostedPanicked` (the host's own probe of a factory has `ExtensionProbePanicked`). The routes keep the frames of the extension's call, so a test asserts `Scope.runCommand.func1.ExtensionCommandPanicked`. A failure sets the state of the extension in that scope to *failed* (`Scope.Failure(id)`: the error, what was called, and the box text "<Name> failed"), takes everything it contributed away (the declared contributions too), logs the error with its route, and shows one notification (error, source the name, button Show Log, which runs `workbench.panel.output.focus`); the other tabs and the other extensions are untouched. An error that a command handler returns is the error of the command (`ExtensionCommandFailed`) and does not fail the extension; a command that panics returns nil, because the user was told once already. Turning the extension off and on again in the page tries again.
- **`extensions.disabled`** is an application setting, an array of extension ids, in the `settings.json` of the profile of the window; each tab follows it (`Scope.Refresh`). A disabled extension is installed nowhere: its commands are not in the palette, its menu items and keys are not there. The ids that name no extension are ignored.
- **The page "Extensions"** is an editor input (`emetos.extensions`, restored with the window) opened by the command `workbench.extensions.action.showInstalledExtensions` (Show Installed Extensions), from the View menu, the Preferences submenu, the Manage menu and Ctrl+Shift+X. It lists each extension with its name, version, description, id, activation events and state (`Active in <tabs>.`, `Not active yet.`, `Failed in <tab>: <Name> failed.`, `Disabled`), follows the host while it is open, and has Disable/Enable, which write `extensions.disabled`. There is no activity bar entry yet: the activity bar shows the view containers of the side bar, and an icon that opens a page needs the work of step 11.5.
- **Rules of `internal/archtest`** (§5.3): `ExtensionImportsInternal`, `ExtensionImportsExtension`, `ExtensionImportsForbidden` and `ExtensionsImportedByInternal`.

**As built (step 11.2).** The event bus of a scope, and the core events. Where the text above leaves room:
- **The API** (`extension/events.go`, `Events()` of the `API`). `Publish(topic, value) error`; `Subscribe(pattern, fn) (cancel, error)`; `Request(ctx, topic, value, reply func(Event, error)) error`; `Handle(topic, fn EventHandler) error` and `HandleAsync(topic, fn AsyncEventHandler) error`. **`Request` takes a reply function and returns at once** (the UI thread must never wait): `reply` is called once, on the UI thread, with the reply event or an error; it is not called when the requesting extension was deactivated; a request refused at once (a malformed topic, a value that is not JSON) returns the error and never calls `reply`. An extension that wants to wait does it in a goroutine with a channel. `Handle` answers at once (`func(ctx, Event) (any, error)`, run on the UI thread); `HandleAsync` gets a `reply(value, err)` function that any goroutine may call once, for long work (the Agents extension answers its requests that way). A scope has one handler per topic (`EventHandlerTaken`); the handlers go with the extension.
- **The event.** `Event{Topic, Publisher, Scope, Seq, Data json.RawMessage, Batch []json.RawMessage}`. `Publisher` is the extension's id, or `emetos` for the core events. `Seq` grows with every event and request of the scope. `Data` is the JSON of the value; every receiver gets bytes of its own (`Event.Decode`, `extension.EventValue[T]`, `extension.EventValues[T]` read them). The value is encoded when `Publish`, `Request` or the reply is called (`EventValueInvalid`, `EventReplyInvalid` for a value that is not JSON), so the sender may change its value at once.
- **Topics and patterns.** A topic is one or more segments of letters, digits, `-` and `_` joined by dots (`EventTopicInvalid`; case matters: `emetos.editor.activeChanged`). A pattern (`EventPatternInvalid`) has the same segments, where `*` stands for exactly one segment anywhere and a last segment `**` for one or more segments; `a.*` matches `a.x` and not `a` or `a.x.y`, `a.**` matches both of those, `**` matches every topic. Subscribing is free inside a scope (any extension may subscribe to any pattern); `Manifest.Events.Subscribes` lists the patterns for the reader and is checked for syntax only.
- **Ownership.** `Manifest.Events` is `EventDecl{Publishes []EventSpec{Topic, Fast}, Handles []string, Subscribes []string}`. An extension publishes the topics under `<its id>.` and the ones in `Publishes`, and handles the topics under `<its id>.` and the ones in `Handles`; anything else fails with `EventTopicNotOwned`. The host leaves out an extension that declares a topic under another extension's id, or under `emetos.` without being under its own id (`ExtensionTopicForeign`, listed in `Host.Problems`), and `extension.CheckManifest` refuses the ids that Emetos publishes under: `emetos`, `emetos.document`, `emetos.editor`, `emetos.workspace` and `emetos.sharing` (`ExtensionIDReserved`). The core events are published only through `Scope.PublishCore`, which the window calls (`CoreTopicUnknown` for any other topic).
- **Delivery.** `Publish` queues the event; a drain on the UI thread (the scope's `Post`) delivers every event that is not fast, in order, to every matching subscriber of the scope (the publisher's own included). A subscriber never runs inside another: an event published from a subscriber is delivered after the current pass. **Fast topics** are the core `emetos.document.changed` and `emetos.editor.selectionChanged` and the topics an extension lists with `Fast: true`: they wait for the end of the frame (`ScopeOptions.Frame`, the post-frame callback of the window) and are delivered as **one event per publisher and topic per frame**, with `Batch` holding every value of the frame, oldest first (`Data` and `Seq` are the last one's); a fast event always has a `Batch`, even of one. **Order:** per publisher and topic always; and an event is never delivered before an earlier one: when an event that is not fast comes due, the fast events published before it are delivered first, as their batches.
- **Requests.** The request is delivered to its handler on the UI thread, soon after the call. The wait ends with the first of: the reply; `EventTimeout` when the context of the request reaches its deadline, or after **10 seconds** (`DefaultRequestTimeout`, a timer of `ScopeOptions.After`, the window's timers, a fake clock in tests) when it has none; `EventCanceled` when the context is cancelled; `EventHandlerGone` when the handler's extension was deactivated; `EventNoHandler` when the scope has no handler for the topic. The `ctx` of the handler ends with the request, so a handler that works in a goroutine sees the timeout; a reply that comes later is dropped. An error the handler returns reaches the requester as `EventHandlerFailed` (the handler's error is its cause for `errors.Is`) and does not fail the extension.
- **The slow-handler log.** A subscriber, a handler or a reply function that takes longer than **50 ms** (`exthost.SlowHandler`, measured with `ScopeOptions.Now`) is logged as a warning with the extension, the topic and the time; it is not a failure.
- **Containment.** A panic in a subscriber fails the extension with `ExtensionEventSubscriberPanicked`, in a handler with `ExtensionEventHandlerPanicked` (the requester gets `EventHandlerPanicked`, and the extension that handles is off in that scope), in a reply function with `ExtensionRequestReplyPanicked`; each is handled like the failures of step 11.1 (one notification, the log with its route, the other extensions and scopes untouched). The requester-side errors are plain errors of the call, not failures.
- **The core events** (`emetos.*`, payloads are JSON objects; the Go types are in `extension/events.go`; positions are `{"line", "col"}`, zero-based, `col` in bytes of the UTF-8 line as the buffer counts, D6):

  | Topic | Payload | When |
  |---|---|---|
  | `emetos.workspace.opened` | `{kind, name, folder}` | once, when the scope starts (after the extensions that start with it were activated; delivered right after) |
  | `emetos.workspace.closed` | `{kind, name, folder}` | when the tab closes; delivered at once, before the extensions are deactivated, with everything still queued |
  | `emetos.windowTab.activated` | `{kind, name, folder}` | when the tab comes to the front (and at its start when it is there) |
  | `emetos.document.opened` | `{uri, languageId, version}` | a document is added to the workspace (the ones open when the scope starts too) |
  | `emetos.document.changed` (fast) | `{uri, version, cause, changes: [{range, text}]}` | the text changed; `cause` is `edit`, `undo`, `redo`, `lineEnding` or `setText`; the ranges of one event are in the text before it |
  | `emetos.document.saved` | `{uri, version, as, previousUri?}` | the document was written; `as` for a Save As, which gives the new `uri` and the old one as `previousUri` |
  | `emetos.document.closed` | `{uri}` | the document was closed |
  | `emetos.editor.activeChanged` | `{uri, languageId?}` | another text editor is in front, or none (`uri` is empty, also when the active tab shows no text); looked at on the UI thread's next turn, so opening several editors in a row says where it ended |
  | `emetos.editor.selectionChanged` (fast) | `{uri, selections: [{anchor, active}]}` | the selections of the active editor changed, and right after `activeChanged` for the new editor; not published while they are the ones last published |
  | `emetos.sharing.revoked` | `{from, fromName, topics?, reason}` | a link that let another tab's events reach this one was removed, or that tab became private (step 11.3); published in the receiving tab only |

  `api.Documents().Read` was built in step 11.1 and needs nothing more here; the sharing rules come with step 11.3.
- **Delivery to other scopes** was left to step 11.3 (`bus.deliver` checks the links, see "As built (step 11.3)").
- **Seams for tests.** `ScopeOptions.Frame`, `After` and `Now` (all nil in a bare scope: `Frame` is then `Post`, the others the standard library's), so the batching, the timeout and the slow log are tested with a queue and a fake clock.
- **Existing test changed.** `TestASettingOfAnotherExtensionIsTaken` used the extension id `emetos`, which is reserved now; it uses `ext` and `ext.api`. `TestPostRunsOnTheUIThreadUnlessTheExtensionIsGone` counts the functions it hands to the UI thread after the one `emetos.workspace.opened` that the start of the scope posts.

**As built (step 11.3).** Event sharing between window tabs (`internal/core/storage/sharing.go`, `internal/gui/exthost/sharing.go`, `internal/gui/app/eventsharingpane.go`, `internal/gui/extensionsui/sharingpage.go`). Where the text above leaves room:
- **The file** `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/event-sharing.json` (`Paths.EventSharingPath`, the same for every profile) is `{"version": 1, "links": [{"from": "<scope id>", "to": "<scope id>", "events": ["emetos.document.*"]}], "private": ["<scope id>"]}`, written indented, atomically, mode 0600, at once on every change made in the UI (`storage.SharingStore`), read once when the process starts. `events` empty or missing carries every topic the extensions ask for. Links with an empty end or from a scope to itself are dropped when read, and a link between two scopes already in the file is merged (patterns added). A file that cannot be used (not readable, not JSON, another version) is ignored: the store is empty, one warning is logged (`SharingFileUnreadable`, `SharingFileCorrupt`, `SharingVersionUnsupported`), and the next change writes a new file. A change that cannot be written (`SharingWriteFailed`) is not kept for **Allow** (the link is kept for the session instead and a warning notification says so) and is kept for this session for a removal or a private switch, so the user's "no" always works.
- **Scope ids.** `ScopeInfo.ID` (and `Event.Scope.ID`, `WorkspaceInfo.ID`) is the cleaned absolute folder of a workspace, and will be `<extension id>:<tab id>` for an extension tab (step 11.7). **A workspace tab with no folder has no id (empty)**: no link can name it, so it sends nothing to other tabs and hears nothing from them, and a request or a `Read` out of it fails (`EventSharingUnnamed`, `ExtensionReadUnnamed`). Open a folder to take part. A link names a folder, not a tab: it keeps working when the folder is reopened in another tab or after a restart, and a tab that opens another folder is another scope.
- **The API.** `Manifest.Events.CrossTab` is the list of topic patterns (`CheckPattern`) the extension may receive from, or ask of, other tabs. `Subscribe(pattern, fn, extension.FromOtherScopes())` or `FromScopes(ids...)` **adds** the other tabs to the own scope (events of the own scope are always delivered); `Request(ctx, topic, value, reply, extension.ToOtherScopes())` or `ToScopes(ids...)` looks for the handler **in those tabs only** (the own scope's handler of the same topic is not used; the first tab in the order the tabs were opened that has a handler, is not private and is linked wins); `Documents().Read(ctx, uri, extension.FromScope(id))`. A subscription pattern or a request topic must be **within** the cross-tab list (`extension.PatternWithin`: every topic it can match is matched by an entry), else the call fails with `EventCrossTabNotDeclared` (Subscribe), `EventRequestCrossTabNotDeclared` (Request) or `ExtensionReadNotDeclared` (a read needs `emetos.document.changed` within the list): the topic is never asked about and never crosses. A subscription without the option never hears another tab, whatever the links say.
- **Delivery.** The check is made at delivery, for every event, on the UI thread (`bus.deliver`): the event goes to the subscriptions of another scope that listen to the source (`FromOtherScopes`/`FromScopes`) when both scopes have an id, the source is not private and a link `source → target` (saved or session) carries the topic. So a link removed, or a tab made private, stops even the events that are queued. A fast event crosses as the same batch. The event carries the source in `Event.Scope` (name, folder, id). Where no link exists the event is **not delivered** (the first events are lost until the user answers).
- **Requests.** A request with `ToOtherScopes`/`ToScopes` needs a link from the handler's scope to the requester's, covering the topic, and goes by the rules of delivery; it waits for the answer to a question while one is on screen, and its timeout runs meanwhile. The reply goes back along the same link and is checked again when it arrives: a link removed meanwhile ends the request with `EventSharingRevoked`. Other errors in the reply: `EventSharingPrivate` (the requester is private: a request is something it sends), `EventSharingUnnamed`, `EventSharingSourcePrivate` (every tab that handles the topic is private), `EventSharingRefused` (no link and nothing can be asked: the receiving window cannot ask, or the user denied the extension before), `EventSharingDenied` (the user answered Deny), `EventNoHandler`.
- **Reading across tabs.** `Documents().Read(..., FromScope(id))` needs a link that lets the document events of that tab (`emetos.document.changed`) reach the reader, and the tab must not be private; nobody is asked (the call is synchronous, on the UI thread), a read without a link fails with `ExtensionReadNotShared` (`ExtensionReadPrivate`, `ExtensionScopeUnknown`, `ExtensionSourceDocumentsUnavailable`). The source tab's own rules (open documents, files of its folder only) apply. A read of the own scope needs nothing.
- **The question.** It is asked **lazily, at delivery**: when an event is published in tab A, tab B has a subscription that listens to A (or a request is made) whose pattern is within the cross-tab list, nobody denied it, A is not private and no link carries the whole pattern. It is shown in B's own dialog host (`Workspace.Dialogs`, §10.7), so it waits there while B is not the tab on screen; the window does not switch tabs. Title "Let events from <A> reach <B>?", the detail names the extension, the topics (the subscription patterns) and the two folders, and the buttons are **Allow** (default; saves the link `A → B` with those patterns, merged with an earlier link), **This Session Only** (an in-memory link) and **Deny** (also Escape and the close button). Only one question per pair of tabs is on screen at a time; what is asked about the same pair meanwhile waits and is asked again after the answer if the new link does not carry it; the same extension and pattern are asked once. **Deny stores nothing and is remembered until the extension is deactivated** (it is asked again at its next activation, and not again while it runs); **removing a link on the page counts as a Deny** for the extensions that listened to it, so that they do not ask again at the next event.
- **Private.** A private workspace sends no event, answers no request, allows no `Read` out, and starts no question (nobody is asked about a private tab), whatever the links say; it still receives along links. Its own requests to other tabs are refused too (a request carries the requester's value). Turning it on tells the tabs it had links to, as removing a link does.
- **`emetos.sharing.revoked`** is a core event published in the receiving tab (it is local: a subscription needs no option and no cross-tab entry) when a link is removed (`reason` `removed`) or its source becomes private (`private`): `{from, fromName, topics, reason}` (`extension.SharingRevoked`). Not published when the link was not there.
- **The page "Extensions › Event Sharing"** is an editor input (`emetos.extensions.eventSharing`, restored with the window), opened by the command `emetos.extensions.manageEventSharing` ("Manage Event Sharing", category Extensions; command palette only) and by the button "Event Sharing..." of the Extensions page. It lists the saved links, then the session ones ("until Emetos quits"), as `from → to` with the topics (or "every topic an extension asks for"), the two folders and a **Remove** button, and under "Window tabs" every open tab with an id and every private scope that is not open (listed by its id), each with the switch "Private: never send events to other tabs". It follows the host, so a link made by an answer shows at once.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `SharingFileUnreadable`, `SharingFileCorrupt`, `SharingVersionUnsupported`, `SharingWriteFailed`, `SharingEncodeFailed`, `EventCrossTabNotDeclared`, `EventRequestCrossTabNotDeclared`, `EventSharingUnnamed`, `EventSharingPrivate`, `EventSharingSourcePrivate`, `EventSharingRefused`, `EventSharingDenied`, `EventSharingRevoked`, `ExtensionReadNotDeclared`, `ExtensionReadUnnamed`, `ExtensionScopeUnknown`, `ExtensionReadPrivate`, `ExtensionReadNotShared`, `ExtensionSourceDocumentsUnavailable`.
- **Existing tests and goldens changed.** `internal/gui/exthost/rig_test.go` gave each test tab an id and a seam for the question (`newRigStore`, `tab.asked`); the goldens `extensions_page_dark` and `extensions_page_light` gained the button "Event Sharing...". No test was weakened.

**As built (step 11.4).** The language packs (`extensions/<pack>/`, `extensions/internal/langpack`, `internal/gui/exthost/languages.go`, `internal/core/language`). Where the text above leaves room:
- **The packs.** 22 extensions with the ids `emetos.<pack>`: `golang` (Go), `json` (JSON, JSON with Comments, JSON Lines, Code Snippets), `yaml` (YAML, Compose), `markdown`, `python`, `javascript` (JavaScript, JavaScript React), `typescript` (TypeScript, TypeScript React), `html`, `css`, `scss`, `less`, `xml` (XML, XSL), `sql`, `shellscript`, `makefile`, `docker`, `ini` (INI, Properties), `cpp` (C, C++, CUDA C++), `rust`, `diff`, `git` (Git commit, Git rebase, Ignore) and `gomod` (go.mod, go.work, go.sum). They are the folders of VS Code's own extensions (one pack per VS Code extension folder, as VS Code groups languages), and Go's module files are a pack of their own because their grammar comes from `golang/vscode-go`; `extensions.All()` lists them first, in the order the languages were registered before this step (that order decides the number of each language and which language wins when two claim a file). Each pack is `New() extension.Extension` over `langpack.New(Spec{ID, Name, Description, Assets})`, where `Assets` is the pack's `//go:embed all:assets` (the VS Code extension's `package.json`, language configurations, `syntaxes/`, `cgmanifest.json`, copied by `scripts/update-assets.sh`, which now writes `extensions/<pack>/assets/`). The themes and the Seti icon theme stay in `core/theme`; the core keeps plain text only.
- **The contribution is declarative: `Manifest.Contributes.Languages fs.FS`** (the files of a VS Code extension rooted at its `package.json`; `extension/` needs only `io/fs`). The step text said the pack registers "from its `Activate` at `onStartup`"; it does not, because the registry has to know every language **before any tab and before the first file**: the documents that come back from the last session, the files of the command line and `Process.WarmGrammars` all run before any extension is activated (a scope is made and started last, when a workspace is complete). A declaration is read by the host when the process starts. The pack still declares `onStartup` and a no-op `Activate`, so that the page "Extensions" shows it as active in the tabs where it is on; `Activate` is the place where a later step adds the rest of a pack (the Go commands, the Markdown preview). A pack whose assets folder is not a path fails at `Activate` with `LanguagePackAssetsInvalid`.
- **Process-wide registry, per-tab activation: the host counts holds.** `exthost.Host` (`HostOptions.Languages`) registers the languages of every pack when it is made, with the settings defaults the pack gives languages (`contributes.configurationDefaults`: Go indents with tabs, YAML with two spaces; they go through `RegisterLanguageDefaults`, and `settings.Registry.UnregisterLanguageDefaults` takes them back). From then on a language pack is in the registry while at least one scope has the extension **enabled**: installing the extension in a scope (`Scope.install`, which a new scope and the switching on of an extension in the page both do) holds it, uninstalling it (the tab closes, the user disables it, it fails) releases it, and the release of the last hold calls `RemoveExtension` and takes the defaults back. So two tabs that run the pack register it once, closing one leaves it in the other, and the last tab to go (or to disable it) removes it. Packs come back with the numbers they had. `Host.SyncLanguages(disabled)` makes the registry follow `extensions.disabled` without a scope: the window calls it when it is made, before it opens or restores a file (`newWorkspace`), and a scope calls it when it starts, so a pack that the user disabled never gives a language to a document of the first tab. **Disabling `emetos.markdown` therefore makes `.md` files plain text (and removes its grammar and configuration) for files opened afterwards; a document that is already open keeps the id `markdown`, has no grammar and shows as plain text.** `extensions.disabled` is per tab (§10.15 "As built (step 11.1)"), the registry is the process's: a pack that one tab disables stays while another tab has it enabled (the languages of the pack are in the registry as long as any tab uses them).
- **Grammars that include other grammars** (Markdown's fenced blocks, HTML's CSS and JavaScript, TypeScript's JSON for `tsconfig`) find them across packs by scope name, as they did across the folders of the old assets: the registry is one for the process, and a rule whose grammar is not registered (its pack is off) is left out. `Process.Grammar` makes its grammars again when `language.Registry.Version()` changes, so the embedded languages of the grammars made so far follow the packs that came or went.
- **The tests get the languages from the source tree.** A package under `internal/` cannot import `extensions/` (`ExtensionsImportedByInternal`, tests included), so `internal/core/language/packfs` (no dependencies: the folders of the packs, in the order of `extensions.All`, found from the repository root) and `internal/core/language/languagetest.Bundled()` (the registry of the files, in that order) give them the same files the packs embed. `ProcessOptions.Languages` takes a registry that has languages already (the editor leaves it nil); `newTestProcess` of `internal/gui/app` passes `languagetest.Bundled()`. `cmd/emetos` is where `extensions` and `internal` meet, so its test (`languagepacks_test.go`) holds `packfs.Names` to the order of `extensions.All`, compares the registry the host builds with the one the tests build (languages, numbers, grammars, detection, settings defaults), and tests disabling `emetos.markdown`.
- **Snippets.** VS Code's snippets of the languages are not bundled: nothing in Emetos reads a snippet contribution of an extension (the snippet service reads the user's files), and `scripts/update-assets.sh` never copied them. A step that adds snippet contributions adds them to the packs' `assets/`. Emmet stays in `core/emmet`.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `ExtensionKeyEmpty`, `ExtensionKeyTaken` (`Registry.AddNamedExtension`), `LanguagePackAssetsInvalid`, `RepoRootNotFound` and `PackNotFound` (`packfs`); `BundledExtensionUnreadable` is gone with `language.Bundled`.
- **Existing tests changed** (none weakened, no golden changed): the 10 tests that made their registry with `language.Bundled()` call `languagetest.Bundled()` (same data, same order); `bundled_test.go` of `core/language` defines `Bundled()` over `packfs` for the tests of the package, `TestEveryBundledGrammarCompiles` walks the packs' `syntaxes/` instead of the old embedded folder, and `TestAddExtensionsErrors` went with `addExtensions` (the tag `BundledExtensionUnreadable`); `internal/gui/exthost/rig_test.go` got `newRigLanguages` (the old constructor calls it); `newTestProcess` passes the languages.

**As built (step 11.5).** Side bar views, panel views and the contributions to the built-in parts (`extension/views.go`, `extension/builtin.go`, `extension/ui`, `internal/gui/exthost/{views,box,builtin}.go`, `extensions/todo`, `extensions/tasks`). Where the text above leaves room:
- **What an extension declares.** `Contributes.ViewContainers` (`ViewContainerSpec{ID, Title, Icon, Order}`: an icon in the activity bar and the title of the side bar), `Contributes.Views` (`ViewSpec{ID, Name, Container, When, Order, Collapsed}`: in a container of the extension or of Emetos), `Contributes.PanelViews` (`PanelViewSpec{ID, Title, Icon, Order}`: a tab of the panel with one body) and `Contributes.ViewActions` (`ViewActionSpec{View, Command, Icon, Tooltip, When, Order}`: the title actions). Icons are the short names of the Codicons (`checklist`, `play`). Every id starts with the id of the extension and a dot (`ExtensionViewIDForeign`, `ExtensionViewDuplicate`, `ExtensionViewInvalid`, `ExtensionViewActionInvalid`, tags of `CheckManifest`). Order 0 puts the icon or the tab after everything Emetos has (1000); the Explorer is 0, Problems 0 and Output 1. The declarations are registered when the extension is enabled in a scope, so the icon and the tab are there before it runs; **showing a declared view activates the extension** (`onView:<id>` is implicit for the views the manifest declares), which then gives it content. The commands `workbench.view.extension.<container id>` ("Show <Title>", `extension.ShowViewCommand`) and `workbench.panel.extension.<view id>.toggle` ("Toggle <Title>", `extension.ToggleViewCommand`; it shows the tab, or hides the panel when the tab is shown), and a View menu entry for each panel view (group `5_panel`, after Output), are added with them. Each window tab has its own registry of views (`command.ViewRegistry.Fork`, made from the process's); `Registry.OnChange` and `workbench.Views.Changed` rebuild the activity bar, the side bar and the panel tabs when a container or a view comes or goes, and the container that was shown and went is replaced by the first one.
- **The content: `api.Views().Provide(viewID, extension.ViewContent{Build, SaveState, RestoreState})`.** `Build(bc) widgets.Widget` makes the widget (Glutter's `widgets.Widget`; the colors and the kit's widgets come from `extension/ui`); the handle's `Refresh()` builds it again, `SetBadge(count, tooltip)` puts the count pill of the Problems tab on a panel view's tab (a side bar view has none), `Reveal(focus)` shows the view (the container and the side bar, or the tab and the panel, and the focus goes to that part), `Dispose()` takes the content away. Errors: `ExtensionViewNotDeclared`, `ExtensionViewProvided`, `ExtensionViewContentInvalid`. `api.Context().Set(key, value)` / `Reset(key)` set the context keys the `when` of the views, the title actions, the commands and the keybindings read; a key starts with the id of the extension and a dot (`ExtensionContextKeyForeign`), and they go with the activation.
- **`extension/ui`: the widgets across the boundary.** The contract (`extension/`) imports nothing of Emetos; `extension/ui` is the one package under it that imports the editor, and only `internal/gui/kit` and `internal/gui/kit/fonts` (rules `ExtensionContractImportsEmetos` and `ExtensionUIImportsInternal`, §5.3, with fixtures). It re-exports a curated set as aliases and thin constructors: `Colors`, `Theme(bc)`, `TextStyle`, `Icon(name, size, color)`, `CodiconCode(name)`, `Button`, `IconButton`, `InputBox`, `Badge`, `Checkbox`, `Hover`, `ProgressBar`, `List`/`ListViewModel`/`ListController`, `Tree`/`TreeModel`/`TreeController` with their options and `RowState`. A widget the kit has and the list does not is added there when an extension needs it. `extension/ui/uitest` shows a widget in a window with Dark Modern or Light Modern and the test fonts, for the widget tests and the goldens of an extension.
- **The box** (`exthost.Scope.ViewBody`; `viewBox`). The workbench puts a box where the body of the view goes (the body of a side bar view, the panel body of a tab). The box gives the content the constraints of the body, clips what it paints to them (`ClipRect`), sets the text style of the theme, sets `focusedView` while the focus is inside, and wraps the content in a `Focus` node that does not take the focus itself: a key the widget of the extension does not handle goes on to the keys of the workbench as from any focused widget (Escape and the global keys work; a key the widget handles does not reach them). **A panic** in `Build` fails the extension in that scope with `ExtensionViewBuildPanicked`, one anywhere below it (in a widget it built, in a `State`'s `InitState` or `Build`, in a `LayoutBuilder` or the item of a lazy list) with `ExtensionViewWidgetPanicked`, one in `SaveState` or `RestoreState` with `ExtensionViewStatePanicked`: the handling is that of step 11.1 (one notification with Show Log, the log has the error with its route, the contributions are taken away, the other tabs and extensions are untouched), and the box shows "<Name> failed" with a **Show Log** button (the view stays declared while the extension is failed, so its icon and tab show it; turning the extension off removes them, and on again tries once more). The failure is made on the UI thread's next turn, not during the build. The box is a `widgets.ErrorBoundary` (Glutter 1.8.1, 28.20) around what the extension built, made for the instance of the extension (an extension that is turned on again has one that has not failed): its `OnError` fails the extension with `ExtensionViewWidgetPanicked` and it builds the "<Name> failed" box in place of the whole view in the same frame, so no widget of the extension needs a guard of its own (step 11.5 had `ui.NewBuilder` and `ui.BoxScope` for that; they are gone). The panic of `Build` itself is still caught in the box, so that its value and its route are exact (`ExtensionViewBuildPanicked`); Glutter's `OnError` of the application gets the errors below `Build` as well.
- **State per scope and restore.** `ViewContent.SaveState() (any, error)` returns a value that encodes to JSON (nil keeps none) and `RestoreState(json.RawMessage) error` gets it back. `SaveState` is called when the box goes off screen (another tab of the panel, another container, the panel closed), when the extension is deactivated or disposes the view, and when the window state is written; the answer is kept in the scope by view id (`Scope.ViewStates`). `RestoreState` is called before the first build of each box, with what was kept. The window state (`windows/<id>.json`, §10.10) has `"views": {"<view id>": <json>}` (`storage.WindowState.Views`, written with the layout and the grid, read when the window restores: `Scope.SetViewStates`), so the state of a view is per workspace and survives a restart. What the extension keeps in its own Go values (a list of lines, a tree model) lives as long as the activation, so a tab switch costs the view only the widgets; the saved state is for what the widgets hold and for what must outlive the session. The tab that is open in the panel is not part of the saved layout: after a restart the panel shows Problems until a tab is chosen, and a view restores when its box is built.
- **The built-in parts.** `api.Output().Channel(name)` makes a channel of the Output panel (`OutputChannel{Name, AppendLine, Clear, Show(preserveFocus), Dispose}`), listed from its creation; a name that is empty or `Emetos` (`ExtensionOutputChannelInvalid`) or that the extension has open (`ExtensionOutputChannelDuplicate`) fails. The Output panel is the window's, so two window tabs that open the same name share the lines and the channel goes with the last of them (`logs.Store.Add`/`Remove`; the Output view goes back to the Emetos log when its channel goes). `api.Problems().Set(owner, uri, markers)` / `Clear(owner)` set the markers of a file (`file:///...`); the owner is the extension's own name (`ExtensionProblemsOwnerInvalid`, `ExtensionProblemsURIInvalid`), stored as `<extension id>:<owner>` so another extension cannot replace it; the source is the name of the extension unless the marker has one; they go with the activation. `StatusBar().Add` was built in step 11.1 and is used by both extensions. An extension that is turned off loses its channels, markers, context keys, status items, views and commands together.
- **The folder for an extension.** `api.Workspace().Files()` is the list of the files of the file index (the paths relative to the folder, with `/`; `Complete` says whether the walk has ended) and `ReadFile(ctx, path)` reads one file of the folder from disk as UTF-8 text (up to `MaxReadFileSize`, 2 MiB), safe from any goroutine. The folder is opened as an `os.Root`, so a path with `..`, an absolute path and a link that points out of it all fail (`ExtensionFilePathInvalid`, `ExtensionFileReadFailed`; `ExtensionNoFolder`, `ExtensionFileTooLarge`, `ExtensionFileNotText`); it sees no unsaved changes (`Documents().Read` does, on the UI thread). The core event **`emetos.files.changed`** (`extension.FilesChanged{Changes: [{Kind, Path, OldPath}]}`, paths relative to the folder) reports what the watcher saw (`created`, `changed`, `deleted`, `renamed`, `rescan`), outside the folder left out, a batch of more than 500 as one `rescan` of `.`, and `listed` when the list of files itself changed (the walk found more, or ended). `api.Documents().Show(uri, line, column, preview)` opens a file in the active group with the cursor at the place, as a click on a problem does (`ExtDocumentShowUnsupported`, `ExtDocumentShowUnavailable` in the window; a column counts UTF-16 units).
- **Processes.** An extension runs a process with `os/exec`. `extensions/tasks` shows how: a shell (`sh -c`) in a process group of its own (`Setpgid`), started in the folder; the output of both streams is read by a goroutine and handed to the UI thread with `api.Post` (one `Post` for every burst of lines); when the scope's `ctx` ends, or the task is stopped, the group gets SIGTERM and, after two seconds, SIGKILL; when the shell ends, whatever it left in the group is killed too, so no child outlives its task.
- **`extensions/todo`** (`emetos.todo`, the side bar view "TODOs" in its own container, icon `checklist`, order 50): lists the `TODO` and `FIXME` comments (the setting `emetos.todo.tags`) of the files of the file index, grouped by file in a `ui.Tree` (the files open the first time they are seen; the expanded files are its saved state). A tag counts in a comment (after `//`, `#`, `/*`, `<!--`, `--`, or on a line that continues a block comment with `*`) and as a whole word. A goroutine reads the files in batches of 64 and hands the comments over; `emetos.files.changed` rescans the files that changed, forgets the deleted and renamed ones and reads the files a `listed` event brings; the Refresh command (the title action) reads everything again; a click on a comment opens the file there. Binary file types and files over 2 MiB are not read; the view keeps at most 5,000 comments. A status bar item counts them and reveals the view.
- **`extensions/tasks`** (`emetos.tasks`, the tab "Tasks" of the panel, order 5, after Output): the setting `emetos.tasks.commands` (a list of command lines, default `go test ./...`) is shown as buttons (a click runs it), over the output of the last run (the last 5,000 lines, a line that names a place is red or yellow and opens the file when clicked). `emetos.tasks.run` ("Tasks: Run Task") runs the first command, or the command line or the number it is given; `emetos.tasks.stop` ("Stop Task") and `emetos.tasks.clear`. One task runs at a time. The output also goes to the Output channel `Tasks`, and a line `file:line:col: message` (or `file:line: message`) whose file is a file of the folder becomes a marker of the owner `task` (a warning when the message says so), replacing the markers of the earlier run; the tab's badge is their number; the status bar item shows the state; the context key `emetos.tasks.running` switches Run and Stop in the title actions. The last command, how it ended and the last 200 lines are the view's saved state.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `ExtensionViewIDForeign`, `ExtensionViewDuplicate`, `ExtensionViewInvalid`, `ExtensionViewActionInvalid`, `ExtensionViewNotDeclared`, `ExtensionViewProvided`, `ExtensionViewContentInvalid`, `ExtensionViewBuildPanicked`, `ExtensionViewWidgetPanicked`, `ExtensionViewStatePanicked`, `ExtensionOutputUnavailable`, `ExtensionOutputChannelInvalid`, `ExtensionOutputChannelDuplicate`, `ExtensionProblemsUnavailable`, `ExtensionProblemsOwnerInvalid`, `ExtensionProblemsURIInvalid`, `ExtensionNoFolder`, `ExtensionFilePathInvalid`, `ExtensionFileReadFailed`, `ExtensionFileTooLarge`, `ExtensionFileNotText`, `ExtensionContextKeyForeign`, `ExtensionContextUnavailable`, `ExtDocumentShowUnsupported`, `ExtDocumentShowUnavailable`, and the `Fake...` tags of `extensions/internal/fakeapi`.
- **Not built:** an activity bar entry for the Extensions page (it needs a container that opens a page, not views; the page is still reached by its command, the menus and Ctrl+Shift+X), badges on the activity bar icons of extensions, views that move between the side bar and the panel, saving which panel tab was open, the panel body of an extension that is not one tab (several views in a panel container), dynamic registration of views at run time (every view is declared in the manifest), a quick pick for choosing a task, task problem matchers other than `file:line:col: message`, task output with colors or a terminal.
- **Existing tests and goldens changed.** `extensions/internal/testext/testext_test.go`: its `recorder` embeds `extension.API` (nil) so that it still implements the interface, which has five new methods; no assertion changed. `internal/archtest/testdata/clean/extension/ok.go` no longer imports the core (the contract imports nothing of the editor, which the clean fixture now says, with `extension/ui/ok.go` as the clean bridge). No golden image changed; the new ones are `extensions/todo/testdata/goldens/todo_view_{dark,light}.png` and `extensions/tasks/testdata/goldens/tasks_panel_{idle,run}_{dark,light}.png`, and the proof image is `docs/implemented-proof-images/11.5-extension-views.png` (`testdata/proof/11.5/`).

**As built (step 11.6).** Editor tabs, editor title actions and file views (`extension/editors.go`, `extension/ui/markdown`, `internal/core/editorgroup/exttabinput.go`, `internal/gui/exthost/editors.go`, `internal/gui/app/{exttabs,exttitle,fileviews,extlanguages}.go`, `extensions/markdown`, `extensions/notes`). Where the text above leaves room:
- **What an extension declares.** `Contributes.EditorKinds` (`EditorKindSpec{ID, Name, Icon}`: a kind of editor tab; `Icon` is the name of a Codicon), `Contributes.EditorActions` (`EditorActionSpec{Command, Icon, Tooltip, When, Order}`: an icon at the right end of the tab strip of every group) and `Contributes.FileViews` (`FileViewSpec{ID, Name, Icon, Languages, Globs, Order}`: a view of a file, chosen by language id or by glob). Ids of kinds and file views start with the id of the extension (`ExtensionEditorIDForeign`, `ExtensionEditorDuplicate`, `ExtensionEditorInvalid`, `ExtensionEditorActionInvalid`). The activation event `onEditor:<kindID>` is new; a declared kind activates its extension without listing the event, and a declared file view activates it through `onView:<view id>`, like the views of step 11.5.
- **Editor tab kinds: `api.Editors()`.** `Provide(kindID, EditorKind{Create})` gives the code of a kind; `Create(tab EditorTab, state json.RawMessage) (EditorTabContent, error)` is called once for every tab (a new one with the state `Open` was given, a restored one with the state it saved), and returns `EditorTabContent{Build, SaveState, OnClose}` (the same shape as `ViewContent` of step 11.5: `Build(bc)` makes the widget in the box, `SaveState` the JSON-encodable state, `OnClose` is told when the tab closes for good). `Open(kindID, state, EditorOpenOptions{Group, Inactive})` opens a new tab (a tab with no file and no resource; several of a kind may be open) and returns the `EditorTab` handle: `ID()` (the instance id, unique in the workspace), `Kind()`, `SetTitle`, `SetHint` (the tooltip), `SetDirty`, `SetBusy`, `Refresh`, `Reveal(focus)`, `Group()` and `Close()`. `Tabs(kindID)` lists the open ones. The tab is a pinned tab of the group; it can be split (Split Editor makes a **second instance with a copy of the saved state**: `ExtensionTabInput` is a `Copier`; the state is taken from `SaveState` and given to a new `Create`), moved between groups and closed like any tab. The tab is **restored with the window**: the input is serialized as `emetos.extensionTab` with `{ext, kind, id, title, icon}`, and its state is in `WindowState.Views` under the view id `editor:<instance id>`; a tab whose extension is disabled or gone stays as a placeholder with the title and an empty body and comes back when the extension is enabled, and the state of a tab that was closed is dropped. The tab body is a `viewBox` like a side bar view (the same panic containment: `ExtensionEditorCallbackPanicked` and `ExtensionEditorCreatePanicked` fail the extension). A kind is provided once (`ExtensionEditorKindProvided`), must be declared (`ExtensionEditorKindNotDeclared`), must be provided before it is opened (`ExtensionEditorKindNotProvided`), and its state must be valid JSON (`ExtensionEditorStateInvalid`).
- **Proposed changes: `api.Editors().OpenProposedChange(ctx, change)`** (step 13.3) shows a change to a file in the diff editor, with Accept and Reject, and blocks until the user answers (`ProposedResult`: accepted, the text of the right side, edited); a closed tab is a rejection and a cancelled `ctx` closes the tab. See §10.16 "As built (step 13.3)" for its contract and the host (`EditorHost.OpenProposed`).
- **Dirty, busy and hot exit.** *Dirty is only a mark*: it shows in the tab like a document's, but closing a dirty extension tab asks nothing (`editorgroup.CloseUnasked`, a new interface that `PlanClose` consults: an input that implements it with `true` never counts as unsaved), and it makes no backup and no Save prompt on quit, because the data of the tab is the extension's own and is kept in the state it saves with the window state (`views`), which is written like the rest of the state (on quit, on a timer, when the tab closes). An extension that wants to keep something on disk does that itself. *Busy* replaces the icon of the tab by the Codicon `loading` (static; it does not turn).
- **Editor title actions.** The actions of all active extensions are shown at the right end of the tab strip of **each group**, as 22 px micro icons (`kit.TabsOpts.Actions`, a function of the width the strip has, built in a `LayoutBuilder`), sorted by `Order` (0 sorts last, as in the views) then by extension. An action shows when its `when` is true **for that group's active editor**: the host evaluates it with an overlay of the context keys of the group on top of the window's: `activeEditor` (the type id of the editor input: `emetos.textEditor`, `emetos.diff`, `emetos.extensionTab` and so on), `activeEditorIsDirty`, and, for a text editor, `resourceLangId`, `resourceScheme`, `resourceExtname` and `resourceFilename`. The command runs with the argument `{"groupId": <number>}` (`extension.GroupOfArgs(args)` reads it; 0 when absent), so a handler acts on the group the icon was in, not the active one. **Overflow:** the icons may take up to 40% of the width of the strip; those that do not fit go into a `...` menu (the group's tab menu controller, items with the tooltip as the label).
- **File views.** For a file the tab shows, `exthost.Scope.FileViewsFor(file, languageID, folder)` returns the views of the active extensions whose `Languages` has the file's language id or whose `Globs` match (on the base name, or on the path relative to the folder), in the order of `Order` (0 last) then extension. When it returns any, the **micro-tabs** appear: at the right end of the breadcrumbs row, or, when breadcrumbs are hidden, in a 22 px strip of their own above the editor. **Text is always first** and is the default; a file with no view has no micro-tabs and no strip. The choice is **remembered per editor tab** (`textEditor.fileView`) and **restored**: the editor's view state in the window state is the plain `editor.ViewState` JSON when the view is Text, and `{"viewState": ..., "fileView": "<view id>"}` when a view is chosen (`decodeEditorState` reads both, so states written before this step still load). A file opened in a new editor starts in Text unless `workbench.editor.defaultFileViews` says otherwise. `workbench.editor.defaultFileViews` (application scope, an object) maps a glob to a view id (`{"*.md": "emetos.markdown.preview"}`); it applies when an editor is **created** (not to an existing one, not to a restored one), the keys are tried in sorted order and the first whose glob matches and whose view is available for the file wins. The command `workbench.action.cycleFileView` ("Cycle File View", category View, no key) shows the next view of the active editor: Text, the views in order, then Text again; it does nothing for a file with no views.
- **The file view API: `api.FileViews()`.** `Provide(viewID, FileViewProvider{Open})`; `Open(doc DocumentHandle, tab FileViewTab) (FileViewContent, error)` is called when a view is shown for the first time in an editor (one instance per editor and view, kept while the editor lives, so switching micro-tabs keeps the scroll), and returns `FileViewContent{Build, Close}`; `FileViewTab.Refresh()` rebuilds it. **`DocumentHandle`** is what the view sees of the file: `URI()`, `LanguageID()`, `Version()`, `Text()`, `ReadOnly()`, `Folder()`, `Edit([]TextEdit)` (**edits go through the document API**, with a stack element before and after, so one `Edit` call undoes as one step with Ctrl+Z; refused for a read-only document), `OnChange(fn) cancel` (called on the UI thread after every change, with `ViewDocumentChange{Version, Cause}`), `TopLine()` and `OnScroll(fn) cancel` (the first visible line of the Text editor of the same tab, so a preview can follow it), and `OpenFile(path)` (opens a file in the editor). The callbacks of a view are wrapped (`guardedDoc`): a panic in them fails the extension (`ExtensionFileViewPanicked`). **A view that fails** (its `Open` returns an error or panics, it has no `Build`, it is not provided, its extension is disabled or failed) **falls back to Text** for that editor (`FileViewBody` returns `ok == false`); the failure is logged as a warning. `api.FileViews().Open(uri, viewID, FileViewOpenOptions{Side, Group})` shows a file in a view: `uri` empty means the document of the active text editor of the group; `Side` opens it in the group on the side (`workbench.editor.openSideBySideDirection`; made when there is none, and the asked group when it cannot be made) and otherwise in `Group` (0 is the active group). Only `file:` files can be shown (`ExtEditorsFileOnly`). The tags `ExtensionFileViewNotDeclared`, `ExtensionFileViewInvalid`, `ExtensionFileViewProvided` and `ExtensionFileViewContentInvalid` are those of `Provide` and `Open`.
- **The highlighting bridge: `api.Languages()`.** `Resolve(name) (languageID, ok)` finds a language by its id, name, alias or extension, `Tokenize(languageID, text) ([][]Token, error)` returns for each line the tokens `Token{Start, End, Scopes}` (offsets in the line; scopes from the outermost to the innermost) that the grammar of the language gives. The app implements it with the grammar of the process, a throwaway untitled document and the tokenizer run to the end (`tokens.Tokenizer.Settle`); text over **256 KiB** is refused (`ExtensionTokenizeTooLong`), an unknown language is `ExtensionLanguageUnknown`. The extension does not see colors: `extension/ui` turns the scopes into a style with `kit.TokenLookOf(bc, scopes, fallback)`, which looks the scopes up in the token theme of the theme in force (a `TokenLook` is color, bold, italic, underline), so a code block in a preview changes with the theme. `kit.BundledTokens` is the token theme the test harness (`uitest`) uses for goldens.
- **`Workspace().OpenURI(ctx, uri)`** was added to the contract: `http`, `https` and `mailto` go to the desktop (`desktop.OpenURI`), a `file:` uri opens in the editor (`Workspace.OpenURI`); anything else is refused (`ExtensionOpenURIUnavailable` when the host has no way to do it, `ExtOpenURIUnavailable` in the app).
- **`ViewStates` and `Provide` changed.** A view that was **provided** now saves its state even when it is not on screen (before, only views with a live box did; a tab in a background group would lose its state on quit otherwise), and `Views().Provide` restores the saved state **at once**, not only when the box is built. The views of step 11.5 are not changed by this beyond saving more.
- **`extension/ui/markdown`: the renderer.** `markdown.NewView(src string, Options{Tokenize, OnLink, ResolveImage, Controller}) widgets.Widget` turns Markdown into widgets. It is a package under `extension/ui`, so it may import the kit: **no change to the archtest rules was needed** (`extension/ui/...` already allows `internal/gui/kit` and `kit/fonts`); the test `TestAPackageOfTheBridgeMayUseTheKit` and the fixture `testdata/clean/extension/ui/markdown` pin this. The parser (`ast.go`, `block.go`, `inline.go`) covers CommonMark with GFM tables, strikethrough and task lists: ATX and setext headings, paragraphs, block quotes, nested bullet and ordered lists, fenced and indented code, thematic breaks, tables with alignment, HTML blocks (shown as text), emphasis, strong, code spans, links, autolinks, images, hard and soft breaks and entities. Known gaps: reference-style links and link definitions, raw inline HTML (shown as text), footnotes, and the rarest CommonMark edge cases of lazy continuation. Code uses the monospace font of the theme (the family `monospace` when it is empty) with tabs expanded to spaces. `Options.Tokenize` highlights a fenced block by the language of its info string (nil leaves it plain); `Controller.ScrollToLine(line)` scrolls so that the block the line belongs to is at the top (it waits for the first layout) and `TopLine()` gives the first source line in view. **Seven colors were registered** with VS Code's defaults and added to `kit.Colors`: `textLink.activeForeground`, `textSeparator.foreground`, `textPreformat.foreground`, `textPreformat.background`, `textBlockQuote.background`, `textBlockQuote.border`, `textCodeBlock.background`.
- **Links and images in the preview** (`extensions/markdown`). `http`, `https` and `mailto` links go to `Workspace().OpenURI` (a failure is a warning notification); a relative link to a file **inside the folder** opens in the editor through `DocumentHandle.OpenFile` (a `#fragment` is dropped); a link with only a `#fragment` does nothing (anchors are not built); a file that does not exist or a path that leaves the folder gives an information notification ("The linked file ... is not in the workspace."). Images: a relative or absolute path inside the folder is shown (`NewImageFile`, no wider than the view; the alt text when it cannot be read); **web images are not loaded** (privacy: a document must not make the editor call a server), and the alt text is shown in their place.
- **`extensions/markdown`** (`emetos.markdown`, the language pack of step 11.4 plus): the file view `emetos.markdown.preview` ("Preview", icon `preview`, language `markdown`), the command `emetos.markdown.openPreviewToSide` ("Open Preview to the Side", category Markdown) and the editor title action with the icon `open-preview` and `when: resourceLangId == markdown`, order 1. **"Open Preview to the Side" opens the same document in the group on the right, in the preview view** (`FileViews().Open("", PreviewView, {Side: true, Group: GroupOfArgs(args)})`), so the user edits in one group and reads in the other. The preview draws again after every change of the document (`OnChange`, no debounce) and follows the scroll of the Text editor of the same editor tab (`OnScroll`); a preview opened in the group on the side is its own editor, so it follows the document but not the scroll of the Text editor in the other group.
- **`extensions/notes`** (`emetos.notes`): the view container `emetos.notes.container` (icon `note`, order 60) with the side bar view `emetos.notes.list` (a list of the notes, with a "New Note" action), the editor kind `emetos.notes.note`, the commands `emetos.notes.newNote` ("New Note", category Notes) and `emetos.notes.deleteNote`, and the editor title action "New Note" (icon `new-file`, shown in every group). A note has an id, a title and a text, is edited in a tab with a title box and a text box, and the tab is named by the title ("Untitled Note" when empty). The notes are kept in the state the extension saves: the list in the state of the view, and each open note also in the state of its tab; several tabs of one note show the same text. Deleting a note closes its tabs. The extension exists to exercise the whole contract (a side bar view, tabs with several instances, split, restore, title and the title action, commands); it does not use the dirty and busy marks. The text of the step called the command `notes.newNote`; it is `emetos.notes.newNote` by the rule that command ids start with the id of the extension.
- **The proof.** `docs/implemented-proof-images/11.6-editor-extensions.png` (made with `scripts/proof.sh ... --config testdata/proof/11.6/config` over `testdata/proof/11.6/project`): the Markdown README in its preview with the micro-tabs "Text | Preview" and the title icons, a second group with a note tab, and the Notes side bar.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `ExtensionEditorIDForeign`, `ExtensionEditorDuplicate`, `ExtensionEditorInvalid`, `ExtensionEditorActionInvalid` (the manifest); `ExtensionTabInputInvalid`; `ExtensionEditorKindNotDeclared`, `ExtensionEditorKindInvalid`, `ExtensionEditorKindProvided`, `ExtensionEditorKindNotProvided`, `ExtensionEditorStateInvalid`, `ExtensionEditorsUnavailable`, `ExtensionEditorCreatePanicked`, `ExtensionEditorContentInvalid`, `ExtensionEditorCallbackPanicked`; `ExtensionFileViewNotDeclared`, `ExtensionFileViewInvalid`, `ExtensionFileViewProvided`, `ExtensionFileViewPanicked`, `ExtensionFileViewContentInvalid`; `ExtensionOpenURIUnavailable`, `ExtensionLanguageUnknown`, `ExtensionTokenizeTooLong`; in the app `ExtEditorsUnavailable`, `ExtEditorsFileOnly`, `ExtEditorsNoDocument`, `ExtFileViewNoFolder`, `ExtOpenURIUnavailable`; `NotesStateInvalid`, `NotesTabStateInvalid`; and the `Fake*` tags of `extensions/internal/fakeapi`.
- **Tests and goldens.** Tests in `extension` (the manifest checks, `GroupOfArgs`), `editorgroup` (`exttabinput_test.go`: the input, copy, restore, the route of an invalid value, `CloseUnasked` in `PlanClose`), `exthost` (`editors_test.go`, `editors_rig_test.go`: kinds, tabs, state, marks, title actions, file views, fallbacks, the languages), `app` (`exteditors_test.go`: open, split, move, close and restore of tabs, the marks, the title actions in the right group and the overflow, the micro-tabs, disabling an extension, an edit and its undo through a view, `defaultFileViews`, the restored choice, failing views, the encoding of the editor state, `OpenFileView`, `docHandle`, the languages), `kit` (`Tabs` with `Actions`), `core/settings` (`defaultFileViews`), `archtest`, `extension/ui/markdown` (parser and renderer), `extensions/markdown`, `extensions/notes` and `fakeapi`. Goldens (Dark Modern and Light Modern, each looked at): `extension/ui/markdown/testdata/goldens/preview_{dark,light}.png`, `extensions/markdown/testdata/goldens/markdown_preview_{dark,light}.png`, and the goldens of `extensions/notes` for the list and a note tab.
- **Existing tests changed** (none weakened, no existing golden changed): `internal/gui/exthost/rig_test.go` gained fields for the new seams (editors, languages, uris, changed) and passes them in the scope options; `extension/ui/uitest` gives the harness the token theme `kit.BundledTokens` and a monospace font family (the todo and tasks goldens did not change); `extensions/internal/fakeapi` gained the fakes of the new API methods.
- **Not built:** a lazy preview for very large files (done in step 17b.2, "As built (step 17b.2)" below), anchors (`#fragment`) in the preview, web images, scrolling the preview with the Text editor of another group, a spinning busy mark, and a menu of the title actions that an extension can extend.

**As built (step 17b.2, a fast Markdown preview; `extension/ui/markdown/{preview,controller,heights,estimate,keys,images,imageview,tokens,render,view}.go`, `extensions/markdown`, `gui/app/devquery.go`, `extension/ui/uitest/mdfixture`).** The preview of `docs/IMPLEMENTED.md` (700 KB, 150 images) took the window and 2 GB (SPEC §14); the page of a document is now a virtual list. Where the text above and the step leave room:
- **Two paths.** `NewView` makes the **virtual list** (`preview`) for the page of a document and the old column (`view`) for the three small looks (`Options.Hover`, `Flow`, `Compact`: a hover, a message, the details of a suggestion), whose text is short, built whole and parsed on the UI thread as before. The size of a text that is parsed on the UI thread in the list is `syncParseLimit` (16 KB, a quarter of a millisecond); a bigger text is parsed on a goroutine and the first frame of the view is drawn with no blocks (`Stats.Parsing`), so a restored session with the preview of a big file does not wait for it.
- **The list and its heights.** The rows are the top-level blocks. A Fenwick tree (`heightIndex`) holds the height of each block plus the 10 px gap below it: measured when the block was laid out, or estimated (`estimator`: the characters of the text at 0.55 em in the width of the page, the lines of code, the rows of a table, 320 px for an image that has not loaded, from VS Code's `markdown.css` sizes). The content is `16 + sum - 10 + 40` pixels high (the page's padding) and the scroll position is `16 + prefix(anchor) + offset`. A new width of the page drops the measurements and estimates again; the heights of the blocks of an edited text are kept by block key.
- **The window and the anchor.** Only the blocks within 250 px of the viewport (`cacheMargin`, Flutter's default; kept small because the Vulkan renderer draws what is off screen, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`) are built, chosen from the heights with the estimates of the blocks never laid out shrunk by 20% (so that an estimate that is too high does not leave a gap). They are laid out by a `CustomMultiChildLayout` delegate from an **anchor**: the block at the top of the viewport and the distance from its top to the top of the viewport; the blocks before it are placed above it and the ones after it below, each at the height it has when laid out. A block above the viewport that turns out taller than estimated (an image that loaded) therefore moves nothing that is on screen; the heights it reports are written to the table, the scroll bar is told after the frame, and the first block of the page and the last block (with the page's bottom padding) are never moved off the viewport's edges.
