A frame whose blocks leave a gap in the viewport asks for another build (at most four times in a row). `kit.ScrollableElement` with a `ScrollModel` gives the scroll bar and the wheel; a click on the track jumps by estimate and costs the blocks of one window (`BenchmarkPreviewJump`: 1 ms for the 700 KB document).
- **Scroll sync.** `Controller.ScrollToLine(line)` puts the last block that starts at or before the line at the top of the viewport (the block, not the line: as before) and waits when the view has no blocks yet; `TopLine()` is the first line of the block under the top edge; both work on estimated and on measured heights, and `Controller.Stats()` (`Blocks`, `Built`, `Builds`, `Measured`, `Parsing`, `TopLine`, `ScrollTop`, `ContentHeight`, `ImageBytes`, `Images`) says what the view holds.
- **Updates.** A change of the text is taken the way VS Code's preview takes it (`preview.ts`: `refresh` runs at once the first time, and later a timer of `#delay` = 300 ms is started by the first change and takes the document as it is when it ends): the first text is parsed at once, a later one 300 ms after the first change, off the UI thread when it is over 16 KB, and a result that is no longer the latest text is dropped. Each top-level block has a **key** (`blockKey`: a 64-bit hash of what it shows, not of its lines, and the count of equal blocks before it), the widgets of the window are kept by key (`LayoutId` of the key, and a cache of the built widgets), so an edit builds the widgets of the changed block only (`Stats.Builds` counts them), the viewport stays at the block it was at (found by its key, or by its line when it was the edited block), and the measured heights of the unchanged blocks are kept. A change of the theme or of the pixel ratio drops the built widgets.
- **Highlighting.** The code of a block is highlighted when its block is built (the window), through `Options.Tokenize` on the UI thread, and the tokens are cached by language and text (`tokenCache`, the last 256 blocks; a block the highlighter refused is cached too).
- **Images.** `markdown.ImageCache` (`Options.Images`; the extension makes one for all its previews, `DefaultImageBudget` = 64 MB of pixels) decodes off the UI thread (two at a time) at the size the image is shown at: the box width the page gives it (at most 800 px, 600 px high, never larger than the file's own pixels) times the pixel ratio of the screen, so a screenshot of 1920 px shown 700 px wide at a ratio of 1.25 costs 875 px across. The entry is identified by the path, the size and modification time of the file, the box and the pixel ratio; the least recently used entries are dropped when the pixels pass the budget (the entry just added stays), failures are entries too (the alt text stays, as when `NewImageFile` failed), a decoding that no view waits for any more is not started, and an image over 64 million pixels is not decoded (`ImageTooLarge`). The formats are PNG, JPEG, GIF (the first frame), BMP and WebP. A block builds its image widget when it enters the window, so only the images near the viewport are loaded; the alt text shows while it loads. Tags (each with a route test): `ImageStatFailed`, `ImageOpenFailed`, `ImageDecodeFailed`, `ImageTooLarge`, `ImageRequestCancelled`.
- **Dev command.** `dev.markdown` (step 17b.2, §15.2) lists the previews on screen with their `Stats` and their place, failing with `DevMarkdownNoWindow`; it reads them from the states that implement `markdown.Inspector`.
- **Measured** (headless, release-equivalent frame stats; `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`): see there; the target is §14's row. The fixture is `extension/ui/uitest/mdfixture` (700 KB, 150 images of 960 x 540, generated in a temporary folder).
- **Not built:** keyboard scrolling of the preview (it had none), the highlighting of a code block off the UI thread (the cost is in the frame that builds the block: a window the first time costs up to 40 ms headless with the Go grammar), and rows below the top level (a list of 10,000 items is one row).

**As built (step 11.7).** Window tab extensions (`extension/windowtabs.go`, `internal/gui/exthost/windowtabs.go`, `internal/gui/app/exttab.go`, `internal/gui/workbench` (`Options.EditorOnly`, `TitleBarOptions.NewMenu`, `WorkspaceTab.IconCode`), `internal/core/storage` (`WorkspaceTab.Kind/Title/State`), `extensions/scratchpad`). Where the text above leaves room:
- **What an extension declares.** `Contributes.WindowTabKinds` (`WindowTabKindSpec{ID, Title, Icon, PlusMenuLabel}`): the `ID` starts with the id of the extension and a dot and is new (`emetos.scratchpad.tab`; the tags of the manifest check are `ExtensionWindowTabIDForeign`, `ExtensionWindowTabDuplicate` and `ExtensionWindowTabInvalid` for a kind with no title); `Title` is the name on the tab until the extension sets one, and the name the Extensions page and the questions of the event sharing call the tab; `Icon` is the name of a Codicon (the icon `window` when empty or unknown); `PlusMenuLabel` is the text of the entry of the "+" menu (the title when empty). The activation event `onWindowTab:<kind>` is implied by the declaration (an extension need not list it), and an extension that is turned on later is activated for a tab that is open (`Scope.replay` now also looks at the implied events).
- **The scope: `ScopeWindowTab`.** Every tab of an extension is a scope of its own (`extension.ScopeWindowTab`; `ScopeInfo.WindowTab` is the kind, `Name` the title of the kind, `Folder` empty) and **holds the extension that owns the kind only** (`exthost.ScopeOptions.Only`): the others are not installed there, never activated by it (an `onStartup` extension does not start in a window tab), and the Extensions page lists a scope for an extension only where the extension is. The owner is activated by `onStartup` (if it lists it) and by `onWindowTab:<kind>`, at once when the tab is made, with an `API` bound to the tab: `Commands`, `Keybindings`, `Menus`, `Settings`, `Notifications`, `Context`, `Events` (with the sharing of §10.15), `Workspace().OpenURI`, `Post` and `Log` work as in a workspace; `Documents` reads nothing (the tab has no documents), `Workspace().Files` and `ReadFile` fail with `ExtensionNoFolder`, and the APIs of the parts a window tab does not have fail with their own tags: `StatusBar().Add` with `ExtensionStatusBarUnavailable` (new), `Output().Channel` with `ExtensionOutputUnavailable`, `Problems().Set` with `ExtensionProblemsUnavailable`, `Editors().Open` with `ExtensionEditorsUnavailable`; no side bar or panel view is declared in the tab (`Views().Provide` fails with `ExtensionViewNotDeclared`) and `Languages` knows none. The commands and menu items the owner declares are in the palette and the menus of the tab. The core event `emetos.windowTab.activated` is published in the scope when its tab becomes the active one; the document, editor and workspace events are not (a window tab has none).
- **The scope id: `<extension id>:<tab id>`.** The tab id is the stable id of the window tab (the `id` in `workspaceTabs`, §10.10), the same after a restart, so a link `/work/notes -> emetos.scratchpad:3f2a...` survives restarts and is listed by the Extensions › Event Sharing page like any other. A tab that is closed for good takes its id with it (its links stay in the file, as the links of a folder that is not open do). Two Scratchpad tabs are two scopes with the same name; the question names the kind ("Scratchpad") and the id tells them apart in the page.
- **The API: `api.WindowTabs()`.** `Provide(kindID, WindowTabKind{Create})`, called in `Activate`; `Create(tab WindowTab, state json.RawMessage) (WindowTabContent, error)` is called once for the activation, at once, with the state the content saved in the session before (nil for a new tab), and returns `WindowTabContent{Build, SaveState, OnClose}`. `Build` is the widget of the tab; `SaveState` returns the state (a JSON value, nil for none; called when the tab goes off screen, when the extension ends and when the list of the tabs is written); `OnClose` is called when the tab is closed for good (not when Emetos quits and not when the extension is turned off). `WindowTab` has `ID`, `Kind`, `SetTitle`, `SetHint` (the tooltip; both are kept across restarts), `StateChanged` (the state is written within 250 ms, with the state store's own delay after that: not only at the end), `Refresh`, `CaptureKeys(capture bool)` (step 15.4: while it is true and the content of the tab has the focus, every chord that is not one of B's own window shortcuts, §10.18 "As built (step 15.4)", goes to the content's key handler instead of the commands of the tab; a tab that shows another machine's window uses it) and `Close` (without a question). The tags: `ExtensionWindowTabKindNotDeclared`, `ExtensionWindowTabUnavailable` (the scope is not the tab of that kind), `ExtensionWindowTabKindInvalid` (no `Create`), `ExtensionWindowTabKindProvided`, `ExtensionWindowTabContentInvalid` (no `Build`); an error of `Create` is not a failure of the extension: the tab shows "This tab could not be made: <message>". The content is the `viewDecl` of the scope, so the box, the saved state and the failure are those of a view.
- **What the tab shows around the widget.** The tab is a `Workspace` that holds the services (the commands and keys of the tab, its notifications, quick input, dialogs, settings, themes, with no folder, no documents and no UI state file) and whose page is the shell in extension mode: `workbench.New(Options{EditorOnly: true})` is **the title bar row with the strip, the menu and the buttons of the window, over the editor area alone**, which holds the box of the extension (the whole area below the title bar is its constraints). There is **no activity bar, side bar, panel or status bar** (`Options.EditorOnly` ignores the layout and does not follow its settings; the commands that toggle those parts change a layout nothing shows). The quick input (Help and the command palette; no files, go to line or editor providers), the toasts and the dialogs (the question of a link shows here) are over it as in a workspace. A command that needs a part of a workbench (Open File, the settings editor, an editor command) is not bound in a window tab and fails with the usual notification; the commands of the strip, the tab switching and moving, New Workspace Tab, Close Window (closes the tab), Quit, full screen and zen mode work. The title of the window is "<title> - Emetos". "Show Log" of a failure (`workbench.panel.output.focus`) brings the workspace tab used last to the front with the Output panel, or opens a No Folder tab first.
- **The strip, the `+` menu, the tray, the picker and the keys.** The tab is in the strip with the icon of its kind (`WorkspaceTab.IconCode`), its title and tooltip, no dirty dot, and the same close button and context menu. The `+` menu is **Workspace...** and then one entry for each kind of the extensions that are turned on (`Workspace.extensionTabItems`, built when the menu opens, so an entry goes with its extension and comes back with it); choosing one runs `emetos.windowTab.open` with `{"kind": id}`, which is also in the palette as **New Window Tab...** (a picker of the kinds when run without arguments). The tray menu lists the tab by its title like any other (radio item; the tooltip counts the workspaces, not the tabs of extensions), and the picker of Switch Workspace Tab... lists it with its icon, its title and "current · <extension name>". The keys (Ctrl+Alt+PageUp/PageDown, Ctrl+Alt+1...9, move left and right) work from the tab, since every tab has the key dispatcher of its workspace; `workspaceTabCount` and the other context keys are set in its keys too.
- **State.** The list of the tabs (`workspaceTabs`, §10.10) has an entry for the tab: `{"id": ..., "kind": "emetos.scratchpad.tab", "title": "...", "state": <JSON>}`, with no folder, state id or profile (`storage.WorkspaceTab.Kind` is the id of the kind; `storage.ValidTabKind` is the form of one; a kind that is neither a workspace nor of that form drops the entry when the file is read). It is written when the tabs change, when the title or hint changes, when the content says `StateChanged`, when the extension ends (turned off, failed) and before the application quits, and the content is asked for its state at each of these (so it is on the UI thread). At the start `window.restoreWindows` decides: `all` and `preserve` bring the tabs of extensions back in their place with their title and state, `folders` leaves them out, `none` opens none, `one` may pick one (the active one); a kind that no extension of this Emetos has any more is left out and logged (the next write forgets it). A tab that comes back is a new activation: `Create` gets the state, and the tab id and the scope id are the same.
- **Closing.** A tab of an extension closes with no question: it has no documents, and its data is its state (`Workspaces.Close` finds no closer). The extension is told with `OnClose`, the state is dropped, and the scope is closed. Closing the last tab, if it is the tab of an extension, opens a No Folder workspace tab first (as for a workspace; Emetos never has no tab). A launch of the command line (`emetos file`) while a tab of an extension is active goes to the workspace tab used last (and brings it to the front), or opens a No Folder tab when only tabs of extensions are open (`Workspaces.launchTarget`). Quitting asks nothing of the tab and does not call `OnClose`.
- **Turning the owner off.** The tab **stays** (Emetos does not close the tabs of the user): its content goes, the box says "<Name> is turned off. Turn it on in the Extensions page to use this tab.", the state it saved is kept in the list of the tabs, and turning the extension on again activates it and `Create` gets that state. Its entry of the "+" menu and the commands go; `OpenExtensionTab` fails with `WindowTabKindDisabled`. A tab that comes back at the start with its extension off is the same.
- **Failures** stay in the scope of the tab: a panic in `Create` (`ExtensionWindowTabCreatePanicked`), in `Build` or a widget (`ExtensionViewBuildPanicked`, `ExtensionViewWidgetPanicked`), in `SaveState` (`ExtensionViewStatePanicked`) or in `OnClose` (`ExtensionWindowTabCallbackPanicked`) fails the extension in that tab: the tab shows "<Name> failed" with Show Log, one notification says so, the strip and the other tabs are untouched.
- **Dev commands** (§15.2): `dev.openWindowTab {"kind"}` opens a tab of the kind after the active tab (`DevOpenWindowTabInvalid` without a kind; `WindowTabKindUnknown`, `WindowTabKindDisabled`) and `dev.openPlusMenu` opens the menu of the "+" button (`DevOpenPlusMenuUnavailable` without a strip on screen).
- **`extensions/scratchpad`** (`emetos.scratchpad`): the kind `emetos.scratchpad.tab` ("Scratchpad", icon `note`, "+" entry **Scratchpad**). The tab has a text for notes on the left (kept in its state: `{"notes": "..."}`, written as the user types) and the feed **RECENT EDITS** on the right: it subscribes to `emetos.document.changed` of the other tabs (`FromOtherScopes`, declared in `Events.CrossTab` with `emetos.sharing.revoked`), so **nothing reaches it until the user answers the question**, which comes with the first edit made in another tab and is shown in the Scratchpad tab ("Let events from **<tab>** reach **Scratchpad**?"); Allow saves the link `<folder> -> emetos.scratchpad:<tab id>`. Each document of another tab is one row (name, then "<tab> · N changes · time"), the newest first, 40 at most; the feed is live (not saved); when a link is removed or the source goes private it says "The edits of <tab> no longer reach this tab." `NewWithClock` gives tests the clock.
- **The proof.** `docs/implemented-proof-images/11.7-window-tab-extension.png` (made with `scripts/proof.sh ... --commands '[["dev.openWindowTab",{"kind":"emetos.scratchpad.tab"}],["dev.openPlusMenu"]]' -- testdata/proof/11.7/project`): a workspace tab and a Scratchpad tab, with the menu of the "+" button open.
- **Tests and goldens.** `extension` (the manifest checks), `internal/gui/exthost/windowtabs_test.go` (kinds, scope, only the owner, state and the notice when the owner is off, close, failures, the checks of `Provide`, no status bar, the question and the link), `internal/core/storage` (the entry of the tab and `ValidTabKind`), `internal/gui/workbench` (the icon, the controller of the "+" menu, `EditorOnly`; goldens `titlebar_extension_tab_*` and `titlebar_extension_new_menu_*`), `internal/gui/app/exttab_test.go` (the "+" menu, opening, restoring, closing, the links, the tray, the picker, the keys, a failure, turning the owner off, launches, the dev commands; goldens `window_tab_extension_*` and `plus_menu_extension_*`), `extensions/scratchpad` (goldens `scratchpad_tab_*` and `scratchpad_tab_empty_*`) and `extensions/internal/fakeapi`.
- **Existing tests changed** (none weakened): `internal/core/storage/state_test.go` compares `[]WorkspaceTab` with `reflect.DeepEqual` (the struct holds a `json.RawMessage` now) and its test of a file with tabs gained entries; `internal/gui/exthost/scope_test.go` and `rig_test.go` are untouched (the new rig is in `windowtabs_test.go`).
- **Not built:** a tab of an extension that is a workspace's second view (Remote Work, M15, builds it on this API), the window geometry saved while a tab of an extension is the active one (the workspace tabs that are on screen write it when the window changes), drag of a tab out of the strip, a status bar or side bar in a window tab, the extension adding items to the menu bar of its tab beyond the commands and menu items it declares, views of the same extension in a window tab.

**Not built:** loading extensions at run time, extension processes, VS Code extensions, a marketplace or downloads (D4), typed APIs between extensions, extensions calling each other's commands, moving a view between the side bar and the panel (a view stays where its extension put it), a secondary side bar, per-profile extension lists.

It ran sessions of the user's own `claude` program (steps 13.1 to 13.3); its text as built is in the history of this file (`git show step-17.1:docs/SPEC.md`). The section number is kept so that the others do not change. ### 10.17 The Go extension (`extensions/golang`)

The Go language pack (§8.1, step 11.4) grows into what VS Code's Go extension does, on top of the language server client of area 3 (M12; its sections are written in step 12.1).
- **gopls**: the server is `gopls` from `PATH` (or `go.goplsPath`), started per workspace with Go's settings (`gopls` settings under `go.gopls`), restarted by "Go: Restart Language Server"; completion, hover, signature help, definition, references, rename, formatting and organize imports on save (`editor.formatOnSave`, `editor.codeActionsOnSave` with `source.organizeImports`), diagnostics, code actions, inlay hints and semantic tokens come through the area 3 client.
- **Tools**: "Go: Install/Update Tools" runs `go install` for `gopls`, `dlv`, `staticcheck` in a panel view with its output; a missing tool shows a notification with Install.
- **Commands**: Go: Add Tags to Struct Fields, Remove Tags, Fill Struct, Generate Unit Tests for Function (through `gopls` commands where it has them, else the tools), Toggle Test File, Test Function at Cursor, Test File, Test Package, Run, Show Go Environment.
- **Tests**: code lenses "run test | debug test" above `Test`, `Benchmark`, `Example` and `Fuzz` functions (the lenses come from the extension's own code lens provider, not from `gopls`: step 14.3); results in a panel view "Go Tests" with pass/fail per test and the output, failures in Problems; the last run can be repeated.
- **Lint and vet**: `go vet` and `staticcheck` (or `golangci-lint`, `go.lintTool`) on save into Problems (`go.lintOnSave`, `go.vetOnSave`).
- **Status bar**: the Go version of the workspace and the state of `gopls` (starting, ready, error) with a menu (Restart, Show Output).
- **Debugging** with `dlv dap` is area 6 and is not built here.

**As built (step 14.1, `extensions/golang`, `extension/{languageservers,quickpick,extension,manifest}.go`, `gui/exthost/serverapi.go`, `gui/app/extensions.go`).** gopls, the status bar item and the tools. Where the text above leaves room:
- *The extension.* `emetos.golang` is now named **Go** (it was "Go Language Basics"; the name is the source of its notifications). It wraps the language pack (`langpack.New`, so its languages, grammars and activation are what they were) and adds to its manifest the commands, the panel view, the settings, the server's own UI and the subscription to `emetos.editor.activeChanged`; its `Activate` runs the pack's and then its own. Files: `golang.go` (manifest, activation, the status item's follow-up of the editor), `settings.go`, `status.go` (the item and its menu), `tools.go` (the tools, the panel, the missing tool), `env.go` (Show Go Environment), `run.go` (programs), `gotest/` (the fake go for tests).
- *Settings* (`Manifest.Contributes.Settings`, new: declared like VS Code's `contributes.configuration`, so their keys are free; the host registers them while the extension is enabled in a tab, before it is activated, and `Settings().Get` reads them; `Settings().Register` still wants the id prefix; a key the editor or another extension has is left out with a line in the log; `CheckManifest` refuses an empty key, a type that is not a JSON type and a repeated key: `ExtensionSettingDeclInvalid`, `ExtensionSettingDeclDuplicate`). Registered, category "Go": **`go.gopls`** (object, default `{}`; the section the server reads, §9.12), `go.alternateTools` (object; `go`, `dlv` and `staticcheck` are read), `go.toolsManagement.go` (string), `go.toolsGopath` (string) and `go.toolsEnvVars` (object), with VS Code Go's descriptions; `go.goplsPath` is the host's (§9.12). **`go.gopls` is one object, not one setting per property**, as in VS Code (`"go.gopls": {"ui.semanticTokens": true}`; the object is sent to the server whole, so the 12.9 fixture's nested form works): a setting for each property would send every default to the server. The settings editor has no schema for the properties of an object, so the description lists them: `extensions/golang/gopls-settings.json` (name, type, default, enum and description of each of the 43 settings of gopls, from `golang/vscode-go` v0.59.0's `package.json`; `scripts/update-assets.sh` writes it, MIT, `NOTICE` item 5) is embedded and `goplsDescription()` makes the Markdown from it (the first paragraph of each, cut at 220 characters). Not registered, because nothing reads them yet or at all: `go.useLanguageServer` (gopls is the only provider), `go.toolsManagement.checkForUpdates` and `autoUpdate` (no update checks), `go.formatTool` (gopls formats), `go.lintTool`, `go.lintOnSave` and `go.vetOnSave` (step 14.3), `go.goroot`, `go.gopath` and the others of VS Code Go.
- *Server state for extensions* (`extension.LanguageServers`, `api.LanguageServers()`): `Status(serverID) (ServerStatus, error)` with `ServerStatus{State, Starts, Crashes, Progress}` (`State` is `ServerIdle`, `ServerStarting`, `ServerRunning`, `ServerFailed`, `ServerMissing` or `ServerStopped`; `Progress` is the text of the work done progress that runs, the same the host's own item shows: "Loading packages 40%"), `OnChange(serverID, fn(ServerStatus)) (cancel, error)` (called on the UI thread, once for a burst of changes, with the status as it is then; none after the activation ended; a panic fails the extension, `ExtensionServerCallbackPanicked`), `Restart(serverID)` (what `<id>.restartServer` does, for the menu) and `ShowOutput(serverID, preserveFocus)`. An id the manifest does not declare fails with `ExtensionServerUnknown`; a server the host has not made yet (the call is in `Activate`) is idle. `LanguageServerSpec.OwnUI` says that the extension shows the state itself: the host makes **no status bar item and no "was not found" notification** for that server (the Output line and the crash notification stay); `LanguageServerSpec.Category` is the category of the restart command ("Go" gives **"Go: Restart Language Server"**, the command `emetos.golang.restartServer` of step 12.3).
- *The list: `api.QuickPick().Show(opts, done)`* (new; the status menu needs it, and VS Code's `showQuickPick` is what its Go status item uses). `QuickPickOptions{Placeholder, Items, MatchOnDescription}`, `QuickPickItem{Label, Description, Detail, Command, Args}`; a label may start with `$(codicon)`; an item with a `Command` runs it (through the commands of the tab, arguments as given) when chosen. `done(index)` is called once on the UI thread, after the list is hidden, with the index in `Items` (an item without a label is left out and keeps its index) or `-1` when closed or replaced by another quick input (`ExtensionQuickPickInvalid` with no item to show, `ExtensionQuickPickUnavailable` in a scope that cannot show it, `ExtensionQuickPickCallbackPanicked`). The window shows it in its quick input (`exthost.ScopeOptions.QuickPick`, `app.extensionQuickPick`).
- *On save.* The **`[go]` language block of VS Code's Go extension** is merged into the package.json of the Go pack by `scripts/update-assets.sh` (so the pack, `packfs` and the tests all read the same file): `editor.insertSpaces` false, **`editor.formatOnSave` true, `editor.formatOnSaveMode` `file`, `editor.codeActionsOnSave` `{"source.organizeImports": "explicit"}`**. They are language defaults: they apply to Go files only, below the user's own values, and the save participants of §9.12 "As built (step 12.8)" do the rest (organize imports, then format, one undo step; 750 ms limits; an auto save skips both). The block is not given to `go.mod` and `go.work`, as VS Code Go does not.
- *The status bar item* (`status.go`; right side, priority 100.05, just after the language mode). It is shown **while the editor in front is a Go file** (`go`, `go.mod` or `go.work`: the language of `emetos.editor.activeChanged`; at the start a Go document among the open ones counts) and the server is not stopped. Text: `Go 1.26.1` (the version of `go env GOVERSION` without `go`; `Go` until it is known), with an icon and a word for the state of gopls: starting `$(sync~spin) Go 1.26.1`, running `$(check) Go 1.26.1`, running with work `$(sync~spin) Go 1.26.1: Loading packages 40%`, crashed five times `$(error) Go 1.26.1: gopls stopped`, not found `$(warning) Go 1.26.1: gopls not found`; no `go` program or a `go env` that fails `$(warning) Go` with the reason in the tooltip. The version is asked for off the UI thread, in the folder of the workspace, with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` (a question asked in the background never downloads a toolchain), under a 20 s limit, at the activation and again when `go.alternateTools` or `go.toolsEnvVars` change (an older, slower answer is dropped). **A click opens the menu** (the quick pick): Restart Language Server, Show gopls Output, Install/Update Tools, Show Go Environment, Open Settings (`workbench.action.openSettings` with `go.gopls`).
- *Install/Update Tools* (`emetos.golang.installTools`, "Go: Install/Update Tools"; `{"tools": ["gopls"]}` as argument installs only those, an unknown name fails with `ToolUnknown`). The tools are `gopls` (`golang.org/x/tools/gopls`), `dlv` (`github.com/go-delve/delve/cmd/dlv`) and `staticcheck` (`honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck`), all `@latest`. The **panel view "Go Tools"** (id `emetos.golang.tools`, order 50) shows before any run the list and an Install/Update Tools button, and then the run: the state of each tool (waiting, installing, installed, failed, not installed), the output of the programs as it comes, and **Cancel** while it runs (the program's whole process group is killed, the tools after it are not started). The tools are installed **one after the other**, each by `go install <package>@<version>` in a fresh temporary folder (the `go.mod` of the project must not matter; removed afterwards), under a 15 minute limit, with the environment of Emetos plus `go.toolsEnvVars` plus `GO111MODULE=on` (and `GOPATH` and `GOBIN=<go.toolsGopath>/bin` when that is set; `GOFLAGS` is left as the user has it). The program is `go.toolsManagement.go`, else the go of the project (`go.alternateTools.go`, else `go` in `PATH`); without one a notification says so and nothing runs. A run that is going on is only shown by a second command. At the end an Info notification lists what was installed, an Error one names the tools that failed (with Show Output), a cancel says so; and **when gopls was installed and its server was missing or crashed for good, the server is started again**. The summary reminds that the tools are in `GOBIN` (or `GOPATH/bin`), which must be in `PATH`: Emetos does not look in those folders itself.
- *The missing tool.* When the host says gopls was not found (`ServerMissing`; its own notification is off, `OwnUI`) the extension shows once per activation the warning "gopls was not found. It provides the language features of Go: ... Set go.goplsPath if it is somewhere else." with **Install** (installs that tool only and shows the panel). §10.17 names only Install, and an extension has no place to keep a "don't show again" answer between sessions, so there is no such choice (the notification comes back once in the next session while the tool is missing). The same function serves `dlv` and `staticcheck`, which have no trigger before the steps that use them.
- *Show Go Environment* (`emetos.golang.showEnvironment`, "Go: Show Go Environment"): the Output channel **"Go"** (made on first use) is cleared, shown, and gets `$ go env` and the lines of `go env` in the folder of the workspace as they come (60 s limit); a missing or failing go says so there. An Output channel, not a read-only document: an extension has no virtual document of its own yet.
- *Programs* (`run.go`). Every program (`go env GOVERSION`, `go env`, `go install`) runs in **a process group of its own**, with one pipe for its output and its errors (lines over 1 MiB end the output that is read), and the whole group is killed when its context ends (the activation, a Cancel, a limit) and again when the program ends, so nothing it started outlives it; the group is not left to `cmd.Wait` (which waits for the processes that hold the pipe). `ProgramNotFound`, `ProgramStartFailed` and `ProgramFailed` are the tags.
- *Tags* (each has a route test): `ExtensionServerUnknown`, `ExtensionServerCallbackPanicked`, `ExtensionQuickPickInvalid`, `ExtensionQuickPickUnavailable`, `ExtensionQuickPickCallbackPanicked`, `ExtensionSettingDeclInvalid`, `ExtensionSettingDeclDuplicate`, `ToolUnknown`, `ProgramNotFound`, `ProgramStartFailed`, `ProgramFailed`, and the test helpers `FakeGoBuildFailed` (`extensions/golang/gotest`), `FakeServerUnknown` and `FakeQuickPickInvalid` (`extensions/internal/fakeapi`).
- *Tests.* `extension` (the manifest rules), `exthost/serverapi_test.go` with the fake server (the states and progress an extension is told, Restart, ShowOutput, an unknown id, a server with its own UI and the missing program, the category of the restart command, a panicking listener and quick pick callback, declared settings registered before the activation and served to the server as its section, the quick pick's answers), `app` (the quick pick in the quick input; the Go defaults make a save organize imports and format as one undo step and leave Markdown alone), `extensions/golang` over `fakeapi` with a **fake go program** built by the tests (`gotest`, built once by `TestMain`, `PATH` an empty folder unless a test puts the fake in it, `HOME` and the XDG folders temporary; a test that has no go program has none even when the environment of the run has one, so **no test can run a real `go install`**): the status item in every state and for Go files only, the version and its re-asking (the older answer dropped), the menu, the settings, the installs one by one (arguments, folder, environment, output, failure, cancel with the group's processes gone, the end of the activation, the missing tool), Show Go Environment, the process helper (both streams, a child left behind, a line that is too long, the end of the context, the errors), goldens of the panel (`tools_{idle,running,failed}_{dark,light}`). With the build tag `emetos_gopls`: `extensions/golang/real_test.go` (the real `go env GOVERSION` and `go env`, only reads) and `gui/exthost/gopls_test.go` (the real gopls under the declaration of this extension: the states told to the extension, a restart, nothing left running).
- *Not built.* Update checks of the tools and of Go (`go.toolsManagement.checkForUpdates`, `autoUpdate`), a multi-select picker of the tools, "Go: Choose Go Environment" and the Go versions of `go.goroot`, the `go.useLanguageServer` switch, a "don't show again" choice, finding tools in `GOBIN` outside `PATH`, and a virtual document for the environment.

**As built (step 14.2, `extensions/golang/{tags,tagscmd,fillstruct,gentest,toggletest,runpanel,editor}.go`, `extension/{api,languageservers,inputbox}.go`, `gui/exthost/{api,servercommands,inputbox}.go`, `gui/app/extensions.go`).** The commands of VS Code's Go extension that gopls and the tools give. Where the text above leaves room:
- *Commands* (category "Go", ids `emetos.golang.<name>` like those of step 14.1, so VS Code Go's ids such as `go.add.tags` are not aliased; the titles are VS Code Go's, with its capitalization): `emetos.golang.addTags` "Add Tags To Struct Fields", `removeTags` "Remove Tags From Struct Fields", `fillStruct` "Fill Struct", `generateTestsForFunction` "Generate Unit Tests For Function", `toggleTestFile` "Toggle Test File" and `run` "Go: Run" (VS Code Go has no such command, so the id and the title are this step's). All are in the palette with no `when`: a command run with no Go file in front says so in a notification ("... needs a Go file: open one and put the cursor in it."; a `go.mod` is not one, it has no structs or functions). **The editor context menu** (`Menus`, group "Go group 1" as in VS Code Go, order as listed in this paragraph, `when` `editorTextFocus && editorLangId == go`) has Toggle Test File, Add Tags, Remove Tags, Fill Struct and Generate Unit Tests; Run is only in the palette. VS Code Go's `go.editorContextMenuCommands` (a switch for each item) is not built: `config.<setting>` keys of the menus read registered settings, and an object's members are not, so the items are always there for Go files.
- *The editor in front.* The commands act on the editor the user looked at last: the extension also subscribes to `emetos.editor.selectionChanged` (as the Agents extension does), keeps the URI, the language and the primary selection, and reads the text with `Documents().Read` when a command runs (the text with its unsaved changes). Positions are the events' (line and column from 0, in bytes). A command that needs a selection and has none yet (an editor that was not shown) says "click in the struct first".
- *API added to `extension/`.* `Documents().Apply(ctx, WorkspaceEdit)`: the edit goes through `langfeatures.Apply` over the window's edit host, as the edit of a rename does (one undo step for the edits of a document in a run of changes, the cursors of the editors keep their places, a document that was not open is opened with the change unsaved; `ExtensionEditInvalid` for a bad kind or URI, `ExtensionDocumentUnavailable` for a scope with no edit host). `LanguageServers().Commands(serverID)` (the commands of `executeCommandProvider` and those the server registered, sorted; empty while it does not run), `ExecuteCommand(ctx, serverID, command, args, done)` (workspace/executeCommand; it returns at once and `done(err)` is called on the UI thread, because the edits the server makes meanwhile with workspace/applyEdit need the UI thread, so the extension must not wait for the answer on it; `ExtensionServerNotRunning`, `ExtensionArgumentsInvalid`) and `ApplyCodeAction(ctx, serverID, uri, CodeActionRequest, done(title, err))`: the code actions of the kinds in `Only` at the range, the first that is not disabled and is of a kind asked for (the preferred one before the others), resolved when it has no edit and no command, its edit applied as `Documents().Apply` does and its command executed; `title` is empty when the server offers none. `InputBox().Show(InputBoxOptions{Prompt, Value, Validate}, done(value, ok))` is `showInputBox` over the quick input's prompt (`exthost.ScopeOptions.InputBox`, `app.extensionInputBox`; `ExtensionInputBoxUnavailable`, `ExtensionInputBoxCallbackPanicked` for a panic in `done` or in `Validate`). The fake of the API (`extensions/internal/fakeapi`) has all of them. The new tags are listed at the end of this paragraph.
- *Settings* (declared like those of 14.1, category "Go"): **`go.addTags`** (`tags`, `options`, `promptForTags`, `transform`, `template`; default `{"tags": "", "options": "", "promptForTags": false, "transform": "", "template": ""}`) and **`go.removeTags`** (`tags`, `options`, `promptForTags`), with VS Code Go's descriptions and defaults. The arguments of the command (`{"tags": "json", "transform": "camelcase", "promptForTags": true, ...}`) replace the members of the setting that they name, as in VS Code Go. `go.alternateTools`, `go.toolsEnvVars` and `go.toolsManagement.go` of 14.1 decide the program and the environment of Run.
- *Add Tags and Remove Tags.* The user is asked when `promptForTags` is true or when the setting has neither tags nor options: an input box "Enter comma separated tag names" and one "Enter comma separated options (tag=option)", each with the configured value in it, and for Add a list "Select transform" (snakecase, camelcase, lispcase, pascalcase, keep; the configured one is marked "default"). Closing any of them ends the command with no change (VS Code Go's Escape counts as an empty answer and removes every tag; here it cancels). An empty answer to both of Remove removes all the tags (and their options); an empty answer to both of Add says "no tags or options were given, so nothing was added". The selection is what the command acts on: with a cursor the **innermost struct type that holds it** (a cursor in the name before the keyword `struct` is in none: "the cursor is not in a struct type"), with a selection the fields it touches; a field that holds a struct that contains the range is changed too, as in gomodifytags. The text and the selection are read again after the prompts. **With gopls**: when the server runs and announces `gopls.modify_tags`, the extension executes it with `ModifyTagsArgs` (`Modification` add or remove, `URI`, `Range` in UTF-16 characters, as gopls counts them, `Add`, `AddOptions`, `Remove`, `RemoveOptions`, `Clear` and `ClearOptions` for an empty remove, `Transform`, `ValueFormat` for `template`), and gopls applies the edit; a failure is shown ("gopls failed: ...") and is not tried again here. **Otherwise** `tags.go` does it on the text of the document: it parses the file (`go/parser`; a file with syntax errors is refused), changes the tags in the syntax tree with the algorithm of gomodifytags (ported from `modifytags.go`, with the parser of `fatih/structtag` and the word splitter of `fatih/camelcase`; BSD-3-Clause and MIT, `third_party/gomodifytags/`, `NOTICE` item 14), prints the whole file the way gofmt does (`go/format`, as gopls does, so that the tags are aligned and other code that gofmt would change changes too) and applies the difference as edits, one for each line that changed (so that cursors stay), as one `Documents().Apply` (one undo step). Transforms: snakecase (the default), camelcase, lispcase, pascalcase, titlecase, keep; `template` replaces `{field}` (or the old `$field`) in the name; `json:name` in the tags gives the name; the first exported name of a field with several names names the tag; an embedded field is named by its type. The test cases are in `extensions/golang/testdata/tags/cases.json` (26 structs and arguments, in the shape of the arguments of gopls), read by the test of the pure Go editor and by the test of the real gopls (`internal/gui/exthost/gopls_test.go`, build tag `emetos_gopls`), which must give the same text: it does for 24; **for two, gopls v0.24.0 does something else, and the file says what** (`goplsDiffers`: it does not pass `SkipUnexportedFields` on to gomodifytags, and it asks a form when only `ClearOptions` is set; the commands do not offer either, only the editor in Go does).
- *Fill Struct* is `ApplyCodeAction` with the kind `refactor.rewrite.fillStruct` at the selection (anchor and active put in order), so gopls, the resolve and the undo step are those of any code action. It needs gopls to run: otherwise a warning says in what state it is ("needs gopls, which is not installed (see Go: Install/Update Tools)"); an answer with no action says "gopls offers nothing to fill at the cursor. Put it in a struct literal with fields that are not set."
- *Generate Unit Tests For Function* (`gentest.go`) writes the test of the function whose declaration (with its doc comment) holds the cursor, as the template of gotests does, with no tool to install (VS Code Go asks gotests or the addTest action of gopls; its `go.generateTestsFlags` is not read, and "for File" and "for Package" are not built). The test is `TestFoo`, `Test_foo` for an unexported function, `TestRecv_Method` and `Test_recv_method` for an unexported receiver type; a table `tests` with `name`, `fields` (when the receiver is a struct found in the file or in the other non-test files of the package folder, at most 500 of at most 4 MiB, read from disk; else a field named as the receiver variable holds the receiver), `args` (the parameters, `in1`, `in2`, ... for those with no name or `_`, a variadic one as a slice and called with `...`), `want`, `want1`, ... for the results that are not the error and `wantErr` when the last result is `error`, and `// TODO: Add test cases.`; the call, the check of the error (`return` after it when there are results) and `reflect.DeepEqual` of each result (the messages `Foo() = %v, want %v`, `Recv.Method() got1 = %v, want %v`). A receiver struct with fields gets `type fields struct` and `f := &Recv{A: tt.fields.A, ...}`. The function is printed with `go/format`. Imports: `testing`, `reflect` when there are results, and the packages the types in the test use that the source file imports (the name of a package is guessed from its path: the last element without a major version, `.v3`, `go-` or `-go`; a guess that fails leaves the import out). **A new test file** is written whole with `O_EXCL` (package clause, one import block with the standard library apart, the function), not through the document API, so that no empty Go file is left on disk if it is not saved. **An existing test file** (on disk, or open with unsaved text) is read with `Documents().Read` and the test is added with `Documents().Apply` (one undo step, the file stays unsaved): the function at the end after a blank line, and the imports it lacks in the order of the paths into the group of the standard library or of the others of the first import block, as a new group, or in a block made of a single `import "x"`, or after the package clause; an empty file is replaced by a whole test file; a file that does not parse is refused. A test of that name that exists already is not added: the file is shown at it and a notification says so. The file is shown with the cursor on the line of the new test (`Documents().Show`, not a preview). Not supported, with a notification: a generic function or a method of a generic type, a function in a test file, a cursor outside a function. Not done: the special case of `io.Writer` parameters of gotests, subtests flags, templates.
- *Toggle Test File* shows `foo_test.go` for `foo.go` and `foo.go` for `foo_test.go`. VS Code Go opens the path and leaves the missing file to VS Code's error; here **a file that is not there is made with the package clause alone** (`package foo`; for a `foo_test` package the name without `_test`; written whole with `O_EXCL` like a new test file), without asking, and a notification says so; a source without a package clause makes nothing and says so. An open document with no file on disk counts as there.

### 10.18 Remote Work: remote control of a workspace (`extensions/remotework`)

One workspace of an Emetos on laptop A can be used from an Emetos on laptop B, as its own view (D19). **Its name is "Remote Work"** everywhere it shows, on both laptops (the user's choice): the extension `emetos.remotework` on the Extensions page, the page "Remote Work" on A, the `+` menu entry "Remote Work..." on B, the banner "Remote Work: <key comment> connected"; a tab on B is titled `<host>: <workspace>` with a remote icon. The extension holds the login, the transport and the protocol (`extensions/remotework/...`, with `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` and `github.com/quic-go/quic-go`); the second view comes from a new `extension/` call, `api.Workspace().NewHeadlessView(size)` (implemented in `internal/gui/app`), which gives the frames of a view of the workspace rendered off screen, takes input events and resizes, and is closed with the session. The Remote Work page and the remote window tab are the extension's contributions (§10.15).
- **On A**: the page "Remote Work" (command `emetos.remotework.manage`) turns Remote Work on or off per workspace, sets the port (default 47123, the same number for TCP and UDP), the idle timeout (default 30 minutes) and the list of allowed SSH public keys (`authorized_keys` lines, each with its comment shown). They are kept in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/remote-work.json` (mode 0600), written only by that page; no settings file can turn Remote Work on. A listens only while at least one workspace has Remote Work on. A banner in that workspace shows "Remote Work: <key comment> connected" with Disconnect, every login and every refused attempt is logged and raises a notification, and failed attempts are rate-limited (5 per minute per address).
- **On B**: the `+` menu of the window tab strip has "Remote Work..." (a window tab kind of the extension): host, port and the private key file (or the SSH agent); the tab shows `<host>: <workspace>` with a remote icon and reconnects after a dropped connection.
- **Login (SSH).** A runs an embedded SSH server (`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh`) on TCP: public-key login only, with the allowed keys; no shell, no port forwarding, one channel type `emetos-remotework` and nothing else. A's SSH host key (Ed25519, made when Remote Work is first turned on, kept with mode 0600) is pinned on B like `known_hosts` (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/remote-work-hosts.json`): the first connection shows the fingerprint to compare with A's page, a changed one is refused with a warning. B reads the private key itself (OpenSSH format, a passphrase asked in a dialog) or uses `ssh-agent` (`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent`).
- **The session.** Over the authenticated SSH channel A sends B a 256-bit random session token (kept only in memory on both sides) and the SHA-256 fingerprint of A's QUIC certificate (self-signed, made at start). B then opens **QUIC** (`github.com/quic-go/quic-go`, TLS 1.3 inside, UDP, same port) and presents the token; B accepts A's certificate only if it matches that fingerprint. The token expires on disconnect, on the idle timeout, and when Remote Work is turned off; a dropped QUIC connection is resumed with it while the SSH connection lives. When UDP does not get through (no QUIC handshake within 3 s), the session runs over SSH channels instead (TCP fallback), with the same messages.
- **The view.** B's tab size makes A open a **second view of the workspace** at that size (its own focus, cursor and scroll; the same documents, so both users see each other's edits), rendered off screen (Glutter's `offscreen.View`, its software renderer) when it changes. A sends the 64x64 tiles that changed since the frame B confirmed, compressed (deflate), as QUIC **datagrams** (latest picture wins: no queue of old frames; a lost tile is repaired by the next frame and by a full refresh every 5 s); input (keys with their text, so layouts and IME work; mouse; scroll), clipboard text (only on copy and paste), notifications of the workspace (with their actions, run on A) and control messages (resize, ping, disconnect with a reason) go on reliable QUIC streams. The protocol is versioned, length-prefixed, with a size limit on every message, and the code that runs before login is minimal.
- **Security** (what the user must know, also on the page): a listed key gives the power of the user in that workspace (edit and delete files, run tasks); the first connection is as safe as comparing the fingerprint; over the internet it is as safe as SSH with key-only login, and a VPN is better still.
- **Public keys by QR code** (here and in Relay, §10.19; code shared in `extensions/internal/keyqr`). Wherever an allowed key is added, next to pasting the `authorized_keys` line or choosing a `.pub` file there is a **Scan QR Code** button: it opens a dialog with the live picture of the machine's camera (read directly through Linux's V4L2 interface with `golang.org/x/sys/unix`, cgo-free; MJPEG frames decoded with `image/jpeg`, YUYV converted; about 10 frames a second, decoded off the UI thread), a picker when there are several cameras, and closes as soon as a QR code holding a valid public key line is seen (decoded with `github.com/makiuchi-d/gozxing`, the line parsed with `ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey`), showing the key's type, fingerprint and comment to confirm before it is added. The camera is opened only while the dialog is open and released when it closes; no frame is kept or sent anywhere. A machine with no camera shows the button disabled with the reason. The other side of the flow: where a client chooses its key (Remote Work's "Remote Work..." dialog on B, Relay's Add Host), **Show My Public Key as QR Code** shows the public half of the chosen key (or of an `ssh-agent` key) as a QR code (encoded with gozxing) to scan from the host's camera; the private key never leaves the client.
- **Not built:** sharing more than one workspace per session, sound, file drag and drop between the laptops, a mirror of A's own view.

**As built (step 15.1, `extensions/remotework/protocol`, `extensions/remotework/tiles`, `extension/headless.go`, `gui/exthost/builtin.go`, `gui/app/{headless,headless_clipboard,viewworkspace}.go`).** The message format, the tile differ and the second view; the login (15.2), the transport (15.3) and the tab on B (15.4) are the steps after it. Where the text above leaves room:

- **The wire format** (`protocol`, which imports nothing of Emetos but the errors package, so Relay and the tests of the transports can use it). A message is `type:1 | length:4 | payload`, the length big endian and checked against the limit of the type before the payload is read or allocated. Integers are big endian, floats IEEE 754 binary32, texts UTF-8 and never padded. The type numbers are on the wire (a change is a new `Version`, 1):

  | # | Type | Payload (bytes) | Limit |
  |---|------|-----------------|-------|
  | 1 | `Hello` | magic `EMRW` 4, version u16, token length u8, token (at most 64) | 128 |
  | 2 | `Tile` | frame u64, base u64, width u16, height u16, x u16, y u16, total u32, deflated pixels (the rest, 1 to 17,408) | 17,436 |
  | 3 | `FrameConfirm` | frame u64 (at least 1) | 16 |
  | 4 | `Refresh` | none | 0 |
  | 5 | `Key` | kind u8 (0 down, 1 up, 2 repeat), physical u64 (USB HID usage), logical u64 (Glutter's key id), text length u8 and text (at most 32) | 64 |
  | 6 | `Mouse` | kind u8 (0 move, 1 down, 2 up), buttons u8 (bits 1 primary, 2 secondary, 4 middle), x f32, y f32 | 16 |
  | 7 | `Scroll` | x, y, dx, dy f32 | 32 |
  | 8 | `Clipboard` | text (the rest, UTF-8) | 1 MiB |
  | 9 | `Notification` | id u64, severity u8 (0 info, 1 warning, 2 error), source (u16 length, at most 128), message (u16 length, at most 4096), actions u8 (at most 8), each label (u16 length, at most 128) | 8 KiB |
  | 10 | `NotificationAction` | id u64, action u8 (below 8) | 16 |
  | 11 | `Resize` | width u16, height u16 | 8 |
  | 12 | `Ping` | seq u64, reply u8 (0 or 1) | 16 |
  | 13 | `Disconnect` | reason u8 (0 closed, 1 host, 2 idle, 3 off, 4 protocol, 5 version, 6 replaced, 7 workspace closed), text (u16 length, at most 256) | 512 |
  | 14 | `Missing` | frame u64, total u32 (1 to 4,096), bitmap of (total+7)/8 bytes: a bit set for each tile of the picture the client lacks (step 15.3) | 524 |

  The largest message is 5 bytes and 1 MiB (`protocol.MaxMessage`). A picture is at most 7680 pixels a side and 3840x2160 pixels (`ValidSize`); a tile is 64x64 pixels of 4 bytes (R, G, B, A of `image.RGBA`, the view being opaque), the ones at the right and bottom edges smaller.
- **What the decoder guarantees.** `Decode` (one message that fills a datagram) and `Reader.Next` (a stream) look at the 5 bytes first and refuse a type that is not one of the 14 (13 in step 15.1; `Missing` is the 14th, step 15.3) (`RemoteWorkUnknownType`: the two sides have the same version, so there is nothing to skip; the stream is closed after any error, as the format cannot find the next message) and a length over the limit of its type (`RemoteWorkTooLarge`), before anything of the payload is read. The reader's buffer is at most the limit of the type it reads, is dropped after a message over 64 KiB, and a header that lies costs no allocation (tested). Then the payload must be exactly what the fields need (`RemoteWorkTruncated`, `RemoteWorkTrailing`) and every field valid (`RemoteWorkBadValue`: an enum or flag out of range, a text that is not UTF-8, a float that is NaN or infinite, a size of 0 or over the limits, a tile outside its picture or a frame number that is 0 or not above its base; `RemoteWorkBadMagic`; a count or text over its limit is `RemoteWorkTooLarge`). The format is canonical, so what decodes encodes back to the same bytes (checked on 20,000 seeded random and mutated inputs and by the fuzz target), and `Append` refuses what `Decode` would (`RemoteWorkEncodeInvalid`, `RemoteWorkEncodeTooLarge`, `RemoteWorkNilMessage`). A peer is checked by version with `Hello.Check` (`RemoteWorkVersion`: the versions must be equal). Stream failures are `RemoteWorkReadFailed` and `RemoteWorkWriteFailed` (the cause, such as `io.EOF`, is kept for `errors.Is`). Encoding into a buffer that is large enough allocates nothing (tested).
- **The pictures** (`tiles`). The host's `Differ` is given each new picture and returns the `Tile` messages of the tiles that differ from the picture the client confirmed, each deflated **on its own**, so a lost tile costs no other (measured at `BestSpeed`: tiles of their own make a whole picture 6% smaller than one deflate stream for it). It keeps hashes of the tiles (`hash/maphash`) and no pictures: 8 bytes a tile for each of the last 16 pictures sent and not confirmed (33 KB at 1280x800, 261 KB at 4K). Frames are numbered from 1; `Tile.Base` is the last frame the host knows the client confirmed (0: the tile is of a whole picture), so a lost tile is sent again by the next picture, which has every tile that differs from the confirmed one, not only the ones that changed since the last. `Next` returns frame 0 and no tiles when nothing differs and nothing is unconfirmed, and when the picture is back to the confirmed one but unconfirmed pictures were sent (the client may show tiles of them) it sends one tile so that the client completes a picture and puts the others back. `Refresh()` makes the next picture a whole one (the periodic refresh of every 5 s, which the session of 15.3 times; the client keeps its picture), `Reset()` forgets what the client has (it sent `Refresh`), a size change does the same, and a confirm the host does not know (`Confirm` returns false: older than the last 16) makes the next picture a whole one. The client's `Canvas` shows tiles as they arrive, drops a tile whose frame is older than the newest it saw or whose base is not its confirmed frame (`Stale`; `StaleRun` counts them, and a client that sees it grow sends `Refresh`), ignores a repeated tile (`Duplicate`), and when the newest frame's last tile arrives (`Complete`) keeps the tiles as its confirmed picture, puts back the tiles an older, unfinished frame changed that this one does not, and says to send `FrameConfirm`. It inflates at most the size of the tile (`TilesDataSize`, `TilesInflateFailed`: a bomb costs the size of a tile) and keeps two pictures (8 MB at 1280x800). A lossy-link simulation (20% of the tiles lost, repeated and reordered, confirms late or lost) checks that every complete picture is exactly the picture of its frame and that the canvas converges.
- **Measured** (`tiles/testdata`: three 1280x800 pictures of a headless view over a Go file, `go test -v -run TestARealEditor ./extensions/remotework/tiles`; the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 of the development machine). At `flate.DefaultCompression`, which `tiles.Level` is: a whole picture is 260 tiles and 113 KB (the pixels are 4.1 MB; 435 bytes a tile) in 7.8 ms; one typed character is 7 tiles (the line, the caret, the dot of the tab, the position in the status bar and the minimap) and 6.0 KB in 0.44 ms; a scroll of four notches is 132 tiles and 129 KB in 6.4 ms; applying a whole picture on the client takes 2.9 ms. The other levels, for the pictures of the same three cases: `BestSpeed` 132 KB, 6.9 KB and 147 KB in 5.3 ms for the whole picture (14% and 12% larger, half the time); `BestCompression` 110 KB, 5.7 KB and 125 KB, in 73 ms for the whole picture (2.4% smaller, seven times as long); `HuffmanOnly` 795 KB, 25 KB and 486 KB. The default was chosen: the encoder runs on a goroutine of its own, the pictures come at most a dozen a second (below), and the bytes are what a lossy link pays for. A tile is 435 bytes on average and 850 where text is, and at most 17 KB, which is more than a datagram: step 15.3 cuts the ones that do not fit into fragments (below).
- **The headless view** (`api.Workspace().NewHeadlessView(size)`; `extension.HeadlessView`). The API is `extension/headless.go` (`Size`, `KeyEvent`, `PointerEvent`, `ScrollEvent`, `HeadlessView` with `Size`, `OnFrame`, `Refresh`, `Resize`, `SendKey`, `SendPointer`, `SendScroll`, `SetClipboard`, `OnCopy`, `Done` and `Close`; every method may be called from any goroutine, `NewHeadlessView` is called on the UI thread); `exthost` checks the size (positive, at most `MaxHeadlessSide` a side and `MaxHeadlessPixels`: `ExtensionHeadlessSize`), asks the workspace (`ScopeOptions.NewHeadlessView`; `ExtensionHeadlessUnavailable` for a scope that has none) and closes the view with the activation (`ExtensionDeactivated` after it); `extensions/internal/fakeapi` has a fake (`HeadlessViews`, `Emit`, `Copy`, the recorded input). Every extension that is activated in a workspace may call it (the privileges of 16.1 are only about events and commands); the compiled-in extensions are trusted, D18.
  - *A second binding in the same thread.* The view is an `offscreen.View` of Glutter (since Glutter 1.9.1; "As built (Glutter 1.9.1)" below): a second Glutter binding of its own (a `widgets.WidgetsBinding` over a dispatcher with no window) that shares the application's UI thread, so it has its own focus manager, hardware keyboard, gesture arena, overlay and animations, and the focus, the cursor and the scroll of its editors are its own. The view asks for its frames itself (at most `MaxFrameRate` a second), and the UI thread runs its work between the application's, so the documents and models both views share are touched by one thread only. The text engine is the application's, so the view looks like the window; its locales, text scale, brightness and fonts are copied from the application's when the view is made (`viewSetup`, the root of the view, does it before the shell reads them). **The caret of the view does not blink** (the platform configuration of the view sets Glutter's caret blink to never, and the editors of a view get `editor.cursorBlinking` `solid` whatever the setting says; a blink is a picture twice a second for a client that sees none of it, and a view nobody types in makes no frames, tested). The window of the view has no decoration, is maximized and has the focus (no title bar, no buttons; the menu bar has a row of its own; `applyWindow`) and it cannot end the application.
  - *The view's workspace* (`newViewWorkspace`) is a `Workspace` of its own with `viewOf` set, so that the shell of the window runs on it unchanged: the process, the folder and its model, the settings, snippets, theme, **documents**, notifications, problems, keybindings, file operations and the copy memory of the editors are the parent's (an edit is in both views, a document stays open while either shows it, and the editors count their uses of it); the commands (a fork of the process's, so what the view's shell binds is the view's), menus, context keys, focus scopes, key dispatcher (a pending chord is the view's), layout, views, dialogs, quick input, status bar, find switches, zoom (it starts at `window.zoomLevel` and the zoom commands change the view's only, whatever `window.zoomPerWindow` says) and recent files are its own. The shell of a view (`initView`) has the editor group (starting with the documents of the parent's active group, the one in front first), the menus, the panels, the Explorer, the quick input, the status bar and the save commands, and no tab strip, backups, auto save, UI state, closing, launches, dev commands or folder watcher (the parent's keeps both up to date). The commands that act on Emetos itself (quit, the window tabs, other workspaces, new window) are not bound in it, so the registry refuses them (tested); Save As asks for the path in the quick input and links open nothing (`FileChooserUnavailable`, `HeadlessOpenURIUnavailable`: the desktop of the host is not the screen of the user). **Not in the view:** the contributions of the extensions (their commands, views, menu items and status items live in the scope the parent holds; the view has the editor, the Explorer, the Problems and Output panels and the commands of the workspace), and a view of a view. The view closes when the workspace closes or opens another folder (`Done`).
  - *Input* is delivered as the platform delivers it: a key is a `ui.KeyData` through `PlatformDispatcher.DispatchKeyData` (the character of the key is what the editor and the text fields type, so layouts and input methods work, and a shortcut goes through the dispatcher of the view's workspace), a mouse event and a scroll are `ui.PointerData` through `DispatchPointerDataPacket` with the rules of Glutter's Linux backend (the pointer is added at its first event, a hover is a move while a button is down, the first button is a down and the last one an up, a scroll is a signal of a hover), so menus, dialogs, the quick input, the editor and the scroll bars take them as they take a user's. A copy or cut in the view calls `OnCopy`; a paste takes what `SetClipboard` set. The **clipboard of the view is its own** (`viewClipboard`, `clipboardParent`): what its user copies, and the primary selection, stay in the view, and what its client sent is what a paste reads, so a client never reads or replaces the clipboard or the primary selection of the desktop of the host, in the editors and in the input boxes alike ("As built (Glutter 1.9.1)" below).
  - *Frames.* A frame is made when the view asked for one, at most 30 a second (`headlessFrameRate`, Glutter's `ViewOpts.MaxFrameRate`: the old cap of 33 ms). The UI thread builds, lays out, paints and detaches the scene; Glutter draws it on a goroutine of the view into a surface that redraws only the damage and calls `frame` with the pixels, which copies them (the image is the view's own and is drawn into again as soon as the call returns) and hands the copy to the function of `OnFrame` on that same goroutine, one call at a time; a slow function costs the view the pictures in between, never UI thread time. The first picture, and the first after a resize, are handed over whole; a frame that changes no pixel makes no call. The numbers are in "As built (Glutter 1.9.1)" below. The memory of a view is its widgets, the surface (4 MB at 1280x800) and the copy of the latest picture (which `Refresh` hands over again), plus the pictures the extension holds. `Close` takes the widgets away on the UI thread (so the editors release their documents), ends the goroutine of the view and is the same as the end of the activation.
  - *Pictures* are those of `image.RGBA`; the three goldens (`internal/gui/app/testdata/goldens/headless_{editor,typed,scrolled}.png`) are the picture of a view over `testdata/headless/project`, and copies of them are the fixtures of `tiles`; the golden test compares the pictures the view hands over (drawn by the damage of its frames) with them, and runs under the race detector too.
- **Decisions of this step:** a fixed 4-byte length, not a varint (a datagram is one message; the header is 5 bytes); an unknown type is refused, not skipped; the version must be equal; frames are of the confirmed picture and carry what changed since it (not since the last sent); a tile is deflated alone at the default level; hashes, not pictures, on the host; the view shares the theme of the workspace (the window has none of its own beyond the settings) and has its own zoom; the view draws with the application's fonts; no blink; the caps above; the keys of a client are delivered with their text, and an input method's composition is not a message of its own (the client sends what it committed).
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `RemoteWorkUnknownType`, `RemoteWorkTooLarge`, `RemoteWorkTruncated`, `RemoteWorkTrailing`, `RemoteWorkBadValue`, `RemoteWorkBadMagic`, `RemoteWorkVersion`, `RemoteWorkReadFailed`, `RemoteWorkWriteFailed`, `RemoteWorkEncodeInvalid`, `RemoteWorkEncodeTooLarge`, `RemoteWorkNilMessage` (`protocol`); `TilesLevelInvalid`, `TilesSizeInvalid`, `TilesCompressFailed`, `TilesInflateFailed`, `TilesDataSize`, `TilesInconsistent` (`tiles`); `ExtensionHeadlessSize`, `ExtensionHeadlessUnavailable` (`exthost`, the app and the fake), `HeadlessRasterFailed`, `HeadlessOpenURIUnavailable`, `FileChooserUnavailable` (the view's Save As; the tag Glutter's desktop gives too) (`app`).
- **Not built here:** the transports and their datagrams (15.3), the notifications of the workspace as messages (the API gives the view's own toasts in the picture; the host's `Notify` service is what 15.4 forwards), the clipboard messages' use, the contributions of extensions in the view, damage-limited rendering (needs Glutter, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`), a view for a workspace that is not on screen (it needs a shell: `ExtensionHeadlessUnavailable`).


**As built (Glutter 1.9.1, `gui/app/{headless,headless_clipboard}.go`).** Glutter 1.9.1 has a public way to draw a view off screen (`offscreen.NewView`, its SPEC §9.9 and D28), so the workaround of step 15.1 is gone: the hand-made binding of the view and the platform host that drove its frames (`headlessEngine`, `headlessHost`; only a parent binding that holds the view's clipboard is left, below), the rasterizer made of a `gluttertest.Tester` that was replaced every eight frames (`rasterizer`, `rasterRecycle`), the pace of `headlessPaceFactor`, the delivery goroutine and the entry of `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`. The editor binary no longer links `gluttertest` (`go list -deps ./cmd/emetos | grep gluttertest` prints nothing; `testing` is still linked, by a non-test file of Glutter's own `internal/platform/linux/dl`: `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`). The API of `extension.HeadlessView` is the same (the notes of its comments about the pace are updated). Decisions:

- **How the view runs.** `makeHeadlessView` calls `offscreen.NewView(main, size, root, frame, ViewOpts{DevicePixelRatio: 1, MaxFrameRate: 30})` on the UI thread, with the shell of the view's workspace under `viewSetup` as the root. Input goes to `View.Binding().PlatformDispatcher()` as before (`DispatchKeyData`, `DispatchPointerDataPacket`), a resize is `SetSize`, and `Close` is `View.Close` (on the UI thread; it waits for a running `frame`, so `frame` never waits for the UI thread). `frame` copies the picture (4 MB at 1280x800, new for each frame: the extension keeps it) and calls the function of `OnFrame`, so `Refresh` hands over the last copy again. `callMu` keeps the calls one at a time, as `OnFrame` promises, between a frame, the picture that waited for the function and `Refresh`.
- **Pace: 30 frames a second**, Glutter's own limit (`MaxFrameRate`), which is the old cap of the SPEC; the factor of 2 times the last picture is not needed now that the drawing is not on the UI thread. An idle view makes no frames (`TestAViewNobodyTypesInMakesNoFrames`).
- **The caret stays solid.** Glutter 1.9.1 damages one tile for a blink, but the view would still make a frame, copy 4 MB, hash the tiles and send a tile every 500 ms for as long as a client is connected, for a client that sees a solid caret anyway; the platform configuration of the view sets the caret blink to never and the editors keep `cursorBlinking` `solid`.
- **Glutter's configuration is not the application's.** An `offscreen.View` starts with the default platform configuration and a window that is not activated, so `viewSetup` (the root of the view, whose state starts before the shell) copies the fonts, locales, text scale and brightness from the application and sets the window (no decoration, activated, maximized), and `Resize` sets the window again after `SetSize`, which replaces it (`// Glutter:` comments, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`).
- **The clipboard** of an `offscreen.View` is the one of the binding it was given as its parent, which would be the application's: a client could read the clipboard and the primary selection of the desktop of the host (Ctrl+V, Shift+Insert or the check whether there is something to paste in the quick input or the find widget, which are Glutter's `EditableText`) and would replace them with what it copies, and `OnCopy` and `SetClipboard` would have nothing to work on. The parent of a view is therefore not the application's binding but `clipboardParent`: a `widgets.WidgetsBinding` of its own that never draws (its platform host is `clipboardHost`, which ignores frames and exit and posts to the application's UI thread) and shares the application's UI thread, error reporter, debug flags, assets and text engine. Its platform host is the `viewClipboard`, a `ui.ClipboardHost` and `ui.RichClipboardHost` that holds the view's own system clipboard, primary selection, images and URIs, so every path that reaches a clipboard from the view (the editors, the copy of a path, the Explorer's files, `EditableText`'s copy, cut, paste, primary selection and paste check) is the view's, with no widget changed. A text put on the system clipboard of the view goes to `OnCopy`. `TestTheInputBoxesOfAViewNeverTouchTheClipboardOfTheHost` (the quick input and the find widget, Ctrl+V and Shift+Insert, copy and cut, with sentinels on the host's clipboard and primary selection) and the test of the editors prove it, and `TestTheInputBoxesOfTheWindowKeepTheClipboardOfTheDesktop` that the window's boxes still use the desktop's. The input boxes have no middle-click paste and no context menu, so the selection's write to the primary selection and the pastes are all there is.
- **Damage is not used by the tile differ.** `offscreen.Frame.Damage` says what a frame redrew, but Glutter 1.9.1 damages the whole picture for a typed character and for a scroll of the editor (Glutter's step 29.6 notes it: typing damages the whole surface); only the animation of the minimap's slider gives a small rectangle (4.6% of the picture). Hashing 1280x800 takes 0.19 ms of the 0.52 ms the differ needs for a typed character, so even a perfect damage would save at most a third of the differ's time, on the encoder's goroutine, and the API (`OnFrame`, `Presenter.Present`, the differ's `Next`) would have to carry the union of the damage of the frames that were dropped, with a full diff for a resize, a refresh and a reset. That is not worth it now; when Glutter damages only what changed, the differ can take the rectangles (it keeps the hashes of the previous picture, which is all it needs).
- **Threads and the race detector.** The UI thread does only build, layout, paint and detach; the drawing and `OnFrame` are on the goroutine of the view. The headless tests pass under `go test -race -count=5`, and so does the golden test, which was skipped under the race detector because the old rasterizer was 100 times slower there (`raceEnabled` is gone).
- **Measured** (`BenchmarkHeadlessFrame`, a 1280x800 view over a Go file, the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 of the development machine). After a typed character the UI thread spends **4.7 ms** on the view (build, layout, paint and detach; the window's own rebuild for the same edit, 2.1 ms, is not in it) and the picture is in the hand of `OnFrame` **20 ms** after the key, so the drawing, on the goroutine of the view, takes about 13 ms; a step of the wheel in the editor costs the UI thread 2.5 ms and the picture comes after 25 ms (about 22 ms of drawing). A typed character and a whole picture cost the same, because the damage is the whole picture. With the workaround on Glutter 1.9.1 (its faster software renderer) the UI thread paid 2.7 ms for the build and 20.5 ms for the picture, 23 ms in all; with Glutter 1.8.3 it paid 82 ms for the picture. At 30 frames a second a view that is typed in takes 14% of the UI thread at most (it was a third, with the pace) and a smaller view costs less. Binary: 89,657,808 bytes before, 89,381,256 after (88,613,688 and 88,331,360 with `glutter_release`).

**As built (step 15.2, `extensions/internal/sshlogin`, `extensions/internal/statefile`, `extensions/remotework`, `extensions/remotework/{login,loginui}`, `extension/banners.go`, `gui/exthost/banners.go`, `gui/workbench/banners.go`, `gui/app/extensions.go`).** The login, the page and the banner; the transport (15.3) and the tab on B (15.4) come after it. `golang.org/x/crypto` v0.58.0 (`ssh`, `ssh/agent`) is the one new dependency. Where the text above leaves room:

- **The server on A** (`sshlogin.Server`, shared with Relay; the channel type is a parameter). *Login:* public keys only. The configuration has a `PublicKeyCallback` and a `VerifiedPublicKeyCallback` and no password, keyboard-interactive or GSSAPI callback, and `NoClientAuth` is false, so the server advertises `publickey` alone (a client with a password stops after "none"). Keys are compared by their wire bytes (`SameKey`), against the list read at each attempt, so a key taken out of the list stops working at once; a certificate never matches. The key that logs in is the one that passed `VerifiedPublicKeyCallback` (the signature was checked), not the last one asked about. The host key algorithm is Ed25519 only, `MaxAuthTries` is 5, the user name is ignored (a client sends `emetos`). *Channels and requests:* after the login one channel of the type the server was made for is accepted, with at most 256 bytes of open data, a second one is refused (`ResourceShortage`), a channel of any other type (`session`, `direct-tcpip`, ...) is refused and the connection is closed, every channel request (`shell`, `exec`, `pty-req`, `env`, `subsystem`, forwarding) is refused and the connection is closed, and every global request (keepalive, `tcpip-forward`) gets a refusal. *Deadlines:* 10 s for the connection to finish logging in, 10 s for a logged-in client to open the channel (then it is closed), at most 16 connections logging in at once (the 17th is closed before the handshake). *The rate limit* (`sshlogin.Limiter`): 5 failed attempts in a sliding minute block an address, and a blocked address's connections are closed at the accept, before any handshake work; an attempt is a failed public key (or any other method), and a connection that ends before it tried anything (a scanner, a timeout, a bad signature, a client that dropped the connection at the host key, as one does on first use) counts as one. An IPv6 address counts as its /64 and an IPv4-mapped one as the IPv4. The limiter keeps at most 4096 addresses (the oldest is forgotten for a new one) and at most 5 times for each, forgets an address a minute after its last failure, and takes its clock as a parameter. *Logging and events:* every login and every refusal is a line of the log (`slog`, with the address, the key's fingerprint and comment; never a password, a token or a passphrase) and a call of `OnLogin` and `OnRefused`; the reasons are `KeyNotListed`, `KeyRefused`, `PasswordRefused`, `MethodRefused`, `HandshakeFailed`, `RateLimited`, `ChannelType`, `Request`, `NoChannel` and `TooManyPending`. A block is logged once for each address and window, not for every refused connection.
- **A's host key** (`LoadOrCreateHostKey`): an Ed25519 key in OpenSSH format in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/remote-work-host-key`, made the first time it is needed, **when the page opens or Remote Work is first turned on** (so the user can read the fingerprint before the first client asks), with mode 0600 in a folder of mode 0700. An existing file that is not a regular file, that the group or others can read or write, that is over 64 KiB or is not an Ed25519 key is refused and never replaced.
- **The client** (`sshlogin.Dial`, `KeyFileAuth`, `AgentAuth`, `HostStore`). The client never reads `~/.ssh`, `~/.ssh/config`, `known_hosts` or the environment: the caller names the key file and the agent socket (`AgentSocket(os.Getenv)` reads `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`). *Key file:* OpenSSH or PEM, at most 64 KiB; a passphrase is asked by a `PassphraseFunc(attempt)` up to 3 times, the bytes are overwritten as soon as the key is parsed and are never stored or logged, a wrong one gives `SSHLoginWrongPassphrase` after the third try, a cancel `SSHLoginPassphraseCancelled`. (The text box of the dialog holds the text as a Go string, which cannot be overwritten; the dialog clears the box and lets go of it when it is answered. The limit is the garbage collector's.) The permissions of a key file are not checked: it is the user's own file, chosen by the user. *Agent:* `AgentAuth(ctx, socket, fingerprint)` connects to the socket and offers every key of the agent in its order, or only the one with the fingerprint; `AgentKeys` lists them (for the "Show My Public Key as QR Code" of 15.5). *Pinning* (`HostStore`, `remote-work-hosts.json`, `{"version":1,"hosts":{"host:port":{"type","fingerprint","key","firstSeen"}}}`, the key of a pin is the address as typed with the host in lower case): `Dial` connects; a host that is not pinned drops the connection at the host key, before any login is sent, and the user is asked through `ConfirmHost(FirstUse{Address, Type, Fingerprint})` with **no connection open** (so the question may take as long as the user needs and A never waits for a person; the first-use connection counts as one failed attempt for A's rate limit); on yes the key is pinned and the connection is made again; a key that differs from the pin is refused with `SSHLoginHostKeyChanged` (metadata `pinned` and `presented`), before anything is sent, and never put to the user as a question; `HostStore.Forget(addr)` is what the user chooses after reading the warning (the next connection is a first use again). The host key algorithm of the client is Ed25519 only. Several calls of one store are serialized and each reads the file again.
- **The conversation on the channel** (`remotework/login`).
