The client opens the channel `emetos-remotework` with `Request` (one version byte and the workspace name, at most 200 bytes; empty asks for the only one), and A answers with one `Grant`: a 4-byte big endian length (at most 8 KiB) and a strict JSON object (`version`, `status`, `workspace`, `token`, `certSha256`, `workspaces`; an unknown field, a second value, a wrong version or an invalid combination is refused). `status` is `ok` (the workspace granted, the 256-bit token, and the SHA-256 fingerprint of the QUIC certificate, which is empty when A offers no QUIC, which 15.3 turns into the SSH-channel fallback), `none` (no workspace has Remote Work on), `ambiguous` (several do and none was named; the names are listed) or `unknown` (the name is not one of them; the names are listed). `login.Connect` is the client's call (Dial, open, read the grant with a 15 s limit; a denial is `RemoteWorkLoginDenied` with the status and the names in its metadata). The workspaces are named by the name of their folder, or by the whole folder when two share the name. After the grant the channel carries the messages of `protocol` (15.3's fallback); when A ends a session it writes a `Disconnect` with the reason (`host`, `idle`, `off`, `replaced`, `workspace closed`) and closes the connection, and gives the client 2 s to take it.
- **The session** (`remotework.Hub`, `Session`). The token is 32 bytes of `crypto/rand`, kept in memory only (never written to a state file or the log), valid while the session lives: it expires the moment the session is asked to end (`SessionByToken` compares in constant time and skips an ended session), on disconnect, on the idle timeout (`Session.Touch` starts it again; the transport of 15.3 calls it for every message; the timer is `HubOptions.After`, so tests move time by hand), when the key is removed, when Remote Work is turned off for the workspace or the port changes, and when the workspace closes. **One session for each workspace: a new login replaces the old one** (the old client gets `replaced`), which is also what lets a client that lost its connection reconnect while A still holds the half-open old one (15.4). The QUIC certificate fingerprint comes from `HubOptions.Cert`, a function 15.3 fills (a test gives a stand-in of 32 bytes), and `HubOptions.OnSession` is the place where 15.3 starts the transport once the grant is sent. The idle timeout is 1 minute to 24 hours (default 30); there is no way to turn it off.
- **Listening.** The listener is made by the hub: it listens on `:<port>` (TCP; the UDP socket of 15.3 has the same number) **only while at least one open workspace with a folder has Remote Work on**, and closes, ending every session with `Remote Work was turned off`, when the last one is turned off or closes. A port change moves the listener at once (and ends the sessions); a failure to listen (the port is taken, the state folder cannot be used) is shown on the page, raises an error notification in the workspaces that have it on and is logged. The hub is made once by `extensions.All()` (`remotework.NewFactory`), and the instances of the extension (one for each workspace) share it; a workspace with no folder cannot have Remote Work on, because workspaces are named by their folder.
- **The state files** (`extensions/internal/statefile`). `remote-work.json` (`{"version":1,"port","idleMinutes","workspaces":[folders that are on],"keys":[{"line","added"}]}`), the host key and `remote-work-hosts.json` are in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/` (the folder of the default profile: the extension has no profile), written atomically (a temporary file in the same folder, flushed, renamed) with mode 0600 in a folder of mode 0700, **only by the page** (the hub's mutators and the host key's creation; activation never writes). **The read policy** (decided here): a state file is read only if it is a regular file (a link, a pipe or a device is refused; it is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_NONBLOCK`), of at most 1 MiB (4 MiB for the pins), and the group and the others cannot **write** it (it decides who may log in and which host a client trusts), and a private key also only if they cannot **read** it. A file that fails is not used and not replaced: `remote-work.json` leaves Remote Work off and the page read-only with the reason and the fix ("chmod 600"); a pins file refuses every connection. A file that is readable by others is accepted (it holds public keys and a port). A file with anything wrong in it (a version this Emetos does not know, a port or idle timeout out of range, a workspace that is not a clean absolute path, a key that does not parse, with options, or listed twice, more than 256 keys) is refused as a whole, so a damaged file never lets in a key the user did not list. The keys are checked when they are added: one line only (several lines, a comment line or two keys are refused), without options (`command=`, `from=`, `restrict` would not be applied, so they are refused), not a certificate, of a type that is Ed25519, ECDSA, RSA of at least 2048 bits or a security key, with the comment cleaned of control characters and cut to 128 characters; a key that is listed already is refused. Tests isolate every state file in the `XDG_*` folders of the test.
- **The page** (`remotework/page.go`; the command `emetos.remotework.manage`, "Remote Work: Manage", opens or shows the editor tab of the kind `emetos.remotework.page`, which has no state of its own). From the top: the switch "Allow other computers to use <workspace>" with the folder and what the listener does (off; listening on port N; cannot listen: why; another workspace has it on) and the clients connected to this workspace, each with Disconnect; **Connection** (the port, default 47123, and the idle timeout in minutes, default 30, with Apply; a number out of range is told and nothing is written); **Allowed keys** (each with its comment, type and fingerprint and Remove; a box for a pasted line with Add, **Choose .pub File...** that asks for the file with the new `FileChooser` and adds the key in it, and the place of the **Scan QR Code** button of 15.5, where nothing is shown yet); **Host key of this computer** (the fingerprint to compare with the one a client shows on first use); **Security** (the five notes: the power a key gives, the first connection is as safe as the comparison, over the internet it is as safe as SSH with a key and a VPN is better, the listener and the rate limit, and that every login and refusal is logged and shown). The work that starts or stops the listener runs off the UI thread. The page follows the hub (`Hub.OnChange`), so two pages and the banner agree.
- **The banner and the notifications.** A login shows the banner "Remote Work: <key comment> connected" (the fingerprint when the key has no comment), with the icon `remote` and the button **Disconnect**, below the title bar of the workspace, and the notification "Remote Work: <comment> logged in from <ip>." in it. A refused attempt (`KeyNotListed`, `KeyRefused`, `PasswordRefused`, `MethodRefused`, `ChannelType`, `Request`, `NoChannel`) raises a warning "Remote Work refused a login from <ip>: <why>." in every workspace that has Remote Work on, **at most once a minute for each address**; the block of an address (`RateLimited`) is announced on its own the same way. A connection that ended before it tried to log in (`HandshakeFailed`) is in the log but raises nothing: it is also what a client on its first use does while its user compares the fingerprint.
- **The dialogs of B** (`remotework/loginui`). Widgets and a `Prompter`, for the tab of 15.4: the passphrase of a key file (a masked box, "That passphrase is wrong. Try again." from the second attempt), the first use of a host (its address, the type and fingerprint of the key and the instruction to compare it with the page of A; Trust or Cancel) and the warning that the key of a host changed (both fingerprints; the connection was refused and nothing was sent; Forget the Old Key or Close; no way to trust the new key from it). `Prompter.Passphrase(file)` and `Prompter.ConfirmHost()` give `sshlogin` the functions it calls from the goroutine of the login; the prompter posts the question to the UI thread and the goroutine waits for the answer, for the context to end or for `Prompter.Close`; `Prompter.Build` is what the tab stacks over its content. A new question cancels the one on screen.
- **API added to `extension/`** (the fake in `extensions/internal/fakeapi` has them): `api.Banners().Show(Banner{Text, Icon, Actions})` returns a `BannerHandle` (`Update`, `Dispose`); the banners of a workspace are a column of strips under the title bar of its workbench (`workbench.Banners`, `workbench.Options.Banners`; the headless view has none), go when the activation ends, and a button that panics fails the extension (`ExtensionBannerInvalid`, `ExtensionBannersUnavailable`, `ExtensionBannerActionPanicked`); `api.FileChooser().Open(ctx, FileChooserOptions{Title, AcceptLabel, Filters, Folder})` shows the file chooser portal of the desktop (`desktop.OpenFiles`) from a goroutine of the extension and gives the path or "" for a dialog that was closed (`ExtensionFileChooserUnavailable` for a scope with no dialog or a tab that is not on screen, `ExtensionFileChooserFailed` for the desktop's error, with its cause, which is `FileChooserUnavailable` on a desktop without the portal). `ui.InputBoxOpts.Obscure` (kit) makes the box a password box. `scripts/isolated.sh` and `scripts/proof.sh` take `--state <dir>`, copied into the state folder of the run with modes 0600 and 0700.
- **Decisions of this step:** the host key is made when the page opens or Remote Work is turned on (not only on turning on); one session for each workspace, a new login replaces the old; the workspaces are named by their folder name (the whole folder when two share it) and a client with several workspaces on must name one; no QUIC means an empty fingerprint in the grant; the first-use connection is dropped before the login and made again after the question; a changed key is refused, never asked about; the read policy of the state files (above); `remote-work.json` that cannot be used leaves Remote Work off and the page read-only instead of being replaced; a key with options is refused; passwords, keyboard-interactive and "none" logins do not exist; any channel request or channel of another type ends the connection; the state folder is the default profile's; the idle timeout has a minimum of 1 minute and no "never"; the notification for a refused attempt is limited to one a minute for each address; the key file's permissions are not checked.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `SSHLoginServerInvalid`, `SSHLoginAcceptFailed`, `SSHLoginKeyLineInvalid`, `SSHLoginKeyUnsupported`, `SSHLoginKeyNotListed`, `SSHLoginHostKeyInvalid`, `SSHLoginHostKeyCreateFailed`, `SSHLoginKeyFileUnreadable`, `SSHLoginKeyFileInvalid`, `SSHLoginPassphraseRequired`, `SSHLoginPassphraseCancelled`, `SSHLoginWrongPassphrase`, `SSHLoginAgentUnavailable`, `SSHLoginAgentFailed`, `SSHLoginAgentNoKey`, `SSHLoginAddressInvalid`, `SSHLoginHostsFileInvalid`, `SSHLoginDialInvalid`, `SSHLoginHostKeyChanged`, `SSHLoginHostKeyRejected`, `SSHLoginHostKeyUnknown`, `SSHLoginConfirmFailed`, `SSHLoginConnectFailed`, `SSHLoginAuthFailed`, `SSHLoginChannelRefused` (`sshlogin`); `StateFileWriteFailed`, `StateFileReadFailed`, `StateFileNotRegular`, `StateFileUnsafeMode`, `StateFileTooLarge` (`statefile`); `RemoteWorkRequestInvalid`, `RemoteWorkGrantInvalid`, `RemoteWorkGrantWriteFailed`, `RemoteWorkGrantReadFailed`, `RemoteWorkLoginDenied` (`login`); `RemoteWorkConfigInvalid`, `RemoteWorkConfigUnusable`, `RemoteWorkSettingInvalid`, `RemoteWorkKeyDuplicate`, `RemoteWorkTooManyKeys`, `RemoteWorkKeyUnknown`, `SSHLoginPubFileUnreadable`, `SSHLoginPubFileInvalid` (`sshlogin.ReadPublicKeyFile`, since step 16.2; they were `RemoteWorkKeyFileUnreadable` and `RemoteWorkKeyFileInvalid`), `RemoteWorkListenFailed`, `RemoteWorkNoStateDir`, `StateFileDirUnknown` (`statefile.DirFromEnv`, since step 16.2; it was `RemoteWorkStateDirUnknown`), `RemoteWorkTokenFailed` (`remotework`); `LoginUICancelled` (`loginui`); `ExtensionBannerInvalid`, `ExtensionBannersUnavailable`, `ExtensionBannerActionPanicked`, `ExtensionFileChooserUnavailable` (`exthost` and the fake), `ExtensionFileChooserFailed` (`app`).
- **Not built here:** the QUIC listener and the certificate (15.3), the "Remote Work..." tab, the dialogs' place in it and the reconnection (15.4), the Scan QR Code button and Show My Public Key as QR Code (15.5), a limit on the number of sessions beyond one for each workspace, a way to change the idle timeout of a live session, an Extensions-page switch for the listener.

**As built (step 15.3, `extensions/remotework/transport`, `extensions/remotework/{hub,session}.go`, `protocol` `Missing`).** The transports: the session's messages over QUIC on UDP or over the SSH channel, and the picture flow on top of either. `github.com/quic-go/quic-go` v0.64.1 is the one new dependency (in `go.mod` it brings `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0; `go.sum` also lists the modules of its tests). The tab on B (15.4) is the next step. Where the text above leaves room:

- **One interface for both transports** (`transport.Conn`; implemented by `HostConn` on A and `ClientConn` on B): `Send(m)` queues a message on the reliable, ordered path (it never waits for the peer: a full queue is `TransportQueueFull`, and the message is encoded at once); `SendTiles(frame, tiles)` hands over one picture's tiles (only the newest picture waits); `Next(ctx)` gives the messages that arrived (the reliable ones in order, the tiles as they complete; after the end it gives what had arrived, the peer's `Disconnect` among it, then `TransportClosed`); `OnTilesSent(f)` says when the last tile of a picture has gone out for the first time; `Kind()` (`KindQUIC`, `KindSSH`, `KindNone` while a link is being made), `Done()`, `Err()`, `Stats()` and `Close(reason, text)`. The transport makes `Hello` and `Missing` itself (`Send` refuses them and `Tile`: `TransportMessageInvalid`). `Presenter` (A) and `Screen` (B) are the picture flow on a `Conn` (below); the tab of 15.4 feeds the headless view's frames to `Presenter.Present`, hands `FrameConfirm` and `Refresh` from `Next` to `Presenter.Handle`, hands tiles to `Screen.Handle` and draws what `Screen.Draw` gives.
- **A's side.** The hub makes a `transport.Host` when it starts listening: a QUIC listener on a UDP socket with the same port number as the SSH listener (`HubOptions.ListenUDP`; if the socket cannot be opened the hub logs it and runs without QUIC, the grant then carrying no fingerprint, so every session uses the SSH channel; `HubOptions.NoQUIC` does so on purpose, `NoTransport` leaves the channel to the caller as in 15.2). `Host.Attach` makes the `HostConn` of a session **before the grant is written** (so the token is known when B uses it); `Session.Conn()` is that connection, `OnSession` runs after the grant. `Session.End` says goodbye through `HostConn.Shutdown`, which writes the `Disconnect` on the SSH channel (never between the bytes of a message: it takes the same write lock) and closes QUIC with an application error code that carries the reason (`0x100` + the reason), so B learns it even from a stream that is gone. The host closes with the listener (`Hub.stopListening`).
- **The certificate and the token.** At start the host makes a P-256 key and a self-signed certificate **in memory** (never written; valid for 100 years: nobody checks its dates), and its SHA-256 fingerprint goes into the grant (`HubOptions.Cert` may override it, for a test). TLS 1.3 only, ALPN `emetos-remotework/1`, no client certificate. B's `tls.Config` has `InsecureSkipVerify: true` (which only turns off the chain and name checks) and a **`VerifyConnection`** that accepts exactly one certificate whose SHA-256 equals the fingerprint of the grant, in constant time; nothing consults the system roots, and `VerifyConnection` (not `VerifyPeerCertificate`) runs for every connection, resumed ones included. A different certificate is `TransportCertMismatch` and ends the attempt before a stream is opened (the token is never sent to it), and it does **not** fall back to the SSH channel (decided: something answering on the UDP port that the host did not start is a fact the user should see; the SSH channel is still authenticated, so falling back would be safe, but it would hide it). The first thing on B's first stream is a `Hello` with the token (`protocol.Hello`, the version checked); A looks it up with `Hub.SessionByToken` (constant time, skips an ended session) and answers with a `Hello` that has no token. A connection that presents a wrong or expired token, another version, something that is not a `Hello`, or nothing within 5 s is closed with a code and a reason ("the token is not the token of a live session", ...) and held no longer; at most 32 connections wait for their `Hello` (the 33rd is closed with "busy"); the first message is checked by its header (type `Hello`, length at most 128) before its payload is read, so such a connection costs 133 bytes whatever it says (`readHello`). Each refusal is logged and given to `HostOptions.OnRefused`.
- **Reliable streams.** B opens one bidirectional QUIC stream; the messages of `protocol` are written on it one `Write` each. A bounded queue (512 messages and 8 MiB; a clipboard is up to 1 MiB) is written by one goroutine; a write that takes 15 s (the peer does not read) gives the link up. The reader of each side delivers to `Next` through a channel of 256 messages and waits when it is full, so the peer is slowed by the stream's flow control instead of the side buffering. B's `Refresh` after a resume goes first in the queue.
- **How tiles travel (the decision).** *Tiles go as QUIC datagrams, a tile that does not fit one is cut into fragments, and the client asks for the tiles of the newest picture that did not arrive.* The numbers that decided it (the three 1280x800 pictures of `tiles/testdata`): a tile is 128 bytes at the median, 1.8 KB at the 95th percentile and at most 3 KB (17.4 KB is the limit, for noise); **86% of the tiles of a whole picture fit one datagram** of 1,100 bytes of data (75% of the scroll's), a whole picture of 260 tiles is 301 datagrams (334 for the scroll) and a typed character 7 tiles. So the usual tile is one datagram with no cost, and only text-heavy tiles are two or three; the rare 17 KB tile is 16 fragments. A datagram is `frame:8 | index:2 | total:2 | fragment:1 | fragments:1 | chunk` (14 bytes of header): the chunks in order are one encoded `Tile` message, decoded with `protocol.Decode` (so every rule of the decoder applies) and checked against the header (`TransportDatagramInvalid`). The chunk is 1,100 bytes, below QUIC's minimum packet; if the path takes less, `SendDatagram` says so (`DatagramTooLargeError`) and the chunk shrinks to what it allows (never below 600; a tile is at most 30 fragments). *Rejected:* a QUIC stream per tile or picture (reliable, but a lost packet holds the picture and the bytes of a picture that is already old; the stream would have to be reset by hand to be "latest wins"), and a datagram with the whole tile (it does not fit). *Receiving:* the client follows the newest picture only: a fragment of an older picture is dropped (`TilesStale`), one of a newer starts it over, a tile counts when all its fragments arrived, and a repeat is ignored (`TilesDuplicate`); at most 256 partial tiles and 2 MiB of fragments are held (the oldest goes first), and the tiles that completed wait for `Next` in a buffer of 4,096 tiles and 16 MiB (a tile that finds it full is lost and asked for again: `TilesDropped`). *Sending:* only the newest picture waits to be sent (`BatchesDropped` counts the ones replaced before they were out), tiles go in the order the differ made them, and `SendDatagram` (queue of 32, paced by QUIC's congestion control) is what holds the sender back, so nothing is queued beyond one picture.
- **Repair of lost tiles (`protocol.Missing`, type 14; the one change of the protocol).** At 5% loss a picture of 130 tiles has all its tiles with probability 0.1%, and a `Canvas` completes a picture only with every tile of it, so without a repair a picture would never be confirmed. A `Missing` is `frame:8 | total:4 | bitmap` with one bit for each tile of the picture (in the order the host sent them) that the client lacks (at least one, none past the total, canonical like every message; at most 524 bytes). When the newest picture has been quiet for 1.5 round trips plus 20 ms (at least 40 ms; the round trip is QUIC's smoothed RTT) and lacks tiles, the client sends one on the reliable stream, and again after twice as long each time (at most 2 s), up to 8 times without any new tile; a tile that arrives starts it over. The host sends again the requested tiles of the picture it still holds (`TilesResent`), after the first pass, and ignores a request for another picture. The protocol `Version` stays 1: nothing was released with 13 types, and the numbers 1 to 13 did not change. `FuzzDecode` has `Missing` among its seeds (30 s, `-parallel=1`, `GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB`: no failure).
- **The flow of pictures** (`Presenter` on A, `Screen` on B). A gets the headless view's frames from the tab (15.4) and keeps only the newest (`Present`). It asks the differ for tiles when the window allows: **at most 2 pictures in flight** (sent, not confirmed); a third waits for a `FrameConfirm`, or `Hold` (400 ms) and is then sent anyway, replacing any picture still waiting. B's `Screen` puts each tile on the `Canvas`, shows tiles as they arrive, sends `FrameConfirm` when a picture is complete and `Refresh` when a tile contradicts its frame or 16 tiles in a row were dropped for their base. **The full refresh of every 5 s lives in the `Presenter`** (decided here, not in 15.4): while pictures are being sent over QUIC, a whole picture goes 5 s after the last whole one, and none while the view is idle (nothing changed, nothing to repair); over the SSH channel there is none (nothing is lost). Over QUIC an unconfirmed picture is **sent again 600 ms after it was out** (a picture all of whose datagrams were lost leaves the client no way to know there was one), counted from the moment `OnTilesSent` says the last tile went out, and pushed back whenever the client asks for lost tiles: a slow link needs seconds to send a picture, and sending it over again would replace the picture the client is putting together (measured: without this the first picture of a 5% loss link did not arrive in 30 s). Over the SSH channel the tiles are messages, one each, written by the goroutine that sends tiles under the same write lock as the reliable messages, so a key or a clipboard waits for at most the tile being written; only the newest picture waits there too.
- **Resume.** A dropped QUIC connection (the client's reader fails, or QUIC's idle timeout of 15 s with a keep-alive of 5 s fires) does not end the session: the client dials again with the same token, up to 3 times (3 s for each handshake), and the host replaces the link it had with the new one (the old one is closed with "another connection took the session"); the queue of reliable messages stays, a message that was on the wire is lost, and the client puts a `Refresh` first so that A sends a whole picture. If UDP does not come back the client moves to the SSH channel (below). The session lives as long as the SSH connection and the hub's idle timer. `Stats.Resumes` counts them.
- **The fallback.** `ClientConn` tries QUIC for 3 s (`FallbackAfter`, on the injected clock: `Clock`); if the handshake has not completed it sends the `Hello` with the token on the SSH channel instead and A answers on it; from then on the channel carries the same messages, and A takes the channel as the link when it sees that `Hello` (also in the middle of a session, after a resume that did not work). A grant with no fingerprint skips QUIC. A QUIC connection that was refused after its handshake (token, version) or showed another certificate is an error, not a reason to fall back. A session whose client opened no transport within 20 s ends (`FirstLink`).
- **The idle timeout.** The hub's timer (`Session.Touch`, `HubOptions.After`) is touched for every message A receives from B (not for the tiles it sends, not for QUIC's keep-alive), so a client that sends nothing, pings included, is cut off after the idle timeout with `ReasonIdle`; B's tab decides whether to ping.
- **Goroutines and shutdown.** Each connection has per link a reader, a writer of reliable messages, a sender of tiles and (QUIC) a reader of datagrams, plus the SSH reader; all stop when the link or the connection ends, and `go test` checks that none is left (a settle loop on `runtime.NumGoroutine`) in the tests that open sessions. Closing is clean in every direction: the host's `Shutdown`, the client's `Close`, a `Disconnect` from the peer, the SSH connection ending (A ends the session; B ends the connection), the listener closing.
- **Lossy-link measurement** (`go test -v -run TestLossyLinkMeasurement ./extensions/remotework/transport`; the real differ on the three 1280x800 pictures, loopback, the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 of the development machine). A UDP proxy delays every packet by 50 ms in each direction (a round trip of 100 ms) and drops 5% of the packets (a seeded generator). Typing is a picture every 100 ms for 4 s (7 tiles change, and one tile that carries the picture's number), a scroll changes 132 tiles. *Shown* is a picture of which the client had a tile on screen, *complete* one that is exactly the picture and was confirmed.

  | link | first picture (260 tiles, 113 KB) | typing: pictures shown / complete a second (of 10 offered), latency median / 95th | last typed picture complete after it was presented | scroll (132 tiles, 129 KB) | and back |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | no loss, no delay | 17 ms | 10.0 / 10.0, 2 ms / 2 ms | 2 ms | 14 ms | 11 ms |
  | no loss, 50 ms each way | 197 ms | 6.8 / 6.8, 54 ms / 58 ms | 57 ms | 278 ms | 73 ms |
  | **5% loss, 50 ms each way** | **1.45 s** | **6.2 / 5.0**, 55 ms / 221 ms (complete: 55 ms / 540 ms) | 540 ms | **3.6 s** | 3.6 s |

  Over 6 seeds of the lossy link (3 s of typing): the first picture took 0.78 to 1.41 s (median 1.0 s), the typing showed 6.0 to 7.3 pictures a second (median 6.5) with a picture complete 52 ms to 0.94 s after the last one was presented (median 57 ms), a scroll 3.4 to 4.6 s (median 4.0 s) and the picture back 2.3 to 3.5 s (median 2.7 s). Before the retry waited for the first pass to be out and for the repair, the same link took up to 20 s for a scroll and 7 s for the first picture, and the first picture sometimes never completed. The scroll's 129 KB in about 4 s is 33 KB/s, which is what QUIC's congestion control gives a flow with 5% random loss at 100 ms (the model rate is about 1.22 x 1,200 bytes / (0.1 s x sqrt(0.05)) = 65 KB/s, and the datagrams carry 14 bytes of header and the repair adds duplicates); the typing, a few KB a picture, runs at the rate of the window of 2 pictures at a round trip of 100 ms plus the loss. The frame rate with no loss and 100 ms of round trip is bounded by the window (2 pictures a round trip: 6.8 shown a second, of the 10 offered); the host's UI thread makes about 6 a second anyway (§10.18 "As built (step 15.1)").
- **Decisions of this step:** tiles as datagrams with fragments, 1,100-byte chunks, 14-byte header, `Missing` repair (a new protocol message, `Version` 1); the full refresh of 5 s and the retry of 600 ms in the `Presenter`, not in the tab; a window of 2 pictures with a hold of 400 ms; a certificate mismatch is fatal and not a fallback; the fingerprint compared in `VerifyConnection`; a P-256 certificate of 100 years; the token checked by `Hub.SessionByToken` and the transport attached before the grant; the SSH `Hello` as the fallback signal, also mid-session; 3 resume attempts before the SSH channel; QUIC idle timeout 15 s with a keep-alive of 5 s; the session's idle timeout touched by received messages only; the farewell goes on the SSH channel and in the QUIC close code; the transport is attached to every session unless `HubOptions.NoTransport`; a hub whose UDP port cannot be opened runs over SSH.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `TransportCertFailed`, `TransportListenFailed`, `TransportHelloInvalid`, `TransportTokenInvalid` (`Host`), `TransportOptionsInvalid`, `TransportCertMismatch`, `TransportDialFailed`, `TransportRefused` (`Connect`, `ClientConn`), `TransportMessageInvalid`, `TransportQueueFull`, `TransportTilesInvalid`, `TransportClosed`, `TransportCancelled`, `TransportLinkFailed` (`Conn`), `TransportDatagramInvalid` (the datagram layer); and `RemoteWorkBadValue`, `RemoteWorkEncodeInvalid`, `RemoteWorkEncodeTooLarge` for `Missing` (`protocol`).
- **Not built here:** the use of the transport by the tab and by the headless view (15.4), notifications and clipboard as the workspace's own messages (15.4), a congestion signal beyond QUIC's own, forward error correction (the repair asks instead), path migration, and a limit on the number of sessions beyond one for each workspace.

**As built (step 15.4, `extensions/remotework/{tab,tabform,tabsession,tabview,tabstate,hostview,dev}.go`, `extension/{windowtabs,headless}.go`, `gui/app/{keys,exttab,headless}.go`, `gui/exthost/windowtabs.go`, `core/notify`, `scripts/proof-remotework.sh`).** The window tab on B and the wiring of the headless view on A; the QR code of the key (15.5) comes after it. No new dependency. Where the text above leaves room:

- **The kind and the scope.** The manifest declares the window tab kind `emetos.remotework.tab` (title "Remote Work", icon `remote`, `+` menu label "Remote Work..."). `Activate` runs in two scopes: in a workspace (the hub, §10.18 15.2) and in `ScopeWindowTab` (the tab: `Provide`, and the dev command). A tab never listens and the hub never makes a tab; both are `remoteWork` with different fields, so `FactoryOf(hub)` lets the end-to-end tests give a tab the hub of the other instance.
- **The dialog (the form of a new tab).** Host, port (47123), the way to choose the key (a dropdown: **Private key file** with a text box and **Choose...**, which runs the desktop's file chooser; or **SSH agent**, whose keys are listed by comment and fingerprint, read once on the UI's behalf off the UI thread; an unreachable agent says so in the form) and **Connect**; under the key a slot (`keyQRSlot`, empty in 15.4) for step 15.5's "Show My Public Key as QR Code". Host and port are checked by `connectParams` (`RemoteWorkHostInvalid`, `RemoteWorkPortInvalid`, `RemoteWorkKeyChoiceInvalid`: a user@host, a space, a port outside 1..65535, no file); the error shows under the field.
- **The flow.** Connect runs, off the UI thread and under a generation number (a late result of a replaced session is dropped): the key (`sshlogin.KeyFileAuth`, with the passphrase dialog of `loginui`; or the agent's key), `login.Connect` (the first-use and changed-key dialogs of `loginui`, with the key of the host pinned in B's `remote-work-hosts.json`), the grant, and `transport.FromLogin`. While it runs the tab shows a **Connecting** card with Cancel (hidden while a dialog of the login is up, so there is one Cancel). A grant with several workspaces and no choice made shows the **picker** of the workspace names (Connect / Cancel; `RemoteWorkChoiceCancelled`); one workspace is taken; none or "unknown" is the card with the host's answer. The tab is titled `<host>: <workspace>` (the host is the name typed) with the `remote` icon once connected; before that it is titled "Remote Work".
- **The picture.** The tab is a `LayoutBuilder`; the **logical-pixel size of its box** is sent in `Resize` (a size change must stay for 150 ms, `TabOptions.ResizeDelay`, before it is sent; the first one, sent when the connection is made, goes at once; a larger tab than the protocol allows is cut to its limits by `fitSize`), and A makes its view of exactly that size. **HiDPI (decided):** the picture is at scale 1 of the logical size and B draws it with one pixel of the image for one logical pixel of its box (`RawImage` at its natural size in an `OverflowBox` inside a `ClipRect`): on a screen with a scale of 2 it is stretched and a little soft, text included. The alternative (a `Resize` with a device pixel ratio, a view on A at that ratio and 4 times the tiles) was left for later: the protocol has no field for it, and §10.18 asks for no more. Until the first picture of a size arrives the old picture stays (not stretched). The picture is decoded (`DecodeImageFromPixels`) once for each change, and a change that comes while one is being decoded replaces the queued one (`pictureChanged` / `refreshPicture`).
- **Input and the split of the shortcuts.** The picture is in a `Focus` and a `Listener`. B's own window shortcuts stay on B: `WindowTab.CaptureKeys(true)` makes the **workspace's key dispatcher** hand over every chord that does not belong to B's window, only while the content of the tab has the focus (`focusedView` is `exthost.WindowTabViewID`), not in the middle of a chord sequence, and never a modifier alone. A chord belongs to B when it is bound to one of `emetos.workspaceTab.*`, `emetos.windowTab.*`, `workbench.action.closeWindow`, `newWindow`, `quit`, `switchWindow` or `toggleFullScreen` (as the user's keybindings say, so a rebound key follows). Every other key (the command palette, Ctrl+S, F5, Escape, text) goes to A, which runs it in its own keybindings. Keys go as `Key` messages with their text; the pressed keys are tracked so that a key released after the focus left is released on A. A mouse move is sent at most every 8 ms (the newest wins); buttons, wheel and the position follow the order of the other messages. **IME and composed text**: the tab is a text input client (`services.TextInput`, delta model); a commit is sent as one `Key` press and release with the text and `Logical` = its first rune (Physical 0), and A types the text (tested). The composing region is B's alone and is not shown on A.
- **Clipboard (only on copy and paste, both ways).** A's `OnCopy` gives the text of a copy done in the view; B puts it on its own clipboard (`Clipboard`, no more than 1 MiB; B never reads its clipboard at any other time). On a paste chord (Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Shift+V, Shift+Insert) B reads its clipboard first (a wait of up to 1 s), sends `Clipboard` with it and only then the `Key`, in that order (the outbox of the input surface holds the key behind the clipboard), so A pastes what B copied.
- **Notifications (`HeadlessView.OnNotification`, `RunNotificationAction`).** A forwards the notifications of the workspace that are not silent (`ViewNotification{ID, Severity, Source, Message, Actions}`; the text is cut to the protocol's limits), except those whose source is "Remote Work" itself (the banner "connected"). The view's own toasts are muted while A forwards (`notify.Presenter.Mute`), so the toast shows on B and not in the invisible view; the toast of the workspace on A is unchanged. B shows the notification with its actions in its own toast; pressing an action sends `NotificationAction{id, index}`, and A runs it in the workspace (`notify.Service.RunAction`, which the toast of the workbench now uses as well). Silent notifications (status-bar messages) are not forwarded.
- **Reconnection.** When the transport ends with no `Disconnect` from A (the network failed, A stopped), the tab shows **Reconnecting (attempt n)** over the last picture and logs in again with the backoff 1 s, 2 s, ... 30 s (`TabOptions.Backoff`), as long as the failures are the network's (`retryable`: connect failed, grant unreadable, channel refused, transport dial or link failed; and a `Disconnect` with `ReasonClosed` from A, which A sends when its side of the SSH connection ended or the hub stopped, not a choice of its user, so B treats it as a drop); a key that is refused, Remote Work off, a changed host key or a cancelled dialog ends it with that card. The key file is read and unlocked once (the passphrase is asked once, used and wiped; the **unlocked key stays in memory** for the reconnections of this tab and is dropped when the tab ends). B sends no pings (QUIC's keep-alive of 5 s keeps the link and every message B sends touches A's idle timer; A answers a `Ping` it gets). A new login replaces the old session on A (one session for each workspace), so a reconnection makes a new view on A: the old one is closed with the old session.
- **Disconnect reasons (the card of an ended session).** `Disconnect` reasons: host ("Disconnected by <host>"), idle ("The session was idle for too long"), off ("Remote Work was turned off on <host>"), replaced ("Another computer took the session"), workspace closed ("The workspace was closed on <host>"), version mismatch and protocol error (in the error colour), others with the host's text; a refused key ("<host> refused the key": its public key is not in the list of the Remote Work page on that computer, or it was taken out of it), Remote Work off, an unknown workspace, a changed host key (the loginui warning, with the forget button). The card has **Connect Again**, **Edit Connection** (back to the form with its values) and **Close Tab**.
- **A's side (`hostview.go`).** The session's `serve` runs a `hostView` unless `HubOptions.NoView`: on B's `Resize` it calls `HeadlessView` (`NewHeadlessView(size)`, one for each session; the first one makes the view, later ones `Resize` it), wires `OnFrame` to `Presenter.Present`, `OnCopy` to a `Clipboard` message, `OnNotification` to a `Notification` message, and the view ending (the workspace closed) to `Disconnect` with the reason workspace-closed; B's input messages go in order to the UI thread (`SendKey`, `SendPointer`, `SendScroll`, the clipboard first, `RunNotificationAction`); `FrameConfirm` and `Refresh` go to the `Presenter`; a message that is not for A ends the session with `ReasonProtocol` (`RemoteWorkViewFailed` when the view could not be made, logged and the session ended). The view closes when the session ends (disconnect on the banner, idle, B's close, the SSH connection ending).
- **Saved state.** The tab saves `{host, port, key: "file"|"agent", keyFile, fingerprint, workspace}` and nothing else (the parser refuses an unknown field, so a passphrase or a token can never come back from the file: `RemoteWorkTabStateInvalid`). A tab restored with Emetos **does not connect by itself**: it shows the form with its values and a Connect button (a restart is not a reason to open a session on another computer; the decision is the user's). The agent key is chosen again by its fingerprint.
- **API added.** `WindowTab.CaptureKeys(bool)` (§10.15 "The API: `api.WindowTabs()`"); `HeadlessView.OnNotification(func(ViewNotification))` and `RunNotificationAction(id uint64, action int)` with `NotificationSeverity` (`NotificationInfo`, `NotificationWarning`, `NotificationError`); `exthost.WindowTabViewID`; `notify.Service.RunAction` and `Presenter.Mute`. The fake API (`extensions/internal/fakeapi`) has all of them (`WindowTab.Capturing`, `HeadlessView.Presses`, `FailHeadlessViews`).
- **A test rule changed (§5.3).** A `_test.go` file under `internal/gui/` may import `extensions/...` (`ExtensionsImportedByInternal` skips it): the end-to-end test of two Emetos instances in one process needs the extension. Non-test code of `internal/` still never does.
- **Dev command.** `dev.remotework.connect {"host", "port", "keyFile", "workspace"}` (or `{"host","port","agent":true,"fingerprint"}`) fills the form of the Remote Work tab in front and presses Connect (`RemoteWorkDevConnectInvalid` without a tab or host or key); registered only in the debug build and with the tag `emetos_dev` (`dev_on.go` / `dev_off.go`), like the other dev commands.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `RemoteWorkTabStateInvalid`, `RemoteWorkHostInvalid`, `RemoteWorkPortInvalid`, `RemoteWorkKeyChoiceInvalid`, `RemoteWorkChoiceCancelled`, `RemoteWorkViewFailed`, `RemoteWorkDevConnectInvalid`.
- **Tests.** `extensions/remotework/tab_test.go`, `tab_session_test.go`, `tab_form_test.go` (a hub on A and a tab on B in one process on loopback with the fake API: connect, resize, input, clipboard, notification, disconnect reasons, reconnection, refused key, first-use and changed key, picker, closing, the form, the agent through a fake agent socket; goldens `testdata/goldens/tab_{form,form_agent,connecting,connected,reconnecting,ended_host,ended_refused,picker}_{dark,light}.png`), `hostview_test.go` (A's side), and `internal/gui/app/remotework_test.go`: **two complete `multiApp`s in one process**, A with a folder, a key and Remote Work on, B with the tab, connected over loopback: typing on B changes the document on A and the other way round, copy and paste both ways, the split of the shortcuts (the palette on A, Ctrl+Alt+PageUp on B), a notification with its action, Disconnect on A, a dropped connection, closing the tab; each test counts the goroutines when it ends. The e2e and tab tests were run with `-race -count=3`.
- **The proof (method B).** `scripts/proof-remotework.sh docs/implemented-proof-images/15.4-remote-tab.png` builds Emetos, makes with `scripts/proof-remotework-setup` (in a temporary folder removed at the end; the keys are made on every run and never kept) a client key, A's host key, A's `remote-work.json` (port picked free for TCP and UDP, the workspace `testdata/proof/15.4/project` on, the key allowed) and B's `remote-work-hosts.json`, starts A (own headless compositor, `scripts/isolated.sh`, own process group, opens `main.go`), then B through `scripts/proof.sh` (`dev.openWindowTab`, `dev.remotework.connect` with the key file, a wait) which saves B's window: its own tab "local" and the tab `127.0.0.1: project` showing A's workspace with `main.go`. **A's host key is pinned in B's file before the run** (so that the picture is not the first-use dialog, which the 15.2 proof shows and the tests cover); nothing in the product is bypassed. A listens on every interface (the product's default) and only 127.0.0.1 is used.
- **Decisions of this step:** keys captured by the tab through `CaptureKeys` in the key dispatcher (B's window commands stay, everything else to A); the picture at the logical size and scale 1 (HiDPI stretched, documented); a resize debounce of 150 ms; no pings from B; IME commits as `Key` with the text; a clipboard sent only on a paste chord and before the key; notifications that are not silent forwarded and muted in the view; reconnection forever for network failures with a backoff of 1 s to 30 s and the unlocked key kept in memory; a restored tab stays on the form; a notification of "Remote Work" itself is not forwarded; the pin of A's host key done by the proof's setup; `_test.go` of `internal/gui` may import extensions.
- **Not built here:** sound, a device pixel ratio above 1, a composing (pre-edit) text shown on A, drag and drop, more than one tab on the same workspace.

**As built (step 15.5, `extensions/internal/keyqr`, `extensions/internal/keyqr/qrui`, `extensions/internal/sshlogin` `PublicKeyOfKeyFile`, `extensions/remotework/{page,tabform,cameras,dev}.go`, `extension/ui` `Picture` and `Image`, `internal/gui/kit/image.go`).** Public keys by QR code; Relay (16.2, 16.3) reuses `keyqr` and `qrui` as they are. Where the text above leaves room:

- **The dependency.** `github.com/makiuchi-d/gozxing` v0.1.1 (a Go port of ZXing; its one dependency is `golang.org/x/xerrors`). Its license is **MIT** (not Apache-2.0 as the step's text said); ZXing, which it ports, is Apache-2.0, so `third_party/gozxing/` holds both texts (`LICENSE`, `LICENSE-zxing-apache-2.0`) and `NOTICE` lists them (entry 15). The module is allowed to `extensions/` in the architecture test (`allowedExtensionModules`).
- **Where the code is.** `keyqr` (no widgets): the camera (`camera.go` the `Source` and `Stream` interfaces, `capture.go` the capture over a `driver`, `v4l2.go` the real `Source`, `v4l2_linux.go` the ioctls, `fake.go` a `FakeSource` that plays frames from memory), `frames.go`, `qr.go`, `scanner.go`. `qrui`: the **Scan QR Code** dialog (`ScanDialog`) and the **Show My Public Key as QR Code** dialog (`ShowDialog`), widgets that their owner (a page or a window tab) stacks over its content with `Build` while open; the owner gives `Post` and `Refresh` and drops the dialog in its `Close` function. Remote Work uses them in the page (`Scan QR Code...`, in the row of the ways of adding a key) and in the "Remote Work..." dialog (`Show My Public Key as QR Code`, under the choice of the key).
- **The camera: V4L2 through ioctls (no cgo).** `v4l2_linux.go` (build tag `linux && (amd64 || arm64)`, the layouts of 64-bit Linux; another platform builds `v4l2_other.go`, which finds no camera) writes the structs of `linux/videodev2.h` (`v4l2_capability` 104 bytes, `v4l2_fmtdesc` 64, `v4l2_pix_format` 48, `v4l2_format` **208**, `v4l2_requestbuffers` 20, `v4l2_buffer` **88**) and the numbers of `_IOR`/`_IOWR` computed from their sizes (`VIDIOC_QUERYCAP` 0x80685600, `VIDIOC_S_FMT` 0xc0d05605, `VIDIOC_DQBUF` 0xc0585611, ...); a test checks the sizes, the offsets of the fields and the numbers against the kernel's. `ioctlDriver` is the thin shell (ioctl with `EINTR` retried, `unix.Mmap`/`Munmap`, `unix.Poll` with a timeout, the device opened `O_RDWR|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC`); everything that decides is above it in `capture.go` behind the `driver` interface, which is the kernel's own (`QueryCap`, `Formats`, `SetFormat`, `RequestBuffers`, `MapBuffer`, `Queue`, `Dequeue`, `StreamOn`/`StreamOff`, `Wait`, `Close`), and is tested against a fake driver. **Only the shell has never run against a device in the tests**: the ioctl calls, the mmap and the poll are checked by sizes and numbers and by the manual check `TestRealCamera` (build tag `emetos_camera`, `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`), which the user runs with a real camera; the tests never open `/dev/video*`.
- **Listing and opening.** `V4L2.Cameras` opens each `/dev/video*` for a moment to ask what it is (`VIDIOC_QUERYCAP`; this starts nothing) and lists the ones that capture video and stream (the device's own capabilities when it has them, so the metadata node that a camera has beside its video node is left out), in the order of their numbers; a device that is busy or gone is skipped, and when none can be used and one is denied the answer is `KeyQRCameraDenied` ("is it in the video group?"). Multi-planar capture devices are not offered.
- **The format.** MJPEG when the camera has it, else YUYV, else `KeyQRNoFormat`. **Decided:** MJPEG is asked at **1280x720** and YUYV at 640x480 (the step said "modest, 640x480 or the nearest"): an RSA 4096 key is a code of 113 modules a side, and at 640x480 the code is 2.8 pixels a module, which is read in 22 of 54 test frames, at 1280x720 in 40 of 54 (below); a camera that has not the size gives the nearest, and a size above 1920x1080 is refused (`KeyQRFrameTooLarge`). YUYV is not compressed, so 640x480 is what USB 2 carries at a good rate. Four buffers are asked for (at least 2 are needed, `KeyQRBuffersFailed`; a buffer larger than 16 MiB is refused), mapped, queued, and the capture started.
- **Frames, bounds and cancel.** `Stream.Next` waits (poll in slices of 50 ms, so a cancel is answered in that time), takes every frame the camera has ready, gives the older ones back at once and converts the newest, then gives its buffer back: **a slow reader drops frames and never falls behind**, and the image is its own memory, so no frame is kept in a kernel buffer. A frame the camera marks as damaged, or that cannot be decoded, is skipped (30 in a row end the capture, `KeyQRTooManyBadFrames`); a camera that gives nothing for 5 s is `KeyQRNoFrames`. `Close` (from any goroutine, more than once) turns the capture off (`StreamOff`), unmaps and closes, and wakes a `Next` that waits; the stream is also closed when the context of `Open` ends. MJPEG: `DecodeMJPEG` puts the standard Huffman tables (annex K.3 of the JPEG standard, the ones Go's encoder writes) in front of the scan when the frame has none (many UVC cameras leave them out), reads the size with `image.DecodeConfig` **before** `Decode` (a header that says 4000x3000 costs nothing: `KeyQRFrameTooLarge`), and refuses more than 16 MiB. YUYV: `YUYVToImage` unpacks to an `image.YCbCr` of 4:2:2 (the rows may be padded: the camera's `bytesperline`).
- **Errors of the system become tags where they are detected**: `KeyQRCameraBusy` (`EBUSY`), `KeyQRCameraDenied` (`EACCES`, `EPERM`), `KeyQRCameraGone` (`ENODEV`, `ENOENT`, `ENXIO`, `EIO`, also during the capture), `KeyQRCameraOpenFailed` and `KeyQRCaptureFailed` (the rest), with messages for the user ("the camera is in use by another program"); the cause stays for `errors.Is`.
- **Reading the codes.** `DecodeQR` makes gozxing look at the brightness of the frame (the Y plane of a camera's image, used as it is), with `TRY_HARDER`, restricted to QR codes, in any orientation; the detector of the library finds the same code at one size and not at the next, so when nothing is found it looks again at the frame reduced to 2/3 and to 1/2. A frame of noise of 1920x1080, the worst case, takes 61 ms (a blank one 8 ms). It cannot be interrupted, so the size is what bounds it. `Scan` runs on a goroutine of the caller: it takes the newest frame, shows it (`OnFrame`), reads it (`OnCode`) and waits so that a frame is looked at **every 100 ms** (a frame that takes longer is followed by the newest one at once). The text of a code is parsed by `ParseKey`, which is `sshlogin.ParseAuthorizedKey` (the rules of 15.2: no options, no certificates, RSA of at least 2048 bits, one line of at most 8 KiB): other text is refused with `SSHLoginKeyLineInvalid` or `SSHLoginKeyUnsupported`, and the dialog says "That QR code is not a public key".
- **Robustness (6 seeded variants of 9 conditions each: plain, rotated 5, 15, -30 and 45 degrees, blurred, noise of 20 and of 40 gray levels, and rotated 7 + blurred + noise 15; the code 60% to 70% of the height of the frame, a bilinear scale as a camera makes; `qr_test.go`).** Frames of 1280x720 (MJPEG): Ed25519 54 of 54 read, ECDSA 53 of 54, RSA 4096 40 of 54. Frames of 640x480 (YUYV): Ed25519 54 of 54, ECDSA 53 of 54, RSA 4096 22 of 54 (5 of 6 plain frames, 1 of 6 rotated by 45 degrees, none with rotation, blur and noise together). A live camera gives a new frame every 100 ms, so a code that is read in one frame of three is read in under half a second; the tests set the minimum for each case with room. Also read: a code scaled to 700, 350, 175 and 120 pixels, through the JPEG of a camera with no Huffman tables, through a YUYV frame, and a window of a larger picture.
- **The encoder.** `EncodeQR` makes the code black on white with the quiet zone of 4 modules, each module a whole number of pixels (the largest that keeps the side within the size given), with error correction **M**, or **L** when the text does not fit at M (`KeyQREncodeFailed` when it does not fit at L either: 2953 bytes). `EncodeKey` parses the line under the rules of the login first and encodes its canonical form (`type base64 comment`), so **only a public key is ever drawn**: a private key or any other text is refused with the tags of `ParseKey`. Sizes: an Ed25519 line (94 bytes with a comment) is 49 modules a side with the quiet zone, ECDSA P-256 (173 bytes) 61, **RSA 4096 (744 bytes) 113, at level M**; the dialog asks for at most 452 pixels (the room in the card), so the codes are 441, 427 and 452 pixels, which a monitor shows at one pixel to a pixel and a phone or a camera resolves. A comment that has non-ASCII characters is marked UTF-8 (a mark costs bits, so ASCII is not).
- **The image widget.** There was none. `extension/ui` gets `Picture` (an image ready to draw, with its own copy of the pixels, made by `NewPicture(image.Image)` from any goroutine, at most 4096 pixels a side: `PictureInvalid`, `PictureTooLarge`) and `Image`/`NewImage(pic, ImageOpts{Upscale, Pixelated})`, implemented in `internal/gui/kit/image.go` over Glutter's `RawImage` and `DecodeImageFromPixels` (no workaround is needed: nothing is added to `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`). The picture is scaled down to fit the box it is given (up too with `Upscale`), keeping its proportions, in the middle of a box of a fixed size and as large as it is drawn in a box that is only a limit; `Pixelated` draws the pixels of a QR code as squares. The widget is plain code with no host service, so it has no fake: tests use `uitest`. A picture is drawn at a scale of 1 logical pixel to a pixel, as the Remote Work tab does (§10.18 "As built (step 15.4)").
- **The Scan QR Code dialog.** The button is on the Remote Work page, next to Add and Choose .pub File; the page looks for the cameras off the UI thread when it opens and keeps the button **disabled, with the reason on a line under it**, while the look runs ("Looking for cameras...") and when there is nothing to scan with ("No camera was found on this computer.", "this user may not open the cameras (is it in the video group?)", "This computer has no camera that Emetos can read." when the hub has no `Source`). Pressed, it opens a card over the page with the title, the picture of the camera (a box of 448x252, the frame made at most 480 pixels wide and shown 10 times a second), a drop-down of the cameras when there are several (changing it lets the first one go and opens the other), the hint "Hold the QR code of the public key in front of the camera." and Cancel. **The camera is opened by the dialog and released when it closes**: on Cancel, when the page closes, when the context of the extension ends, and as soon as a key was read. **The first valid key ends the scan at once** (the goroutine of the camera cancels its context before it tells the UI, so no more frame is looked at and the camera is let go), and the card becomes the confirmation: "Add this key?" with the **type, the SHA-256 fingerprint and the comment** and "Compare the fingerprint with the one the other computer shows. Add the key only if they are the same: whoever holds it can log in." with Cancel, **Scan Again** and **Add Key**; only Add Key gives the key to the page (`Hub.AddKey`, which says "this key is in the list already" or "the list holds at most 256 keys" as for a pasted line). A QR code that is not a public key is ignored; "That QR code is not a public key." shows for 1.5 s after it was last seen. A camera that cannot be opened or stops shows the reason with Try Again. **No frame is kept**: the only picture is the one on screen, replaced by the next and dropped when the dialog closes or a key is read, and nothing is written or sent. **Decided:** the confirmation does not show the frame the key was read from (that would keep a frame), so the proof has two images.
- **Show My Public Key as QR Code (the "Remote Work..." dialog).** The button is under the choice of the key and does nothing while the tab connects. With a **key file**: the `.pub` file beside it (`<file>.pub`, read with the limits of the "Choose .pub File" button: a small regular file) when there is one, with its comment; when there is none, **the public key is read out of the key file itself**: a key in OpenSSH format keeps its public half in the clear in front of the private part, so `sshlogin.PublicKeyOfKeyFile` reads that and **needs no passphrase** (the private part is never parsed; the bytes read are overwritten); another format (PEM) has no public half and is parsed as the login parses it, asking the passphrase dialog when the key has one (the step said "with the passphrase if needed"). A key read this way has no comment ("(none)" is shown). With the **ssh-agent**: the key chosen in the list; with one key in the agent, that key; with several and none chosen, "The ssh-agent has several keys: choose the one to show." (the agent tells no comment). The dialog shows the code, the type, the fingerprint and the comment and says that only the public key is shown; the code is made smaller in a window too low for it. `NewShowDialog` is given the **line of a public key** and refuses anything else (a private key put in the `.pub` place included), so the private key is never drawn.
- **API.** `HubOptions.Camera` (the `keyqr.Source` of the cameras; nil means none; `extensions.All` passes `keyqr.NewV4L2()`, which opens no device before the page looks for cameras), `Hub.Cameras()` and `Hub.SetCameras`. **Dev commands** (debug builds and `emetos_dev`): `dev.keyqr.fakeCamera {"comment", "text", "nothing", "cameras"}` puts a camera that plays pictures from memory in place of the real ones (a room with a sheet that has the QR code of a public key made now, its private half dropped, or of the text given; `nothing` for a room with no code; `cameras: 2` adds a second camera) and `dev.remotework.scanQR` opens the dialog of the page that is open. Run the first before the page is made: the page looks for cameras when it is made. A page that closes is forgotten by the extension.
- **Tags** (each has a route test): `KeyQRFrameInvalid`, `KeyQRFrameTooLarge`, `KeyQRNoCode`, `KeyQREncodeFailed`, `KeyQRCameraListFailed`, `KeyQRCameraDenied`, `KeyQRCameraBusy`, `KeyQRCameraGone`, `KeyQRCameraOpenFailed`, `KeyQRCameraNotCapture`, `KeyQRNoFormat`, `KeyQRFormatRejected`, `KeyQRBuffersFailed`, `KeyQRCaptureFailed`, `KeyQRNoFrames`, `KeyQRTooManyBadFrames`, `KeyQRStreamClosed`, `KeyQRCancelled`, `PictureInvalid`, `PictureTooLarge`, `RemoteWorkDevFakeCameraInvalid`, `RemoteWorkDevScanInvalid`; `ParseKey` and `EncodeKey` return the tags of 15.2's parser (`SSHLoginKeyLineInvalid`, `SSHLoginKeyUnsupported`).
- **Tests.** `keyqr`: the round trip of an Ed25519, an ECDSA and an RSA 4096 public key (their public lines are in `testdata/*.pub`; the private halves were thrown away), the conditions above, text that is not a key, the encoder, MJPEG with and without tables and the bounds, YUYV, the kernel's sizes and numbers, the capture against a fake driver (the choice of the format, the setup order, the buffers that cycle, the newest frame, damaged frames, a cancel, `Close` racing `Next`, every tag), the listing, the scanner (about ten frames a second, a slow reader drops frames) and the fake source. `qrui`: the dialog with a fake camera that plays a sequence of frames (it closes on the first valid key, ignores other codes, releases the camera on Cancel, on the context and with a key, a picker, Scan Again, a camera that fails or is busy, no camera) and the Show dialog (what is on screen decodes to the key). `remotework`: the page (the reasons, the add, a key that is listed, the page that closes), the dev commands, and the dialog of the tab for a `.pub`, an OpenSSH key with and without a passphrase, a PEM key that asks for it, the agent, and what is in the way. The manual check is `go test -tags emetos_camera -run TestRealCamera -v ./extensions/internal/keyqr` (`docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`).
- **The proofs (method B).** `docs/implemented-proof-images/15.5-scan-qr.png`: the Scan QR Code dialog after the fake camera showed a QR code of a key, with the confirmation (`scripts/proof.sh docs/implemented-proof-images/15.5-scan-qr.png --config testdata/proof/15.5/config --state testdata/proof/15.5/state --commands '[["sleep","1s"],["dev.keyqr.fakeCamera",{"comment":"alice@laptop"}],["emetos.remotework.manage",null],["sleep","1s"],["dev.remotework.scanQR",null],["sleep","4s"]]' --after 3s -- testdata/proof/15.5/project`), and `15.5-scan-qr-preview.png`: the live picture with two cameras (the same command with `{"nothing":true,"cameras":2}` and 2 s). Neither opens a real device.
- **Not built here:** the controls of a camera (focus, exposure), a mirrored preview, multi-planar and H.264 cameras, 32-bit machines, a name field in the confirmation, the Escape key in the dialogs, Relay's own uses (16.2, 16.3).

### 10.19 Relay: event control of a workspace from another machine (`extensions/relay`)

One user controls several Emetos workspaces on different machines through their **events and commands** (D21; the user's design, for research and experiment). Nothing but events, requests, replies and command results crosses the network: no pictures, no keys, no clipboard. Its name is **"Relay"** everywhere (the extension `emetos.relay`, the `+` menu entry "Relay", the window tab "Relay").

- **The tab.** "Relay" in the `+` menu opens a Relay window tab (an extension window tab, §10.15). Its left side has two sections:
  - **Hosts**: "Add Host" (address, port, private key file or `ssh-agent`, an optional name, and **Show My Public Key as QR Code**, §10.18), the saved hosts with their state (disconnected, connecting, connected: watch-only or watch and send), connect and disconnect, remove; under a connected host, the workspaces it shares with this key. Several hosts may be connected at once.
  - **Be a Host**: a switch to listen (port, default 47124), the workspace tabs of this Emetos with a checkbox each to share them, and the allowed SSH public keys (`authorized_keys` lines, each with its comment; added by pasting, a `.pub` file or **Scan QR Code**, §10.18) with, per shared workspace, **Watch only** or **Watch and send** (default Watch only).
  Selecting a shared workspace of a connected host shows two panels on the right:
  - **Events**: a live log of every event published in that workspace (the core events of §10.15 and every extension's events): time, topic, publisher, the value (collapsed JSON, expandable), batches of fast topics as one row with their count; the requests made in that workspace with their reply or error and duration; a topic filter (a pattern), Pause, Clear, and a cap of 10,000 rows.
  - **Send** (hidden for Watch only): a topic and a JSON value with **Publish** and **Request**, and **Run Command** (a picker of the host's commands from `emetos.commands.list`, with JSON arguments); the reply, the error or the command's result under it; a history of what was sent (kept in the tab's state).
- **The host side.** The host's Relay extension is active in each shared workspace. It subscribes to every topic of that workspace and forwards the events to the clients connected to it (to each client only its granted workspaces); for a client with Watch and send it publishes the client's events, makes its requests and runs its commands **in that workspace's scope only**, and returns the results. The host's Relay is the only thing that acts on what a client sends; **a client never answers anything for the host** (it has no handlers). A banner in a shared workspace shows "Relay: <key comment> connected (watch only | watch and send)" with Disconnect; every connection and refusal is logged and raises a notification; failed logins are rate-limited (5 per minute per address).
- **Privileges (D21).** An extension may normally publish and handle only its own topics and never runs another extension's commands (§10.15). A manifest field `Privileges` (`events.publishAny`, `commands.execute`) lifts that inside the extension's own scope, and the host grants it **only to `emetos.relay`** (a fixed allowlist in the host; any other extension declaring it is refused with a problem on the Extensions page).
- **Core request topics** (new, answered by Emetos in every workspace scope, available to every extension; `emetos.commands.execute` needs the `commands.execute` privilege): `emetos.commands.list` (id, title, category, whether it is allowed for clients), `emetos.commands.execute` (`{id, args}` → `{result}` or the command's error), `emetos.files.list` (`{path, depth}` relative to the folder → entries with kind, size, modification time), `emetos.files.stat`, `emetos.files.read` (`{path}` → text up to 2 MiB, UTF-8, confined to the folder like `ReadFile`), `emetos.document.open` (`{path, line, col}` → opens it in the workspace), `emetos.document.read` (`{uri}` → the text and version of an open document), `emetos.document.edit` (`{uri, version, edits}` → applied as one undo step), `emetos.document.save`, `emetos.document.close`, `emetos.editor.reveal` (`{uri, line, col}`). Extensions' own handled topics (for example the terminal's, §10.25) are requested as they are.
- **Confinement.** Everything a client sends acts only in the workspace it was given. Commands that reach outside it are refused for clients with `RelayCommandRefused`: the window tab commands (`emetos.workspaceTab.*`, `emetos.windowTab.*`), quitting and closing the window, opening or replacing a folder, new windows, profile switching, and writing user or profile settings (workspace settings are allowed); `emetos.commands.list` marks them as not allowed. A client cannot address a workspace by anything but the id the host gave it.
- **Login and transport.** SSH over TCP with the login of Remote Work (§10.18: public-key only, the listed keys, the host key pinned on the client on first use, passphrase dialog or `ssh-agent`), in `extensions/internal/sshlogin`, shared by both extensions. One SSH channel type `emetos-relay`; on it, versioned, length-prefixed JSON messages with a size limit each (hello with the protocol version and the granted workspaces; subscribe; event; publish; request and reply; execute and result; disconnect with a reason). No QUIC (no pictures to send).
- **State.** The host's settings (listening, port, the shared workspaces, the keys and their permissions) in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/relay.json` (mode 0600, written only by the tab); the client's pinned host keys in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/relay-hosts.json` (the saved hosts themselves, the selection and the history are the Relay tab's own state, §10.19 "As built (step 16.3)"). No settings file can turn hosting on.
- **Security** (also shown in the Be a Host section): a key with Watch only sees every event of the workspace, including document text and edits; a key with Watch and send can do anything the user can do in that workspace through its commands (edit and delete files, run tasks); typing in the host's terminals needs **Allow terminals** as well (§10.25). The rest is as Remote Work's notes.
- **Not built:** a client answering requests of the host, sharing events of window tabs that are not workspaces, recording and replaying sessions, scripting the Send panel.

**As built (step 16.1; `extension/core.go`, `internal/core/confine`, `internal/core/command/clientpolicy.go`, `internal/gui/exthost/{core,corefiles,coredocs}.go`, `internal/gui/app/extcoredocs.go`, `internal/gui/extensionsui`, `extensions/internal/fakeapi/requests.go`).** What the step decided where the text above leaves room:
- **Who answers.** The core topics are answered by the `Scope` of the window tab the request is made in (`bus.start` looks for a core topic before it looks for a handler of an extension), for the scopes of kind workspace; a window tab of an extension has no answer (`EventNoHandler`). An extension cannot own a topic under `emetos.` (`ExtensionTopicForeign`, and `emetos.commands` joins the ids `CheckManifest` reserves), so no handler can shadow one. The request is delivered, answered and replied on the UI thread like any request; the reply event has the publisher `emetos`. **The errors reach the requester untouched**: the error's tag is the failure's (`RelayCommandRefused`, `ConfineOutside`, `RelayStaleVersion`), not `EventHandlerFailed`, so the host's Relay can send the tag to its client. A request has the timeout of every request (its deadline, else 10 seconds, `EventTimeout`); a panic in the answering code is `CoreHandlerPanicked` and does not fail the requester. A payload that is not JSON of the request's type is `CorePayloadInvalid`; a request payload of `null` or nothing is the empty request.
- **Privileges.** `Manifest.Privileges []string` holds `extension.PrivilegeEventsPublishAny` (`events.publishAny`) and `extension.PrivilegeCommandsExecute` (`commands.execute`); `CheckManifest` refuses another name (`ExtensionPrivilegeUnknown`). The host keeps a fixed, read-only allowlist (`exthost.privilegedExtensions`, the one id `extension.RelayID` = `emetos.relay`); an extension that declares a privilege and is not on it is **left out as a whole** (`ExtensionPrivilegeRefused`, in `Host.Problems`; it is not installed, has no row, is never activated and is not asked to activate without the privilege), and the Extensions page lists it above the extensions under "Left out: these extensions were refused when Emetos started and are not installed." with the id, the reason and the tag (`extensionsui.Options.Problems`; every left-out extension is listed, not only these). The host reads the privileges from the manifest it probed when it started, never from what an extension returns later. `events.publishAny` lets the extension publish any valid topic in its scope (a core topic included; the event's publisher is the extension, so a receiver tells it from a core event, whose publisher is `emetos`; it is not delivered as a fast batch unless the manifest declares the topic with `Fast`); handling stays limited to the own topics, and subscribing and requesting were free already. `commands.execute` gates `emetos.commands.execute` only (`ExtensionPrivilegeMissing`); `commands.list` and the files and document topics need no privilege.
- **Commands.** `emetos.commands.list` takes no payload and answers `{commands: [{id, title, category, description, enabled, refused?, refusedClass?, reason?}]}` for every command of the registry of the window tab (those of Emetos and those of its extensions), ordered by id; `enabled` is "has a handler and its precondition holds in the context keys of the tab now". `emetos.commands.execute` takes `{id, args}` (`args` any JSON; none or `null` is nil) and runs the command in the registry of the requester's own window tab, with the source `SourceAPI`, on the UI thread; it answers `{result: null}` (a command returns no value, so the reply says only that it ran) or fails with `RelayCommandRefused` (metadata `command`, `class`), `CoreCommandNotFound`, `CoreCommandDisabled` (no handler here, or the precondition does not hold), `CoreCommandFailed` (the command returned an error of another package; an `*errors.Error` it returns reaches the requester as it is) or `CoreCommandsUnavailable`. Every run is logged at info level with the extension and the command. A command that opens a dialog or an input returns at once, and the dialog waits for the user of that machine.
- **Refused commands** (`command.ClientRefusal`, one list in `internal/core/command/clientpolicy.go`: exact ids and prefixes per class, the classes named by the `extension.Refused*` constants; a test checks that every id it names exists and that every command whose id looks like a window, folder, profile, quit or theme command is refused or allowed on purpose). Classes: `windowTab` (`emetos.workspaceTab.*`, `emetos.windowTab.*`), `quit` (`workbench.action.quit`, `closeWindow`), `window` (`newWindow`, `switchWindow`), `folder` (`workbench.action.files.openFolder`, `closeFolder`, `openRecent`, `clearRecentFiles`, `openRecentFolder`, `openRecentFile`), `profile` (`workbench.profiles.*`), `settings` (the commands that open or write the user's settings, keybindings and themes: `openSettings`, `openSettings2`, `openSettingsJson`, `openGlobalSettings`, `openGlobalKeybindings(File)`, `toggleAutoSave`, `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `zoomReset`, `selectTheme`, `selectIconTheme`, `editor.changeLanguageMode`, `keybindings.editor.*`, and `emetos.extensions.manageEventSharing`, the links between window tabs; the commands of the settings of the workspace stay allowed) and `remote` (`emetos.relay.*`, `emetos.remotework.*`). `emetos.commands.list` marks them with `refused: true`, `refusedClass` and `reason`. Anything else is allowed: a client can do what the user can do in that workspace.
- **Files** (`internal/core/confine`; `list`, `stat` and `read` run off the UI thread, in at most `exthost.FileOpSlots` = 4 at once per scope, the others wait for a slot within their deadline, `CoreFileWaitCanceled`; each takes the context of the request, so a timeout stops it). A path is relative to the folder of the scope, with forward slashes: `""` and `.` are the folder; an absolute path, an element `..` (even one that stays inside), a NUL or more than 4096 bytes is `ConfinePathInvalid`. **Confinement is `os.Root`**: every call opens the folder as a root (`openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH` on Linux, so every component is resolved beneath an open directory by the kernel: a symbolic link that points out, an absolute link even when it points inside, a `..` through a link, a link swapped in while the call runs, and a folder that is itself reached through a link cannot lead outside) and does everything through it, which closes the check-then-use race that `EvalSymlinks` and a later open would leave; the failure is `ConfineOutside`; a loop of links is `ConfineSymlinkLoop`, a missing path `ConfineNotFound`, a missing folder of the scope `ConfineRootFailed`, a scope with no folder `ConfineNoFolder`. A link that stays inside is followed by `stat`, `read` and a walk through it. `read` refuses a folder (`ConfineIsDirectory`) and a fifo, socket or device (`ConfineSpecialFile`) before it opens anything, opens the regular file with `O_NONBLOCK` (so a fifo swapped in cannot block it), and compares the opened file with the one it looked at (`os.SameFile`, else `ConfineChanged`). `emetos.files.list` takes `{path, depth, offset, limit}` and answers `{entries: [{path, name, kind, symlink?, size, modTime}], more?}`: `depth` 1 (the default) lists the children, at most 16; the entries are in the order of a walk that sorts each folder by name and lists a folder before what is in it; links are listed with kind `symlink` and not followed; `limit` defaults to 1000 and is at most 5000; **paging is by `offset`** (the next page asks with `offset + len(entries)` while `more` is true; the walk stops after the entries asked for and one more); a folder below the first that cannot be opened is skipped; a folder of more than 100,000 entries is `ConfineDirTooLarge`; a path that is not a folder is `ConfineNotDirectory`. `emetos.files.stat` takes `{path}` and answers the entry (a link inside is followed: the kind of what it points to and `symlink: true`). `emetos.files.read` takes `{path, maxBytes?}` and answers `{path, text, size, modTime}`: the file's bytes as a string, **UTF-8 only** (`ConfineNotText` otherwise), **at most 2 MiB** (`extension.MaxFilesReadSize`; `maxBytes` can lower it, not raise it; a larger file is `ConfineTooLarge` and is not truncated), with its line endings and byte order mark as they are; no other encoding is read. Memory is bounded by the slots times the limit.
- **Documents.** The positions of the document topics are those of the events: a zero-based line and a zero-based column in bytes of the UTF-8 line. The window's part is `exthost.CoreDocuments` (the `Documents` of the scope may implement it; else `CoreDocumentsUnavailable`), done by `extensionDocuments` in `gui/app`. `emetos.document.open` takes `{path, line, col}` (a file of the folder, checked as above: `CheckFile`, then opened by the window like any file, in the active group, with the cursor there; a window tab not on screen keeps the document open without an editor) and answers the document's info `{uri, languageId, version}`; the check is made before the window reads the file, so a link swapped in between is not covered (the window reads with its own file reader); a request that ends while the file is read lets go of the document (`ExtDocumentOpenCanceled`). `emetos.document.read` takes `{uri}` and answers `{uri, languageId, version, text, dirty?}` for any document that is open in the workspace, in or out of the folder (the events show its text already; `CoreDocumentNotOpen`, `CoreDocumentTooLarge` above 8 MiB, the tag `URIInvalid` for a bad URI). `edit`, `save`, `close` and `reveal` act on an open document that is a **file of the folder** (the path is checked with `confine.Contains` off the UI thread, links resolved, the folder given through a link accepted by its real path too; another file is `ConfineOutside`) or an untitled one (not for `save`, which would ask for a name); any other scheme is `CoreDocumentSchemeUnsupported`. **The version model**: a document's version (`Document.Version()`, the `version` of the events) grows with every edit, undo and redo (a client compares it for equality only); `emetos.document.edit` takes `{uri, version, edits: [{range, text}]}` and applies the edits only when `version` is the current one (`RelayStaleVersion`, metadata `version` and `current`: the client reads again and retries; no merging is attempted). The ranges are in the text of that version, as in `emetos.document.changed`, are checked as a whole before the first change (inside the text, on a character boundary, ending at or after their start, not overlapping; touching is fine: `CoreEditInvalid`; at most 10,000 edits and 4 MiB of text: `CoreEditTooLarge`; a read-only document: `CoreDocumentReadOnly`), and are made as **one undo step** with `document.Edit` (`KindOther`, between two `PushStackElement`, as the edit of a rename), while the window keeps the cursors of its editors in place; the reply is `{uri, version, changed}` with the new version. `emetos.document.save` takes `{uri}` and answers `{uri, version, as: false}` when the file is written, through the window's Save command path (the save participants of the language, format on save and the conflict handling run; a save that does not happen, a read-only document, a failed write, a window tab not on screen, is an error and the window tab shows its notification as it does for the user). `emetos.document.close` takes `{uri, discard?}`: the editors that show the document close without a question and the document goes with the last; **a document with unsaved changes is closed only with `discard: true`** (`CoreDocumentDirty`). `emetos.editor.reveal` takes `{uri, line, col}`, brings the editor of the open document to the front of the active group with the cursor there (a new editor when none shows it; `ExtDocumentRevealUnavailable` when the window tab is not on screen) and answers `{uri}`.
- **Test seams.** `rig.noCommands` and `rig.noCoreDocs` (exthost tests), `fakeCoreDocs` (real `document.Document`s behind the `CoreDocuments` of a test scope). **For 16.2 and 16.3: `fakeapi` has no core**; a test routes a request to a double with `api.OnRequest(topic, fn)` or `fakeapi.OnRequestValue[P](api, topic, fn)` (the core topics and the handled topics of other extensions are faked this way; the fake also records `Requests()` and `PublishedEvents()`, answers an unfaked topic with `EventNoHandler`, routes the extension's own requests to its own `Handle` handlers, and lets a test call them with `Ask`). The replies come on `Pump`, as the UI thread does. The core's own behavior is tested in `exthost` and in `app` over a real workspace.
