- **Tags** of this step: `ExtensionPrivilegeUnknown`, `ExtensionPrivilegeRefused`, `ExtensionPrivilegeMissing`, `RelayCommandRefused`, `RelayStaleVersion`, `CorePayloadInvalid`, `CoreHandlerPanicked`, `CoreCommandsUnavailable`, `CoreCommandNotFound`, `CoreCommandDisabled`, `CoreCommandFailed`, `CoreFileWaitCanceled`, `CoreDocumentsUnavailable`, `CoreDocumentNotOpen`, `CoreDocumentSchemeUnsupported`, `CoreDocumentTooLarge`, `CoreDocumentReadOnly`, `CoreDocumentDirty`, `CoreEditInvalid`, `CoreEditTooLarge`, `ExtDocumentOpenCanceled`, `ExtDocumentNotSaved`, `ExtDocumentSaveUnavailable`, `ExtDocumentRevealUnavailable`, and in `core/confine`: `ConfinePathInvalid`, `ConfineNoFolder`, `ConfineRootFailed`, `ConfineOutside`, `ConfineSymlinkLoop`, `ConfineNotFound`, `ConfineFailed`, `ConfineNotDirectory`, `ConfineIsDirectory`, `ConfineSpecialFile`, `ConfineChanged`, `ConfineTooLarge`, `ConfineNotText`, `ConfineDirTooLarge`, `ConfineCanceled`. `NewHeadlessView` stays not privilege-restricted (§10.18 "As built (step 15.1)").

**As built (step 16.2; `extensions/relay/{relay,config,hub,hubstate,session,ops,outbox,tab,dev}.go`, `extensions/relay/protocol`, `extensions/relay/client` and `client/clienttest`, `extensions/internal/{pageui,statefile,sshlogin}`, `extensions/all.go`, `scripts/proof-relay.sh`).** The host, its protocol and the "Be a Host" section of the tab; the client's side of the tab (16.3) comes after it. No new dependency. Where the text above leaves room:
- **Shared code.** What Remote Work and Relay both needed moved out of `extensions/remotework` into `extensions/internal`: `pageui` (the gaps, the section with its heading, the line under a control, the problem box, the labelled field), `statefile.DirFromEnv` (the state folder from `XDG_STATE_HOME` or `~/.local/state`, `/emetos`), `sshlogin.ReadPublicKeyFile` (a `.pub` file: one line, at most 16 KiB, `SSHLoginPubFileUnreadable`, `SSHLoginPubFileInvalid`) and `sshlogin.{HostOf, RefusalWords, Throttle}` (the notice of a refusal, one for each address a minute). Remote Work's tests pass unchanged apart from what they imported.
- **The extension.** `emetos.relay` (`relay.NewFactory(HubOptions)`, listed by `extensions.All()` with `Camera: keyqr.NewV4L2()`); its manifest declares the privileges `events.publishAny` and `commands.execute` and the window tab kind `emetos.relay.tab` ("Relay", `+` menu). One `Hub` per `extensions.All()` call (no global state) is shared by the instance of each workspace scope and by each Relay tab, as Remote Work's is. A real `extensions.All()` registration is checked to be granted the privileges (`exthost/relay_test.go`); its own calls are checked like any other (a refused command is `RelayCommandRefused`).
- **State.** `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/relay.json` (version 1: `listening`, `port`, `workspaces` as folders, `keys` with `line`, `added` and `permissions` by folder: `none`, `watch`, `send`; a folder not listed is `watch`; the entries of folders that are not shared are kept) is read with `statefile.Read` (refused when others can write it, not a regular file, or over 1 MiB) and written only by the tab, atomically with mode 0600. A file that is not valid leaves hosting off and the tab read-only with the reason (`RelayConfigInvalid`, `RelayConfigUnusable`); no setting turns hosting on. The host key is `relay-host-key` in the same folder (mode 0600, made the first time it is needed by `sshlogin.LoadOrCreateHostKey`): a key of its own, so that Relay's fingerprint is not Remote Work's. At most 256 keys (`RelayTooManyKeys`; a duplicate is `RelayKeyDuplicate`) and 64 shared workspaces (`RelayTooManyWorkspaces`). **Only an open workspace with a folder can be shared** (a tab with no folder cannot, and two tabs of one folder share the first: `RelayWorkspaceInvalid`); a folder that stays in the file while its workspace is not open is shared again when the workspace opens, with a new ID.
- **Listener.** TCP on the port (47124 by default; 1 to 65535) on every interface, only while the switch is on; the switch writes `relay.json` first, then opens the listener; a port that cannot be bound is shown in the tab in the color of errors with the reason (`RelayListenFailed`, `Hub.ListenError`) and as a notification, and the switch stays on (the setting is the user's), with hosting off in fact; Apply tries again. The login is `sshlogin.NewServer`: public key only, the keys of the list, one channel type `emetos-relay`, a limit of 5 failures a minute for each address (the limiter of 15.2); **no other channel and no session request**. A client that has logged in and sends no Hello within 10 s (`HelloTimeout`) is ended with reason `protocol`. The host serves at most `MaxSessions` = 32 clients; the 33rd gets a Disconnect of reason `busy`. A key that is not in the list never reaches the channel.
- **Dev knob.** `EMETOS_DEV_RELAY_BIND` (`DevBindEnv`), read only in debug builds and builds with `emetos_dev` (`dev_on.go`/`dev_off.go`, D15), makes the default listener bind one address instead of every interface, so that a proof or a check of a real Emetos listens on `127.0.0.1` only. A release build ignores it. Tests give `HubOptions.Listen` their own loopback listener.
- **The protocol** (`protocol`, version 1). A message is `type:1 | length:4 (big endian) | JSON:length`. The length is checked against the limit of the type before anything is read or allocated; a type that is unknown or that the sender may not send is refused before its payload is read; the payload must be valid UTF-8 and JSON, nested at most 64 levels, one object with nothing after it, decoded with unknown fields refused; every field is checked and a message is refused, never repaired; an accepted message encodes back to the same value (raw JSON values are compacted). Tags: `RelayTruncated`, `RelayUnknownType`, `RelayWrongDirection`, `RelayTooLarge`, `RelayTrailing`, `RelayBadJSON`, `RelayTooDeep`, `RelayBadValue`, `RelayVersionMismatch`, `RelayEncodeTooLarge`, `RelayEncodeInvalid`, `RelayNilMessage`, `RelayReadFailed`, `RelayWriteFailed`.

  | Type | From | Fields | Limit of the payload |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Hello | both | `magic` ("EMPA"), `version` (1), host only: `workspaces` [{`id`, `name`, `permission`: `watch` or `send`}], at most 64 | 32 KiB |
  | Subscribe | client | `id`, `workspace`, `patterns` (at most 16, each a topic pattern of at most 200 bytes; none means every topic of the workspace), `off` (stop) | 8 KiB |
  | Event | host | `workspace`, `seq` (per client and workspace), `at` (Unix milliseconds), `topic`, `publisher`, `data` or `batch` (a fast topic's values, at most 10,000), `truncated` and `size` (the values were left out because they are larger than 1 MiB) | 1 MiB + 4 KiB |
  | Publish | client (send) | `id`, `workspace`, `topic`, `data` | 1 MiB + 4 KiB |
  | Request | client (send) | `id`, `workspace`, `topic`, `data`, `timeoutMillis` (at most 60,000) | 1 MiB + 4 KiB |
  | Execute | client (send) | `id`, `workspace`, `command`, `args` | 1 MiB + 4 KiB |
  | Reply / Result | host | `id`, `data` or `error` {`tag`, `message` of at most 1,024 bytes} | 16 MiB + 4 KiB |
  | Disconnect | both | `reason` (`host`, `off`, `keyRemoved`, `closed`, `protocol`, `version`, `stalled`, `busy`) and `text` of at most 512 bytes | 2 KiB |

  An operation's `id` is a number from 1 to 2^53-1 chosen by the client; a workspace `id` is 8 to 64 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores; a topic and a pattern follow §10.15's syntax. The first message in each direction is a Hello and a side that sends anything else first is ended with reason `protocol`; a Hello of another version is answered with a Disconnect of reason `version`. The host sends a new Hello whenever the grants of the client change (a workspace shared or unshared, a permission changed), so the client's list is always the host's. The event `emetos.relay.dropped` {`count`} (publisher `emetos.relay`) tells a client how many events it missed.
- **Workspace IDs.** The id a client knows a workspace by is 128 random bits in hex, made when the workspace becomes shared and open and kept while it stays so: it is derived from nothing on the machine (no path, no tab id), and a workspace that is unshared and shared again gets a new one. The name is the folder's base name, with " (2)" and so on for the same name twice. A client that names a workspace it was not granted, one that is no longer shared or one that does not exist gets the same `RelayWorkspaceUnknown`, which tells it nothing about the others.
- **Forwarding.** The instance of a shared workspace subscribes to `**` in its own scope and, on the UI thread, hands each event to `Hub.forward`, which queues it for each client that is granted the workspace and subscribed to its topic (a Subscribe with no patterns means every topic; the same event is encoded once for all clients). Nothing but a queue push happens on the UI thread: it never blocks. The queue of each client holds at most 1,024 events and 8 MiB (`MaxQueuedEvents`, `MaxQueuedBytes`); when it is full the new events are dropped and counted, and the count is queued as one `emetos.relay.dropped` event in the place of the run, so the client sees the gap where it is; a client that takes nothing for 60 s (`StallTimeout`) is ended with reason `stalled`. Replies are not dropped. A value over 1 MiB is not sent: the event is sent with `truncated` and its `size`.
- **Watch only and Watch and send.** Both are checked twice, when the message is read (a quick refusal) and again on the UI thread of the workspace just before the operation acts, so that a permission taken back or a workspace unshared in between stops it (`RelayWatchOnly`, `RelayWorkspaceUnknown`). A client with Watch only may Subscribe and nothing else. A client with Watch and send publishes with the privilege `events.publishAny` (the event's publisher is `emetos.relay`, so a receiver tells it from a core event), requests any topic (the core topics of 16.1 and the handled topics of other extensions) and executes commands through `emetos.commands.execute`, all in the scope of that workspace and no other; the refusal of §10.19 "Confinement" is `RelayCommandRefused`, and the tag of a failure reaches the client as it is (`CoreCommandNotFound`, `ConfineOutside`, `EventTimeout`, ...). A request has the timeout the client asked for (at most 60 s) or 10 s (`RequestTimeout`). A client has at most 16 operations running (`MaxInFlight`; `RelayTooBusy`) and may not reuse the id of one that is running (`RelayDuplicateID`). A reply larger than the limit is answered with `RelayReplyTooLarge`, and the operations of a client end with it (`RelaySessionEnded`). **A client never answers anything for the host**: it has no handler, and the host reads no Reply or Result.
- **Changes while connected.** Removing a key ends its sessions (reason `keyRemoved`); unsharing a workspace takes it from the Hello of the clients (they get a new Hello) and removes the banners; changing a permission sends a new Hello (a client that lost Send fails its next Publish with `RelayWatchOnly`); turning the switch off or changing the port ends every session (reason `off`); the user's Disconnect ends one (reason `host`); Emetos closing ends them (`closed`).
- **Banners, notifications, logs.** Each shared workspace shows one banner for each client given it: "Relay: <key comment> connected (watch only | watch and send)" with Disconnect (the banner's text changes when the permission does and goes when the client does). Every connection, disconnection and refused login is logged at info and warn level with the key's comment and fingerprint, the address and the reason, and raises a notification in the shared workspaces: a refusal one for each address a minute (`Throttle`, so a flood of attempts is one line), a connection or disconnection each time. The log carries no event, no text of a document and no command argument; a refused or failed operation is logged with its tag and the topic or the command's id only.
- **The tab** (`relay.go`, `tab.go`). Its title is "Relay". The page has the heading, the section **Be a Host** (the switch with the state under it, the port with Apply, "Workspaces to share" with a checkbox for each open workspace, "Allowed keys", "Host key of this computer" with the fingerprint, and the "Security" notes of §10.19) and, for 16.3, nothing yet: the **Hosts** section, the Events and Send panels and the saved hosts are step 16.3's. Under "Allowed keys" each key shows its comment, type and fingerprint, **Remove**, and for each shared workspace a drop-down of **No access**, **Watch only** (the default for a new key) and **Watch and send**; a key is added by pasting an `authorized_keys` line, by **Choose .pub File...** (the file chooser of the desktop, `ReadPublicKeyFile`) or by **Scan QR Code...** (the dialog of 15.5 over `keyqr` and `qrui`, with the Camera of `HubOptions`; the button is disabled with the reason when no camera can be read). A key listed twice is `RelayKeyDuplicate`. The tab keeps no state of its own (a state it does not know is refused: `RelayTabStateInvalid`); the hub does not depend on a tab being open (the instances of the workspaces keep it running). The tab is the one writer of `relay.json`; two tabs write through the same hub, under its lock.
- **The client package** (`extensions/relay/client`, for 16.3; imports `protocol` and `sshlogin` only): `client.Connect(ctx, Options)` logs in with `sshlogin.Dial` (a key file, the passphrase of a dialog, or `ssh-agent`; the host key pinned through a `HostStore`) and opens the channel `emetos-relay`; the first message is the Hello and **the client refuses a Hello of another version** (`RelayHandshakeFailed`, `RelayHelloTimeout`). `Client.Subscribe`, `Publish`, `Request`, `Execute` return the reply (`RelayRemoteError` carries the host's tag and message), `Events()` is a bounded channel (a client that does not read it is ended by the host as `stalled`), `Workspaces()` is the host's list and `Close`. Tags: `RelayConnectionClosed`, `RelayCancelled`, `RelayValueInvalid`. `client/clienttest` has a host double that speaks the protocol, for 16.3's tab. All of it is tested over loopback against the real host.
- **Tests.** The protocol (every message round-trips; every limit, a truncated, trailing, deep, wrong-direction and unknown message; a fuzz target `FuzzDecode` with the seed corpus in the normal run and 30 s of fuzzing at `-parallel=1`, `GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB` once at the end of the step), the config (read policy, write mode, the file refused when others can write it), the hub on loopback with real SSH clients (login and refusal of unlisted keys and passwords, the 5-a-minute limit, the one channel type, forwarding to the granted workspaces only, Watch only refusing every operation, Watch and send acting in its workspace only, the tags of the core reaching the client, a permission taken back while connected, a workspace unshared, a key removed, the switch off, subscribe patterns, batches and large events, the banner and its Disconnect, several clients at once, a client that breaks the protocol, a duplicate ID, the limits on operations and sessions, drop counting and the stall watchdog), the tab (goldens in dark and light of on, off and "port taken": `extensions/relay/testdata/goldens/tab_{on,off,port_taken}_{dark,light}.png`, and the behavior of every control), and four end-to-end tests over real windows (`internal/gui/app/relay_test.go`: a client that watches, requests and runs commands in a shared workspace of a real `Workspaces` with the real core topics of 16.1 and changes nothing else; a request that reaches the extensions of the workspace with a timeout that ends it; a Watch only key that changes nothing; unsharing and closing a workspace). The tests use the isolated `XDG_*` folders and a loopback listener on an ephemeral port.
- **Proof.** `scripts/proof-relay.sh docs/implemented-proof-images/16.2-relay-host.png` (method B): the tab with hosting on, two shared workspaces (`notes` and `server`), a key (alice) with Watch only in `notes` and Watch and send in `server`, and a key (bob) with Watch only in `notes` and no access to `server`. The state is `testdata/proof/16.2/state/relay.json.template` with **public keys only** (the private halves were never kept); the script fills in the checkout's path and a free port and runs the debug build with `EMETOS_DEV_RELAY_BIND=127.0.0.1`. (`scripts/proof.sh --launch` reports "the launch failed" when the capture ends the editor before the launch's connection closes, for the proof of 9b.3 too; the image is complete.)
- **Not built here:** the Hosts section and the Events and Send panels (16.3); the client's saved hosts and `relay-hosts.json` (16.3).
- **Tags** of this step: `RelayConfigInvalid`, `RelayConfigUnusable`, `RelayDuplicateID`, `RelayIDFailed`, `RelayKeyDuplicate`, `RelayKeyUnknown`, `RelayListenFailed`, `RelayNoStateDir`, `RelayPermissionInvalid`, `RelayReplyTooLarge`, `RelaySessionEnded`, `RelaySettingInvalid`, `RelayTabStateInvalid`, `RelayTooBusy`, `RelayTooManyKeys`, `RelayTooManyWorkspaces`, `RelayWatchOnly`, `RelayWorkspaceInvalid`, `RelayWorkspaceUnknown` (and `RelayCommandRefused` of 16.1, sent to the client as it is), those of `protocol` above, those of the client (`RelayCancelled`, `RelayConnectionClosed`, `RelayHandshakeFailed`, `RelayHelloTimeout`, `RelayRemoteError`, `RelayValueInvalid`), and `StateFileDirUnknown` of `statefile.DirFromEnv` and the tags of `ReadPublicKeyFile`.


**As built (step 16.3; `extensions/relay/{clientstate,clienttab,hostconn,eventlog,eventsview,sendpanel,hostsview,dev}.go`, `extensions/internal/keyform`, `extensions/internal/loginui`, `extensions/relay/client/clienttest`, `scripts/proof-relay-client.sh`).** The client side of the tab: the Hosts section and the Events and Send panels. No new dependency. Where the text above leaves room:
- **Shared code.** The choice of the key (a private key file, or a key of the ssh-agent; the box, the dialog of the desktop, the list of the agent's keys, the line of the public key that Show My Public Key as QR Code draws) moved out of Remote Work's connect dialog into `extensions/internal/keyform` and is used by both (Remote Work's goldens are unchanged; its tests changed only in the names of the fields they read). `loginui` gained a `Wording` (`Prompter.SetWording`; Remote Work's is the default) so that the first-use question says "Open the Be a Host section of the Relay tab on that computer" and the warning of a changed key says "or Relay was set up again there". `clienttest` gained `Proxy` (a loopback forwarder with `Drop`, for a network that fails) and `HostStore` (pins and reads `relay-hosts.json` from a test that cannot import `sshlogin`).
- **State.** The tab saves `{hosts, selected, history}` (`tabState`; unknown fields, more than 64 hosts, a duplicate ID, a selected host that is not saved, more than 50 history items, or a value over 8 KiB are `RelayTabStateInvalid`/`RelayHostInvalid`). A saved host is `{id, name?, host, port, key: "file"|"agent", keyFile?, fingerprint?}`: a path or a fingerprint, **never a passphrase** (the type has no field for one). The pins stay in `relay-hosts.json` (`sshlogin.HostStore`, one pin for each `host:port`, kept when a host is removed, as `known_hosts` keeps one). The selection is a host ID and the **name** of a workspace, because the ID the host gives a workspace is new each time it is shared; it is resolved against the host's list at every Hello. A restored tab shows its hosts as disconnected (nothing connects by itself, so no question appears at start) and subscribes to the selected workspace when its host is connected. Two tabs have two lists. The same `host:port` twice is `RelayHostDuplicate`; a tab holds at most 64 hosts (`RelayTooManyHosts`).
- **The Hosts section.** Each host shows its name (or address), its address, its state (Disconnected; Connecting...; Connected, N workspaces, watch only | watch and send; Connection lost, connecting again (attempt n); Ended: <reason> with what the user can do, in the color of errors for a failure) and **Connect** or **Disconnect**, **Remove**; a connected host lists the workspaces it grants this key with their permission, and a click selects one. **Add Host...** opens the form: address, port (47124), an optional name, the key (`keyform`) and Show My Public Key as QR Code (the dialog of 15.5; a key file asks its passphrase only if its public half is not in the clear). Several hosts are connected at once, each with its own goroutine and state; questions to the user (the passphrase, the fingerprint) are asked one at a time. At most one workspace is selected in the tab; selecting another subscribes to it and unsubscribes from the old one (the host only forwards what is subscribed), and **starts a new log**.
- **Pinning.** `client.Connect` with `sshlogin.Dial`: an unknown `host:port` shows the fingerprint dialog and pins on Trust (Cancel is "You did not trust ...", nothing is pinned or sent); a pinned key is trusted silently; a different key is refused before anything is sent (`SSHLoginHostKeyChanged`), the host shows "The key of <address> changed" and the warning dialog with both fingerprints, whose **Forget the Old Key** makes the next connection a first use again.
- **Reconnection.** After a connection that had been made drops (the read fails, or the host says `closed` or `stalled`), the client waits 1 s, then 2, 4 ... at most 30 s (`ClientOptions.Backoff`), shows "Connection lost" and the attempt, and connects again, then watches the selected workspace again and says "Connected again" in the log. A first connection that fails is not retried (the user sees why); neither is anything the host decided (`host`, `off`, `keyRemoved`, `protocol`, `version`, `busy`: the host is "Ended" with the reason), nor a refused key or a changed host key; only `SSHLoginConnectFailed`, `SSHLoginChannelRefused` and `RelayHelloTimeout` after a connection are the network's. The key file's key is unlocked once (the passphrase dialog; the bytes are wiped when used) and the **unlocked key is kept in memory only, for the reconnections of that conversation**; Disconnect, an end and closing the tab drop it, and the next Connect asks again. The ssh-agent is asked at every connection.
- **The Events panel.** The log of the selected workspace: a row has the time (the tab's time zone), the topic, the publisher, a count for a batch (`x18`; a batch is **one row with its count and its last value**) and the value as one line of JSON; a tap expands it into its lines (two spaces of indent, at most 120 lines of 240 bytes; the lines are made the first time the row is expanded, never before, and the row's height is known without building it). `emetos.relay.dropped` shows as a row of its own ("N events were dropped by the host"). **What this client sends** (publish, request, run) is a row too, with its reply or its error (tag and message) and the **duration measured here**: the requests of other clients and of the host's own code are not events the bus forwards, so the panel cannot show them. Lines of the client's own ("Connected", "Watching <workspace>", "Connection lost ...", "Disconnected", the reason of an end) are notes that the filter never hides. **Filter**: a text with a star is a topic pattern (§10.15: `emetos.document.*`, `emetos.**`), any other text is a case-insensitive part of the topic; a text with a star that is not a pattern shows every row and says so. **Pause** holds the rows that come (at most 10,000, the oldest dropped) and Resume adds them in order; what the user sends shows at once. **Clear** empties the log and what is held; the filter and the pause stay. **Caps**: 10,000 rows and 16 MiB for a log (the oldest go first); a row keeps at most 4 KiB of its value (a longer one is cut on a character boundary and says how large it was; a value the host did not send, over its 1 MiB, says so).
- **Rendering and threads.** A Glutter `ListView` builder in reverse (the newest row at the bottom; at the end it stays there; scrolled up it is moved by the height of the rows that arrive, so what the user reads does not move, `// Glutter:`, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`) with an item extent for every row: only the rows in view are built. The connection's goroutine makes the row of an event without parsing its value (only the marker of dropped events is read), puts it in a bounded inbox (10,000 rows and 16 MiB; what is lost is counted and shown) and, for the first row after a drain, starts one timer (33 ms, `ClientOptions.DrainDelay`) whose function carries every row to the UI thread with one `Post`: **never one post for each event**, and the tab is built once for a whole burst. Events of a workspace that is not the one selected are dropped there. All goroutines stop on Disconnect, Remove and tab close (the tests check for leaks).
- **The Send panel** (only for a selected workspace of a connected host whose permission is Watch and send; nothing of it shows for Watch only, and a send that is forced anyway is refused locally, `RelaySendInvalid`): Topic and a JSON value (Publish, Request); **Run Command**: a drop-down of the host's commands (`emetos.commands.list`, asked once for a workspace when it is selected), the refused ones listed, dimmed and not choosable with "not allowed for clients (class)", and the JSON arguments; under them the reply (indented, at most 60 lines of the first 16 KiB), the error with its tag (`failed: RelayCommandRefused`, `ConfineOutside`, `EventTimeout`) or "nothing came back". A topic must be a topic (§10.15) and a value valid JSON or empty. The history keeps the last **50** items (the same thing twice in a row is one), none whose value is over 8 KiB, in the tab's state; a tap puts an item back in the boxes. A client has no handlers and answers nothing for the host.
- **Dev commands** (debug builds and `emetos_dev`, in the scope of the tab; they do what the user does): `dev.relay.addHost`, `dev.relay.connect`, `dev.relay.select`, `dev.relay.send`.
- **Tests.** The tab on a fake API against real hosts on loopback (`client_test.go`: events from a host, first use and a refused first use, a changed key and Forget, filter, Pause, Clear and the 10,000 cap, expanding a row, a burst as one drain, the dropped marker, the place of the list, the Send panel with replies, errors and the history, Run Command and the refused ones, no Send panel for Watch only, a dropped connection, a passphrase asked once and never saved, several hosts, a host that ends it, Remove, closing the tab, the saved state coming back, Add Host and Show My Public Key as QR Code, the ssh-agent, the dev commands, what went wrong in words), the log, the inbox and the state on their own (`eventlog_test.go`, `clientstate_test.go`), goldens (`client_{events,send,watchonly,hosts}_{dark,light}.png`; the goldens of Be a Host changed because the Hosts section is above it), and two Emetos in one process on loopback (`internal/gui/app/relayclient_test.go`: the client sees `emetos.document.changed` while a file is edited on the host, lists files, opens, reads and edits a file with the document topics (a stale version is refused), runs Save and a command of an extension of the host, requests the handled topic of that extension, is refused outside the workspace (`ConfineOutside`, `ConfinePathInvalid`, `RelayCommandRefused`), sees no Send panel for Watch only, connects again after a drop, holds two hosts, asks about a new host and refuses a changed key).
- **Proof.** `scripts/proof-relay-client.sh docs/implemented-proof-images/16.3-relay-client.png` (method B): two isolated instances on loopback; the host (A) listens on 127.0.0.1 only (`EMETOS_DEV_RELAY_BIND`) and shares `testdata/proof/16.3/server` (Watch and send) and `notes` (Watch only) for a key made at run time by `scripts/proof-relay-client-setup` in a temporary folder that is removed afterwards (**no private key is committed**); the client's `relay-hosts.json` already holds A's host key (the pin of a user who compared the fingerprint), so the proof does not stop at the first-use dialog; the dev commands of B add the host, connect, select "server" and send three requests (open, edit, list).
- **Tags** of this step: `RelayHostInvalid`, `RelayHostDuplicate`, `RelayTooManyHosts`, `RelaySendInvalid`, `RelayReplyInvalid`, `RelayDevInvalid`, and `ClientTestProxyFailed` (of `clienttest`); `RelayTabStateInvalid` and `RelayIDFailed` have new constructors.
- **Fixes to the host of 16.2 found by this step's tests.** (1) A **lock-order inversion**: `Hub.forward` asked each session (`Session.mu`) with the hub's lock held while `Session.applyGrants` asked the hub (`Hub.mu`) with the session's lock held, so forwarding events while the grants changed could deadlock. The order is written at `Hub` (recMu, then `Hub.mu`, then `Session.mu`; the hub never calls a session with its lock held, a session never calls the hub with its lock held; immutable fields are read without a lock); `forward` copies the sessions and asks them after letting go, `applyGrants` asks the hub before it takes its own lock; `TestForwardingAndGrantChangesRunTogetherWithoutDeadlock` runs both at once under `-race` and hangs on the old code. (2) The tab let go of its input boxes from the goroutine that cancels the extension's context, which raced with the window tearing the widgets down; the boxes are now let go on the UI thread when the tab is closed (`disposeClientUI`).
- **Not built here:** a log for each workspace kept while another is selected, connecting at start, copying a value or searching in an expanded one, showing the requests of other clients.

### 10.20 Containers: Docker and Podman (`extensions/containers`, `extensions/podman`)

Two extensions in the spirit of VS Code's **Container Tools** (`microsoft/vscode-containers`, MIT: its design, texts, templates and command ids may be ported, each ported file saying so with a `// Ported from vscode-containers: <path>` line, and its license added to `NOTICE`), one for Docker (`emetos.containers`, named "Containers" on the Extensions page, its commands `containers.*`) and one for Podman (`emetos.podman`, "Podman", `podman.*`). They share the engine client and the views, so they look and behave alike; Podman adds what only Podman has (D22).

- **The engine client** (`extensions/internal/containerapi`, plain Go, no new dependency): the Docker Engine API (version negotiated with `/_ping` and `/version`, at least 1.41) and Podman's libpod API (`/v4.0.0/libpod/...`, at least Podman 4) over HTTP on a Unix socket (`net/http` with a dialer), or on `tcp://` with TLS (`DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY`, `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`). List, inspect, create, start, stop, restart, pause, unpause, kill, remove and rename containers; images (list, inspect, pull with progress, tag, remove, history, prune); networks and volumes (list, inspect, create, remove, prune); the event stream (`/events`, which drives refreshes: no polling); logs (follow, timestamps, tail, the multiplexed stream split into stdout and stderr); `exec` (create and start, non-interactive, output captured); `system df`. Every call takes a `ctx`; streams end on cancel; response bodies are limited; errors keep the engine's message (`ContainerAPI*` tags).
- **Which engine.** Docker: `containers.host` (setting), else `DOCKER_HOST`, else the current Docker context (`$DOCKER_CONFIG` or `~/.docker/config.json` and `contexts/meta`), else `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`; the view's title bar has a context picker. Podman: `podman.host`, else `CONTAINER_HOST`, else the user's socket `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock`, else rootful `/run/podman/podman.sock` when it can be opened; when no socket answers, Emetos starts **its own** `podman system service --time=0 unix://$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/emetos/podman-<pid>.sock` as a child (in its own process group, stopped when Emetos ends or the extension is turned off), so nothing has to be enabled in systemd. A missing engine shows a view with the reason and a Retry button, not an error.
- **The side bar view** (one activity bar icon each, the Codicons of Container Tools): sections **Containers** (grouped by Compose project, or by pod for Podman; state icon, image, ports, uptime; a filter), **Images** (grouped by repository; size, age; dangling images marked), **Networks**, **Volumes**, and for Docker **Contexts**, for Podman **Pods** and **Connections** (`podman system connection list`, rootless and rootful). Items have context menus with the actions above; Start, Stop, Restart and Remove act on a multi-selection. The view refreshes from the event stream, debounced.
- **Container actions.** View Logs (a panel tab per container, following, with stdout and stderr colored, a filter, pause and clear, bounded to 10,000 lines), Inspect (the JSON in a read-only editor tab), Open in Browser (a published HTTP port), Copy ID, Open Shell (the user's terminal emulator, `containers.terminal` / `podman.terminal`, else `$TERMINAL`, `x-terminal-emulator`, `gnome-terminal`, `konsole`; running `docker exec -it <id> <shell>`; Emetos has no integrated terminal), Run Command (a non-interactive `exec` whose output goes to a panel tab), Explore Files (the container's files as a read-only tree and editor tabs, through `exec ls`/`cat` or the archive endpoint, bounded in size).
- **Image actions.** Run (a form: name, ports, environment, volumes, `--rm`), Run Interactive (in the terminal emulator), Pull (with progress in a notification), Tag, Push (through the `docker`/`podman` CLI so the user's credential helpers are used), Remove, Inspect, History. **Build Image** from a `Dockerfile`/`Containerfile` (explorer and editor context menus, the command palette): the CLI's `build` with the folder as context, the output streamed into a panel tab, errors with `file:line` into Problems.
- **Compose** (Docker: `docker compose`; Podman: `podman compose` or `podman-compose`, whichever is found): Compose Up, Up (select services), Down, Restart and Logs on a `compose.yaml`/`docker-compose.yml` (explorer and editor context menus, and on a Compose group of the Containers section). The CLI is used, run in the workspace folder.
- **Podman only.** Pods (create from selected containers, start, stop, restart, remove, inspect; containers grouped under their pod), **Generate Kube YAML** (`podman kube generate`, opened in an editor tab), **Play Kube** (`podman kube play` on a YAML file, and `kube down`), **Generate Quadlet** (a `.container` unit for systemd from a container's settings, opened as an untitled editor; written by the user, never installed by Emetos).
- **Scaffolding.** "Add Docker Files to Workspace" (ported from Container Tools' templates for Go, Node.js, Python, .NET and a plain image): asks the platform, port and Compose, writes `Dockerfile`/`Containerfile`, `.dockerignore` and optionally `compose.yaml`, refusing to overwrite without a confirmation.
- **Language support.** The Dockerfile and Compose grammars are bundled already (§8.1). When `docker-langserver` (dockerfile-language-server-nodejs) or `docker-compose-langserver` is on `PATH` (or set in `containers.dockerfileLanguageServer.path`), the extension declares it as a language server (§9.12); it never installs them.
- **Safety.** A remove, a prune and a `system prune` ask first, listing what goes (the count and the size from `system df`); running containers are never removed without the "force" choice. Access to the Docker socket is power over the computer (root-equivalent): the README and the view's first-run note say so.
- **Events** published (other extensions may subscribe): `emetos.containers.changed` / `emetos.podman.changed` `{kind, id, action}`, debounced, and `emetos.containers.buildFinished` `{image, ok}`.
- **Not built:** registries other than through the CLI (no Docker Hub, ACR or GHCR explorer), Docker Swarm and Kubernetes clusters, remote engines over `ssh://` (a `tcp://` with TLS works), "Attach Visual Studio Code" (dev containers), debugging inside containers, an interactive shell inside Emetos (needs the integrated terminal).

### 10.21 SQL databases (`extensions/sql`)

`emetos.sql` ("SQL Databases"): connections to **PostgreSQL**, **MySQL and MariaDB**, **SQLite** and **SQL Server** (D23), a side bar explorer of their schema, `.sql` editors bound to a connection, and the results in a panel.

- **Drivers** (all pure Go, through `database/sql`): `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` (`stdlib`), `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql`, `modernc.org/sqlite`, `github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb`. Each engine has a small dialect (`extensions/sql/dialect`): how to list databases, schemas, tables, views, columns (type, nullable, default, primary key), indexes, foreign keys, functions and procedures; identifier quoting; `LIMIT` versus `TOP`; how to cancel a running statement (pgx's cancel request, MySQL's `KILL QUERY`, SQL Server's attention, SQLite's interrupt).
- **Connections** (shared with MongoDB and Redis, `extensions/internal/dbconn`): a form (name, engine, host, port, user, database; or a file for SQLite; or a connection URL; TLS mode and CA file; a color; **read-only**), kept in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/db-connections.json` (mode 0600, written only by the form) with a scope: the user (every workspace) or this workspace. **Passwords are never written to an Emetos file**: "Save password" keeps it in the desktop's keyring through the **Secret Service** D-Bus API (`org.freedesktop.secrets`, with `github.com/godbus/dbus/v5`, which Glutter already brings in), labelled "Emetos: <connection>"; otherwise it is asked when connecting and kept in memory until disconnect. A password may also come from an environment variable named in the form (`${env:PGPASSWORD}`). No SSH tunnel (not built).
- **The explorer** (an activity bar icon "Databases", shared by the three database extensions: each adds its own root items): connections with their state; under a connected one, databases → schemas → Tables, Views, Functions/Procedures → columns (name, type, key icons) and indexes; lazy loading, a filter, Refresh. Context menus: New Query, Select Top 1000 (opens a query and runs it), Copy Name, Generate `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` and `CREATE` (from the dialect), Drop (generated as text, never run without the user running it), Disconnect, Edit Connection, Delete Connection.
- **Query editors.** New Query opens an untitled `.sql` editor bound to the connection and database (shown in the status bar, changed with a picker; a `.sql` file of the workspace can be bound too, the binding kept in the workspace state). **Run** (Ctrl+Enter): the selection, or the statement under the cursor (split by the dialect's rules: strings, comments, dollar quotes, `DELIMITER` for MySQL, `GO` for SQL Server); **Run All** (Ctrl+Shift+Enter); **Cancel** (a button and Escape in the results). Statements run off the UI thread with a `ctx`. **Autocommit** by default; Begin, Commit and Rollback commands, the open transaction shown in the status bar, and a dirty transaction asked about on disconnect. Completion of keywords, schemas, tables and columns from the explorer's cache (a Go completion provider, §9.12), and the dialect's keyword list for highlighting is the bundled SQL grammar.
- **The results panel** (a panel tab "Query Results", shared grid `extensions/internal/resultgrid`): one tab per result set, a virtualized grid (column resize, sort on the client, cell selection, copy cell/row/column/as TSV, NULL shown as such, long values cut with a tooltip, binary shown as hex, dates in ISO form), the row count and the time, a **row limit** (`sql.maxRows`, 1000, with "Fetch More"), messages and the rows affected for statements without rows, errors with their position marked in the editor. **Export** the result to CSV, JSON or SQL `INSERT`s (a save dialog). Results are kept per editor (the last 10 runs, bounded in rows and bytes) and never written to disk or logged.
- **Safety.** A **read-only** connection refuses statements that are not reads (the dialect classifies them; and the session is set read-only where the engine has it: `SET default_transaction_read_only`, `SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, SQLite's `mode=ro`, SQL Server's `ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly` as a hint). A `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, `ALTER`, or a `DELETE`/`UPDATE` without `WHERE` asks first (`sql.confirmDestructive`, on). The connection color tints the editor's status bar item.
- **Events:** `emetos.sql.connected` / `disconnected` `{connection}`, `emetos.sql.queryFinished` `{connection, ok, rows, millis}` (no SQL text and no values).
- **Not built:** SSH tunnels, Oracle and other engines, a visual table designer, editing cells in the grid, execution plans as a diagram, ER diagrams, import from CSV.

### 10.22 MongoDB (`extensions/mongodb`)

`emetos.mongodb` ("MongoDB"), with the official driver `go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2` (D23).

- **Connections** as §10.21 (`dbconn`), or a connection string (`mongodb://`, `mongodb+srv://`; the password part of a pasted string moves to the keyring and is removed from the string that is kept); auth source and mechanism (SCRAM, X.509), TLS, replica set and direct connection, read preference; read-only.
- **The explorer** (under "Databases"): connections → databases (size) → collections (document count, estimated) → Indexes (keys, unique, TTL) and **Schema** (the fields and their types, sampled from up to 100 documents, `mongodb.schemaSampleSize`), Views and time series marked. Context menus: Open Collection (the first 20 documents in the results), New Playground, Copy Name, Create/Drop Collection and Create/Drop Index (generated as a playground, run by the user), Refresh.
- **Playgrounds** (`.mongodb` files, a language of their own, highlighted by a small TextMate grammar): **a subset of the `mongosh` syntax, parsed and run by Emetos** (Emetos has no JavaScript engine): `use <db>`; `db.<coll>.find(filter, projection)` with `.sort()`, `.skip()`, `.limit()`, `.project()`, `.count()`; `findOne`, `aggregate([...])`, `countDocuments`, `estimatedDocumentCount`, `distinct`, `insertOne`, `insertMany`, `updateOne`, `updateMany`, `replaceOne`, `deleteOne`, `deleteMany`, `bulkWrite`, `createIndex`, `dropIndex`, `getIndexes`, `drop`; `db.getCollection("name")`; `db.runCommand({...})`, `db.adminCommand({...})`; `show dbs`, `show collections`. Values are **relaxed JavaScript literals**: unquoted keys, single or double quotes, trailing commas, comments, `ObjectId("…")`, `ISODate("…")`/`new Date("…")`, `NumberLong`, `NumberInt`, `NumberDecimal`, `UUID("…")`, `BinData`, `Timestamp`, `MinKey`/`MaxKey`, `/regex/flags`, `true`/`false`/`null`; anything else (variables, functions, loops) is refused with its position (`MongoParse*` tags). Run (Ctrl+Enter) runs the statement under the cursor or the selection; Run All runs them in order, stopping at an error. The playground's connection and database are shown in the status bar.
- **Results** (the shared panel and grid of §10.21): for documents, three views: **Tree** (expandable fields with their BSON types), **JSON** (Extended JSON, relaxed, in a read-only editor), **Table** (top-level fields as columns); counts, write results (matched, modified, upserted, deleted), errors with their code. A cursor is fetched in pages (`mongodb.pageSize`, 20, with "More"); nothing is fetched beyond what is shown.
- **Editing a document.** A document in the results opens in an editor tab as Extended JSON; saving it runs `replaceOne({_id}, doc)` after a confirmation that shows the changed fields; Delete Document asks first. Read-only connections offer none of this.
- **Safety.** `drop`, `dropDatabase`, `deleteMany({})`, `updateMany({}, …)` ask first (`mongodb.confirmDestructive`).
- **Events:** `emetos.mongodb.connected` / `disconnected`, `emetos.mongodb.commandFinished` `{connection, ok, millis}`.
- **Not built:** full JavaScript (mongosh), change streams view, GridFS browsing, Atlas management, schema validation editor, export and import of collections.

### 10.23 Redis (`extensions/redis`)

`emetos.redis` ("Redis"), with `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` (D23). Works with Redis, Valkey and other servers that speak RESP.

- **Connections** as §10.21 (`dbconn`), or a URL (`redis://`, `rediss://`); user and password (ACL), TLS, database index, a key separator (`:` by default) for the tree; Sentinel (master name) and Cluster; read-only.
- **The explorer** (under "Databases"): connections → databases (`db0`…, with their key counts from `INFO keyspace`) → keys as a **tree by the separator** (`user:42:name` under `user` › `42`), loaded with **`SCAN`** in pages (`redis.scanCount`, 500; "Load More"; never `KEYS`), with a pattern filter (`MATCH`); each key with its type icon, and its TTL on hover. Cluster mode scans every master. Context menus: Open, Copy Key, Rename, Set TTL / Persist, Delete (asks), New Key (a form: type and first value).
- **The key editor** (an editor tab per key, refreshed on demand, showing type, TTL, memory usage and encoding): **string** (text, or a JSON view when it parses, or hex for binary; editable, saved with `SET` keeping the TTL); **hash** (a grid of fields and values; add, edit, delete fields); **list** (index and value; push, set, remove); **set** (members; add, remove); **sorted set** (member and score; add, change score, remove); **stream** (entries with their ids and fields, newest first, `XRANGE` in pages; add an entry); **ReJSON** values when the module is there (`JSON.GET`, shown as JSON). Large values load in pages (`HSCAN`, `SSCAN`, `ZSCAN`, `LRANGE` ranges) and big strings are cut at 1 MiB with a note.
- **The console** (a panel tab "Redis Console" per connection, and `.redis` files run like playgrounds): a command line with history and completion of command names (from `COMMAND DOCS` when the server has it), quoting as `redis-cli` does; replies formatted by type (RESP3 maps and sets as such), errors in red. **Pub/Sub** (Subscribe and PSubscribe in a panel tab: the live messages, bounded, with pause and clear; Publish) and **Monitor** are their own tabs. **Server info** (`INFO` by section, `SLOWLOG GET`, `CLIENT LIST`, `MEMORY STATS`) in an editor tab.
- **Safety.** `FLUSHDB`, `FLUSHALL`, `SHUTDOWN`, `CONFIG SET`, `DEBUG`, `KEYS`, `SCRIPT FLUSH`, `CLIENT KILL`, and `DEL` of more than one key ask first (`redis.confirmDangerous`); a read-only connection refuses commands the server's `COMMAND INFO` flags as `write` (or a built-in list when it has none). `MONITOR` warns that it slows the server down.
- **Events:** `emetos.redis.connected` / `disconnected`, `emetos.redis.commandFinished` `{connection, ok, millis}` (no keys and no values).
- **Not built:** SSH tunnels, RedisTimeSeries/RediSearch views, import and export, a memory analyzer of the whole keyspace, Lua script debugging.

### 10.24 What the database and container extensions share, and Relay

- **Shared packages:** `extensions/internal/containerapi` and `extensions/internal/containerui` (§10.20); `extensions/internal/dbconn` (connections, the keyring, the form, the "Databases" view's roots) and `extensions/internal/resultgrid` (the virtualized grid, copy and export) (§10.21–10.23).
- **A container's database.** When a container runs an image the database extensions know (`postgres`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server`, `mongo`, `redis`, `valkey/valkey`), its context menu has **Connect to Database**: the container extension publishes `emetos.containers.connectDatabase` `{engine, host, port, user, database}` from the published port and the image's environment (`POSTGRES_USER`, `MYSQL_DATABASE`…; never a password: the form asks, or reads `${env:…}`), and the database extension handling that engine opens its connection form prefilled.
- **Relay** (§10.19): the commands of these six extensions reach outside the workspace (the Docker socket is power over the computer; a database is not in the folder), so `command.ClientRefusal` gets a class `outside` with `containers.*`, `podman.*`, `sql.*`, `mongodb.*` and `redis.*`: a Relay client cannot run them. Their events are forwarded as any event (they carry no secrets, no SQL text and no values).
- **Privacy** (§12): these extensions talk only to the engines and databases the user configured; result values are never logged; passwords live only in the keyring or in memory.

### 10.25 The terminal (`extensions/terminal`)

VS Code's integrated terminal, built as an extension (`emetos.terminal`, D27): shells in pseudo-terminals in the panel, with VS Code's command ids, settings, keys and colors. Its terminals are also **events and requests** (§10.15), so the Relay extension (§10.19) can show a host's terminals to a client and, when the host allows it, let the client type in them. Requested by the user on 2026-10-27 ("Put a new extension to run terminal and working with events for the relay extension") and on 2026-10-28 ("make the terminal extension work like in vscode"): what VS Code's terminal does by default on Linux is built, and what is not is listed under **Not built**.

- **The process.** A shell from `terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.linux` and `terminal.integrated.profiles.linux` (VS Code's defaults: the shells found among `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `pwsh`, `tmux` and `sh`; with no profile, `$SHELL`, else `/bin/sh`), its arguments, in `terminal.integrated.cwd` (default: the workspace folder; else the home folder), with the environment of Emetos plus `terminal.integrated.env.linux` and `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `TERM_PROGRAM=emetos`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`. It runs in a pseudo-terminal (`extensions/internal/pty`, `/dev/ptmx` through `golang.org/x/sys/unix`, cgo-free) as the leader of a new session with the terminal as its controlling terminal; a resize sets the window size (`TIOCSWINSZ`). Its output is read on a goroutine and handed to the UI thread at most once a frame; when the emulator falls behind, reading pauses (VS Code's flow control: pause above 100,000 unprocessed characters, resume below 5,000), so a flood of output never freezes the window. Closing a terminal sends `SIGHUP` to its process group, then `SIGKILL` after 5 seconds; `terminal.integrated.confirmOnKill` and `confirmOnExit` as VS Code (default `editor` and `never`: asking only for a terminal with a child process running). Emetos ending ends every terminal.
- **The emulator** (`extensions/terminal/emulator`, no UI): a port of xterm.js (MIT; pinned in `scripts/reference-versions.txt`, every ported file saying so): the VT500 escape sequence parser, the input handler with the sequences xterm.js supports (cursor movement and erasing, scroll regions, insert and delete, tabs, character sets, SGR with 16, 256 and true colors, bold, dim, italic, underline styles, blink, inverse, invisible, strikethrough, overline; DEC private modes: application cursor and keypad keys, origin, autowrap, the alternate screen (47, 1047, 1049), bracketed paste (2004), mouse tracking (9, 1000, 1002, 1003 with the 1006 and 1015 encodings), focus events (1004), cursor visibility and style; device status and attribute replies; OSC 0/1/2 titles, OSC 4/10/11/12 colors, OSC 7 the working folder, OSC 8 hyperlinks; OSC 52 (clipboard) is ignored, as VS Code does by default), the buffer (lines of cells with attributes, wide characters by the Unicode version xterm.js uses, combining marks), the scrollback (`terminal.integrated.scrollback`, default 1000 lines), reflow of wrapped lines on resize, the encoding of keys and mouse events into bytes (xterm.js `Keyboard.ts`), and **serialization** (xterm.js's serialize addon: the screen and the scrollback written back as escape sequences, so a copy of the emulator fed with them draws the same terminal).
- **The UI.** The panel view "Terminal" (VS Code's container id `terminal`); several terminals, with VS Code's tabs list at the right of the view when there are two or more (`terminal.integrated.tabs.enabled`, the title from the process name or the title a program set, `terminal.integrated.tabs.title` `${process}`), and **splits** side by side in one tab. View actions: New Terminal (`+`), a profile dropdown, Split, Kill (trash). The widget draws the cells on a grid in `terminal.integrated.fontFamily` (default: the editor's font), `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `fontWeight`, `fontWeightBold`; the cursor (`terminal.integrated.cursorStyle` block, `cursorBlinking` false, `cursorWidth`, `cursorStyleInactive` outline); the theme's colors (`terminal.background`, `terminal.foreground`, the sixteen `terminal.ansi*`, `terminal.selectionBackground`, `terminal.selectionForeground`, `terminal.inactiveSelectionBackground`, `terminalCursor.background` and `terminalCursor.foreground`, `terminal.border`, `terminal.tab.activeBorder`, registered with VS Code's defaults), `terminal.integrated.drawBoldTextInBrightColors` and `minimumContrastRatio`; the wheel (`mouseWheelScrollSensitivity`, `fastScrollSensitivity` with Alt) and the scrollbar; selection with the mouse (drag, double-click a word with `terminal.integrated.wordSeparators`, triple-click a line, Shift+click extends, Alt forces selection while a program tracks the mouse), `terminal.integrated.copyOnSelection` (false), `rightClickBehavior` (Linux default: the context menu with Copy, Paste, Select All, Clear, Split, Kill); typing through the key encoder, with the keys of `terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell` (VS Code's default list) going to the workbench and `sendKeybindingsToShell` (false); text from an input method through the text input path of the editor (§9.3); paste as bracketed paste when the program asked for it, with VS Code's multi-line warning (`terminal.integrated.enableMultiLinePasteWarning`). The bell (`terminal.integrated.enableBell`, false: no sound; the tab's bell icon with `enableVisualBell`).
- **Commands, keys and context keys** (VS Code's ids and Linux keys): `workbench.action.terminal.toggleTerminal` (Ctrl+\`), `workbench.action.terminal.new` (Ctrl+Shift+\`), `workbench.action.terminal.split` (Ctrl+Shift+5), `workbench.action.terminal.kill`, `focus`, `focusNext`, `focusPrevious`, `focusNextPane`, `focusPreviousPane`, `resizePaneLeft/Right/Up/Down`, `copySelection` (Ctrl+Shift+C), `paste` (Ctrl+Shift+V), `selectAll`, `clear`, `scrollUp`/`scrollDown` (Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down), `scrollUpPage`/`scrollDownPage` (Shift+PageUp/PageDown), `scrollToTop`/`scrollToBottom` (Shift+Home/End), `runSelectedText`, `runActiveFile`, `sendSequence` (`{text}`), `rename`, `selectDefaultShell`, `focusFind` (Ctrl+F in a terminal), `findNext`/`findPrevious`, `hideFind`; context keys `terminalFocus`, `terminalIsOpen`, `terminalCount`, `terminalProcessSupported`, `terminalTextSelected`, `terminalFindVisible`, `terminalSplitTerminal`, `terminalHasBeenCreated`. The commands are refused to Relay clients like any command that reaches outside the workspace (`command.ClientRefusal` class `terminal`); clients use the requests below.
- **Find and links.** Find in the terminal (the find widget of §9.8 in the terminal: case, whole word, regular expression, over the scrollback). Links (VS Code's detectors): web links, file paths with `:line:col` that exist under the folder (opened in an editor), and OSC 8 hyperlinks; Ctrl+click opens, a hover says so.
- **Events and requests** (topics under `emetos.terminal`, for any extension and for Relay; positions and sizes in cells):
  - events: `emetos.terminal.created` `{id, name, profile, cwd}`, `emetos.terminal.title` `{id, title}`, `emetos.terminal.output` `{id, seq, data}` (the text the program wrote, UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced by U+FFFD, escape sequences included; one event at most every 50 ms or 64 KiB per terminal; `seq` counts the events of that terminal), `emetos.terminal.input` `{id, data, by}` (`by`: `user`, `relay:<key comment>` or an extension id), `emetos.terminal.resized` `{id, cols, rows}`, `emetos.terminal.exited` `{id, code}`, `emetos.terminal.closed` `{id}`;
  - requests: `emetos.terminal.list` → `{terminals: [{id, name, title, cols, rows, exited}]}`; `emetos.terminal.snapshot` `{id}` → `{cols, rows, seq, data}` (the serialized screen and scrollback, and the `seq` of the last output event it includes); `emetos.terminal.create` `{profile?, cwd?, name?}` → `{id}` (`cwd` relative to the folder, confined as §10.19); `emetos.terminal.write` `{id, data}` (bytes for the terminal as typed); `emetos.terminal.run` `{id?, text}` (the text and Enter, in the active terminal or a new one: VS Code's `sendText`); `emetos.terminal.kill` `{id}`.
- **Relay** (§10.19). The host forwards the terminal's events like any event. The client's tab gets a third panel, **Terminals**, next to Events and Send for a selected shared workspace: the host's terminals (from `list` and the events); selecting one draws it with the same emulator, from `snapshot` and then the `output` events in `seq` order (a gap or a reconnect takes a new snapshot), at the host's size (scrolled or clipped to fit). With **Watch and send** and the host's **Allow terminals** for that key and workspace, the panel takes the keyboard (keys go through the same encoder and become `write` requests, a paste too) and has New Terminal and Kill; otherwise it is read-only. On the host, `create`, `write`, `run` and `kill` from a client are refused (`RelayTerminalRefused`) unless **Allow terminals** is checked in Be a Host for that key and workspace (off by default; a new checkbox under Watch and send, with the warning "A client that can type in a terminal can do anything you can do on this computer"). A terminal a client typed in shows "Relay: <key comment>" in its tab until the client disconnects; the host's banner (§10.19) says so too.
- **Shell integration** (VS Code's, `terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled` true): Emetos injects VS Code's scripts (`reference/vscode/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/`, MIT, copied by `scripts/update-assets.sh`) into bash, zsh, fish and pwsh the way VS Code does (`getShellIntegrationInjection`: arguments and environment, `ZDOTDIR` for zsh, `VSCODE_*` variables kept as they are so the scripts run unchanged), and reads their sequences (OSC 633, and OSC 133, OSC 1337 `CurrentDir` and `SetMark` from other shells' scripts): where each prompt, command and output starts and ends, the command line, its exit code, and the working folder. With them:
  - command decorations in the gutter (`terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.decorationsEnabled` `both`): a circle per command, blue when it succeeded, red when it failed, gray when it is running, and a menu on click (Rerun Command, Copy Command, Copy Output, Copy Output as HTML);
  - navigation: `workbench.action.terminal.scrollToPreviousCommand` / `scrollToNextCommand` (Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down), `selectToPreviousCommand` / `selectToNextCommand` (Ctrl+Shift+Up / Down);
  - sticky scroll (`terminal.integrated.stickyScroll.enabled` true, `stickyScroll.maxLineCount` 5): the command whose output fills the view stays at the top, and a click there scrolls to it;
  - `workbench.action.terminal.runRecentCommand` (Ctrl+Alt+R) and `goToRecentDirectory` (Ctrl+G): a quick pick of the commands and folders of this terminal and of the shell's history (`terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.history` 100, kept in the extension's state per shell type);
  - the working folder the shell reports is the one a split or a new terminal starts in (`terminal.integrated.splitCwd` `inherited`) and the one links are resolved against;
  - quick fixes (`terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.quickFixEnabled` true; VS Code's built-in ones: a git command that git says is similar, `git push --set-upstream`, the link of a pull request git prints, a port in use (kill the process), shown as a light bulb on the failed command's decoration).
- **Terminal IntelliSense** (`terminal.integrated.suggest.enabled` true, as in VS Code; needs shell integration): while the user types a command line, a suggest list (the editor's suggest widget of §9.12, in the terminal) offers the commands found in `PATH` and the shell's built-ins, files and folders for arguments (relative to the shell's folder, with `~`), the command lines of the history, and the subcommands and options of the completion specs VS Code bundles that are data (`reference/vscode/extensions/terminal-suggest/src/completions/`: `git`, `npm`, `code`, `cd` and the others; converted to JSON by `scripts/update-assets.sh`; a spec's generator that runs a shell command is not built). Tab or Enter accepts (`terminal.integrated.suggest.selectionMode` `partial`), Escape closes, Ctrl+Space opens it (`workbench.action.terminal.triggerSuggest`), with `quickSuggestions` and `suggestOnTriggerCharacters` as VS Code's defaults.
- **Terminals in the editor area**, as VS Code: `workbench.action.createTerminalEditor` (a terminal in an editor tab), `workbench.action.terminal.moveToEditor` and `moveToTerminalPanel`, `terminal.integrated.defaultLocation` (`view`, or `editor`), and a terminal dragged from the tabs list onto the editor area; a terminal in an editor tab is a tab like any other (split, moved between groups, its title and icon in the tab, closing it kills it as `confirmOnKill` says).
- **The rest of the tabs list**: `changeIcon` and `changeColor` (a Codicon and one of the `terminal.ansi*` colors, in the tab and the tabs list), drag to reorder, `joinTerminals` and `unsplit`, `killAll`, `newWithProfile` and `newWithCwd`, `sizeToContentWidth` (Alt+Z), the hover of a tab (the process, its id, the folder, the shell integration state), and a terminal's process name as its title (`${process}`, the foreground process of the terminal, read from `/proc` with the terminal's `TIOCGPGRP`).
- **Persistent sessions** (`terminal.integrated.enablePersistentSessions` true, `persistentSessionReviveProcess` `onExit`, `persistentSessionScrollback` 100): when Emetos ends, each terminal's name, icon, color, place (panel or editor, splits) and working folder are saved with its last 100 lines serialized; at the next start each comes back with that content, a line VS Code writes to say the session was restored, and a new shell of the same profile in the same folder. The processes themselves end with Emetos (VS Code keeps them only across a reload of a window, which Emetos does not have).
- **Not built:** local echo (VS Code uses it only for remote terminals with latency), the GPU renderer settings, profiles of other platforms, moving a terminal to another window and attaching to a terminal of another window, the accessible buffer and the other accessibility commands, the chat and voice features, running tasks and debugging in terminals (areas 6 and 8 are later; when they come, they run in this terminal), an API of Go calls for other extensions (they use the requests).

## 11. Configuration

### 11.1 Settings (`core/jsonc`, `core/settings`)

- `settings.json` files are JSON with comments and trailing commas. `core/jsonc` parses them with positions, and edits a value while keeping comments and formatting (as VS Code's `jsonc-parser` does), given formatting options (tab size, spaces, line ending).
- Layers, lowest to highest: defaults, user (profile), workspace (`<folder>/.emetos/settings.json` only, D12), and language-specific blocks (`"[go]": {...}`) inside each layer.
- Every setting is registered with key, type, default, description, enum values and descriptions, range, scope, and category, by the step that first uses it, with VS Code's values (`editorOptions.ts` for `editor.*`, the workbench's configuration contributions for the rest). Reading an unregistered key is a programmer error (a panic in debug builds). Unknown keys in a file are kept and reported. Change events carry the affected keys. Writing a value creates the file and its folder when needed.
- **Resolution** (as VS Code): the layers are merged (objects key by key, anything else replaced) and then the `[language]` blocks of the merged result are applied for the language asked about, so a block of any layer wins over the plain settings of every layer, a workspace block over a user block, and a block of one language alone over a block shared with others (`"[go][json]"`). A language's defaults (a language contributes them like VS Code's `configurationDefaults`) are blocks of the defaults layer. Settings of the application scope are read from the user file only; a workspace file that sets one gets a problem and the value is ignored. A value that its setting does not allow (type, enum, range) falls back to the default and is listed as a problem; so are syntax errors, unknown keys and ignored keys. Writing a value keeps the comments and the file's own indentation, line ending and byte order mark, edits a setting written as nested objects where it is, and creates the file and its folder.
- The settings UI shows registered settings by category with search, edits user or workspace values, and links to the JSON (step 8.1, below).

**The settings editor as built (step 8.1; `core/settings/{layout,display,uimodel,textsource}.go`, `gui/settingsui`, `gui/app/{settingspane,settingsdocs}.go`).** Ports of `settingsEditor2.ts`, `settingsTree.ts`, `settingsTreeModels.ts`, `settingsLayout.ts` and `preferencesValidation.ts`.
- **Groups.** `DefaultTOC()` is VS Code's table of contents (`tocData`: Text Editor with Cursor, Find, Font, Formatting, Diff Editor, Multi-File Diff Editor, Minimap, Suggestions and Files; Workbench with Appearance, Breadcrumbs, Editor Management, Settings Editor, Zen Mode and Screencast Mode; Window with New Window; Features with Explorer, Search, Problems, Output and Merge Editor; Application; Security) without the groups that no setting of Emetos can be in (Chat, Debug, Terminal, Notebook and so on, which come back with the setting that needs one; the Diff Editor group is shown since step 9.2, which registers `diffEditor.maxComputationTime`). Each group has the key patterns of VS Code (`*` matches anything, whatever the case) and `BuildCategories` places the registered settings as VS Code's `resolveSettingsTree` does: the groups below a group take their settings first, then the group takes those of its patterns that no group has taken, sorted by key (case does not decide; there is no `order`). **Commonly Used** is the first group and has copies of its settings (VS Code's list, the ones that are registered). A setting no group claims goes in **Extensions**, in a group named after the first segment of its key (`emmet.*` is "Extensions > Emmet", where VS Code has the Emmet extension). A group with no setting and no group below it is not shown, and the Workspace tab leaves out the settings a workspace cannot set (the application and machine scopes), as VS Code does. The `Category` field of a setting is not used for the layout.
- **Titles.** `KeyToDisplayFormat(key, groupID)` is `settingKeyToDisplayFormat`: the part of the key before its last dot is the category, written as words (`WordifyKey`: dots become " › ", camel case is split, acronyms and a few product names are capitalized) after the part that the group already says is cut off, and the rest is the label: `editor.fontSize` is "Editor: Font Size" everywhere but in the Font group, where it is "Font Size"; `workbench.editor.showTabs` is "Workbench › Editor: Show Tabs" and "Show Tabs" in Editor Management. A description is the Markdown of the registry rendered as far as the descriptions use it (`RenderDescription`: code spans in the editor's font, `[label](target)` links and `#setting.key#` references drawn as links that do nothing yet, `**` dropped).
- **Rows** (`UIModel.Row`, `RowKind`). A check box for a boolean, a number box for a number or an integer, a text box for a string, a list (`kit.Dropdown`, whose rows show the descriptions of the values) for a setting with `Enum` of the types VS Code renders as a list, and for the rest (arrays, objects, a value of several types such as `workbench.iconTheme`) the link "Edit in settings.json". The value shown is the one in the file of the tab when it sets the setting, else the default (the Workspace tab shows the default of a setting only the user file sets, with "(Also modified in: User)" after the title; the User tab says "Workspace" likewise). A row whose setting is in the file of the tab is **modified**: a 2 px bar in `settings.modifiedItemIndicator` at its left, and the gear (visible while the pointer is over the row or it has the focus, as VS Code shows its toolbar) opens the menu Reset Setting (removes the key from the file with `Store.Remove`, which keeps the comments of the other lines; VS Code's removal also drops the comments that sit next to the key), Copy Setting ID and Copy Setting as JSON; a right click on the row opens the same menu. A value in the file that the setting does not allow is shown as the default with the message "The value in settings.json is not allowed: ... Fix in JSON.". A row is as high as its text and control are (the list is a column in a `kit.ScrollableElement`; its rows are about 180, so it is not virtualized).
- **Committing.** A check box and a list write at once. A number or text box writes on Enter and when it loses the focus, when its text differs from the value shown; a number is checked as the user types, with VS Code's messages ("Value must be a number.", "Value must be greater than or equal to 1.", "Value must be less than or equal to 100.", "Value must be an integer."), shown in a box in `inputValidation.error*` below the input, and a text that is not allowed is kept in the box and not written. The write is `Store.Update` into the user's or the workspace's file (the tab); a write that fails (the file has syntax errors: tag `SettingsFileInvalid`) is reported in a notification and the row keeps showing the old value. The rows follow the store: a change by anything else (typing in `settings.json` and saving, the Auto Save toggle, another window) shows at once, and the text of a box that the user is typing in is replaced only when the value of the setting changed.
- **The page.** A search box ("Search settings", with the filters of step 8.2 below; the Commonly Used group is left out while a search shows), the User and Workspace tabs (the Workspace tab is dimmed, with a tooltip, without a folder, and a saved view of it then shows the User tab), the button that opens the file of the tab (the `go-to-file` icon, "Open Settings (JSON)"; `workbench.settings.editor` set to `json` makes Ctrl+, open the user file instead), and below them a tree of the groups (`kit.Tree`, 220 px, resizable) beside the list. A click in the tree scrolls the list to the header of the group (headers are 26 px for a group of the first level, 22 px for the second, 18 px below); scrolling the list selects the group at its top in the tree. "Edit in settings.json" and the button open the file in a text editor (the file is made, as `{}`, when it does not exist) with the cursor on the name of the setting when the file has it, also written as nested objects.
- **Settings in an open editor** (`settings.TextSource`, `gui/app/settingsdocs.go`). VS Code's `JSONEditingService` edits the text model of `settings.json` and saves it only when it was not dirty. The store does the same: while a document is open for a settings file, `Store` computes its edit against the text of the document (`TextSource.OpenText`) and `TextSource.EditText` applies it to the document as one undo step; a document that was not dirty before the edit is saved at once (through the save of Ctrl+S, so the save participants of its language run), a dirty one stays dirty and the file is left alone until the user saves; with no document open the file is written as before. The layer of the store is read from the document too: the window keeps a copy of the text of each document that shows one of its settings files (updated on every change, readable from the goroutine of the file watcher) and reads the settings again when a change leaves the document not dirty (a revert, a reload, an undo to the saved text) and after every edit of the store; typing in a dirty `settings.json` is not applied until it is saved or the store edits it, as VS Code does not apply it either. Every writer of settings goes this way (the settings editor, the Auto Save toggle, the language picker).
- **Colors** (VS Code's names and defaults): `settings.headerForeground`, `settings.settingsHeaderHoverForeground`, `settings.modifiedItemIndicator`, `settings.headerBorder`, `settings.sashBorder`, `settings.dropdownBackground`, `dropdownForeground`, `dropdownBorder`, `dropdownListBorder`, `settings.checkboxBackground`, `checkboxForeground`, `checkboxBorder`, `settings.textInputBackground`, `textInputForeground`, `textInputBorder`, `settings.numberInputBackground`, `numberInputForeground`, `numberInputBorder`, `settings.focusedRowBackground`, `settings.rowHoverBackground` and `settings.focusedRowBorder`. A control is drawn by the kit widget in a `kit.Theme` that gives it these colors as its own. `settings.dropdownListBorder` and `settings.settingsHeaderHoverForeground` are registered and not painted.
- **Not built** (step 8.3 and later, or never): the editors of arrays and objects (they link to the JSON; VS Code has list and object widgets), the settings of extensions, sync, trusted workspaces, policy and tags, the indicators of "Also modified in" as links, the "modified in" scopes of language blocks, the Markdown of descriptions beyond the part above (the links do not open anything, `#setting#` references do not move to the setting), the sticky group header, the narrow layout without the tree, and the settings of a workspace folder that is not the window's. What step 8.2 leaves out is listed after its description.

**Search and the JSON commands as built (step 8.2; `core/settings/{search,defaultjson}.go`, `core/document/virtual.go`, `gui/settingsui`, `gui/app/{settingspane,virtualdocs}.go`).** Ports of `settingsTreeModels.ts` (`parseQuery`, `matchesAnyId`, `matchesAllLanguages`, the `modified` tag), `preferencesSearch.ts` (`cleanFilter`, `SettingMatches`'s key as words, description and enum values) and the open actions of `preferences.contribution.ts`.
- **The query** (`settings.ParseQuery`): filters first, as VS Code's regexes (`(^|\s)@filter:("value"|value)`), then the free text. `@modified` keeps the settings that the file of the tab sets (VS Code's tag `modified`: "configured in the target"; with `@lang:` the block of that language in that file). `@id:a.b,c.d` (a comma separated list, any number of `@id:` filters; case counts; an id ending in `*` is a prefix: `@id:editor.font*`) keeps those whose key is listed. `@lang:go` (an id or a name, whatever the case, as `Registry.ByName` finds it; only the first `@lang:` counts, and with a list the first of it) keeps the settings a language can set (scope `ScopeLanguageOverridable`; VS Code makes the filter act as a scope filter and not as an implicit `@modified`) and shows them as they are in the `[go]` block (below); a language that does not exist finds nothing and a hint says so. `@tag:`, `@feature:`, `@ext:`, `@hasPolicy` and `@stable` are read, taken out of the text and ignored with a hint line ("@tag:x is not supported and was ignored."). Filters combine (all must hold). What is left is the free text, cleaned of `"` and `:` (VS Code's `cleanFilter`) and split into words; a query with no filter and no word is the whole editor (the Commonly Used group included).
- **Matching and ranking** (`UIModel.Search`; simpler than VS Code's match types, which order a flat list): every word must be found, whatever the case, in the key (written as words, `editor.fontSize` is "editor font size", and also with the dots, the case and the separators left out, so `editorfontsize` finds it), in the title ("Editor: Font Size"), in the string values of an enum, or in the description. A word scores its best place: a whole word of the key 4, a part of the key or of the title 3, a value of an enum 2, a whole word of the description 2, a part of it 1; a setting scores the sum of its words, and a query that is the whole key adds 1000. The results are shown **grouped by the groups of the layout, in layout order** (VS Code shows one flat list in the order of its match types), and inside a group in the order of the scores, the layout order among equal scores. Rows keep the titles of the groups they are in ("Font Size" in Font).
- **Result line, hints and tree.** Under the search box (while the query has a filter or a word) the line "N Settings Found" ("1 Setting Found", "No Settings Found", VS Code's `searchResultsCount`), then one line for each hint (an unsupported filter, an unknown language). The list says "No Settings Found." when there is nothing. The tree has only the groups with results, each labeled with the number of the settings found in it and below it ("Font (4)", VS Code's `settings-toc-count`). The query is part of the view state (§10.3) as before; the box has a clear button (the `clear-all` icon, "Clear Search Results") while it has text, and Escape in the box clears it. The search is applied at every change (VS Code waits 200 ms); there is no suggestions dropdown.
- **The settings of a language** (`@lang:`; `UIModel.RowFor`, `SetValueFor`, `SetTextFor`, `ResetFor`; `Store.UpdateForLanguage`, `RemoveForLanguage`). The list gets a title "Language: Go" and the line "The settings below are those of the [go] block of the file."; a row shows the value the `[go]` block of the file of the tab sets, else the value the language's defaults give (the registry's `[go]` defaults), else the default; it is modified (the mark, Reset) when that block of that file sets the setting; "Also modified in" is not shown. Editing writes `"key": value` inside the `"[go]": {…}` block of the file of the tab (the block is made when it is not there; comments and indentation stay, as for any write), and Reset removes the key from the block **and the block itself when it has no other property** (VS Code's `ConfigurationEditing` leaves no empty override block; the comments inside a block that goes with it go too). The Workspace tab edits the block of the workspace file.
- **Commands** (VS Code's ids, titles and categories; all in the palette, none has a key or a menu row beyond those of §11.2): `workbench.action.openSettingsJson` ("Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)") opens the `settings.json` of the user in a text editor, made as `{` `}` (two lines) when it does not exist; `workbench.action.openWorkspaceSettingsFile` ("Preferences: Open Workspace Settings (JSON)", palette `when workbenchState != 'empty'`) opens `<folder>/.emetos/settings.json` the same way, and without a folder shows "Open a folder to edit the settings of the workspace."; both take `{"revealSetting": {"key": "editor.fontSize"}}` (VS Code's `IOpenSettingsActionOptions`; `edit`, `openToSide`, `focusSearch` and a `query` are read and ignored) and put the cursor on the name of the setting when the file has it (also written as nested objects), else at the start. `workbench.action.openRawDefaultSettings` ("Preferences: Open Default Settings (JSON)") opens the virtual document of §7.1. `workbench.action.openGlobalSettings` ("Preferences: Open User Settings") opens the User tab of the settings editor, as `openSettings` does. `workbench.action.openSettings`, `openSettings2`, `openGlobalSettings` and `openWorkspaceSettings` take the search text as a string or as `{"query": "..."}` (and `{"revealSetting": {"key": k}}` as the query `@id:k`: VS Code scrolls to the setting); with `workbench.settings.editor` set to `json` they open the file. The "Open Settings (JSON)" button of the editor runs `openSettingsJson` (User tab) or `openWorkspaceSettingsFile` (Workspace tab), and "Edit in settings.json" runs the same with `revealSetting`, through the command registry.
